# Kadr — complete documentation for AI agents

> Kadr is a free, offline CapCut-style desktop video editor in which every action is a documented command. AI agents drive it through MCP (`kadr-mcp`), a local REST API (`http://127.0.0.1:7777/api/v1`) or the `kadrctl` CLI — 188 commands with parameters, units and examples — while a human watches the edits live in the editor.

Generated 2026-10-06 from https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/ for Kadr 1.0.0. Part 1 contains the 25 English AI docs pages; part 2 the specification of all 188 commands, generated from the engine's command registry (docs/openapi.json). A running Kadr serves the same specification at http://127.0.0.1:7777/api/v1/commands.

# Kadr for AI agents

Source: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/index.html

*What an AI agent can do in Kadr, how the editor is modelled, how to connect over MCP, REST or the CLI, and how Kadr keeps your machine safe.*

Kadr is a CapCut-style desktop video editor in which every button, slider and menu item is a documented *command*. An AI agent runs the same 180+ commands over MCP, a local REST API or the `kadrctl` CLI — and a human sees every edit appear live in the editor window, with one shared undo history.

- [Quick start: Claude Code](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/claude-code.html): One command connects Kadr; first prompts to try.
- [Claude Desktop](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/claude-desktop.html): A four-line config snippet.
- [Recipes](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/recipes.html): Eleven end-to-end workflows, every call verified against a real engine.
- [Command reference](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference-intro.html): Every command with parameters, units, defaults and examples.

## What an agent can do

| Area | What the agent does | Example commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Assemble | Import files and folders, place clips on a magnetic main track and overlay tracks, trim, split, move, duplicate, freeze, change speed | `media.import`, `timeline.segment.add`, `timeline.segment.trim` |
| Look | 221 transitions, 227 filters, 195 effects with named sliders, colour adjustments with HSL and curves, masks, chroma key, 310 clip animations, keyframes with easing — and a contact sheet of how any of them plays before choosing | `transition.set`, `filter.add`, `keyframe.add`, `library.preview` |
| Text & captions | 175 text templates, 114 word-art effects (patterns, bevels, sparkles, drips…), 137 letter animations, 146 free fonts to install on demand; offline Whisper captions in about 100 languages with 55 caption styles; edit the video by editing its transcript | `text.add`, `font.install`, `captions.auto`, `transcript.remove_fillers` |
| Audio | Volume in dB, fades, 25 voice effects, noise reduction, loudness normalisation, beat detection, 47 synthesised sound effects, text-to-speech with local or ElevenLabs voices | `segment.set_volume`, `audio.detect_beats`, `tts.speak` |
| Smart tools | Auto reframe to any ratio, scene detection and splitting, silence removal, background removal | `ai.auto_reframe`, `ai.remove_silence` |
| Generate | 98 presets of 22 kinds rendered locally — mesh gradients, aurora, bokeh, particles, light leaks, film dust, textures, patterns, timers, banners, frames, test cards — plus 394 stickers, 73 of them animated; no stock footage | `media.generate`, `sticker.add` |
| See | Render any frame, a contact sheet of the whole edit, the on-canvas box of every clip, or how a library item plays; MCP returns pictures as images | `preview.frame`, `preview.contact_sheet`, `preview.layout` |
| Deliver | MP4/MOV in H.264 or HEVC up to 4K (GPU encoders when available), GIF, audio only, SRT/VTT captions | `export.start`, `captions.export` |
| Show the human | Open a project in the window, select a clip, switch the library tab, show a notification | `ui.open_project`, `ui.toast` |

## Three ways in

All three reach the same engine — the open editor (`Kadr.exe`) or the headless `kadr-server.exe` — at `http://127.0.0.1:7777`, and run exactly the same commands.

| Interface | Best for | How it names commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [MCP](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/mcp.html) (`kadr-mcp.exe`) | Claude Code, Claude Desktop and other agent apps. Starts the engine by itself if Kadr is not running; returns frames as images. | Dots become underscores: `timeline_segment_split`; plus `kadr_batch` |
| [REST](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/rest.html) | Your own scripts and services in any language; WebSocket events. | `POST /api/v1/commands/timeline.segment.split` |
| [CLI](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/cli.html) (`kadrctl.exe`) | Terminals, shell scripts, quick checks; accepts times like `2.5s`. | `kadrctl run timeline.segment.split --at_us 2.5s …` |

## Mental model

```text
project          prj_…   canvas, settings, playhead
├─ materials[]   mat_…   imported or generated files (photos: duration 0)
├─ tracks[]      trk_…   tracks[0] is drawn first, at the bottom
│  ├─ main_video         magnetic: clips sit back to back, no gaps
│  ├─ video_overlay · text · sticker · effect · filter · adjustment
│  └─ audio
│     └─ segments[]  seg_…  timeline range + source range in a material
└─ markers[]     mrk_…
```

- **Time is integer microseconds** everywhere: 1 s = `1000000`. Parameters that hold time end in `_us`.
- **Ids are opaque strings** with a type prefix (`prj_`, `trk_`, `seg_`, `mat_`, `exp_`…). Read them from results; never invent them.
- **Commands are either project-scoped** (they take `project_id`, are saved and are undoable) **or global** (projects list, library, export jobs, settings).
- **Every edit is undoable** with `edit.undo`; a batch of edits is one undo step; edits from the UI and from agents share the history.

The full rules — magnet, linked clips, transitions, keyframes, coordinates, units — are in [Concepts](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/concepts.html). How to find, preview and apply library items and fonts is in [Library, previews and fonts](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/library.html).

## The first five calls

A complete edit: create a vertical project, generate a background, add a title, look at it, export. Each tab shows the same calls; the MCP tab is what an agent sends.

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "project_create", "arguments": {"name": "My first video", "ratio": "9:16"}}
{"name": "media_generate", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_74f3bf737c17", "preset_id": "sunset_gradient", "duration_us": 5000000, "add_to_timeline": true}}
{"name": "text_add", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_74f3bf737c17", "text": "Hello from an agent", "template_id": "title_bold", "at_us": 0, "duration_us": 3000000}}
{"name": "preview_frame", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_74f3bf737c17", "time_us": 1000000, "width": 540}}
{"name": "export_start", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_74f3bf737c17", "resolution": "1080p"}}
```

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run project.create --name "My first video" --ratio 9:16
kadrctl run media.generate --project_id prj_74f3bf737c17 --preset_id sunset_gradient --duration_us 5s --add_to_timeline
kadrctl run text.add --project_id prj_74f3bf737c17 --text "Hello from an agent" --template_id title_bold --at_us 0 --duration_us 3s
kadrctl run preview.frame --project_id prj_74f3bf737c17 --time_us 1s --width 540
kadrctl run export.start --project_id prj_74f3bf737c17 --resolution 1080p
```

**curl:**

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7777/api/v1/commands/project.create -H "Authorization: Bearer $KADR_TOKEN" -d '{"name":"My first video","ratio":"9:16"}'
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7777/api/v1/commands/media.generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KADR_TOKEN" -d '{"project_id":"prj_74f3bf737c17","preset_id":"sunset_gradient","duration_us":5000000,"add_to_timeline":true}'
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7777/api/v1/commands/text.add -H "Authorization: Bearer $KADR_TOKEN" -d '{"project_id":"prj_74f3bf737c17","text":"Hello from an agent","template_id":"title_bold","at_us":0,"duration_us":3000000}'
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7777/api/v1/commands/preview.frame -H "Authorization: Bearer $KADR_TOKEN" -d '{"project_id":"prj_74f3bf737c17","time_us":1000000,"width":540}'
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7777/api/v1/commands/export.start -H "Authorization: Bearer $KADR_TOKEN" -d '{"project_id":"prj_74f3bf737c17","resolution":"1080p"}'
```

The export runs in the background; `export.status` with the returned `job_id` reports progress until `state` is `done`. Without `path`, videos go to `%USERPROFILE%\Videos\Kadr`.

## Safety and privacy

- **Local only.** The API listens on `127.0.0.1`; requests addressed to any other host name get `403 forbidden` (DNS-rebinding protection), and browsers may only connect from local origins.
- **Token.** Every request except health and documentation needs the token from `%APPDATA%\Kadr\api-token`. `kadr-mcp` and `kadrctl` read it themselves. Treat it like a password: it gives full control over your projects.
- **Everything is undoable** — except deleting a whole project, which MCP marks as destructive so clients ask first. Imported media files are never modified or deleted.
- **Nothing is uploaded by Kadr.** Commands read and write files on your PC at paths you give. The only network traffic is optional: ElevenLabs voices (the text you synthesise), update checks, the one-time FFmpeg download, and font files from the google/fonts repository when `font.install` runs. Frames and data reach your AI provider only when the agent asks for them through tools you allow.

## Machine-readable files

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| [`llms.txt`](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/llms.txt) | An index of these docs for LLMs (llmstxt.org format). |
| [`llms-full.txt`](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/llms-full.txt) | All AI docs as Markdown plus the full specification of every command — paste it into a model’s context. |
| [`openapi.json`](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/openapi.json) | OpenAPI 3.1 description of every command. A running Kadr serves its own copy at `/api/v1/openapi.json` and an HTML reference at `/docs`. |

# Quick start: Claude Code

Source: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/claude-code.html

*Connect Claude Code to Kadr with one command, check the connection, pre-approve tools and try your first prompts.*

One command registers Kadr’s MCP server with Claude Code for every project on your PC. After that, describe the video you want — Claude edits it in Kadr, looks at rendered frames to check its work, and every change can be undone.

## Before you start

- **Kadr is installed.** The installer puts `kadr-mcp.exe` in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Kadr\` next to `Kadr.exe` and `kadr-server.exe`. In Kadr, **Settings → API & automation** shows the exact path and a ready-made command.
- **Claude Code is installed** and `claude` runs in your terminal.
- **Kadr does not have to be running.** If neither the editor nor a server answers, `kadr-mcp` starts the headless `kadr-server.exe` by itself (about 2 seconds). To *watch* the edits, open Kadr before the first call — see the note below.

## 1. Add the server

Register Kadr once for your user account (`--scope user`), so it is available in every folder. Everything after `--` is the command Claude Code starts.

**Command Prompt:**

```bat
claude mcp add --scope user kadr -- "%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Kadr\kadr-mcp.exe"
```

**PowerShell:**

```powershell
claude mcp add --scope user kadr -- "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Kadr\kadr-mcp.exe"
```

If you kept the installer option *Add kadrctl and kadr-mcp to PATH*, the short form works too: `claude mcp add --scope user kadr -- kadr-mcp`.

## 2. Check the connection

```powershell
claude mcp list
claude mcp get kadr
```

`kadr` should be listed as connected. Inside a session, `/mcp` shows the server, its 178 tools (one per command plus `kadr_batch`) and lets you reconnect after a problem.

## 3. Pre-approve tools (optional)

Claude Code asks before it uses a tool. To stop the prompts for Kadr, allow the whole server in `.claude/settings.json` (one project) or `~/.claude/settings.json` (everywhere):

```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": ["mcp__kadr"]
  }
}
```

Prefer something stricter? Allow only read-only tools, for example `"mcp__kadr__project_list"`, `"mcp__kadr__timeline_get"`, `"mcp__kadr__preview_frame"` and `"mcp__kadr__preview_contact_sheet"`, and keep approving edits one by one. Every edit can be undone anyway.

## 4. First prompts to try

Open Kadr first so you can watch, start `claude` in any folder, and try:

> List my Kadr projects and summarise the timeline of the most recent one.

> Create a 9:16 Kadr project called "MCP test", generate a 5-second aurora_flow background, add the title "It works" with the title_bold template, open the project in the Kadr window and show me the frame at 1 second.

> Import C:\Users\you\Videos\clip.mp4 into "MCP test", put it after the background, add word-highlight captions and show me a contact sheet of the whole video.

> Put a 0.4-second mix transition on every cut in one batch, then export 1080p to C:\Users\you\Videos\Kadr\mcp-test.mp4 and tell me when it is done.

> Undo the last two changes in "MCP test".

More complete workflows, with every call spelled out, are in the [recipes](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/recipes.html).

> **Warning:** **Watching live needs the editor’s engine.** If Kadr was closed when Claude made its first call, `kadr-mcp` started a headless `kadr-server.exe`, which keeps running after the chat. If you then open Kadr, the window cannot take over port 7777 and will not show the agent’s edits. Quit `kadr-server.exe` (Task Manager → Details) before opening Kadr, then run `/mcp` to reconnect.

## Share the setup with a repository

For a folder that always works with Kadr, commit a `.mcp.json` at its root. Claude Code asks each person once before it loads a project-scoped server. With `kadr-mcp` on `PATH` the file is the same for everyone:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "kadr": { "type": "stdio", "command": "kadr-mcp", "args": [] }
  }
}
```

A few lines in that folder’s `CLAUDE.md` save the agent a lot of guessing:

```markdown
## Video editing
- Edit videos through the kadr MCP server. Times are integer microseconds (1 s = 1000000).
- Read state first (timeline_get), apply related edits in one kadr_batch, then check with preview_frame or preview_contact_sheet.
- Show your work: call ui_open_project at the start; export with export_start and poll export_status.
- Media lives in ./footage; exports go to ./exports.
```

## A different port or data folder

To drive a separate engine (for example a test `kadr-server.exe` on port 7790 with its own projects), pass environment variables when adding the server:

```powershell
claude mcp add --scope user --env KADR_ADDR=127.0.0.1:7790 --env KADR_DATA_DIR=D:\kadr-automation kadr-test -- "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Kadr\kadr-mcp.exe"
```

Remove a server with `claude mcp remove kadr --scope user`.

## Tips for Claude Code

- **Large results.** Claude Code caps a tool result at about 25,000 tokens by default (`MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` raises it). Prefer `timeline_get` over `project_get`, pass `include_words: false` to `captions_list`, and keep contact-sheet tiles small (240–320 px).
- **Long jobs.** Captions, transcription and exports run in the background. Asking for `wait: true` is fine for a few minutes of media; for longer jobs ask Claude to poll `captions_status` (with `wait_s`) or `export_status`.
- **Slow first start.** If the server times out while the engine starts, raise `MCP_TIMEOUT` (milliseconds) when launching Claude Code.
- **Files.** Paths are on the PC where Kadr runs. Claude Code’s own file tools and Kadr see the same disk, so Claude can write a batch file or an SRT and hand its path to Kadr.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `claude mcp list` shows kadr as failed | Check the path: `Test-Path "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Kadr\kadr-mcp.exe"`. Quote paths that contain spaces. |
| `Kadr engine did not start … within 10 s` | `kadr-server.exe` must sit next to `kadr-mcp.exe`. Start Kadr yourself, then `/mcp` → reconnect. |
| `unauthorized: missing or invalid API token` | A stale `KADR_TOKEN` or a different `KADR_DATA_DIR` in the server’s environment. Remove them, or re-add the server. |
| Edits don’t appear in the open window | A headless `kadr-server.exe` owns port 7777 — see the warning above. |
| `not_available` from captions or background removal | An optional local component is missing. Ask Claude to run `captions_asr_status` or `ai_capabilities`; the `hint` says what to install. |
