# Claude Desktop

Source: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/claude-desktop.html

*Add Kadr to Claude Desktop with a short claude_desktop_config.json entry, restart, and let Claude edit while you watch.*

Claude Desktop starts `kadr-mcp.exe` for you and shows Kadr’s tools in every chat. It takes one entry in a JSON file and a restart.

### 1. Open the config file

In Claude Desktop open **Settings → Developer → Edit Config**. This opens `claude_desktop_config.json` — normally `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json`. Create the file if it does not exist.

### 2. Add Kadr

Paste this, with your own user name in the path (Kadr’s **Settings → API & automation** shows the exact snippet for your PC). In JSON every backslash is written twice.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "kadr": {
      "command": "C:\\Users\\you\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\Kadr\\kadr-mcp.exe"
    }
  }
}
```

If the file already has an `mcpServers` section, add only the `"kadr": { … }` entry inside it, separated from its neighbours by a comma.

### 3. Restart Claude Desktop completely

Closing the window is not enough: right-click the Claude icon in the notification area and choose **Quit**, then start Claude Desktop again. Open Kadr first if you want to watch the edits.

### 4. Check that it works

Kadr’s tools now appear in the chat’s tools menu. Start a new chat and ask:

> List my Kadr projects.

Claude calls `project_list` and answers. Then try an edit and watch the editor:

> Create a 9:16 Kadr project called "Desktop test", open it in the Kadr window, generate a 4-second sunset_gradient background, add the title "Hello" with the title_bold template and show me the frame at 1 second.

## What Claude gets

- One tool per Kadr command (`timeline_segment_split` for `timeline.segment.split`) with the full description, parameter units and examples, plus `kadr_batch` for atomic multi-step edits. See [MCP tools](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/mcp.html).
- Server instructions that explain the basics: projects → tracks → segments, microseconds, read state first, batch edits, look at frames.
- Pictures: `preview_frame` and `preview_contact_sheet` return image content, so Claude actually sees the result of its edit.

## Another port or data folder

By default the bridge talks to `127.0.0.1:7777` and reads the token from `%APPDATA%\Kadr`. For a separate engine, add an `env` block:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "kadr": {
      "command": "C:\\Users\\you\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\Kadr\\kadr-mcp.exe",
      "env": {
        "KADR_ADDR": "127.0.0.1:7790",
        "KADR_DATA_DIR": "D:\\kadr-automation"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`KADR_TOKEN` can be set instead of `KADR_DATA_DIR`.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No Kadr tools in the chat | The config was not reloaded, or the JSON is invalid. | Quit Claude Desktop from the tray and start it again. Check the JSON (commas, doubled backslashes). |
| “Server disconnected” or the server fails to start | Wrong path to `kadr-mcp.exe`. | Use the full path from Kadr’s **Settings → API & automation**. The server’s log is in `%APPDATA%\Claude\logs\` (`mcp-server-kadr.log`). |
| `Kadr engine did not start … within 10 s` | `kadr-server.exe` is missing next to `kadr-mcp.exe`, or blocked. | Start Kadr yourself and ask again. |
| Edits don’t appear in the open Kadr window | The bridge started a headless `kadr-server.exe` before Kadr was opened; it owns port 7777. | Quit `kadr-server.exe` in Task Manager, keep Kadr open, restart Claude Desktop. |
| `unauthorized: missing or invalid API token` | An old `KADR_TOKEN` or a different `KADR_DATA_DIR` in `env`. | Remove them, or copy the token from `%APPDATA%\Kadr\api-token`. |
| A call stops after 5 minutes | The bridge waits at most 5 minutes per call (for example `wait: true` on long captions). | Run long jobs without `wait` and poll `captions_status` or `export_status`. |

---

# Other MCP clients

Source: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/other-mcp-clients.html

*Connect Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI or any other MCP client to Kadr, test the bridge by hand, and use agents without MCP.*

Any client that can start a local stdio MCP server can drive Kadr. The server is a single executable with no arguments; everything else is optional.

## The settings every client needs

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Transport | stdio |
| Command | Full path to `kadr-mcp.exe` (or `kadr-mcp` when it is on `PATH`), no arguments |
| Environment | Optional: `KADR_ADDR`, `KADR_DATA_DIR`, `KADR_TOKEN` |
| Protocol version | `2025-06-18` |
| Tools | 178: one per command plus `kadr_batch`; read-only commands carry `readOnlyHint`, `project_delete` carries `destructiveHint` |

When the engine is not running, `kadr-mcp` starts `kadr-server.exe` from its own folder and waits up to 10 seconds for it. It reads the API token from the Kadr data folder, so no secret goes into the client’s config.

## Config snippets

The file names and shapes below are what these clients use at the time of writing — check your client’s documentation if a key has changed. Comments are for orientation; remove them if your client rejects comments in JSON.

**Cursor:**

```cursor
// %USERPROFILE%\.cursor\mcp.json (all projects) or .cursor\mcp.json (one project)
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "kadr": { "command": "C:\\Users\\you\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\Kadr\\kadr-mcp.exe" }
  }
}
```

**VS Code:**

```vscode
// .vscode\mcp.json (VS Code agent mode)
{
  "servers": {
    "kadr": { "type": "stdio", "command": "C:\\Users\\you\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\Kadr\\kadr-mcp.exe" }
  }
}
```

**Windsurf:**

```windsurf
// %USERPROFILE%\.codeium\windsurf\mcp_config.json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "kadr": { "command": "C:\\Users\\you\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\Kadr\\kadr-mcp.exe" }
  }
}
```

**Codex CLI:**

```codex
# %USERPROFILE%\.codex\config.toml (Codex CLI)
[mcp_servers.kadr]
command = 'C:\Users\you\AppData\Local\Programs\Kadr\kadr-mcp.exe'
```

**Gemini CLI:**

```gemini
// %USERPROFILE%\.gemini\settings.json (Gemini CLI)
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "kadr": { "command": "C:\\Users\\you\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\Kadr\\kadr-mcp.exe" }
  }
}
```

## Test the bridge by hand

MCP over stdio is one JSON-RPC message per line, so PowerShell can talk to the bridge directly — useful when a client only says “failed to start”:

```powershell
@'
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"test","version":"1"}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"project_list","arguments":{}}}
'@ | & "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Kadr\kadr-mcp.exe"
```

The second line of output is the `project_list` result. Errors come back as tool results with `"isError": true` and the engine’s JSON error (code, message, hint, field), so agents can read the hint and retry.

## Agents without MCP

- **Function calling.** Generate tool definitions from [`openapi.json`](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/openapi.json) (each command’s request body is a JSON Schema) and execute calls with `POST /api/v1/commands/<name>` — see [REST API](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/rest.html).
- **Shell-only agents.** Let the agent run `kadrctl describe <command>` to read documentation and `kadrctl run` to execute — see [kadrctl](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/cli.html).
- **Context.** Give the model [`llms.txt`](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/llms.txt) or the complete [`llms-full.txt`](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/llms-full.txt).

## Kadr on another machine

The API only accepts requests addressed to `localhost`, by design. To drive Kadr on another PC, forward a local port to it (for example `ssh -L 7777:127.0.0.1:7777 user@editing-pc`), copy that PC’s `api-token` into `KADR_TOKEN`, and keep in mind that file paths refer to the remote disk.

---

# MCP tools

Source: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/mcp.html

*How Kadr’s commands appear as MCP tools: naming, annotations, kadr_batch for atomic edits, images from preview tools, errors and timeouts.*

`kadr-mcp.exe` turns every Kadr command into an MCP tool with the command’s full documentation, and adds one extra tool, `kadr_batch`. Calls are forwarded to the running engine, so edits show up live in the editor and land in the same undo history.

> **Tip:** Setting up a client? See [Claude Code](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/claude-code.html), [Claude Desktop](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/claude-desktop.html) or [other MCP clients](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/other-mcp-clients.html). This page explains what the agent gets once connected.

## Tool names and arguments

Many clients reject dots in tool names, so dots become underscores. Arguments are exactly the command’s parameters; project commands need `project_id`.

| Command | MCP tool | Typical arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `project.create` | `project_create` | `{"name": "Trip", "ratio": "9:16"}` |
| `timeline.segment.split` | `timeline_segment_split` | `{"project_id": "prj_…", "segment_id": "seg_…", "at_us": 2500000}` |
| `captions.auto` | `captions_auto` | `{"project_id": "prj_…", "language": "uk", "wait": true}` |
| `preview.frame` | `preview_frame` | `{"project_id": "prj_…", "time_us": 1000000, "width": 960}` |
| `edit.undo` | `edit_undo` | `{"project_id": "prj_…"}` |

In these docs the **MCP** tab of a code block shows the parameters of a `tools/call` request: `{"name": "<tool>", "arguments": {…}}`. Each line is one call.

## What each tool tells the model

- **Description** — what the command does, how it behaves like CapCut, edge cases, then the UI location and hotkey, “Undoable with edit.undo.” for edits, and a `Returns:` line describing the result.
- **Input schema** — JSON Schema with types, enums, ranges, defaults and a description per parameter; units are spelled out (“Unit: microseconds”).
- **Annotations** — `readOnlyHint` on queries such as `timeline_get`, `preview_frame` or `library_list`; `destructiveHint` on `project_delete`, so cautious clients confirm it.

Library ids (transitions, effects, filters, animations, fonts, stickers, caption styles, generated presets, sound effects…) are discovered with `library_list` and `library_get` rather than guessed.

## kadr_batch — several edits, one undo step

`kadr_batch` runs a list of project commands in order as **one atomic step**: either every call succeeds and the project is saved once, with a single undo entry “Batch (N actions)”, or nothing changes. Calls use *dotted* command names, and `project_id` is filled in for every call. `dry_run: true` runs the whole list on a copy and returns the results without saving.

```json
[
  {"command": "transition.set", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_8f2a61c04b9e", "type": "whip_pan", "duration_us": 300000}},
  {"command": "segment.set_volume", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_1d93b7e5a0c2", "volume_db": -12}},
  {"command": "text.add", "args": {"text": "Day one", "template_id": "title_bold", "at_us": 0, "duration_us": 2000000}}
]
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "kadr_batch", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_5c1e7a9d3b20", "calls": [
  {"command": "transition.set", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_8f2a61c04b9e", "type": "whip_pan", "duration_us": 300000}},
  {"command": "segment.set_volume", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_1d93b7e5a0c2", "volume_db": -12}},
  {"command": "text.add", "args": {"text": "Day one", "template_id": "title_bold", "at_us": 0, "duration_us": 2000000}}
]}}
```

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl batch prj_5c1e7a9d3b20 demo-batch.json
```

**curl:**

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7777/api/v1/projects/prj_5c1e7a9d3b20/batch -H "Authorization: Bearer $KADR_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"dry_run":false,"calls":[{"command":"transition.set","args":{"segment_id":"seg_8f2a61c04b9e","type":"whip_pan","duration_us":300000}},{"command":"segment.set_volume","args":{"segment_id":"seg_1d93b7e5a0c2","volume_db":-12}},{"command":"text.add","args":{"text":"Day one","template_id":"title_bold","at_us":0,"duration_us":2000000}}]}'
```

The result holds one entry per call, in order: `{"results": [ … ], "dry_run": false}`.

- **No references between calls.** Arguments are fixed before the batch runs, so a call cannot use an id created by an earlier call in the same batch. Create things first, read their ids, then batch the follow-up edits.
- **Project commands only.** Global commands (for example `export.start`, `project.create`, `library.list`) and `edit.undo`/`edit.redo` are rejected: `call 0: export.start is not a project command and cannot be batched` (call numbers start at 0).
- **Runtime errors** return the failing command’s own error (with its hint); the working copy is discarded.
- **Side effects outside the project** (generated media files, speech files in the cache) are not rolled back by a failed batch or a dry run — they are only files.

## Pictures the model can see

Results that contain a `png_base64` field are returned as an MCP **image** block plus a text block with the remaining fields. That applies to `preview_frame` (one composited frame, exactly as exported), `preview_contact_sheet` (a grid of frames across the edit, with `times_us` for each tile) and `library_preview` (how a transition, effect, filter, animation, text look, caption style, animated sticker or generated clip plays — look before you choose; see [Library, previews and fonts](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/library.html#preview)). For measurements use `preview_layout`: it returns the box of every visible clip, text and sticker in canvas pixels. See [Verifying results](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/verifying.html).

## Errors

A failed call is a tool result with `"isError": true` whose text is the engine’s error as JSON:

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "segment_set_volume", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_5c1e7a9d3b20", "segment_id": "seg_nope", "volume_db": -6}}
```

```json
Error: {
  "code": "not_found",
  "message": "segment \"seg_nope\" not found",
  "hint": "Call project.get (tracks[].segments[].id) or timeline.get to list valid segment ids.",
  "field": "segment_id"
}
```

Read the `hint`: it says how to fix the call. Codes are listed in [REST API → Errors](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/rest.html#errors); `not_available` means an optional local component (Whisper, a matting model, a speech engine, FFmpeg) is missing on this PC.

## Long-running tools

- The bridge waits up to **5 minutes** for a call. Captions, transcription, background removal and exports run as background jobs: call them without `wait` and poll `captions_status` (supports `wait_s` long polling), `ai_jobs` or `export_status`.
- `export_start` always returns immediately with a `job_id`; exports run one at a time and extra jobs wait in state `queued`.

## Engine discovery and auto-start

The bridge connects to `KADR_ADDR` (default `127.0.0.1:7777`) with the token from `KADR_TOKEN` or the data folder. If nothing answers, it starts `kadr-server.exe` from its own folder and waits up to 10 seconds. That headless engine keeps running after the client exits, so later sessions start instantly; quit it in Task Manager before opening the editor if you want to watch edits live.

The tool list comes from the running engine, so it always matches the installed version. On `initialize` the server also sends short instructions: projects contain tracks, tracks contain segments, times are microseconds, read state first, use `kadr_batch` for multi-step edits, look at `preview_frame` after visual edits, and follow error hints.

---

# REST API

Source: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/rest.html

*Call any Kadr command over HTTP on 127.0.0.1:7777: token, response envelope, error codes and hints, batches and dry runs, resource aliases, WebSocket events and binary endpoints.*

Every Kadr command is available over HTTP on your own PC. POST a JSON object of arguments to `/api/v1/commands/<name>` and you get back exactly what the editor’s buttons get.

## Base URL

```text
http://127.0.0.1:7777/api/v1
```

The editor (`Kadr.exe`) and the headless `kadr-server.exe` both serve it. Set `KADR_ADDR` (for example `127.0.0.1:7790`) before starting Kadr to move it. Without a token you can call `GET /api/v1/health` → `{"ok":true,"result":{"status":"ok","version":"…"}}`, `GET /api/v1/openapi.json` and the HTML reference at `GET /docs`.

## Authentication

Everything else needs the API token, created on first run and stored in `%APPDATA%\Kadr\api-token` (Kadr shows the path in **Settings → API & automation**). Send it as a bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

**PowerShell:**

```powershell
$env:KADR_TOKEN = (Get-Content "$env:APPDATA\Kadr\api-token" -Raw).Trim()
```

**Command Prompt:**

```bat
set /p KADR_TOKEN=<"%APPDATA%\Kadr\api-token"
```

**bash:**

```bash
export KADR_TOKEN=$(cat "$APPDATA/Kadr/api-token")
```

Browsers cannot set headers on `<img>`, `<audio>` or WebSocket requests, so those may pass `?token=<token>` instead. `KADR_TOKEN` set before Kadr starts overrides the file; to rotate the token, quit Kadr, delete `api-token` and start Kadr again.

## Calling a command

`POST /api/v1/commands/{name}` with a JSON object of arguments (an empty body means no arguments). Names are the same everywhere — in the reference, in `kadrctl`, and in MCP with underscores.

**curl:**

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7777/api/v1/commands/text.add -H "Authorization: Bearer $KADR_TOKEN" -d '{"project_id":"prj_a049124a748a","text":"Day one","template_id":"title_bold","at_us":0,"duration_us":2000000}'
```

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run text.add --project_id prj_a049124a748a --text "Day one" --template_id title_bold --at_us 0 --duration_us 2s
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "text_add", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_a049124a748a", "text": "Day one", "template_id": "title_bold", "at_us": 0, "duration_us": 2000000}}
```

In PowerShell, `Invoke-RestMethod` turns the answer into objects. Keep `charset=utf-8` in the content type — without it Windows PowerShell 5.1 garbles non-English text.

```powershell
function Invoke-Kadr($Command, $Arguments = @{}) {
  $body = $Arguments | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 -Compress
  $r = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:7777/api/v1/commands/$Command" `
    -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $env:KADR_TOKEN" } `
    -ContentType 'application/json; charset=utf-8' -Body $body
  $r.result
}

$p = Invoke-Kadr project.create @{ name = 'Trip'; ratio = '9:16' }
Invoke-Kadr timeline.get @{ project_id = $p.id }
```

In Windows PowerShell 5.1, `curl` is an alias of `Invoke-WebRequest`; call `curl.exe` by its full name or use `Invoke-RestMethod`.

## Response envelope

Every response is JSON. Success:

```json
{ "ok": true, "result": { … the command’s result … } }
```

Failure — `message` says what went wrong, `hint` how to fix the call, `field` which parameter is at fault (when there is one):

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "invalid_argument",
    "message": "parameter \"ratio\": must be one of [16:9 9:16 1:1 4:3 3:4 21:9 2.35:1 2:1 1.85:1 5.8-inch]",
    "hint": "Canvas aspect ratio. 9:16 is vertical (TikTok/Reels/Shorts), 16:9 is landscape (YouTube), 1:1 is square.",
    "field": "ratio"
  }
}
```

## Error codes and HTTP status

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid_argument` | 400 | A parameter is missing, has the wrong type or is out of range; also a malformed batch. |
| `unauthorized` | 401 | Missing or wrong token. |
| `forbidden` | 403 | The request was not addressed to `localhost`/`127.0.0.1`/`::1`. |
| `not_found` | 404 | Unknown project, segment, material, job, voice or library id. |
| `unknown_command` | 404 | No command has that name. |
| `conflict` | 409 | The edit clashes with the project: a locked track, clips that don’t touch for a transition, overlapping cues. |
| `nothing_to_undo` | 409 | Undo or redo with an empty history. |
| `not_implemented` | 501 | The command is planned but not available yet. |
| `not_available` | 503 | Something needed is missing on this PC — FFmpeg, faster-whisper or a Whisper model, a speech voice, a matting model. The `hint` says what to install; `tools.status`, `captions.asr_status`, `ai.capabilities` and `tts.voices` report what was found. |
| `internal` | 500 | An unexpected failure (for example an FFmpeg error while rendering). |

## Times are microseconds

Every time and duration is an integer number of microseconds, and those parameters end in `_us`: one frame at 30 fps = `33333`, 0.5 s = `500000`, 1 min 30 s = `90000000`. REST takes integers only; `kadrctl` also accepts `2.5s`, `1500ms` and `00:01:02.5`. Other units are written in each parameter’s description (decibels, 0–1 opacity, canvas fractions…).

## Discovering commands

| Request | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/v1/commands` | Every command spec: name, title, category, description, scope, params, returns, errors, examples, menu, undoable, read_only. `?category=Export` filters. |
| `GET /api/v1/commands/{name}` | `{spec, input_schema}` — `input_schema` is a JSON Schema. |
| `GET /api/v1/openapi.json` | OpenAPI 3.1 for the whole API (no token) — generate clients or tool definitions from it. |
| `GET /docs` | The HTML command reference served by your running Kadr. |

## Batches and dry runs

`POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/batch` runs several project commands as **one atomic edit** and one undo step (“Batch (N actions)”). If a call fails nothing is saved. With `"dry_run": true` every call runs on a copy and you see the results, but nothing is saved. `project_id` is filled in for every call.

```json
[
  {"command": "segment.set_background", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_a049124a748b", "type": "blur", "blur": 0.75}},
  {"command": "text.add", "args": {"text": "Day one", "at_us": 0, "duration_us": 2000000}}
]
```

**curl:**

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7777/api/v1/projects/prj_a049124a748a/batch -H "Authorization: Bearer $KADR_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"dry_run":false,"calls":[{"command":"segment.set_background","args":{"segment_id":"seg_a049124a748b","type":"blur","blur":0.75}},{"command":"text.add","args":{"text":"Day one","at_us":0,"duration_us":2000000}}]}'
```

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl batch prj_a049124a748a demo.json --dry-run
kadrctl batch prj_a049124a748a demo.json
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "kadr_batch", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_a049124a748a", "calls": [
  {"command": "segment.set_background", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_a049124a748b", "type": "blur", "blur": 0.75}},
  {"command": "text.add", "args": {"text": "Day one", "at_us": 0, "duration_us": 2000000}}
]}}
```

The answer is `{"ok": true, "result": {"results": [ … one per call … ], "dry_run": false}}`. Calls run in order and see the effects of earlier calls, but arguments are fixed in advance, so a call cannot use an id created earlier in the same batch. Only project commands can be batched; global commands and `edit.undo`/`edit.redo` are rejected with `invalid_argument` (“call 0: …”, counting from 0).

## Resource-style aliases

| Route | Runs |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/v1/projects` | `project.list` — query parameters become arguments, e.g. `?query=trip` (strings only). |
| `POST /api/v1/projects` | `project.create` |
| `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}` | `project.get` |
| `PATCH /api/v1/projects/{id}` | `project.rename`, body `{"name": "…"}` |
| `DELETE /api/v1/projects/{id}` | `project.delete` |
| `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/undo`, `…/redo` | `edit.undo`, `edit.redo` |

## Long-running jobs

Exports, auto captions, transcription and background removal return a job at once and run in the background. Poll `export.status`, `captions.status` (pass `wait_s` to long-poll up to 600 s) or `ai.jobs` — or listen to the events below. Jobs live in memory and are forgotten when Kadr restarts.

## WebSocket events

Connect to `ws://127.0.0.1:7777/api/v1/events?token=<token>` to receive a JSON message whenever something happens — in the editor, through the API, from the CLI or from an agent. Add `&project_id=prj_…` to receive only that project’s events (plus events that belong to no project).

```json
{
  "type": "project.changed",
  "project_id": "prj_1a347e3a7883",
  "source": "mcp",
  "data": { "commands": ["transition.apply_all"] },
  "time": "2026-10-01T16:47:42.9702474+02:00"
}
```

`source` is `ui`, `api`, `mcp` or `cli`, or the module that did background work (`media`, `ai`, `tools`, `update`).

| Event | When | `data` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `project.created` | A project was created or duplicated. | Project summary: `id`, `name`, `ratio`, … |
| `project.changed` | A project was saved after an edit or a background update. | `{commands}` — the commands that changed it |
| `project.deleted` | A project was deleted. | — |
| `history.changed` | Undo/redo availability changed. | `{can_undo, can_redo, undo_label, redo_label}` |
| `command.executed` | A global command changed something. | `{command}` |
| `playhead.moved`, `playback.state` | Seek, frame step, playback. | `{time_us}`, `{playing, time_us}` |
| `media.import.progress`, `media.ready` | Thumbnails, waveforms or proxies are being made / are ready. | `{material_id, stage, progress}` |
| `export.progress` | An export job advanced. | `job_id`, `state`, `phase`, `progress`, `speed_fps`, `eta_s` |
| `export.done`, `export.failed`, `export.cancelled` | An export finished. | `{job_id, path}` / `{job_id, error}` |
| `captions.progress`, `captions.done`, `captions.failed`, `captions.cancelled` | Auto captions or transcription advanced / finished. | Job status: `state`, `phase`, `progress`, `result` |
| `ai.progress` | A background-removal job advanced or finished. | `state`, `progress`, `frames`, `eta_s` |
| `presets.changed` | A My kit preset was saved, renamed or deleted. | `{action, preset_id, kind}` |
| `ui.open_project`, `ui.select`, `ui.library_tab`, `ui.toast` | An agent asked the window to show something. | `{segment_id}`, `{tab}`, `{title, body}` |
| `font.progress`, `fonts.changed` | A `font.install` download advanced; fonts were installed, imported, removed or rescanned. | `{font_id, state, downloaded_bytes, total_bytes, progress, error}`, `{reason, font_id}` |
| `tools.progress` | The FFmpeg download advanced. | `{tool, state, downloaded_bytes, total_bytes, progress, error}` |
| `update.available`, `update.progress`, `update.ready`, `update.failed` | Update check and download. | Version, progress or error |

A listener in Node.js 22+ (built-in `WebSocket`, no packages):

```js
const token = require('fs').readFileSync(process.env.APPDATA + '/Kadr/api-token', 'utf8').trim();
const ws = new WebSocket('ws://127.0.0.1:7777/api/v1/events?token=' + token);
ws.onmessage = (m) => {
  const e = JSON.parse(m.data);
  if (e.type === 'export.progress') console.log(e.data.job_id, Math.round(e.data.progress * 100) + '%');
  else console.log(e.type, e.source, e.project_id || '');
};
```

Events say *that* something changed; read the new state with `timeline.get`. Slow clients lose events rather than slowing the editor down, so re-read state after a reconnect.

## Binary endpoints

Pictures and sound are served as files. They need the token too (header or `?token=`).

| Endpoint (GET) | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `/api/v1/projects/{id}/frame?t_us=&w=&h=&format=jpeg\|png` | The composited frame at `t_us` — the same picture as `preview.frame` and the export. |
| `/api/v1/projects/{id}/stream?start_us=&w=&h=&fps=` | Live MJPEG playback (`multipart/x-mixed-replace`), usable as `<img src>`. |
| `/api/v1/projects/{id}/audio?start_us=&dur_us=&rate=` | The audio mix of that range, 16-bit stereo WAV. |
| `/api/v1/projects/{id}/media/{mid}/thumbnail?h=` | JPEG poster frame of a material. |
| `/api/v1/projects/{id}/media/{mid}/frame?t_us=&h=` | JPEG frame of the source file at `t_us`. |
| `/api/v1/projects/{id}/media/{mid}/waveform?pps=` | JSON `{"peaks_per_second": N, "peaks": [0..1, …]}` |
| `/api/v1/library/{kind}/{id}/thumbnail` | Still preview image (PNG) of a library item. |
| `/api/v1/library/{kind}/{id}/preview` | Animated preview of an item that moves: a JPEG sprite strip, frames side by side, one seamless loop. Size and rate are in the item’s `preview` field; 404 for static items. For a PNG grid an agent can look at, call `library.preview`. |
| `/api/v1/fonts/{id}/preview?text=&h=&color=` | Transparent PNG of sample text in an installed font. |
| `/api/v1/library/sound_effect/{id}/audio` | WAV preview of a sound effect. |
| `/api/v1/exports/{job}/file` | The finished export file. |

## Security model

- **Local only.** Kadr listens on `127.0.0.1`; other computers cannot connect.
- **Host check.** Requests must be addressed to `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `::1`; anything else gets `403 forbidden`. This blocks DNS-rebinding attacks from web pages.
- **Browser origins.** CORS and WebSocket connections are accepted only from loopback origins, and the token is still required.
- **Token.** Stored in your user profile; anyone who has it controls your projects. Never paste it into prompts or commit it.
- **Your files stay put.** Commands read and write files at the paths you give, on the PC where Kadr runs.

---

# Command line: kadrctl

Source: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/cli.html

*List, describe and run any Kadr command from a terminal with human time formats, run JSON batch files, and script whole folders in PowerShell.*

`kadrctl` runs any Kadr command from a terminal. It reads each command’s parameters from the running engine, converts values to the right types (including times like `2.5s`), and prints the result as JSON — handy for quick edits, for scripts, and for agents that only have a shell.

## Setup

`kadrctl.exe` is installed next to `Kadr.exe` in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Kadr\`. With the installer option *Add kadrctl and kadr-mcp to PATH* (on by default) it works from any new terminal: `kadrctl help`, `kadrctl version`.

Unlike `kadr-mcp`, `kadrctl` does **not** start the engine: Kadr or `kadr-server.exe` must be running. It finds the address and token in `%APPDATA%\Kadr` by itself.

## Subcommands

| Subcommand | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `kadrctl commands [category]` | Lists every command with its title, optionally one category (`Export`, `"Smart tools"`…). Planned commands are marked `(planned)`. |
| `kadrctl describe <command>` | The full documentation of one command: description, UI path, hotkey, returns, and each `--parameter` with type. |
| `kadrctl run <command> [--param value]…` | Runs a command and prints its result as indented JSON. |
| `kadrctl batch <project_id> <calls.json> [--dry-run]` | Runs a JSON file of calls as one atomic, undoable edit. |
| `kadrctl version` | Prints the kadrctl version. |

```text
> kadrctl commands Window
ui.library_tab                     Switch library tab
ui.open_project                    Show project in the window
ui.select                          Select clip in the window
ui.toast                           Show a message in the window
```

```text
> kadrctl describe timeline.segment.split
timeline.segment.split — Split

Splits a clip into two at at_us (default: the playhead), exactly like CapCut's Split button / Ctrl+B. …
UI: Toolbar/Split. Hotkey: Ctrl+B.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {track_id, left, right, linked_right_ids?} — both halves (full segments) and the ids of linked right halves.

Parameters:
  --project_id         string   (required) ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). …
  --segment_id         string   ID of the segment (clip) to edit. Optional: when omitted the clip on the main track under at_us is used …
  --at_us              integer  Timeline time in microseconds (1 s = 1000000). Defaults to the current playhead position.
```

## Writing parameters

Each parameter becomes a flag with the same name; `kadrctl` converts the value to the parameter’s type. Unknown flags are rejected before anything runs.

| Form | Example | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--param value`, `--param=value` | `--ratio 9:16` | Quote values with spaces: `--name "Kitchen tour"`. |
| Boolean | `--wait`, `--wait true`, `--snap false` | A bare flag means `true`. |
| Number | `--volume_db -12`, `--scale 0.6` | Negative numbers are fine. |
| Time (`*_us`) | `2500000`, `2.5s`, `1500ms`, `1m2s`, `00:01:02.5` | Converted to microseconds; a plain number already is microseconds. |
| Array or object | `--paths "[\"C:/Clips\"]"` | Must be JSON — see [quoting](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/cli.html#quoting). |

## Quoting JSON on Windows

Array and object parameters (`paths`, `segment_ids`, `style`, `params`, `points`…) are JSON, and its double quotes must survive the shell:

| Shell | Write |
| --- | --- |
| Command Prompt | `--paths "[\"C:/Users/you/Videos/trip\"]"` |
| PowerShell 7.3+ | `--paths '["C:/Users/you/Videos/trip"]'` |
| Windows PowerShell 5.1 | `--paths '[\"C:/Users/you/Videos/trip\"]'` |
| Any PowerShell | `kadrctl --% run media.import --project_id prj_… --paths "[\"C:/Users/you/Videos/trip\"]"` |

The docs use the `--%` form: it works in every PowerShell version, and without `--%` the same line works in Command Prompt. After `--%` PowerShell stops interpreting the line, so `$variables` are not expanded. Inside JSON use forward slashes in paths (`C:/Users/you`) or double backslashes. In PowerShell, quote colours (`"#FFD400"` — `#` starts a comment) and put text containing `$` in single quotes.

## Batch files

A batch file is a JSON array of `{command, args}` objects without `project_id` (it comes from the command line). `--dry-run` checks the batch on a copy without saving. Save the file as UTF-8 **without** a byte-order mark: `kadrctl` rejects a BOM, and Windows PowerShell 5.1’s `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8` writes one — use `[IO.File]::WriteAllText()` as in the [script below](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/cli.html#scripting).

```json
[
  { "command": "transition.apply_all", "args": { "type": "mix", "duration_us": 400000 } },
  { "command": "text.add", "args": { "text": "Kitchen tour", "template_id": "title_bold", "at_us": 0, "duration_us": 2500000 } }
]
```

```powershell
kadrctl batch prj_9d2e4c7a1b05 calls.json --dry-run
kadrctl batch prj_9d2e4c7a1b05 calls.json
```

## A complete edit from the terminal

Two clips become a captioned 9:16 short. Each command prints JSON; copy the ids it returns into the next command (the comments show what came back).

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run project.create --name "Kitchen tour" --ratio 9:16
# "id": "prj_9d2e4c7a1b05"
kadrctl --% run media.import --project_id prj_9d2e4c7a1b05 --paths "[\"C:/Users/you/Videos/kitchen\"]"
# materials: mat_3f81c2d9e0a4 (pan.mp4), mat_7b0e5a1c9d36 (talk.mp4)
kadrctl run timeline.segment.add --project_id prj_9d2e4c7a1b05 --material_id mat_3f81c2d9e0a4
kadrctl run timeline.segment.add --project_id prj_9d2e4c7a1b05 --material_id mat_7b0e5a1c9d36
kadrctl run timeline.get --project_id prj_9d2e4c7a1b05
# main track: seg_51c08e7f2a93 (0–6 s), seg_c2a9e4b7d108 (6–12 s)
kadrctl run timeline.segment.delete_right --project_id prj_9d2e4c7a1b05 --segment_id seg_c2a9e4b7d108 --at_us 9s
# keep only the first 3 s of the second clip
kadrctl run segment.set_background --project_id prj_9d2e4c7a1b05 --segment_id seg_51c08e7f2a93 --type blur --blur 0.75 --apply_to_all
kadrctl run transition.apply_all --project_id prj_9d2e4c7a1b05 --type mix --duration_us 0.4s
kadrctl run captions.auto --project_id prj_9d2e4c7a1b05 --style_id cap_highlight_word --wait
kadrctl run export.start --project_id prj_9d2e4c7a1b05 --resolution 1080p --path C:/Users/you/Videos/Kadr/kitchen.mp4
kadrctl run export.status --job_id exp_6a0d93e1f7c2
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "project_create", "arguments": {"name": "Kitchen tour", "ratio": "9:16"}}
{"name": "media_import", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_9d2e4c7a1b05", "paths": ["C:/Users/you/Videos/kitchen"]}}
{"name": "timeline_segment_add", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_9d2e4c7a1b05", "material_id": "mat_3f81c2d9e0a4"}}
{"name": "timeline_segment_add", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_9d2e4c7a1b05", "material_id": "mat_7b0e5a1c9d36"}}
{"name": "timeline_get", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_9d2e4c7a1b05"}}
{"name": "timeline_segment_delete_right", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_9d2e4c7a1b05", "segment_id": "seg_c2a9e4b7d108", "at_us": 9000000}}
{"name": "segment_set_background", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_9d2e4c7a1b05", "segment_id": "seg_51c08e7f2a93", "type": "blur", "blur": 0.75, "apply_to_all": true}}
{"name": "transition_apply_all", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_9d2e4c7a1b05", "type": "mix", "duration_us": 400000}}
{"name": "captions_auto", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_9d2e4c7a1b05", "style_id": "cap_highlight_word", "wait": true}}
{"name": "export_start", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_9d2e4c7a1b05", "resolution": "1080p", "path": "C:/Users/you/Videos/Kadr/kitchen.mp4"}}
{"name": "export_status", "arguments": {"job_id": "exp_6a0d93e1f7c2"}}
```

Every step can be undone with `kadrctl run edit.undo --project_id prj_9d2e4c7a1b05`, and the editor shows each change as it happens.

## Scripting in PowerShell

This script makes a vertical, reframed short from every `.mp4` in a folder and queues the exports. It runs in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7. The helper `kadr` turns `kadrctl`’s JSON into objects and stops on errors; `kadr-batch` sends JSON through a file, so paths with spaces need no quoting.

```powershell
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
[Console]::OutputEncoding = [Text.Encoding]::UTF8   # read non-English names correctly

# Run kadrctl and turn its JSON output into PowerShell objects.
function kadr {
  $out = kadrctl @args
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "kadrctl $($args[0]) $($args[1]) failed" }
  $out | Out-String | ConvertFrom-Json
}

# Run calls as one batch. JSON goes through a file, so no shell quoting is involved.
function kadr-batch($ProjectId, $Calls) {
  $file = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'kadr-calls.json'
  [IO.File]::WriteAllText($file, (ConvertTo-Json -InputObject @($Calls) -Depth 10))  # UTF-8, no BOM
  kadr batch $ProjectId $file
}

$src = "$env:USERPROFILE\Videos\Raw"
$dst = "$env:USERPROFILE\Videos\Kadr\Shorts"

Get-ChildItem $src -Filter *.mp4 | ForEach-Object {
  $p   = kadr run project.create --name $_.BaseName --ratio 9:16
  $imp = kadr-batch $p.id @(@{ command = 'media.import'; args = @{ paths = @($_.FullName) } })
  $seg = kadr run timeline.segment.add --project_id $p.id --material_id $imp.results[0].materials[0].id
  kadr run ai.auto_reframe --project_id $p.id --segment_id $seg.segment.id --ratio 9:16 | Out-Null
  $job = kadr run export.start --project_id $p.id --resolution 1080p --path "$dst\$($_.BaseName).mp4"
  "{0} -> {1} ({2})" -f $_.Name, $job.path, $job.state
}

kadr run export.list | Format-Table job_id, state, progress, path
```

- Exports run one at a time; extra jobs wait as `queued`, so the loop finishes long before the videos do.
- `export.estimate` shows the final size and path without exporting.
- To test a script safely, point it at a separate engine: `$env:KADR_DATA_DIR` and `$env:KADR_ADDR` for both `kadr-server.exe` and `kadrctl`.

## Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `KADR_ADDR` | `127.0.0.1:7777` | Where the engine listens and where `kadrctl`/`kadr-mcp` connect. |
| `KADR_DATA_DIR` | `%APPDATA%\Kadr` | Projects, settings and the `api-token` file. |
| `KADR_TOKEN` | contents of `api-token` | Overrides the token, for the engine and for clients. |
| `KADR_FFMPEG_DIR` | — | A folder with `ffmpeg.exe` and `ffprobe.exe` for the engine. |
| `KADR_PYTHON` | — | The `python.exe` that has faster-whisper (captions). |
| `KADR_ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` | — | An ElevenLabs key for the engine instead of `tts.set_api_key`. |

```powershell
$env:KADR_DATA_DIR = "D:\kadr-automation"
$env:KADR_ADDR = "127.0.0.1:7790"
Start-Process kadr-server.exe
kadrctl run project.list
```

## Exit codes and errors

On success `kadrctl` prints the result to standard output and exits with `0`. On failure it prints the error to standard error and exits with `1`:

```text
error [not_found]: project "prj_nope" not found
hint: Call project.list to get valid project ids.
```

Problems found before the call is sent start with a plain `error:`:

```text
error: project.list has no parameter "foo" (see `kadrctl describe project.list`)
error: cannot reach Kadr at http://127.0.0.1:7777 (is the editor or `kadr-server` running?): …
```

Error codes are the same as in the [REST API](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/rest.html#errors).

---

# Concepts

Source: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/concepts.html

*The rules an agent needs: projects, tracks, segments and materials, microsecond time, compositing order, the magnetic main track, linked clips, transitions, keyframes and easing, coordinates, volume units, ids and undo.*

Kadr models a CapCut-style timeline. These rules explain what the commands do to it — read them once and most surprises disappear. Every rule here is also written into the descriptions of the commands it affects.

## Projects, materials, tracks, segments

| Object | Id | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Project | `prj_…` | One edit: canvas (ratio, width, height, fps, background), settings, materials, tracks, markers, cover. Stored as `%APPDATA%\Kadr\projects\prj_…\project.json` with a `cache\` folder. |
| Material | `mat_…` | A media file the project uses — imported (`media.import`) or created (`media.generate`, `tts.speak`, `sfx.add`, stickers). Type `video`, `photo` or `audio`; photos have `duration_us` 0. Projects link to files, never copy them. |
| Track | `trk_…` | A row of the timeline with a type: `main_video` (exactly one), `video_overlay`, `text`, `sticker`, `effect`, `filter`, `adjustment`, `audio`. Empty tracks other than the main track disappear. |
| Segment | `seg_…` | A clip on a track: a **target** range on the timeline and, for media clips, a **source** range inside its material, plus all its properties (transform, opacity, volume, speed, filter, effects, animations, keyframes, text style…). |
| Marker | `mrk_…` | A labelled time on the ruler; clip edges snap to it. |
| Jobs | `exp_…`, `cap_…`, `aij_…` | Background exports, caption/transcription jobs and smart-tool jobs. They live in memory until Kadr restarts. |

Ids are opaque: read them from results and from `timeline.get`; never build them. Segment ids survive `project.duplicate`, so ids you know from the original also work in the copy.

## Time

- All times and durations are **integer microseconds** (µs); parameter names end in `_us`. 1 s = `1000000`; one frame at 30 fps = `33333`; at 25 fps = `40000`.
- Timeline times are absolute (from 0). **Keyframe** times are relative to the start of their segment. **Transcript** words are stored in source time and mapped to the timeline by `transcript.get`.
- Omitted `at_us` usually means “at the playhead” — each project has its own playhead (`playback.seek`, `playhead_us` in `timeline.get`). Agents should pass explicit times.

## Track order is compositing order

Tracks are drawn bottom-up: the track with `layer` 0 (`project.tracks[0]`, normally the main track) is drawn first, each higher layer on top. `timeline.get` lists tracks the way the timeline shows them — top to bottom — with each track’s `layer`:

```text
tracks (timeline.get)     layer
sticker                   3      drawn last, on top
text                      2
video_overlay             1
main_video                0      drawn first
audio                     4…     not drawn
```

- **Filter, effect and adjustment segments** on their own tracks change *everything below them* for their time range. A filter applied to a clip (`filter.apply`, `effect.apply`) changes only that clip.
- **New tracks** follow CapCut: overlay tracks go above the main and overlay tracks; text, sticker, effect, filter and adjustment tracks go on top of all visual tracks; audio tracks below the existing audio tracks. So a filter added *after* text sits above it and colours the text too — add filters first, or use `filter.apply` on clips.
- `hidden` tracks are not drawn, `muted` tracks are not heard, `locked` tracks reject edits with `conflict` (`timeline.track.set`).

## The magnetic main track

- With `main_track_magnet` on (default), clips on the main track always sit back to back from 0 — there are never gaps. Adding without `at_us` appends; adding with `at_us` inserts at the clip boundary *nearest* to it and ripples later clips right. Deleting, trimming and speed changes ripple too.
- **Don’t fight the magnet.** To place a clip at an exact time on the main track, build the sequence in order (batch of appends with `duration_us`), or turn the magnet off with `timeline.settings.set`. For free placement use an overlay track (`new_track`).
- On other tracks a clip starts exactly at `at_us`; if that spot is taken, a new track is created directly above.
- **Snapping** (`auto_snapping`) pulls moved and trimmed edges to other edges, the playhead, markers or 0 within 100 ms. Pass `snap: false` to `timeline.segment.move` or `timeline.segment.trim` for exact positions — beat markers are a classic trap.

## Segment ranges and speed

- `start_us`/`duration_us` is where the clip sits on the timeline; `source_start_us`/`source_duration_us` is the part of the material it plays. At speed *s*, `source_duration = duration × s`.
- Video and audio cannot be longer than their material (edges stop at the media end, results report `clamped: true`). Photos, text, stickers, effects and filters stretch freely.
- Default lengths: whole material for video/audio, 5 s for photos, 3 s for text, stickers, effects, filters and adjustment layers, 2 s for a manual caption.
- Video clips keep their own sound until `audio.extract` or `audio.separate`.

## Linked clips

Clips that share a `link_group` (`lnk_…`) move, trim, split and delete together while `linkage` is on (default). Links are created by `audio.extract` / `audio.separate` (video + its sound) and `tts.from_text` (text + its speech). `timeline.get` shows `link_group` on each clip. Turn linkage off with `timeline.settings.set` to edit one side alone.

## Transitions

- A transition is stored on the **left** clip of a cut (`transition_out`) and plays across the cut into the next clip on the same video track. `transition.set` takes the *left* clip’s id.
- The two clips must touch (within half a frame) — otherwise `conflict`. Both must be at least 0.2 s long; the duration is clamped to half of the shorter clip (`clamped: true`).
- Transitions do not change the timeline length: cuts stay where they are, so narration and music timing are unaffected.
- `transition.apply_all` sets one transition on every cut of a track. Directional and soft variants are options (`direction`, `softness`) stored in the type, e.g. `bars_stagger?direction=up`.

## Keyframes and easing

- Animatable properties: `transform.x`, `transform.y`, `transform.scale`, `transform.rotation`, `opacity`, `volume`, `adjust.*` and `filter.intensity`.
- With two or more keyframes a property is interpolated between them; before the first and after the last it **holds** that value. Keyframe values *replace* the static property.
- `time_us` is relative to the segment start. A keyframe within half a frame of an existing one updates it instead of adding another.
- The **left** keyframe of each interval decides the easing: `linear` (default), or cubic `ease_in`, `ease_out`, `ease_in_out`. Put the easing on the first keyframe of a move.
- While a property has keyframes, `segment.set_transform`, `segment.set_opacity`, `segment.set_volume` and `segment.set_adjust` write a keyframe *at the playhead* instead of changing the static value (listed in `result.keyframed`). Use `keyframe.add` with explicit times, or `keyframe.clear` first.

A slow push-in with an eased start, then a check of the interpolated value at 1 s:

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run keyframe.add --project_id prj_3c8e1f0a7b62 --segment_id seg_b41d7e0c9a35 --property transform.scale --time_us 0 --value 1 --easing ease_in_out
kadrctl run keyframe.add --project_id prj_3c8e1f0a7b62 --segment_id seg_b41d7e0c9a35 --property transform.scale --time_us 4s --value 1.2
kadrctl run segment.get --project_id prj_3c8e1f0a7b62 --segment_id seg_b41d7e0c9a35 --time_us 1s
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "keyframe_add", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_3c8e1f0a7b62", "segment_id": "seg_b41d7e0c9a35", "property": "transform.scale", "time_us": 0, "value": 1, "easing": "ease_in_out"}}
{"name": "keyframe_add", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_3c8e1f0a7b62", "segment_id": "seg_b41d7e0c9a35", "property": "transform.scale", "time_us": 4000000, "value": 1.2}}
{"name": "segment_get", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_3c8e1f0a7b62", "segment_id": "seg_b41d7e0c9a35", "time_us": 1000000}}
```

```json
"evaluated": { "transform": { "x": 0, "y": 0, "scale": 1.0125, "rotation": 0 }, "opacity": 1, … }
```

At 1 s — a quarter of the way — the cubic ease-in-out has covered only 6.25% of the move, so the scale is 1.0125; a `linear` keyframe would give 1.05.

## Transform and coordinates

- `x` and `y` move the clip’s centre in **canvas fractions**: 0 = centred, ±1 = centre on an edge (one unit is half the canvas width or height). **+X is right, +Y is down.** Range −2…2.
- `scale` 1 = the clip *fits inside* the canvas (letterboxed if the shapes differ). To fill a 16:9 canvas with 4:3 footage you need about 1.33; with 9:16 footage about 3.16. A clip at scale *s* that has the canvas’s shape can move sideways by *s* − 1 before an edge shows.
- `rotation` is in degrees, clockwise (−360…360). Flips are `flip_h`/`flip_v`.
- Stickers start at scale 0.3; text size 15 is CapCut’s default (stroke, shadow and box values are 0–1).
- To *measure*, use `preview.layout`: boxes in canvas pixels for every visible clip at a time.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run segment.set_transform --project_id prj_3c8e1f0a7b62 --segment_id seg_0f6b2d8e4c91 --y 0.6 --scale 0.8
kadrctl run preview.layout --project_id prj_3c8e1f0a7b62 --time_us 1s
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "segment_set_transform", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_3c8e1f0a7b62", "segment_id": "seg_0f6b2d8e4c91", "y": 0.6, "scale": 0.8}}
{"name": "preview_layout", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_3c8e1f0a7b62", "time_us": 1000000}}
```

## Volume: decibels and linear gain

| Where | Unit |
| --- | --- |
| `segment.set_volume` `volume_db` | Decibels relative to the original: 0 = unchanged, −6 ≈ half as loud, −60 = muted (bottom of the slider), max +20. |
| `volume` in segments, and the `volume` keyframe property | Linear gain: 1 = 0 dB, 0.5 ≈ −6 dB, 0 = silent, max 10. `gain = 10^(dB/20)`. |
| `audio.loudness` | LUFS (`integrated_lufs`, `effective_lufs` including the clip’s volume), true peak in dBFS. |
| `segment.set_fade` | `fade_in_us`/`fade_out_us` in microseconds. |

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run segment.set_volume --project_id prj_3c8e1f0a7b62 --segment_id seg_92d4f6a1c7e3 --volume_db -12
kadrctl run keyframe.add --project_id prj_3c8e1f0a7b62 --segment_id seg_92d4f6a1c7e3 --property volume --time_us 6s --value 0.25
kadrctl run keyframe.add --project_id prj_3c8e1f0a7b62 --segment_id seg_92d4f6a1c7e3 --property volume --time_us 8s --value 0
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "segment_set_volume", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_3c8e1f0a7b62", "segment_id": "seg_92d4f6a1c7e3", "volume_db": -12}}
{"name": "keyframe_add", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_3c8e1f0a7b62", "segment_id": "seg_92d4f6a1c7e3", "property": "volume", "time_us": 6000000, "value": 0.25}}
{"name": "keyframe_add", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_3c8e1f0a7b62", "segment_id": "seg_92d4f6a1c7e3", "property": "volume", "time_us": 8000000, "value": 0}}
```

The first call sets a static −12 dB (gain 0.25); the two keyframes then hold 0.25 until 6 s and fade to silence at 8 s.

## Where new ids appear in results

| Command | New id at |
| --- | --- |
| `project.create`, `project.duplicate` | `id` |
| `media.import` | `materials[].id` (files already in the project are in `duplicates[].material_id`) |
| `timeline.segment.add` | `segment.id` (and `track_id`) |
| `text.add`, `sticker.add`, `effect.add`, `filter.add`, `adjustment.add`, `captions.add` | `segment_id` |
| `media.generate` | `material_id`; with `add_to_timeline` also `segment_id` |
| `tts.speak`, `sfx.add` | `segment_id`, `material_id` |
| `timeline.segment.split` | `left.id` (keeps the original id), `right.id` |
| `ai.remove_silence`, `ai.split_scenes` | `segment_ids` — the remaining pieces in order |
| `captions.auto`, `transcript.transcribe`, `export.start` | `job_id`; caption cue ids come from `captions.list` |

## Undo, history and scopes

- **Project commands** (135 of them) take `project_id`, edit a working copy, and are saved as one undo step each — or one step per batch. A command that changes nothing creates no step. History is shared by the editor and every client; `edit.history` shows the next undo/redo labels.
- **Global commands** do not belong to one project’s history: projects list/create/duplicate/delete, library, presets, export jobs, `captions.auto` and `transcript.transcribe` (jobs; the cues they create are one undo step), tools, updates, `ui.toast`, `ui.library_tab`. They cannot be part of a batch.
- Not undoable: exports, transcripts (analysis data — `transcript.clear` removes one), `project.rename`, `project.delete`, proxy creation and the `ui.*` commands (they change only what the window shows).

---

# Library, previews and fonts

Source: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/library.html

*How an agent finds transitions, effects, filters, animations, text looks, stickers and generated media in Kadr's library, looks at them with library.preview before choosing, installs free fonts and uses the word-art fields of TextStyle.*

Everything an agent can add to a video — transitions, effects, filters, animations, text looks, stickers, generated backgrounds, fonts, sounds — comes from the built-in library. Discover ids with `library.list`, *look* at the candidates with `library.preview`, then apply the one that fits. Never guess an id.

## What is in the library

| `kind` | Items | Use the id with | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `transition` | 221 in 19 tabs | `transition.set` `type`, `transition.apply_all` | Tabs include Wipe, Zoom, Spin, Liquid, Particles, Film, Retro, Split; directional families such as `whip_*`, `wipe_*`, `slide_*`; options in `params.directions` / `params.softness`. |
| `effect` | 195 in 20 tabs | `effect.add`, `effect.apply`, `effect.set_params` | Every effect has `intensity` and `speed`; most add 1–4 named sliders listed in `params.schema` and in the description. |
| `filter` | 227 in 25 tabs | `filter.add`, `filter.apply` | New tabs Cinematic, Vintage, Aesthetic, Mood, Seasons, Duotone, Special; Portrait looks keep skin tones natural. |
| `animation` | 310: 105 in, 105 out, 53 combo, 47 loop | `animation.set` `kind` + `id` | All of them work on video, photo, sticker and text segments. |
| `text_template` | 175 in 22 tabs | `text.add` `template_id` | Templates use built-in fonts, so they never need a download. |
| `text_effect` | 114 in 16 tabs | `text.apply_effect` | Word art; writes fill, outlines, glow, 3D and the [word-art fields](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/library.html#text-style) into the style. |
| `text_animation` | 137: 55 in, 45 out, 37 loop | `text.set_glyph_animation` | Per letter / word / line, e.g. `in_decrypt`, `in_split_flap`, `in_terminal`, `loop_neon_buzz`. |
| `caption_style` | 55 in 12 tabs | `captions.set_style` | Highlight styles now include `pop`, `bounce`, `reveal`, `dim`, `glow`, `sweep_line`, `slide_box`. |
| `sticker` | 394 in 25 tabs, 73 animated | `sticker.add` | See [animated stickers](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/library.html#stickers). |
| `generated` | 98 presets of 22 kinds | `media.generate` `preset_id` | See [generated media](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/library.html#generated). |
| `font` | 4 built-in + this computer's + installed | `text.update` `font` | More with `font.catalog` + `font.install` — see [fonts](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/library.html#fonts). |
| `sound_effect`, `voice_effect` | 47, 25 | `sfx.add`, `segment.set_audio` `voice_effect` | Static items (no preview). |

## Find candidates

`library.list` takes a `kind`, an optional `category` (a tab name from the result's `categories`) and an optional `query` that searches names, ids, categories and descriptions. Narrow the list instead of reading 300 items: descriptions are written for agents — what the item looks like and when to use it.

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "library_list", "arguments": {"kind": "transition", "category": "Liquid"}}
{"name": "library_list", "arguments": {"kind": "effect", "query": "rain"}}
```

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run library.list --kind transition --category Liquid
kadrctl run library.list --kind effect --query rain
```

```text
tide_wipe   Tide        A rolling wave front with a sparkling white foam crest washes the new clip in…
                        params: directions [right left down up], softness true, default_softness 0.2
paint_drip  Paint drip  The new clip pours down from the top like thick glossy paint…
ink_bleed   Ink bleed   Dark ink blots spread with organic tendrils from a few drops…
```

## Look before you choose: library.preview

Names and descriptions only go so far. `library.preview` renders how an item *plays* as one PNG contact sheet — over MCP it comes back as an image the model can see. Use it to compare two or three candidates before applying one.

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "library_preview", "arguments": {"kind": "transition", "id": "tide_wipe", "frames": 6, "columns": 6, "tile_width": 160}}
```

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run library.preview --kind transition --id tide_wipe --frames 6 --columns 6 --tile_width 160
```

```json
{"kind": "transition", "id": "tide_wipe", "name": "Tide", "animated": true,
 "frames": 6, "columns": 6, "rows": 1, "tile_width": 160, "tile_height": 90,
 "phases": [0.159, 0.227, 0.295, 0.364, 0.432, 0.5], "times_us": [344697, …], "loop_us": 2166667,
 "preview": {"url": "/api/v1/library/transition/tide_wipe/preview", "frames": 26, "fps": 12, "width": 192, "height": 108},
 "note": "Tiles run from transition progress 0 (outgoing clip A, a sunny landscape) to 1 (incoming clip B, a night city)…",
 "png_base64": "…"}
```

| Kind | What the tiles show |
| --- | --- |
| Transitions | From a sunny landscape (clip A) to a night city (clip B), left to right, top to bottom. |
| Effects | Evenly spaced moments of the effect on the landscape; static effects such as a vignette show a before/after divider. |
| Filters | A before/after divider sweeping across the picture. |
| Clip animations | A small clip moving on a dark stage; a dashed outline marks its rest position. |
| Text templates, word art, text animations, caption styles | Sample text as it animates, or the spoken-word highlight moving through a caption. |
| Animated stickers, moving generated media | One loop of the sticker's default animation or of the background. |

- `frames` 2–12 (default 6) sets how many moments you see; `columns` (≤ 6) and `tile_width` set the layout. A one-row strip of 6 tiles at 160 px is cheap and easy to compare.
- `note` says what the tiles show for this kind; `times_us` and `phases` place each tile in the preview loop.
- Static items (fonts, voice effects, still stickers and templates) return their thumbnail as one tile with `"animated": false`.
- The sample pictures are not your footage. To see the item *in your edit*, apply it and check with `preview.frame` or `preview.contact_sheet` — see [Verifying results](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/verifying.html).

A complete walk-through is the recipe [Choose a transition and an effect by looking at them](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/preview-before-applying.html).

## The preview field and thumbnails

Every item that moves carries `preview` in `library.list` and `library.get` results — the editor uses it for its hover previews:

```json
"preview": {"url": "/api/v1/library/transition/mix/preview", "frames": 24, "fps": 12, "width": 192, "height": 108}
```

`GET` the `url` (with the API token) for a JPEG sprite strip: `frames` tiles of `width`×`height` side by side, left to right, one seamless loop at `fps`. No `preview` field means a static item. Every item also has a `thumbnail` path (a still PNG). Agents normally prefer `library.preview`; the strip is for your own UI. Strips are cached in memory and under `<DataDir>/library/previews/`.

## Options: directions, softness and effect sliders

A transition item lists what it accepts: `params.directions` and `default_direction`, `params.softness` and `default_softness`. Pass them to `transition.set` (`direction` = the way the motion travels; `softness` 0–1). An effect item lists its sliders in `params.schema` (`{id, label, min, max, default}`); pass values in `params` of `effect.add` / `effect.apply`, or later with `effect.set_params`.

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "transition_set", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_e21b467917e3", "segment_id": "seg_3ccd6c9e2cbe", "type": "tide_wipe", "duration_us": 800000, "direction": "left", "softness": 0.3}}
{"name": "effect_add", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_e21b467917e3", "effect_id": "rain_glass", "at_us": 3000000, "duration_us": 3000000, "params": {"density": 0.7, "fog": 0.3}}}
```

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run transition.set --project_id prj_e21b467917e3 --segment_id seg_3ccd6c9e2cbe --type tide_wipe --duration_us 0.8s --direction left --softness 0.3
kadrctl --% run effect.add --project_id prj_e21b467917e3 --effect_id rain_glass --at_us 3s --duration_us 3s --params "{\"density\":0.7,\"fog\":0.3}"
```

## Fonts: catalogue, install, import

`library.list` with `kind: "font"` lists the fonts that are ready to use. Category tabs say where a font comes from — `Built-in` (4 Go fonts, identical everywhere), `Downloaded` (installed through Kadr), `Bundled` (shipped next to the app), `System` (installed in the OS) — and its style: `Sans`, `Serif`, `Display`, `Handwriting`, `Monospace`, `Pixel`, `Symbol`. `params` has `source`, `styles`, `cyrillic`, `ukrainian` (Ґ Є І Ї) and `variable`.

More fonts come from `font.catalog`: 146 free SIL-OFL families from the google/fonts repository, 123 of them with Cyrillic, each with a note on its look and best use. The catalogue is read-only and offline; `font.install` downloads a family into `<DataDir>/fonts/<id>/`, after which its id works in `text.update` `font`.

### 1. Pick a family

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "font_catalog", "arguments": {"category": "handwriting", "cyrillic": true}}
```

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run font.catalog --category handwriting --cyrillic
```

```text
13 of 146 families
caveat        Caveat        Natural quick handwriting with Cyrillic; notes, annotations and vlogs.   394 KB  installed: false
marck_script  Marck Script  Casual flowing script with Cyrillic; greetings and personal stories.      82 KB
bad_script    Bad Script    Thin lively handwriting with Cyrillic; diaries and travel notes.          180 KB
```

### 2. Install it

The download runs in the background and reports `font.progress` events, then `fonts.changed`. With `wait: true` the call returns when the font is ready. Without internet it fails with `not_available`; an already installed family returns `already_installed: true`.

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "font_install", "arguments": {"id": "caveat", "wait": true}}
```

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run font.install --id caveat --wait
```

### 3. Use it

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "text_update", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_e21b467917e3", "segment_id": "seg_c39f3546d148", "font": "caveat"}}
```

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run text.update --project_id prj_e21b467917e3 --segment_id seg_c39f3546d148 --font caveat
```

- **An id from the catalogue is not usable until it is installed.** `text.update` with an unknown font fails with `not_found` and a hint to call `font.catalog` / `font.install`. Check `installed` in the catalogue first.
- **Fonts travel with the computer, not the project.** A project (or a My kit text preset) that names a font this machine lacks renders with Go Sans. Catalogue fonts are reproducible — one `font.install` on the other machine; `sys_*` fonts depend on that OS.
- `font.import` `{path}` installs a local `.ttf`/`.otf`/`.ttc` (the family name becomes the id); `font.remove` deletes only fonts installed through Kadr; `font.rescan` picks up fonts copied into font folders while Kadr runs.
- For Ukrainian text prefer fonts with `ukrainian: true`; missing letters are borrowed from a system font, which works but may not match.
- `GET /api/v1/fonts/{id}/preview?text=&h=&color=` returns a transparent PNG of sample text in that font.

## Word-art fields of TextStyle

Beyond fill, stroke, shadow, box, glow, gradient, 3D extrude and curve, a text style has optional word-art fields (absent or zero = off). `text.add` accepts them inside `style`; `text.update` has flat parameters for each (`pattern_type`, `bevel_depth`, `sparkle_amount`…); `text.apply_effect` sets them from a word-art preset.

| Field | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `fill.stops` | Positions 0–1 of up to 8 gradient colours; equal neighbours make a hard edge (chrome horizon). |
| `stroke_fill` | Gradient along the outline `{type, colors, angle}`. |
| `pattern` | `{type, colors, scale, angle, opacity, speed}` — 28 types: stripes, pinstripe, checker, gingham, plaid, dots, halftone, hearts, stars, grain, static, scanlines, brushed, foil, carbon, glitter, holo, rainbow, aurora, flow, galaxy, marble, wood, camo, leopard, zebra, frost, grid. |
| `bevel` | `{depth, angle, strength, gloss, highlight, shade, round}` — embossed or puffy lighting. |
| `inner_shadow`, `inner_glow` | Shadow or light inside the letters (`inner_glow`: `{color, intensity, radius}`). |
| `echo` | `{colors (1–6), distance, angle, hollow}` — stacked offset copies behind the text. |
| `distress` | `{type: grunge\|chalk\|stamp\|spray\|scratch\|worn, amount, scale}`. |
| `sparkle`, `drip` | Star glints `{color, amount, size, speed}`; paint drips `{amount, length}`. |
| `rough`, `pixelate` | 0–1: hand-made wobble; blocky pixel art. |
| `box` extras | `fill` (gradient), `border`, `shadow`, `per_line`, `skew`, `pad`, `knockout` (letters cut out of the box). |
| `highlight.text_color` | Letter colour of the spoken caption word for box-like highlight styles. |

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "text_add", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_e21b467917e3", "text": "SUMMER SALE", "at_us": 3000000, "style": {
  "size": 26, "bold": true, "color": "#FFD84D",
  "stroke": {"color": "#FFFFFF", "width": 0.25},
  "stroke_fill": {"type": "linear", "colors": ["#FFFFFF", "#FF3D7F"], "angle": -90},
  "pattern": {"type": "glitter", "speed": 0.6},
  "bevel": {"depth": 0.35, "angle": 135, "gloss": 0.6, "round": true},
  "echo": {"colors": ["#FF3D7F", "#7B2FF7"], "distance": 0.25, "angle": -45},
  "sparkle": {"amount": 0.4, "speed": 1.5}}}}
{"name": "text_update", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_e21b467917e3", "segment_id": "seg_c39f3546d148", "distress_type": "worn", "distress_amount": 0.3, "inner_shadow_opacity": 0.5}}
```

> **Note:** A pattern with `speed` > 0 or sparkles with `speed` > 0 make the text animate by itself, so a single `preview.frame` shows only one moment of it.

## Animated stickers

Stickers whose library item has `params.loop_anim` (plus optional `params.in_anim` and `params.loop_us`) are animated — the 73 in the `Animated` tab. `sticker.add` applies those animations automatically, exactly as `animation.set` would; pass `animate: false` to place the sticker still. Change them later with `animation.set` / `animation.remove`.

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "sticker_add", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_e21b467917e3", "sticker_id": "emoji_grin", "at_us": 0}}
```

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run sticker.add --project_id prj_e21b467917e3 --sticker_id emoji_grin --at_us 0
```

```text
segment.animations: {"in": {"id": "in_pop", "duration_us": 500000}, "loop": {"id": "loop_jelly", "duration_us": 1200000}}
```

## Generated media

`media.generate` draws backgrounds and overlays locally — 22 kinds, 98 presets (`library.list kind=generated`). The newer kinds:

| Kinds | What they make |
| --- | --- |
| `mesh`, `aurora`, `lava`, `plasma`, `bokeh`, `particles` | Moving backgrounds that loop seamlessly every `loop` seconds (also their default length), so copies can be placed back to back. |
| `light_leak`, `film_dust` | Light leaks, film burns, prism streaks, lens flares and old-film dirt drawn on black — put them on an overlay track and set `segment.set_blend` `mode: "screen"`. |
| `texture`, `pattern` | Paper, kraft, grunge, concrete, canvas, denim, marble, watercolour, wood; memphis, waves, dots, halftone, terrazzo, chevron, honeycomb, gingham, scales, cubes, triangles. |
| `timer` | Styled countdowns: flip clock, neon ring, progress bar, dots, pop bursts (optional beeps). |
| `banner`, `frame` | Transparent PNGs for an overlay track: text-free lower thirds, pills, ribbons, glass panels, news bars, brush strokes; film, neon, instant photo, vignette, torn paper, viewfinder and other borders. |

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "media_generate", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_e21b467917e3", "preset_id": "leak_warm", "add_to_timeline": true, "new_track": true, "at_us": 0, "duration_us": 3000000}}
{"name": "segment_set_blend", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_e21b467917e3", "segment_id": "seg_978c06ee7ef6", "mode": "screen"}}
```

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run media.generate --project_id prj_e21b467917e3 --preset_id leak_warm --add_to_timeline --new_track --at_us 0 --duration_us 3s
kadrctl run segment.set_blend --project_id prj_e21b467917e3 --segment_id seg_978c06ee7ef6 --mode screen
```

The full parameter list of every kind is in the description of [media.generate](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/media.html).
