# Working visibly with a human watching

Source: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/working-visibly.html

*Let a person follow an agent’s work in the Kadr window: open the project, select the clip being edited, switch library tabs, move the playhead and narrate with notifications.*

Every edit an agent makes appears in the open Kadr window immediately. The `ui.*` commands go one step further: they steer what the window *shows* — which project, which clip, which library tab — and put short notes on screen, so a person can follow along, learn, and step in.

## When the window can follow

- The agent must be talking to the **editor** (`Kadr.exe`), not to a headless `kadr-server.exe`. `app.version` tells which: its `executable` ends in `Kadr.exe` for the editor.
- `ui.*` commands change no project data, are not undoable, and simply do nothing when no window is open — they are always safe to call.
- Edits from the agent and from the person land in one undo history. The person can press `Ctrl`+`Z` on any agent edit; an agent can `edit.undo` a human edit.

## The commands

| Command | What the person sees |
| --- | --- |
| `ui.open_project` | The window switches to that project, as if it was opened from Home. |
| `ui.select` | A clip is selected on the timeline and its properties appear in the inspector. `segment_id` `""` clears the selection. |
| `ui.library_tab` | The left panel switches to `media`, `audio`, `text`, `stickers`, `effects`, `transitions`, `captions`, `transcript`, `filters`, `adjustment` or `templates` (My kit). |
| `ui.toast` | A short notification at the top of the window: a bold `title` and an optional `body`. |
| `playback.seek`, `playback.play`, `playback.pause` | The playhead moves and the player shows that frame, or plays from there. |

## A narrated edit

Open the project, announce the step, show where the feature lives, select the clip, make the edit, then play the result:

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run ui.open_project --project_id prj_6b0e4d2a9c71
kadrctl run ui.toast --title "Adding a transition" --body "Cube turn between the two shots"
kadrctl run ui.library_tab --tab transitions
kadrctl run ui.select --project_id prj_6b0e4d2a9c71 --segment_id seg_d02f7b9e3a64
kadrctl run transition.set --project_id prj_6b0e4d2a9c71 --segment_id seg_d02f7b9e3a64 --type cube_turn_left --duration_us 0.6s
kadrctl run playback.play --project_id prj_6b0e4d2a9c71 --from_us 2s
kadrctl run playback.pause --project_id prj_6b0e4d2a9c71
kadrctl run ui.select --project_id prj_6b0e4d2a9c71 --segment_id=
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "ui_open_project", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_6b0e4d2a9c71"}}
{"name": "ui_toast", "arguments": {"title": "Adding a transition", "body": "Cube turn between the two shots"}}
{"name": "ui_library_tab", "arguments": {"tab": "transitions"}}
{"name": "ui_select", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_6b0e4d2a9c71", "segment_id": "seg_d02f7b9e3a64"}}
{"name": "transition_set", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_6b0e4d2a9c71", "segment_id": "seg_d02f7b9e3a64", "type": "cube_turn_left", "duration_us": 600000}}
{"name": "playback_play", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_6b0e4d2a9c71", "from_us": 2000000}}
{"name": "playback_pause", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_6b0e4d2a9c71"}}
{"name": "ui_select", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_6b0e4d2a9c71", "segment_id": ""}}
```

## Good habits

- **Open the project first.** Call `ui.open_project` right after creating or choosing a project, before the edits start.
- **Narrate phases, not calls.** One toast per meaningful step (“Cutting to the beat”, “Adding captions — about a minute”) is enough; dozens of toasts are noise.
- **Batch visual edits.** A `kadr_batch` lands as one update and one undo step, so the person sees a clean change instead of flicker.
- **Point at what changed.** `ui.select` the clip and `playback.seek` to the moment you edited, so the player shows it.
- **Ask before big moves.** If the person is editing at the same time, agree who edits what: every command is atomic, but there is no locking between people and agents.
- **Long jobs.** Toast when a caption job or an export starts and when it ends; the window also shows export progress itself.

## Under the hood

The `ui.*` commands publish `ui.open_project`, `ui.select`, `ui.library_tab` and `ui.toast` events. Every open window — the desktop app or the editor in web mode — follows them, and any other client can see them on the [event stream](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/rest.html#events).

---

# Verifying results

Source: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/verifying.html

*Check an edit the way an editor would: read the timeline, look at frames and contact sheets, measure layouts and loudness, then confirm the exported file itself.*

A command that succeeded only proves the call was valid. To know the video is right, an agent should do what an editor does: read the timeline, look at the picture, measure what can be measured, and finally check the exported file.

## 1. Read the structure

`timeline.get` is the compact, agent-sized view: tracks top to bottom, each clip with `start_us`, `end_us`, source range, speed, volume, link group, transition and effects, plus `duration_us` of the whole edit and how often each material is used. Compare it with the plan: right order, no unexpected gaps on non-magnetic tracks, total length as intended.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run timeline.get --project_id prj_e5a2c8f1d940
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "timeline_get", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_e5a2c8f1d940"}}
```

For one clip in depth, `segment.get` with `time_us` returns every property plus `evaluated` — the keyframed values at that moment.

## 2. Look at the picture

`preview.frame` renders one frame with the export renderer. `preview.contact_sheet` renders a grid of evenly spaced frames (`times_us` lists each tile’s time); `start_us`/`end_us` zoom in on a section. Through MCP both arrive as images the model can see.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run preview.frame --project_id prj_e5a2c8f1d940 --time_us 1s --width 960
kadrctl run preview.contact_sheet --project_id prj_e5a2c8f1d940 --count 8 --columns 4 --tile_width 240
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "preview_frame", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_e5a2c8f1d940", "time_us": 1000000, "width": 960}}
{"name": "preview_contact_sheet", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_e5a2c8f1d940", "count": 8, "columns": 4, "tile_width": 240}}
```

![A contact sheet: six frames of a promo in a 3 by 2 grid](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/assets/img/ai/promo-contact-sheet.webp)
*A contact sheet (6 tiles, 3 columns) from the product promo recipe — one image shows the whole edit.*

Without MCP, decode `png_base64` yourself, or fetch a JPEG from the [frame endpoint](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/rest.html#binary):

```powershell
$r = Invoke-Kadr preview.frame @{ project_id = 'prj_e5a2c8f1d940'; time_us = 1000000; width = 960 }
[IO.File]::WriteAllBytes("$PWD\frame.png", [Convert]::FromBase64String($r.png_base64))
```

| Look for | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Black bars or edges during zooms | Contact sheet, then frames at the move’s start and end |
| Text cut off, overlapping captions, stickers on faces | Frames at 960 px or wider |
| Black frames between clips | Dark tiles; gaps in `timeline.get` |
| A weak first frame (the thumbnail) | `preview.frame` at `time_us` 0, or set one with `project.set_cover` |

## 3. Measure

`preview.layout` returns the box of every visible clip, text and sticker at a time, in canvas pixels (`x`, `y`, `w`, `h`, `rotation`, `corners`, `z`). A clip covers the frame when `x` ≤ 0, `y` ≤ 0, `x + w` ≥ `canvas_width` and `y + h` ≥ `canvas_height`; text fits when its box is inside those bounds.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run preview.layout --project_id prj_e5a2c8f1d940 --time_us 1s
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "preview_layout", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_e5a2c8f1d940", "time_us": 1000000}}
```

For sound, `audio.loudness` measures a clip (integrated LUFS, loudness range, true peak, and `effective_lufs` including the clip’s volume). Speech under music reads well when the music sits 10–15 LU lower. For words, compare `captions.list` (cue text and times) with `transcript.get` (what was recognised).

## 4. Check the exported file

`export.start` returns a `job_id` immediately; poll `export.status` every second or two until `state` is `done` (or `failed` with an `error`). The final `path` can differ from the one you asked for: an existing file is never overwritten unless you pass `overwrite`, so Kadr adds “ (1)”.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run export.start --project_id prj_e5a2c8f1d940 --resolution 720p --path C:/Users/you/Videos/Kadr/check.mp4 --overwrite
kadrctl run export.status --job_id exp_2d7f9b1e4c06
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "export_start", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_e5a2c8f1d940", "resolution": "720p", "path": "C:/Users/you/Videos/Kadr/check.mp4", "overwrite": true}}
{"name": "export_status", "arguments": {"job_id": "exp_2d7f9b1e4c06"}}
```

```json
{ "job_id": "exp_2d7f9b1e4c06", "state": "done", "progress": 1, "path": "C:\\Users\\you\\Videos\\Kadr\\check.mp4",
  "size_bytes": 117503, "encoder": "h264_nvenc", "settings": { "width": 1280, "height": 720, "fps": 30, "duration_us": 4000000, … } }
```

Then confirm the file itself. With a shell, `ffprobe` answers in one line. Without one, Kadr can probe it: import the export into a scratch project — the material reports duration, size, codecs and whether it has sound — look at it, and delete the scratch project (imported files are never deleted).

```powershell
ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration:stream=codec_type,codec_name,width,height -of compact "C:\Users\you\Videos\Kadr\check.mp4"
```

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run project.create --name "Scratch: check export" --ratio 16:9
kadrctl --% run media.import --project_id prj_4f9a1c7e0b38 --paths "[\"C:/Users/you/Videos/Kadr/check.mp4\"]"
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "project_create", "arguments": {"name": "Scratch: check export", "ratio": "16:9"}}
{"name": "media_import", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_4f9a1c7e0b38", "paths": ["C:/Users/you/Videos/Kadr/check.mp4"]}}
```

```json
{ "id": "mat_a6e0c3b9d752", "type": "video", "duration_us": 4000000, "width": 1280, "height": 720, "fps": 30,
  "video_codec": "h264", "has_audio": true, "audio_codec": "aac", … }
```

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run timeline.segment.add --project_id prj_4f9a1c7e0b38 --material_id mat_a6e0c3b9d752
kadrctl run preview.contact_sheet --project_id prj_4f9a1c7e0b38 --count 4 --columns 4 --tile_width 240
kadrctl run project.delete --project_id prj_4f9a1c7e0b38
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "timeline_segment_add", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_4f9a1c7e0b38", "material_id": "mat_a6e0c3b9d752"}}
{"name": "preview_contact_sheet", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_4f9a1c7e0b38", "count": 4, "columns": 4, "tile_width": 240}}
{"name": "project_delete", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_4f9a1c7e0b38"}}
```

## Checklist before saying “done”

- `timeline.get`: order, lengths and total duration match the plan.
- A contact sheet of the whole edit, plus frames at every risky moment (zooms, titles, the first frame).
- `preview.layout` confirms coverage and that text fits; `audio.loudness` confirms voice vs. music.
- Captions match the script (`captions.list`); fixes made with `captions.update`.
- `export.status` is `done`; the file’s duration, size and audio are confirmed.
- A short report to the person: what changed, where the file is, anything you were unsure about.

---

# Best practices and pitfalls

Source: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/best-practices.html

*How agents get reliable results in Kadr: read before writing, batch atomic edits, follow error hints, handle long jobs and missing components, and avoid the classic timeline traps.*

Kadr’s commands are forgiving — every edit can be undone — but an agent that works in the right order gets better videos with fewer calls. These are the habits that matter most, and the traps that catch agents most often.

## Read before you write

- Start every session with `project.list` or `project.get`/`timeline.get`. Take ids from results — never construct or guess them.
- Find library ids with `library.list` (`kind`: `transition`, `effect`, `filter`, `animation`, `text_template`, `text_effect`, `text_animation`, `caption_style`, `sticker`, `font`, `generated`, `sound_effect`, `voice_effect`) and check unknown parameters with `kadrctl describe` or the reference.
- **Look before you choose a look.** Narrow candidates with `category` or `query`, then compare two or three with `library.preview` — a contact sheet of how each one plays — instead of picking by name. Fonts from `font.catalog` must be installed with `font.install` before `text.update` accepts their id. See [Library, previews and fonts](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/library.html).
- **Re-read after edits that create or remove clips:** splits, `ai.remove_silence`, `ai.split_scenes`, transcript cuts and magnet ripples change ids and times. Results usually list the new ids (`segment_ids`, `left`/`right`); otherwise call `timeline.get` again.

## Plan, then batch

- Group related edits into one `kadr_batch` (MCP), `POST /projects/{id}/batch` (REST) or `kadrctl batch`: they apply atomically, as one undo step, and the person watching sees one clean change.
- Use `dry_run` to validate a big plan — it runs every call on a copy and reports the first failure without saving.
- Work in phases: create things (and read their ids) → batch the follow-up edits. A batch cannot reference ids created inside the same batch.
- Global commands (exports, captions jobs, project create/duplicate/delete, library, presets) cannot be batched.

## Follow the error hints

Errors carry `code`, `message`, `hint` and often `field`. The hint is written for agents — it names the command that lists valid values or explains the rule that was broken:

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "transition_set", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_c0d7a4e19b5f", "segment_id": "seg_f8a1d3c6e204", "type": "mix"}}
```

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run transition.set --project_id prj_c0d7a4e19b5f --segment_id seg_f8a1d3c6e204 --type mix
```

```text
error [conflict]: segment seg_f8a1d3c6e204 is the last clip on its track; a transition needs a following clip
hint: Transitions sit between two touching clips on the same track: pass the LEFT clip of the pair (the one that ends where the next one starts).
```

| Error | Usual cause | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `not_found` + `field` | A stale or invented id | Re-read with `timeline.get` / `library.list` |
| `invalid_argument` | Wrong enum value, out-of-range number, seconds instead of µs | The message lists the allowed values; convert times to µs |
| `conflict` | Locked track, clips that don’t touch (transitions), overlapping caption times | Unlock, move clips together, adjust neighbours first |
| `not_available` (HTTP 503) | A missing local component | See [below](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/best-practices.html#capabilities); tell the person what to install |
| Result has `clamped: true` | The request was limited (media end, half-clip transition, minimum length) | Read the actual values in the result |

## Long jobs: wait or poll

- **Background jobs:** `captions.auto`, `transcript.transcribe`, `ai.remove_background`, `export.start`. They return a `job_id` immediately.
- `wait: true` (captions, transcription, background removal) blocks until done — fine for a few minutes of media, but MCP and `kadrctl` give up after 5 minutes.
- For longer media, start without `wait` and long-poll `captions.status` with `wait_s` (up to 600 s per call); poll `export.status` every 1–2 s; or listen to `captions.done`/`export.done` events.
- The first Whisper run loads the model and is slower. Exports run one at a time; extra jobs are `queued`. Jobs are forgotten when Kadr restarts.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run captions.auto --project_id prj_c0d7a4e19b5f --language en --style_id cap_clean
kadrctl run captions.status --project_id prj_c0d7a4e19b5f --job_id cap_7e4b1a9d2c05 --wait_s 120
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "captions_auto", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_c0d7a4e19b5f", "language": "en", "style_id": "cap_clean"}}
{"name": "captions_status", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_c0d7a4e19b5f", "job_id": "cap_7e4b1a9d2c05", "wait_s": 120}}
```

## Check optional components first

| Feature | Needs | Check with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Import, preview, export (everything) | FFmpeg | `tools.status` (`tools.install_ffmpeg` downloads it) |
| Captions, transcripts, filler/pause removal | Python + faster-whisper + a model | `captions.asr_status` |
| Background removal | `rembg` or `onnxruntime` + a matting model | `ai.capabilities` |
| Text-to-speech | Windows SAPI voices, eSpeak NG, or an ElevenLabs key | `tts.voices` (`providers` says why one is missing) |

If something is missing, the `hint` says how to install it. Kadr never downloads models by itself; tell the person what to install instead of retrying.

## Timeline traps

- **Don’t fight the magnet.** On the main track `at_us` snaps to the nearest clip boundary and everything ripples. Build sequences in order, use overlay tracks for free placement, or switch the magnet off with `timeline.settings.set`.
- **Exact positions need `snap: false`** on `timeline.segment.move` and `timeline.segment.trim` — otherwise an edge within 100 ms of a marker, the playhead or another edge jumps to it.
- **Keyframed properties:** once a property has keyframes, `segment.set_*` writes a keyframe at the playhead. Edit animated values with `keyframe.add` at explicit times.
- **Transitions** go on the left clip and need clips that touch; durations are capped at half the shorter clip.
- **Filters and effects on tracks** affect everything below them — including text if the text track is lower. Add them before titles, or apply them to clips.
- **Units:** times in µs; `volume_db` in dB but `volume` keyframes linear; positions in canvas fractions with +Y down; scale 1 = fit, not fill.

## Files and paths

- Paths are absolute and refer to the PC where Kadr runs. In JSON use forward slashes (`C:/Users/you/Videos`) or doubled backslashes.
- A folder in `media.import` imports the media files directly inside it (not subfolders, up to 500); files already in the project are reported as `duplicates`.
- Exports never overwrite unless `overwrite` is true — read the final `path` from the result. Without `path` they go to `%USERPROFILE%\Videos\Kadr\<project name>.mp4`.

## Keep results small

- `timeline.get` instead of `project.get` for orientation; `segment.get` for one clip in depth.
- `include_words: false` on `captions.list`; `include_words: false` on `transcript.get` when you only need text.
- Contact sheets of 8–12 tiles at 240–320 px; single frames at 960 px only when reading small text.

## Respect the person

- Open the project in the window (`ui.open_project`) and narrate phases with `ui.toast` — see [Working visibly](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/working-visibly.html).
- Make variants with `project.duplicate` instead of overwriting a finished edit; never `project.delete` without asking.
- Don’t put the API token or cloud keys into prompts, files or logs; `tts.set_api_key` stores keys locally and never returns them.
- Finish with a short report: what changed, where the export is, what you could not verify.

---

# Recipes

Source: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/recipes.html

*End-to-end Kadr workflows for AI agents — TikToks, beat cuts, talking heads, slideshows, audiograms, promos, format variants, self-review, translated captions, an archive documentary and picking looks by eye — with every call as kadrctl and MCP.*

Each recipe is a complete job: a prompt you can paste into Claude, then every call the agent makes, in order, as `kadrctl` and as an MCP tool call. All of them were run end to end against a real Kadr engine — with generated stand-in media — before publishing.

- [Vertical TikTok from a folder of clips](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/vertical-tiktok.html): A folder of clips and a song become a 9:16 video with subject-tracking reframes, whip-pan cuts, word-highlight captions and music at a steady level. · ~3 min
- [Music video cut to the beat](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/beat-cut-music-video.html): Kadr finds the beats in your song and every cut lands on one, with flash transitions, a colour grade and a punch-zoom on the drop. · ~2 min
- [Talking-head cleanup to a vertical short](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/talking-head-cleanup.html): A raw talking-head take becomes a tight 9:16 short with clean audio, no silences or “um”s, and captions. · ~2 min
- [Photo slideshow with Ken Burns motion](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/photo-slideshow.html): A folder of photos becomes a slideshow with slow zoom-and-pan on every photo, dissolves, music and an animated title. · ~2 min
- [Podcast clip as an audiogram](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/podcast-audiogram.html): A podcast audio clip becomes a square video with a moving background, karaoke captions, a pulsing icon and the show’s name. · ~2 min
- [Product promo with word art and voice-over](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/product-promo.html): Generated backgrounds, a product shot, metallic and neon headlines, a price tag, whooshes and a voice-over, exported as MP4 and GIF. · ~3 min
- [One project, three formats](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/batch-export-variants.html): A finished 16:9 edit becomes 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1 videos, reframed or blur-filled, with titles that fit each frame, all exported in one go. · ~2 min
- [Let Claude review and fix its own edit](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/ai-review-loop.html): Claude renders your edit, spots black edges and cut-off titles, measures them, fixes them, checks the fix and undoes anything that looks worse. · ~1 min
- [Translate and re-burn captions](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/translate-and-reburn-captions.html): Claude translates your captions, keeps their timing, and you get a burned-in version plus SRT files in both languages. · ~2 min
- [Documentary from public-domain archive footage](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/documentary-archive-footage.html): Public-domain newsreels from archive.org, Ukrainian ElevenLabs narration, shots timed to the voice, Ken Burns moves, a film-strip look and fixed captions. · ~10 min (mostly downloading)
- [Choose a transition and an effect by looking at them](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/preview-before-applying.html): Claude shortlists transitions and effects, actually looks at how each one moves, picks the one that suits your footage and checks it in your edit. · ~1 min

## How to use a recipe

1. **Connect an agent** — [Claude Code](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/claude-code.html), [Claude Desktop](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/claude-desktop.html) or [another client](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/other-mcp-clients.html) — and open Kadr so you can watch.
2. **Paste the prompt** from “Ask Claude”, with your own paths and wording. The agent works out the calls; the steps show what it will do.
3. **Or run the steps yourself** with `kadrctl` (PowerShell) — copy each id from the previous result.

> **Tip:** Every recipe ends with a check (`preview.contact_sheet`, `preview.frame` or `preview.layout`) before exporting. Keep that step when you adapt a recipe — it is how the agent catches its own mistakes. See [the review loop](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/ai-review-loop.html).

## At a glance

| Recipe | You need | Key commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Vertical TikTok](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/vertical-tiktok.html) | A folder of clips (one where you talk) and a music track | `project.create`, `media.import`, `timeline.segment.add`, `ai.auto_reframe` |
| [Cut to the beat](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/beat-cut-music-video.html) | A song and a folder of clips | `audio.detect_beats`, `timeline.segment.add`, `timeline.segment.trim`, `segment.set_volume` |
| [Talking-head cleanup](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/talking-head-cleanup.html) | A talking-head video (landscape is fine) | `segment.set_audio`, `segment.set_video_cleanup`, `ai.auto_reframe`, `ai.remove_silence` |
| [Photo slideshow](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/photo-slideshow.html) | A folder of photos and a music track | `media.import`, `timeline.segment.add`, `keyframe.add`, `transition.apply_all` |
| [Podcast audiogram](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/podcast-audiogram.html) | A podcast audio clip (WAV or MP3) | `media.generate`, `timeline.segment.add`, `timeline.segment.trim`, `segment.set_audio` |
| [Product promo](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/product-promo.html) | A product photo (a transparent PNG works best) | `media.generate`, `transition.set`, `timeline.segment.add`, `animation.set` |
| [Three formats](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/batch-export-variants.html) | A finished 16:9 Kadr project (for example from the beat-cut recipe) | `project.duplicate`, `project.set_canvas`, `ai.auto_reframe`, `segment.set_background` |
| [Review loop](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/ai-review-loop.html) | Any Kadr project | `preview.contact_sheet`, `preview.layout`, `preview.frame`, `keyframe.list` |
| [Translate captions](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/translate-and-reburn-captions.html) | A Kadr project with captions (for example from the talking-head recipe) | `captions.list`, `project.duplicate`, `captions.update`, `captions.set_style` |
| [Archive documentary](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/documentary-archive-footage.html) | ffmpeg on PATH, an ElevenLabs API key (optional — local voices work too), internet for the footage | `media.import`, `tts.set_api_key`, `tts.voices`, `tts.speak` |
| [Pick by looking](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/preview-before-applying.html) | A Kadr project with two clips that touch | `library.list`, `library.preview`, `transition.set`, `preview.contact_sheet` |

---

# Vertical TikTok from a folder of clips

Source: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/vertical-tiktok.html

*Turn a folder of landscape clips and a song into a 9:16 TikTok, Reels or Shorts video with reframed shots, whip-pan transitions, word-highlight captions and steady background music.*

You get a 1080×1920 video for TikTok, Reels or Shorts. It opens with your talking clip, follows with short b-roll shots, every landscape shot is reframed to fill the vertical screen, the cuts are fast whip pans, captions highlight each word as it is spoken, and your song plays underneath at a steady level.

- **Time:** ~3 min
- **You need:** A folder of clips (one where you talk) and a music track
- **Main commands:** `project.create`, `media.import`, `timeline.segment.add`, `ai.auto_reframe`, `transition.apply_all`, `captions.auto`, `segment.set_volume`, `segment.set_fade`, `audio.loudness`, `preview.contact_sheet`, `export.start`

## Ask Claude

> Make a vertical 9:16 TikTok in Kadr from the clips in C:\Users\you\Videos\tiktok. Start with 01_intro.mp4 in full (that's me talking), then use 2.5-second slices of the other clips, starting 1 second into each. Reframe every clip so it fills the vertical frame and follows the subject. Put 0.3-second whip-pan transitions between all clips. Add word-highlight captions, 3 words at a time, for what I say in the intro. Mute the b-roll's own sound and lay C:\Users\you\Music\beat.mp3 under the whole video about 12 dB down, with a short fade-in and fade-out. Show me a contact sheet, then export 1080p to C:\Users\you\Videos\Kadr\weekend-tiktok.mp4.

## Step by step

> **Note:** Each step shows the same calls twice. The **kadrctl** tab is for PowerShell: a line that starts with `kadrctl --%` passes JSON, and without `--%` the same line also works in Command Prompt. The **MCP** tab is the tool call an agent sends — the tool name and its arguments. Ids such as `prj_…`, `mat_…` and `seg_…` come from the results of earlier steps, so yours will differ. Paths under `C:/Users/you` are examples.

### 1. Create a 9:16 project

`project.create` with ratio `9:16` gives a 1080×1920 canvas at 30 fps. The result is the new project; its `id` is used by every later call.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run project.create --name "Weekend TikTok" --ratio 9:16
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "project_create", "arguments": {"name": "Weekend TikTok", "ratio": "9:16"}}
```

### 2. Import the folder and the song

`media.import` accepts files and folders; a folder imports every media file directly inside it. The result lists each material with its `id`, `type` and `duration_us`. Importing puts nothing on the timeline yet.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl --% run media.import --project_id prj_8a3dc0a150b8 --paths "[\"C:/Users/you/Videos/tiktok\",\"C:/Users/you/Music/beat.mp3\"]"
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "media_import", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_8a3dc0a150b8", "paths": ["C:/Users/you/Videos/tiktok", "C:/Users/you/Music/beat.mp3"]}}
```

### 3. Lay out the clips in one step

Video clips added without `at_us` go to the end of the magnetic main track, so the call order becomes the edit order. The intro is added whole; each b-roll clip becomes a 2.5 s slice starting 1 s in (`source_start_us` + `duration_us`). As a batch, the four adds are one undo step. Save this as `tiktok-layout.json`:

```json
[
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_708d08b25bae"}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_fccc03654420", "source_start_us": 1000000, "duration_us": 2500000}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_9360221234d9", "source_start_us": 1000000, "duration_us": 2500000}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_312fa58a675e", "source_start_us": 1000000, "duration_us": 2500000}}
]
```

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl batch prj_8a3dc0a150b8 tiktok-layout.json
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "kadr_batch", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_8a3dc0a150b8", "calls": [
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_708d08b25bae"}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_fccc03654420", "source_start_us": 1000000, "duration_us": 2500000}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_9360221234d9", "source_start_us": 1000000, "duration_us": 2500000}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_312fa58a675e", "source_start_us": 1000000, "duration_us": 2500000}}
]}}
```

Read the result back with `timeline.get` — a compact tree of tracks and segments with start and end times:

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run timeline.get --project_id prj_8a3dc0a150b8
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "timeline_get", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_8a3dc0a150b8"}}
```

```text
main_video  seg_f3a56bc31a8f  01_intro.mp4   0 s     → 7 s
            seg_a01cb913dfa3  02_city.mp4    7 s     → 9.5 s
            seg_4852e1afa8a7  03_beach.mp4   9.5 s   → 12 s
            seg_4712217ee4d0  04_food.mp4    12 s    → 14.5 s
```

### 4. Fill the vertical frame

`ai.auto_reframe` scales each landscape clip to fill 9:16 without bars and animates its position (keyframes) to follow the subject, using motion, edges and skin tones. It runs locally, about a second per minute of video. All four in one batch, `tiktok-reframe.json`:

```json
[
  {"command": "ai.auto_reframe", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_f3a56bc31a8f", "ratio": "9:16"}},
  {"command": "ai.auto_reframe", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_a01cb913dfa3", "ratio": "9:16"}},
  {"command": "ai.auto_reframe", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_4852e1afa8a7", "ratio": "9:16"}},
  {"command": "ai.auto_reframe", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_4712217ee4d0", "ratio": "9:16"}}
]
```

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl batch prj_8a3dc0a150b8 tiktok-reframe.json
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "kadr_batch", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_8a3dc0a150b8", "calls": [
  {"command": "ai.auto_reframe", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_f3a56bc31a8f", "ratio": "9:16"}},
  {"command": "ai.auto_reframe", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_a01cb913dfa3", "ratio": "9:16"}},
  {"command": "ai.auto_reframe", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_4852e1afa8a7", "ratio": "9:16"}},
  {"command": "ai.auto_reframe", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_4712217ee4d0", "ratio": "9:16"}}
]}}
```

### 5. Add punchy transitions

`transition.apply_all` puts the same transition on every cut of the main track. A short `whip_pan` keeps the pace up. Each transition is stored on the clip to the left of its cut.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run transition.apply_all --project_id prj_8a3dc0a150b8 --type whip_pan --duration_us 0.3s
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "transition_apply_all", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_8a3dc0a150b8", "type": "whip_pan", "duration_us": 300000}}
```

### 6. Caption the talking clip

`captions.auto` recognises speech locally with Whisper and creates cues with per-word timing. `segment_id` limits it to the clip where you talk, so b-roll sound is not transcribed. `cap_highlight_word` highlights each word as it is spoken; `max_words` 3 keeps cues short. `wait` makes the call return when the job is done instead of returning a job id at once.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run captions.auto --project_id prj_8a3dc0a150b8 --segment_id seg_f3a56bc31a8f --language en --style_id cap_highlight_word --max_words 3 --wait
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "captions_auto", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_8a3dc0a150b8", "segment_id": "seg_f3a56bc31a8f", "language": "en", "style_id": "cap_highlight_word", "max_words": 3, "wait": true}}
```

The job ends with `"state": "done"`; the cues are on a new text track named “Captions”.

### 7. Set the sound

Mute the b-roll’s own sound first. `segment.set_volume` takes decibels; −60 dB is the bottom of the slider (silent). Save as `tiktok-mute.json`:

```json
[
  {"command": "segment.set_volume", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_a01cb913dfa3", "volume_db": -60}},
  {"command": "segment.set_volume", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_4852e1afa8a7", "volume_db": -60}},
  {"command": "segment.set_volume", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_4712217ee4d0", "volume_db": -60}}
]
```

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl batch prj_8a3dc0a150b8 tiktok-mute.json
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "kadr_batch", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_8a3dc0a150b8", "calls": [
  {"command": "segment.set_volume", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_a01cb913dfa3", "volume_db": -60}},
  {"command": "segment.set_volume", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_4852e1afa8a7", "volume_db": -60}},
  {"command": "segment.set_volume", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_4712217ee4d0", "volume_db": -60}}
]}}
```

Then add the song from 0 s for the length of the video (14.5 s here). It lands on an audio track. Lower it by a fixed 12 dB so it sits under the voice everywhere, and give it short fades:

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run timeline.segment.add --project_id prj_8a3dc0a150b8 --material_id mat_446985c2caf5 --at_us 0 --duration_us 14.5s
kadrctl run segment.set_volume --project_id prj_8a3dc0a150b8 --segment_id seg_5223e6a5f677 --volume_db -12
kadrctl run segment.set_fade --project_id prj_8a3dc0a150b8 --segment_id seg_5223e6a5f677 --fade_in_us 0.3s --fade_out_us 1.5s
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "timeline_segment_add", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_8a3dc0a150b8", "material_id": "mat_446985c2caf5", "at_us": 0, "duration_us": 14500000}}
{"name": "segment_set_volume", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_8a3dc0a150b8", "segment_id": "seg_5223e6a5f677", "volume_db": -12}}
{"name": "segment_set_fade", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_8a3dc0a150b8", "segment_id": "seg_5223e6a5f677", "fade_in_us": 300000, "fade_out_us": 1500000}}
```

To check the balance, measure both with `audio.loudness`. Background music works well 10–15 LU below speech: compare the voice’s `integrated_lufs` with the music’s `effective_lufs`, which already includes the −12 dB.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run audio.loudness --project_id prj_8a3dc0a150b8 --segment_id seg_f3a56bc31a8f
kadrctl run audio.loudness --project_id prj_8a3dc0a150b8 --segment_id seg_5223e6a5f677
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "audio_loudness", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_8a3dc0a150b8", "segment_id": "seg_f3a56bc31a8f"}}
{"name": "audio_loudness", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_8a3dc0a150b8", "segment_id": "seg_5223e6a5f677"}}
```

### 8. Look at the edit

`preview.contact_sheet` renders a grid of frames from the whole video with the export renderer. Through MCP the agent receives it as an image and can spot black bars, cut-off captions or a weak first frame before exporting.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run preview.contact_sheet --project_id prj_8a3dc0a150b8 --count 8 --columns 4 --tile_width 180
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "preview_contact_sheet", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_8a3dc0a150b8", "count": 8, "columns": 4, "tile_width": 180}}
```

### 9. Export 1080p

`export.start` renders in the background and returns a `job_id` at once. 1080p on a 9:16 canvas means 1080×1920 H.264 MP4; Kadr uses a GPU encoder when one works on your PC. Poll `export.status` until `state` is `done`.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run export.start --project_id prj_8a3dc0a150b8 --resolution 1080p --path C:/Users/you/Videos/Kadr/weekend-tiktok.mp4
kadrctl run export.status --job_id exp_ca964467da2a
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "export_start", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_8a3dc0a150b8", "resolution": "1080p", "path": "C:/Users/you/Videos/Kadr/weekend-tiktok.mp4"}}
{"name": "export_status", "arguments": {"job_id": "exp_ca964467da2a"}}
```

## Variations

- **Keep the whole picture.** Instead of reframing, show each landscape clip in full over a blurred copy of itself: `segment.set_background` with `type` `blur`, `blur` 0.75 and `apply_to_all` on any main-track clip.
- **Other caption looks.** `cap_pop_word` shows one word at a time, `cap_pill_active` puts the active word in a pill, `cap_karaoke_bar` fills words left to right. Switch at any time with `captions.set_style`.
- **Sound on the cuts.** Add `whoosh_fast` just before each cut with `sfx.add` (here at 6.8 s, 9.3 s and 11.8 s).
- **Cut to the music.** Slice the b-roll on the song’s beats instead of every 2.5 s — see [Music video cut to the beat](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/beat-cut-music-video.html).
- **Choose the cover.** `project.set_cover` with `time_us` sets the thumbnail frame.

## Tips

- The first caption job loads the Whisper model and takes longer than later ones. On an NVIDIA GPU the default `small` model runs about five times faster than real time; `model` `base` is faster and slightly less accurate.
- If captions fail with `not_available`, run `captions.asr_status`: its `hint` says what to install.
- To reorder later, `timeline.segment.move` a clip to a new `start_us`; the magnetic main track closes the gaps.

---

# Music video cut to the beat

Source: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/beat-cut-music-video.html

*Detect the beats of a song, cut a set of clips exactly on them in one atomic batch, then add flash transitions, a colour filter, a punch-zoom on the drop and a title.*

You get a music video where every cut lands on a beat, with a white flash on each cut, a teal-and-orange grade over everything, a punch-zoom when the track drops and a title over the first bar. The beats are detected on your PC, and the whole cut list is applied as one undoable step.

- **Time:** ~2 min
- **You need:** A song and a folder of clips
- **Main commands:** `audio.detect_beats`, `timeline.segment.add`, `timeline.segment.trim`, `segment.set_volume`, `transition.apply_all`, `filter.add`, `effect.add`, `text.add`, `export.start`

## Ask Claude

> In Kadr, make a 16:9 music video from C:\Users\you\Music\night-drive.mp3 and the clips in C:\Users\you\Videos\drive. Detect the beats and add beat markers. Cut to a new clip on every bar (every 8th onset — about 2 seconds at this tempo) for the first 16 seconds, cycling through the clips and using a later part of each clip the second time round. Mute the clips' own sound, end the song where the video ends with a 1.5 s fade-out, put a short white flash on every cut, grade everything with teal_orange at 80%, add punch_zoom for one bar at 8 seconds and the title "NIGHT DRIVE" with the cinematic template for the first 3 seconds. Show me a contact sheet, then export 1080p.

## Step by step

> **Note:** Each step shows the same calls twice. The **kadrctl** tab is for PowerShell: a line that starts with `kadrctl --%` passes JSON, and without `--%` the same line also works in Command Prompt. The **MCP** tab is the tool call an agent sends — the tool name and its arguments. Ids such as `prj_…`, `mat_…` and `seg_…` come from the results of earlier steps, so yours will differ. Paths under `C:/Users/you` are examples.

### 1. Create the project and import

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run project.create --name "Night drive" --ratio 16:9
kadrctl --% run media.import --project_id prj_408e1a6dfbd6 --paths "[\"C:/Users/you/Music/night-drive.mp3\",\"C:/Users/you/Videos/drive\"]"
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "project_create", "arguments": {"name": "Night drive", "ratio": "16:9"}}
{"name": "media_import", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_408e1a6dfbd6", "paths": ["C:/Users/you/Music/night-drive.mp3", "C:/Users/you/Videos/drive"]}}
```

The song becomes `mat_971f6c60fb07`; the four clips are `mat_757801976c94`, `mat_eb4ddf31388d`, `mat_f5b1e7278a6f` and `mat_434577267af4`.

### 2. Put the song on the timeline

Audio never goes to the main track: it lands on an audio track, here from 0 s.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run timeline.segment.add --project_id prj_408e1a6dfbd6 --material_id mat_971f6c60fb07 --at_us 0
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "timeline_segment_add", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_408e1a6dfbd6", "material_id": "mat_971f6c60fb07", "at_us": 0}}
```

### 3. Detect the beats

`audio.detect_beats` analyses the song on your PC and returns every onset as a *timeline* time in microseconds, plus a rough tempo. `add_markers` also puts a “Beat” marker on the ruler, so clips you drag later in the editor snap to the music.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run audio.detect_beats --project_id prj_408e1a6dfbd6 --segment_id seg_a685cca02d34 --sensitivity 0.5 --add_markers
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "audio_detect_beats", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_408e1a6dfbd6", "segment_id": "seg_a685cca02d34", "sensitivity": 0.5, "add_markers": true}}
```

```json
{
  "segment_id": "seg_a685cca02d34",
  "count": 120,
  "bpm": 119.8,
  "markers_added": 120,
  "beats_us": [0, 252517, 501769, 720907, 1000998, 1248435, 1501678, 1750567, 2001270, …]
}
```

Shortened. This track has a hi-hat on every eighth note, so onsets come about every 0.25 s at 120 BPM; one 4/4 bar is 8 onsets. Taking every 8th entry gives the cut points 0, 2001270, 4001088, 6001270, 8001088, 10001270, 12001088, 14001270 and 16001088 µs.

### 4. Cut the clips on the beats in one batch

Each shot is added with `duration_us` equal to the distance between two cut points. Clips appended to the magnetic main track sit back to back, so every cut lands exactly on a beat. The second time round, `source_start_us` starts each clip 3 s in, so no shot repeats. Save as `beat-cut.json`:

```json
[
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_757801976c94", "source_start_us": 0, "duration_us": 2001270}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_eb4ddf31388d", "source_start_us": 0, "duration_us": 1999818}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_f5b1e7278a6f", "source_start_us": 0, "duration_us": 2000182}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_434577267af4", "source_start_us": 0, "duration_us": 1999818}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_757801976c94", "source_start_us": 3000000, "duration_us": 2000182}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_eb4ddf31388d", "source_start_us": 3000000, "duration_us": 1999818}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_f5b1e7278a6f", "source_start_us": 3000000, "duration_us": 2000182}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_434577267af4", "source_start_us": 3000000, "duration_us": 1999818}}
]
```

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl batch prj_408e1a6dfbd6 beat-cut.json --dry-run
kadrctl batch prj_408e1a6dfbd6 beat-cut.json
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "kadr_batch", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_408e1a6dfbd6", "calls": [
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_757801976c94", "source_start_us": 0, "duration_us": 2001270}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_eb4ddf31388d", "source_start_us": 0, "duration_us": 1999818}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_f5b1e7278a6f", "source_start_us": 0, "duration_us": 2000182}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_434577267af4", "source_start_us": 0, "duration_us": 1999818}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_757801976c94", "source_start_us": 3000000, "duration_us": 2000182}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_eb4ddf31388d", "source_start_us": 3000000, "duration_us": 1999818}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_f5b1e7278a6f", "source_start_us": 3000000, "duration_us": 2000182}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_434577267af4", "source_start_us": 3000000, "duration_us": 1999818}}
]}}
```

The dry run checks the plan first — for example, it fails if a slice asks for more video than a clip has — and changes nothing. The real run adds all eight shots as one undo step.

### 5. Mute the clips and fit the song

One more batch: mute every shot’s own sound, cut the song where the video ends (16001088 µs) with `timeline.segment.trim`, and fade it out. `snap` `false` puts the edge exactly there instead of snapping to a nearby beat marker. Save as `beat-audio.json`:

```json
[
  {"command": "segment.set_volume", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_896a3c69fde1", "volume_db": -60}},
  {"command": "segment.set_volume", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_4dd4dd6ff8a2", "volume_db": -60}},
  {"command": "segment.set_volume", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_2b7e19c04d5a", "volume_db": -60}},
  {"command": "segment.set_volume", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_c81f3e60a97b", "volume_db": -60}},
  {"command": "segment.set_volume", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_5e0a94d2c1f8", "volume_db": -60}},
  {"command": "segment.set_volume", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_e7b2063d9a14", "volume_db": -60}},
  {"command": "segment.set_volume", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_19c4f7a2e08d", "volume_db": -60}},
  {"command": "segment.set_volume", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_a3d58e1b6c27", "volume_db": -60}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.trim", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_a685cca02d34", "edge": "right", "to_us": 16001088, "snap": false}},
  {"command": "segment.set_fade", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_a685cca02d34", "fade_out_us": 1500000}}
]
```

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl batch prj_408e1a6dfbd6 beat-audio.json
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "kadr_batch", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_408e1a6dfbd6", "calls": [
  {"command": "segment.set_volume", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_896a3c69fde1", "volume_db": -60}},
  {"command": "segment.set_volume", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_4dd4dd6ff8a2", "volume_db": -60}},
  {"command": "segment.set_volume", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_2b7e19c04d5a", "volume_db": -60}},
  {"command": "segment.set_volume", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_c81f3e60a97b", "volume_db": -60}},
  {"command": "segment.set_volume", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_5e0a94d2c1f8", "volume_db": -60}},
  {"command": "segment.set_volume", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_e7b2063d9a14", "volume_db": -60}},
  {"command": "segment.set_volume", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_19c4f7a2e08d", "volume_db": -60}},
  {"command": "segment.set_volume", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_a3d58e1b6c27", "volume_db": -60}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.trim", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_a685cca02d34", "edge": "right", "to_us": 16001088, "snap": false}},
  {"command": "segment.set_fade", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_a685cca02d34", "fade_out_us": 1500000}}
]}}
```

### 6. Flash on every cut

A short transition keeps the cut on the beat. `transition.apply_all` sets it on all seven cuts.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run transition.apply_all --project_id prj_408e1a6dfbd6 --type white_flash --duration_us 160ms
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "transition_apply_all", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_408e1a6dfbd6", "type": "white_flash", "duration_us": 160000}}
```

### 7. Grade, hit the drop, add a title

`filter.add` puts the filter on its own track, so it colours everything below it for its whole length. `effect.add` places `punch_zoom` on the fifth bar, from 8001088 µs for one bar. `text.add` with the `cinematic` template adds the title on a text track.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run filter.add --project_id prj_408e1a6dfbd6 --filter_id teal_orange --at_us 0 --duration_us 16001088 --intensity 0.8
kadrctl run effect.add --project_id prj_408e1a6dfbd6 --effect_id punch_zoom --at_us 8001088 --duration_us 2000182
kadrctl run text.add --project_id prj_408e1a6dfbd6 --text "NIGHT DRIVE" --template_id cinematic --at_us 0 --duration_us 3s
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "filter_add", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_408e1a6dfbd6", "filter_id": "teal_orange", "at_us": 0, "duration_us": 16001088, "intensity": 0.8}}
{"name": "effect_add", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_408e1a6dfbd6", "effect_id": "punch_zoom", "at_us": 8001088, "duration_us": 2000182}}
{"name": "text_add", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_408e1a6dfbd6", "text": "NIGHT DRIVE", "template_id": "cinematic", "at_us": 0, "duration_us": 3000000}}
```

### 8. Check and export

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run preview.contact_sheet --project_id prj_408e1a6dfbd6 --count 8 --columns 4 --tile_width 240
kadrctl run export.start --project_id prj_408e1a6dfbd6 --resolution 1080p --path C:/Users/you/Videos/Kadr/night-drive.mp4
kadrctl run export.status --job_id exp_51d0a7c3e9b2
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "preview_contact_sheet", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_408e1a6dfbd6", "count": 8, "columns": 4, "tile_width": 240}}
{"name": "export_start", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_408e1a6dfbd6", "resolution": "1080p", "path": "C:/Users/you/Videos/Kadr/night-drive.mp4"}}
{"name": "export_status", "arguments": {"job_id": "exp_51d0a7c3e9b2"}}
```

## Variations

### One long clip, split on every beat

`timeline.segment.split` needs no `segment_id` when you pass only `at_us`: it splits whatever main-track clip is under that time. A batch of splits, one per cut point, chops a single long take into beat-length pieces that you can then delete, reverse or speed up one by one.

```json
[
  { "command": "timeline.segment.split", "args": { "at_us": 2001270 } },
  { "command": "timeline.segment.split", "args": { "at_us": 4001088 } },
  { "command": "timeline.segment.split", "args": { "at_us": 6001270 } }
]
```

### More ideas

- **Faster cuts.** Use every 4th onset (one cut per beat) for the chorus and every 8th for the verse.
- **Other cut styles.** Try `flash_zoom`, `glitch`, `whip_pan` or `zoom_blur_through` as the transition, and `rgb_pulse` or `hard_shake` as the drop effect. `library.list` with `kind` `transition` or `effect` lists them all.
- **Vertical version.** See [One project, three formats](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/batch-export-variants.html).

## Tips

- `sensitivity` goes from 0 to 1: 0.7–0.9 for busy percussion, 0.2–0.4 to keep only strong hits. `strengths` gives each beat’s strength (0–1), which helps tell downbeats from off-beats.
- Beat times are already timeline times (the song’s position and speed are taken into account), so they go straight into `at_us` and `duration_us`.
- `audio.detect_beats` is recorded as an undo step even without `add_markers`; that is harmless.

---

# Talking-head cleanup to a vertical short

Source: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/talking-head-cleanup.html

*Clean up a talking-head recording: denoise and level the voice, cut silences, filler words and long pauses, add captions, and reframe to 9:16 for a short.*

You get a vertical short made from a raw talking-head take. Background noise is reduced, the voice is levelled, dead air is cut, every “um” and “uh” is gone, and captions show three words at a time. In our test a 26.8 s take became a 15.9 s short.

- **Time:** ~2 min
- **You need:** A talking-head video (landscape is fine)
- **Main commands:** `segment.set_audio`, `segment.set_video_cleanup`, `ai.auto_reframe`, `ai.remove_silence`, `transcript.transcribe`, `transcript.remove_fillers`, `transcript.remove_pauses`, `captions.from_transcript`, `export.start`

## Ask Claude

> Clean up my talking-head video C:\Users\you\Videos\tips-take3.mp4 in Kadr and turn it into a vertical short. Reduce background noise and normalise the loudness, lightly denoise the picture, and reframe it to 9:16 following me. Cut silences longer than 0.7 s, then transcribe it in English and remove filler words and any pauses over 0.6 s that are left. Show me which fillers you found before cutting them. Add captions with the cap_pill_active style, 3 words at a time. Show me a frame, then export 1080p to C:\Users\you\Videos\Kadr\tips-short.mp4.

## Step by step

> **Note:** Each step shows the same calls twice. The **kadrctl** tab is for PowerShell: a line that starts with `kadrctl --%` passes JSON, and without `--%` the same line also works in Command Prompt. The **MCP** tab is the tool call an agent sends — the tool name and its arguments. Ids such as `prj_…`, `mat_…` and `seg_…` come from the results of earlier steps, so yours will differ. Paths under `C:/Users/you` are examples.

### 1. Create, import and place the take

Start with a 16:9 project; the reframe step switches the canvas to 9:16.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run project.create --name "Tips short" --ratio 16:9
kadrctl --% run media.import --project_id prj_ed95831b1bf0 --paths "[\"C:/Users/you/Videos/tips-take3.mp4\"]"
kadrctl run timeline.segment.add --project_id prj_ed95831b1bf0 --material_id mat_745ea2a4d7e6
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "project_create", "arguments": {"name": "Tips short", "ratio": "16:9"}}
{"name": "media_import", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_ed95831b1bf0", "paths": ["C:/Users/you/Videos/tips-take3.mp4"]}}
{"name": "timeline_segment_add", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_ed95831b1bf0", "material_id": "mat_745ea2a4d7e6"}}
```

### 2. Clean the sound and the picture first

Set these before cutting: every piece made by a later cut keeps its clip’s settings, so you set them once. `segment.set_audio` turns on noise reduction and loudness normalisation; `segment.set_video_cleanup` applies light denoising (0–1) while the video is decoded.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run segment.set_audio --project_id prj_ed95831b1bf0 --segment_id seg_997808f11662 --reduce_noise --normalize_loudness
kadrctl run segment.set_video_cleanup --project_id prj_ed95831b1bf0 --segment_id seg_997808f11662 --denoise 0.3
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "segment_set_audio", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_ed95831b1bf0", "segment_id": "seg_997808f11662", "reduce_noise": true, "normalize_loudness": true}}
{"name": "segment_set_video_cleanup", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_ed95831b1bf0", "segment_id": "seg_997808f11662", "denoise": 0.3}}
```

### 3. Reframe to 9:16

`ai.auto_reframe` with `set_canvas` switches the project to 9:16 and animates the framing to follow the speaker. Running it before the cuts means one call covers the whole take.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run ai.auto_reframe --project_id prj_ed95831b1bf0 --segment_id seg_997808f11662 --ratio 9:16 --set_canvas
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "ai_auto_reframe", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_ed95831b1bf0", "segment_id": "seg_997808f11662", "ratio": "9:16", "set_canvas": true}}
```

### 4. Cut the silences

`ai.remove_silence` measures the audio level and cuts every stretch quieter than −40 dBFS that lasts longer than 0.7 s, keeps 120 ms of padding on each side so words are not clipped, and closes the gaps. The result lists what was removed and the ids of the remaining pieces (`segment_ids`).

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run ai.remove_silence --project_id prj_ed95831b1bf0 --segment_id seg_997808f11662 --threshold_db -40 --min_silence_us 0.7s --padding_us 120ms
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "ai_remove_silence", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_ed95831b1bf0", "segment_id": "seg_997808f11662", "threshold_db": -40, "min_silence_us": 700000, "padding_us": 120000}}
```

### 5. Transcribe

`transcript.transcribe` runs Whisper locally and stores every word with its timing on the material. Kadr maps the words onto the pieces left after the cuts, so the transcript always matches the timeline. Without `segment_id` it transcribes every audible clip.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run transcript.transcribe --project_id prj_ed95831b1bf0 --language en --wait
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "transcript_transcribe", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_ed95831b1bf0", "language": "en", "wait": true}}
```

```text
Hi everyone. Um, today I want to show you three quick editing tips. Uh, the first one is simple,
cut your pauses. The second one is, um, add captions to every video. And the third is to keep it
short and punchy. Thanks for watching.
```

### 6. Remove filler words

`transcript.remove_fillers` with `preview` only reports what it found (here *Um,* *Uh,* and *um,*). Without `preview` it cuts them, and the rest of the timeline moves up to close each gap.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run transcript.remove_fillers --project_id prj_ed95831b1bf0 --preview
kadrctl run transcript.remove_fillers --project_id prj_ed95831b1bf0
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "transcript_remove_fillers", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_ed95831b1bf0", "preview": true}}
{"name": "transcript_remove_fillers", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_ed95831b1bf0"}}
```

### 7. Tighten the remaining pauses

`transcript.remove_pauses` works from word timings rather than the audio level: every gap between words longer than 0.6 s is shortened to 0.25 s. After `ai.remove_silence` it catches pauses filled with breaths or room noise. In our clean test recording there was nothing left to remove.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run transcript.remove_pauses --project_id prj_ed95831b1bf0 --min_pause_us 0.6s --keep_us 250ms
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "transcript_remove_pauses", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_ed95831b1bf0", "min_pause_us": 600000, "keep_us": 250000}}
```

### 8. Captions from the transcript

The transcript already exists, so `captions.from_transcript` creates the cues without running speech recognition again.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run captions.from_transcript --project_id prj_ed95831b1bf0 --style_id cap_pill_active --max_words 3
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "captions_from_transcript", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_ed95831b1bf0", "style_id": "cap_pill_active", "max_words": 3}}
```

### 9. Check and export

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run preview.frame --project_id prj_ed95831b1bf0 --time_us 2s --width 360
kadrctl run export.start --project_id prj_ed95831b1bf0 --resolution 1080p --path C:/Users/you/Videos/Kadr/tips-short.mp4
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "preview_frame", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_ed95831b1bf0", "time_us": 2000000, "width": 360}}
{"name": "export_start", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_ed95831b1bf0", "resolution": "1080p", "path": "C:/Users/you/Videos/Kadr/tips-short.mp4"}}
```

## Variations

- **Cut a phrase by its text.** `transcript.delete_text` with `text` “thanks for watching” finds the words in the transcript and cuts them out of the video; captions follow the cut.
- **Your own fillers.** `transcript.remove_fillers` accepts extra `words` such as `["okay", "right so"]`. It has built-in lists for English, Ukrainian and Russian.
- **Keep it 16:9.** Skip the reframe step for YouTube.
- **Audio only.** Export the cleaned voice for a podcast feed: `export.start` with `audio_only` and `audio_format` `mp3`.

## Tips

- In a noisy room raise `threshold_db` to −30 so the hum counts as silence; in a very quiet room lower it to −50.
- Use `preview` on `transcript.remove_fillers` and `transcript.remove_pauses` first. Every cut can be undone, but checking the list is quicker.
- Transcripts belong to the media, not the timeline. After further edits `captions.from_transcript` rebuilds the captions without transcribing again.
- Names spelled wrong? Pass `prompt` “Kadr, Kyiv, Olena” to `transcript.transcribe` (add `force` to redo an existing transcript).

---

# Photo slideshow with Ken Burns motion

Source: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/photo-slideshow.html

*Turn a folder of photos into a slideshow with slow Ken Burns zoom and pan (keyframes with cubic easing), cross-dissolves, music with fades and an animated title.*

You get a 16:9 slideshow where every photo slowly zooms and drifts, alternating between zooming in and zooming out. Photos blend with 0.8 s dissolves, the music fades in and out, and the title rises in letter by letter.

- **Time:** ~2 min
- **You need:** A folder of photos and a music track
- **Main commands:** `media.import`, `timeline.segment.add`, `keyframe.add`, `transition.apply_all`, `segment.set_fade`, `text.add`, `text.set_glyph_animation`, `preview.layout`, `export.start`

## Ask Claude

> Make a 16:9 slideshow in Kadr from the photos in C:\Users\you\Pictures\summer, 4 seconds per photo. Give every photo a slow Ken Burns move: alternate zooming in from 110% to 125% and zooming out from 125% to 110%, with a gentle sideways drift and ease-in-out, and make sure no black edges ever show. Use 0.8 s mix transitions between all photos. Put C:\Users\you\Music\warm.mp3 under the whole slideshow with a 1 s fade-in and a 2 s fade-out. Add the title "Summer 2026" from 0.3 s to 3.5 s with the title_bold template, letters rising in and fading out. Show me frames at 0.1 s and 3 s, then export 1080p.

## Step by step

> **Note:** Each step shows the same calls twice. The **kadrctl** tab is for PowerShell: a line that starts with `kadrctl --%` passes JSON, and without `--%` the same line also works in Command Prompt. The **MCP** tab is the tool call an agent sends — the tool name and its arguments. Ids such as `prj_…`, `mat_…` and `seg_…` come from the results of earlier steps, so yours will differ. Paths under `C:/Users/you` are examples.

### 1. Create and import

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run project.create --name "Summer slideshow" --ratio 16:9
kadrctl --% run media.import --project_id prj_ea391e038f3f --paths "[\"C:/Users/you/Pictures/summer\",\"C:/Users/you/Music/warm.mp3\"]"
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "project_create", "arguments": {"name": "Summer slideshow", "ratio": "16:9"}}
{"name": "media_import", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_ea391e038f3f", "paths": ["C:/Users/you/Pictures/summer", "C:/Users/you/Music/warm.mp3"]}}
```

Photos are imported with `duration_us` 0: a photo can be stretched to any length on the timeline.

### 2. Place the photos, 4 seconds each

One `timeline.segment.add` per photo, all in one batch (`slides.json`). `duration_us` sets each photo’s length (the default for photos is 5 s).

```json
[
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_35640c6ac4cf", "duration_us": 4000000}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_0d53e39cc91a", "duration_us": 4000000}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_6cf1f65ad462", "duration_us": 4000000}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_c41da8217be6", "duration_us": 4000000}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_bd01c3e803d1", "duration_us": 4000000}}
]
```

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl batch prj_ea391e038f3f slides.json
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "kadr_batch", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_ea391e038f3f", "calls": [
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_35640c6ac4cf", "duration_us": 4000000}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_0d53e39cc91a", "duration_us": 4000000}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_6cf1f65ad462", "duration_us": 4000000}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_c41da8217be6", "duration_us": 4000000}},
  {"command": "timeline.segment.add", "args": {"material_id": "mat_bd01c3e803d1", "duration_us": 4000000}}
]}}
```

### 3. Add the Ken Burns moves

Each photo gets four keyframes: `transform.scale` and `transform.x` at the clip’s start (`time_us` 0) and end (4000000). `keyframe.add` times are *relative to the clip start*, so the same numbers work for every photo. The easing sits on the first keyframe of each pair: it shapes the motion *from* that keyframe to the next (cubic `ease_in_out`). Photos 1, 3 and 5 zoom in; 2 and 4 zoom out. Save as `ken-burns.json`:

```json
[
  {"command": "keyframe.add", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_f81fd1e725f2", "property": "transform.scale", "time_us": 0, "value": 1.1, "easing": "ease_in_out"}},
  {"command": "keyframe.add", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_f81fd1e725f2", "property": "transform.scale", "time_us": 4000000, "value": 1.25}},
  {"command": "keyframe.add", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_f81fd1e725f2", "property": "transform.x", "time_us": 0, "value": -0.05, "easing": "ease_in_out"}},
  {"command": "keyframe.add", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_f81fd1e725f2", "property": "transform.x", "time_us": 4000000, "value": 0.05}},
  {"command": "keyframe.add", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_8915fde933d3", "property": "transform.scale", "time_us": 0, "value": 1.25, "easing": "ease_in_out"}},
  {"command": "keyframe.add", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_8915fde933d3", "property": "transform.scale", "time_us": 4000000, "value": 1.1}},
  {"command": "keyframe.add", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_8915fde933d3", "property": "transform.x", "time_us": 0, "value": 0.05, "easing": "ease_in_out"}},
  {"command": "keyframe.add", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_8915fde933d3", "property": "transform.x", "time_us": 4000000, "value": -0.05}},
  {"command": "keyframe.add", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_40017cbd60ba", "property": "transform.scale", "time_us": 0, "value": 1.1, "easing": "ease_in_out"}},
  {"command": "keyframe.add", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_40017cbd60ba", "property": "transform.scale", "time_us": 4000000, "value": 1.25}},
  {"command": "keyframe.add", "args": {"segment_id": "seg_40017cbd60ba", "property": "transform.x", "time_us": 0, "value": -0.05, "easing": "ease_in_out"}},
```

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**
