### 11. Export

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run export.start --project_id prj_d4a1c9e3b702 --resolution 1080p --path C:/Users/you/Videos/Kadr/dday-1944.mp4
kadrctl run export.status --job_id exp_e2a6c0b9f4d7
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "export_start", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_d4a1c9e3b702", "resolution": "1080p", "path": "C:/Users/you/Videos/Kadr/dday-1944.mp4"}}
{"name": "export_status", "arguments": {"job_id": "exp_e2a6c0b9f4d7"}}
```

When `state` is `done`, `path` and `size_bytes` describe the file. See [Verifying results](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/verifying.html) for checking the exported video itself.

## Variations

- **No ElevenLabs key.** Use `espeak:uk` (or any voice from `tts.voices`) in `tts.speak`; everything else stays the same. Remove a stored key with `tts.set_api_key` and `clear`.
- **Longer films.** Narrate paragraph by paragraph (up to 5000 characters per call) and keep one shot per sentence; build the shot list as one `dday-shots.json` batch.
- **Music bed.** Public-domain or CC0 music from the same archive, added with `timeline.segment.add` at −20 dB (`segment.set_volume`) under the voice.
- **Projector sound.** `sfx.add` with `film_advance` at 0 s adds a projector start.
- **Vertical cut.** Duplicate the project, switch it to 9:16 and reframe each shot — see [One project, three formats](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/batch-export-variants.html).

## Tips

- `tts.speak` fails with `not_found` “voice … is not installed” when the ElevenLabs key is missing or the voice id is not in your account’s list — run `tts.voices` with `refresh` and copy an id from there.
- Speech speed for ElevenLabs is limited to 0.7–1.2 (`rate`); slow narration down there rather than by stretching the clip.
- Text you synthesise is sent to ElevenLabs; everything else — footage, edits, captions — stays on your PC.
- **Plan shots as data.** Keep a small `shots.json` next to the clips — scene, order, file, duration — and name each file after its source and timecode (for example `s2_1_B991.mp4` = scene 2, first shot, source B at 991 s). The plan turns straight into the `dday-shots.json` batch, and the names make re-cuts and credits easy. A long narration line can be covered by two shots that share its time (say 4.0 s + 3.95 s).
- Keep the archive identifiers and timecodes in your notes; the end credit should name the source.

---

# Choose a transition and an effect by looking at them

Source: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/preview-before-applying.html

*Narrow Kadr's 221 transitions and 195 effects to a few candidates with library.list, look at how each one plays with library.preview contact sheets, apply the best with its direction, softness or sliders, and confirm it in the edit.*

You get a transition and an effect chosen by eye, not by name. Claude narrows the library to a few candidates, renders each one as a contact sheet to see how it moves, applies the best one with the right direction and sliders, and checks the result in your own edit.

- **Time:** ~1 min
- **You need:** A Kadr project with two clips that touch
- **Main commands:** `library.list`, `library.preview`, `transition.set`, `preview.contact_sheet`, `effect.add`, `preview.frame`

## Ask Claude

> In my Kadr project "Travel teaser", pick a calm, flowing transition for the cut between the two clips — look at a few liquid transitions with library_preview before you decide, and tell me why you chose it. Then add a weather effect over the second clip that suits a rainy evening, again comparing a couple of options visually. Show me a contact sheet of the cut when you're done.

## Step by step

> **Note:** Each step shows the same calls twice. The **kadrctl** tab is for PowerShell: a line that starts with `kadrctl --%` passes JSON, and without `--%` the same line also works in Command Prompt. The **MCP** tab is the tool call an agent sends — the tool name and its arguments. Ids such as `prj_…` and `seg_…` come from the results of earlier steps, so yours will differ. In this example the project holds two generated 3-second clips: a sunset mesh gradient and a city-lights bokeh.

### 1. Shortlist candidates

A category tab is the quickest filter: *Liquid* has 14 transitions. The descriptions say what each one looks like and when to use it.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run library.list --kind transition --category Liquid
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "library_list", "arguments": {"kind": "transition", "category": "Liquid"}}
```

```text
tide_wipe     Tide          A rolling wave front with a sparkling white foam crest washes the new clip in. Great for beach, travel and summer footage…
ink_bleed     Ink bleed     Dark ink blots spread with organic tendrils from a few drops; the ink clears behind its front to reveal the new clip…
paint_splash  Paint splash  A spiky paint splash with flying droplets bursts from near the centre and floods into the new clip…
```

### 2. Look at each one

> **Note:** Through MCP, `library_preview` comes back as an image, so Claude actually sees the motion. With `kadrctl` or REST you get the same PNG as base64 in `png_base64`.

A one-row strip of six tiles is enough to compare. The tiles run from clip A (a sunny landscape) to clip B (a night city).

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run library.preview --kind transition --id tide_wipe --frames 6 --columns 6 --tile_width 160
kadrctl run library.preview --kind transition --id ink_bleed --frames 6 --columns 6 --tile_width 160
kadrctl run library.preview --kind transition --id paint_splash --frames 6 --columns 6 --tile_width 160
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "library_preview", "arguments": {"kind": "transition", "id": "tide_wipe", "frames": 6, "columns": 6, "tile_width": 160}}
{"name": "library_preview", "arguments": {"kind": "transition", "id": "ink_bleed", "frames": 6, "columns": 6, "tile_width": 160}}
{"name": "library_preview", "arguments": {"kind": "transition", "id": "paint_splash", "frames": 6, "columns": 6, "tile_width": 160}}
```

Tide sweeps a wavy foam line across the frame; Ink bleed grows dark blots that would muddy a bright sunset; Paint splash is loud. For a calm travel teaser Claude picks **Tide**.

### 3. Read its options

The item from step 1 lists what `tide_wipe` accepts: `"directions": ["right","left","down","up"]`, `"softness": true`, `"default_softness": 0.2`. A wave coming in from the right reads as forward motion, and a slightly softer edge suits the gradient.

### 4. Apply it to the cut

The transition goes on the **left** clip of the cut. `direction` is the way the motion travels.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run transition.set --project_id prj_e21b467917e3 --segment_id seg_3ccd6c9e2cbe --type tide_wipe --duration_us 0.8s --direction left --softness 0.3
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "transition_set", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_e21b467917e3", "segment_id": "seg_3ccd6c9e2cbe", "type": "tide_wipe", "duration_us": 800000, "direction": "left", "softness": 0.3}}
```

```text
type tide_wipe?direction=left&softness=0.3   duration_us 800000   clamped false   max_duration_us 1500000
```

### 5. Check it in the edit

The library preview used sample pictures; now look at the real cut. Four tiles across the 0.8 s around the cut at 3 s:

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run preview.contact_sheet --project_id prj_e21b467917e3 --start_us 2.6s --end_us 3.4s --count 4 --columns 4 --tile_width 240
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "preview_contact_sheet", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_e21b467917e3", "start_us": 2600000, "end_us": 3400000, "count": 4, "columns": 4, "tile_width": 240}}
```

At 2.7, 2.9, 3.1 and 3.3 s the foam line travels from the right edge to the left, uncovering the city lights.

### 6. Do the same for an effect

*Weather* has 8 effects. Their items list the sliders in `params.schema` — `rain_glass` has `density` and `fog` besides `intensity` and `speed`. Look at it, then add it over the second clip with denser drops and less fog, and check one frame.

**kadrctl (PowerShell):**

```powershell
kadrctl run library.list --kind effect --category Weather
kadrctl run library.preview --kind effect --id rain_glass --frames 4 --columns 4 --tile_width 200
kadrctl --% run effect.add --project_id prj_e21b467917e3 --effect_id rain_glass --at_us 3s --duration_us 3s --params "{\"density\":0.7,\"fog\":0.3}"
kadrctl run preview.frame --project_id prj_e21b467917e3 --time_us 4.5s --width 640
```

**MCP tool call (tools/call params):**

```json
{"name": "library_list", "arguments": {"kind": "effect", "category": "Weather"}}
{"name": "library_preview", "arguments": {"kind": "effect", "id": "rain_glass", "frames": 4, "columns": 4, "tile_width": 200}}
{"name": "effect_add", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_e21b467917e3", "effect_id": "rain_glass", "at_us": 3000000, "duration_us": 3000000, "params": {"density": 0.7, "fog": 0.3}}}
{"name": "preview_frame", "arguments": {"project_id": "prj_e21b467917e3", "time_us": 4500000, "width": 640}}
```

The effect lands on its own effect track (`segment.effect` = `{"id": "rain_glass", "params": {"density": 0.7, "fog": 0.3, "intensity": 1, "speed": 1}}`) and the frame shows raindrops on glass over the city lights.

## Variations

- **Clip animations:** `kind: "animation"` (categories In, Out, Combo, Loop), then `animation.set`. Use `frames: 8, columns: 4` for longer moves.
- **Text:** `text_template`, `text_effect` and `text_animation` render sample text; apply with `text.add`, `text.apply_effect` or `text.set_glyph_animation`.
- **Filters:** the tiles show a before/after divider, which makes subtle grades easy to compare side by side.
- **Captions:** `caption_style` shows the word highlight moving through a sample caption.

More about ids, the `preview` field and options in [Library, previews and fonts](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/library.html).

# Command reference

Source: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference-intro.html

*How the reference of all 183 Kadr commands is organised: categories, what each entry contains, how to read command names, and the same data as API, OpenAPI and llms-full.txt.*

The command reference documents all 183 commands in 29 categories — the same text an agent receives as MCP tool descriptions, generated from the engine’s own registry. Command descriptions are in English in both languages.

[**Open the full command reference →**](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/index.html)

## What each entry contains

- **Name and title** — the dotted command name (`timeline.segment.split`), its MCP tool name (`timeline_segment_split`) and a short title.
- **Description** — what the command does, how it mirrors CapCut, edge cases and the errors it can return.
- **Parameters** — name, type, required or optional, default, allowed values or range, and unit. Every `*_us` parameter is an integer in microseconds.
- **Returns** — the shape of the result.
- **Flags** — undoable or read-only, project or global scope, UI location and hotkey.
- **Examples** — ready JSON arguments, each checked against the parameter schema.

## Reading command names

The part before the first dot is the namespace — the subject the command acts on: `project.`, `media.`, `timeline.` (clips, tracks, markers), `segment.` (one clip’s properties), `keyframe.`, `animation.`, `text.`, `captions.`, `transcript.`, `audio.`, `tts.`, `sfx.`, `effect.`, `filter.`, `adjustment.`, `transition.`, `library.`, `font.`, `preview.`, `playback.`, `export.`, `ai.` (smart tools), `presets.`, `edit.`, `clipboard.`, `ui.`, `tools.`, `update.`, `app.`. Verbs are consistent: `add` creates a new segment, `apply` changes an existing clip, `set`/`set_*` replaces values, `get`/`list` only read.

## The same reference in other forms

| Source | Use it when |
| --- | --- |
| `kadrctl describe <command>` | You are in a terminal. |
| `GET /api/v1/commands`, `GET /api/v1/commands/{name}` | You need the exact spec of the running engine (with JSON Schema). |
| `http://127.0.0.1:7777/docs` | You want the reference of your installed version in a browser. |
| [`openapi.json`](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/openapi.json) | You generate clients or function-calling tool definitions. |
| [`llms-full.txt`](https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/llms-full.txt) | You want every command spec plus these guides as one Markdown file for a model’s context. |

# Command specifications

All 188 commands, grouped by category. Every command is available as `POST /api/v1/commands/<name>`, as the MCP tool `<name with dots replaced by underscores>` and as `kadrctl run <name> --param value`. Commands that edit one project take `project_id` and can be combined in a batch; global commands (projects list/create/duplicate/delete, library and `library.preview`, fonts, presets, export jobs, `captions.auto`, `transcript.transcribe`, tools, updates, `ui.toast`, `ui.library_tab`) cannot — a batch rejects them with an explicit error. Parameters ending in `_us` are integer microseconds.

## Adjustment

7 commands: `adjustment.auto_enhance`, `segment.reset_adjust`, `segment.reset_curves`, `segment.reset_hsl`, `segment.set_adjust`, `segment.set_curves`, `segment.set_hsl`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/adjustment.html

### adjustment.auto_enhance

**Auto adjust** · MCP tool `adjustment_auto_enhance` · `POST /api/v1/commands/adjustment.auto_enhance` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Adjustment/Basic/Auto adjust

Automatically corrects the colour of a video/photo clip or of an adjustment layer — CapCut's Auto adjust wand. Renders one representative frame (by default the middle of the segment; time_us picks another moment) of what the segment colours — the clip itself WITHOUT its current adjustments, filter and effects, or for an adjustment-layer segment everything on the tracks below it — and analyses it: luminance percentiles set exposure (median towards mid grey without clipping the highlights) and contrast (stretch a flat tonal range), a grey-world estimate on near-neutral midtones sets temperature and tint (removes colour casts such as orange tungsten or blue shade), and low mean chroma raises saturation a little. Writes exposure, contrast, temperature, tint and saturation (other adjustments, HSL and curves are kept; keyframed fields get a keyframe at the playhead). strength scales the correction (0.5 = half). Running it twice gives the same values. Returns the applied values and the measurements. Needs the media to be readable (ffmpeg for video).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `strength` | number | no | `1` | 0 … 1 | How much of the computed correction to apply, 0..1 (default 1). |
| `time_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Frame to analyse, relative to the segment start. Defaults to the middle of the segment. |

**Returns:** {segment, applied: {exposure, contrast, temperature, tint, saturation}, analysis: {median_luma, black_point, white_point, mean_chroma, cast_rgb}, time_us, keyframed?}.

Example — Fix exposure and white balance of a clip:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Gentle correction from the frame at 2 s:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","strength":0.6,"time_us":2000000}
```

### segment.reset_adjust

**Reset adjustments** · MCP tool `segment_reset_adjust` · `POST /api/v1/commands/segment.reset_adjust` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Adjustment/Reset

Returns every colour adjustment of a clip (or adjustment segment) to neutral — basic sliders (incl. hue, fade, grain, shine), all eight HSL bands and every tone curve — and removes its LUT and all adjust.* keyframes: the Reset button of CapCut's Adjustment tab. Filters and effects are not affected (use filter.remove / effect.remove). To reset only HSL or curves use segment.reset_hsl / segment.reset_curves.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |

**Returns:** {segment} without adjustments (an adjustment-layer segment keeps a neutral adjust object).

Example — Reset colour:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### segment.reset_curves

**Reset curves** · MCP tool `segment_reset_curves` · `POST /api/v1/commands/segment.reset_curves` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Adjustment/Curves/Reset

Straightens tone curves of a clip or adjustment segment: one channel (master, r, g or b) or all of them when channel is omitted — the reset button of CapCut's Curves page. Other adjustments are kept. Resetting straight curves is a no-op.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `channel` | string | no |  | `master`, `r`, `g`, `b` | Channel to straighten; omit to reset every channel and the preset. |

**Returns:** {segment} — segment.adjust.curves without the reset channel(s).

Example — Reset all curves:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Reset only the blue curve:

```json
{"channel":"b","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### segment.reset_hsl

**Reset HSL** · MCP tool `segment_reset_hsl` · `POST /api/v1/commands/segment.reset_hsl` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Adjustment/HSL/Reset

Resets the HSL page of a clip's (or adjustment segment's) colour adjustments: one band back to h = s = l = 0, or every band when band is omitted or "all" — the reset button of CapCut's HSL page. Other adjustments (basic sliders, curves, LUT) are kept. Resetting bands that are already neutral is a no-op.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `band` | string | no |  | `red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green`, `cyan`, `blue`, `purple`, `magenta`, `all` | Band to reset; omit (or "all") to reset all eight bands. |

**Returns:** {segment} — segment.adjust.hsl without the reset band(s).

Example — Reset every band:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Reset only blue:

```json
{"band":"blue","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### segment.set_adjust

**Set colour adjustments** · MCP tool `segment_set_adjust` · `POST /api/v1/commands/segment.set_adjust` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Adjustment/Basic

Sets colour/light controls of a video or photo clip, or of an adjustment segment (which applies to all tracks below it) — the Adjustment tab → Basic in CapCut. Pass any subset of: brightness, contrast, saturation, exposure, temperature, tint, highlights, shadows, vignette, hue (global hue rotation, -1..1 = -180°..+180°) and shine (local contrast / clarity; negative = soft glow) — each -1..1, 0 = neutral; CapCut's inspector shows them as -100..100 — and sharpen, fade (lifted blacks) and grain (film grain) 0..1, plus an optional .cube LUT with lut_intensity 0..1. Omitted fields keep their value. Fields animated by keyframes (adjust.<field>) record the value as a keyframe at the playhead. Render order: exposure → brightness → contrast → highlights/shadows → temperature/tint → hue + HSL → saturation → curves → fade → LUT → shine → sharpen → vignette → grain. Per-colour-range changes use segment.set_hsl, tone curves segment.set_curves, automatic correction adjustment.auto_enhance; segment.reset_adjust returns everything (incl. HSL and curves) to neutral.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `brightness` | number | no |  | -1 … 1 | Brightness: -1 darker … +1 brighter. |
| `contrast` | number | no |  | -1 … 1 | Contrast: -1 flat … +1 punchy. |
| `exposure` | number | no |  | -1 … 1 | Exposure: -1 under-exposed … +1 over-exposed. |
| `fade` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Fade: lifts the black point for a washed-out film look, 0 off … 1 strong (blacks become dark grey). |
| `grain` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Grain: film grain, 0 off … 1 heavy. Deterministic per picture (a still image never shimmers; video grain moves with the content). |
| `highlights` | number | no |  | -1 … 1 | Highlights: -1 recover bright areas … +1 boost them. |
| `hue` | number | no |  | -1 … 1 | Hue: rotates every colour around the colour wheel, -1 = -180° … +1 = +180° (0.1 ≈ 18°). |
| `lut` | string | no |  |  | Absolute path of a .cube LUT file to apply ("" removes the LUT). lut_intensity defaults to 1 when a LUT is first set. |
| `lut_intensity` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Strength of the LUT 0..1 (only used when lut is set). |
| `saturation` | number | no |  | -1 … 1 | Saturation: -1 greyscale … +1 vivid. |
| `shadows` | number | no |  | -1 … 1 | Shadows: -1 deepen dark areas … +1 lift them. |
| `sharpen` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Sharpen: 0 off … 1 maximum. |
| `shine` | number | no |  | -1 … 1 | Shine: local contrast / clarity, -1 soft and glowy … +1 crisp textures (unsharp mask with a large radius on luminance). |
| `temperature` | number | no |  | -1 … 1 | Temperature: -1 cool/blue … +1 warm/orange. |
| `tint` | number | no |  | -1 … 1 | Tint: -1 green … +1 magenta. |
| `vignette` | number | no |  | -1 … 1 | Vignette: -1 white edges … +1 dark edges. |

**Returns:** {segment, keyframed?} with segment.adjust.

Example — Warm, punchy look:

```json
{"contrast":0.2,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","saturation":0.15,"segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","temperature":0.3}
```

Example — Darken the edges:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","vignette":0.5}
```

Example — Apply a LUT at 70%:

```json
{"lut":"C:/LUTs/film.cube","lut_intensity":0.7,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Faded film look with grain:

```json
{"fade":0.3,"grain":0.4,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","saturation":-0.15,"segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Crisper textures and a slight hue shift:

```json
{"hue":0.05,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","shine":0.4}
```

### segment.set_curves

**Set curves** · MCP tool `segment_set_curves` · `POST /api/v1/commands/segment.set_curves` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Adjustment/Curves

Sets the tone curves of a video/photo clip or adjustment segment — the Curves page of CapCut's Adjustment tab. A curve maps input level x to output level y (both 0..1, 0 = black, 1 = white) through up to 16 control points joined by a smooth monotone cubic (no overshoot: rising points give a rising curve). The master (luma) curve applies to all channels first, then the r, g and b curves. Ways to call it: preset alone replaces every channel with a built-in look (lighten, darken, fade, contrast, cool, warm, vintage; custom = straight lines to edit by hand); channel + points replaces one channel (channel defaults to master); preset + channel + points starts from the preset and then replaces that channel. points is an array of [x, y] pairs or {x, y} objects; they are sorted by x, x values must differ, and the straight line [[0,0],[1,1]] means 'no change'. Examples of shapes: S-curve [[0,0],[0.25,0.18],[0.75,0.82],[1,1]] adds contrast; [[0,0.1],[1,1]] lifts the blacks (matte); a red curve [[0,0],[0.5,0.56],[1,1]] warms the midtones. Curves render after the basic sliders and HSL and before a .cube LUT.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `channel` | string | no |  | `master`, `r`, `g`, `b` | Channel that points apply to: master (luma, all channels), r, g or b. Defaults to master. |
| `points` | array[] | no |  |  | Control points of the channel: 2..16 pairs [x, y] (or {x, y} objects), each 0..1. [[0,0],[1,1]] = identity (clears the channel). |
| `preset` | string | no |  | `custom`, `lighten`, `darken`, `fade`, `contrast`, `cool`, `warm`, `vintage` | Built-in curve set: custom (straight lines), lighten, darken, fade, contrast, cool, warm or vintage. Replaces all four channels. |

**Returns:** {segment} — segment.adjust.curves {preset, master, r, g, b} (omitted when every channel is a straight line).

Example — Vintage preset:

```json
{"preset":"vintage","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Gentle S-curve on the master channel:

```json
{"channel":"master","points":[[0,0],[0.25,0.2],[0.75,0.8],[1,1]],"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Cool the shadows: lift blue at the bottom:

```json
{"channel":"b","points":[[0,0.08],[0.5,0.52],[1,1]],"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Fade preset with a warmer red channel:

```json
{"channel":"r","points":[{"x":0,"y":0.15},{"x":1,"y":1}],"preset":"fade","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### segment.set_hsl

**Set HSL** · MCP tool `segment_set_hsl` · `POST /api/v1/commands/segment.set_hsl` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Adjustment/HSL

Adjusts one colour range of a video/photo clip or adjustment segment — the HSL page of CapCut's Adjustment tab (8 colour dots). Bands: red (0°), orange (30°), yellow (60°), green (120°), cyan (180°), blue (240°), purple (270°), magenta (300°). Each band has h (hue shift: -1 = -30° … +1 = +30° around the colour wheel), s (saturation: -1 = grey, +1 = double) and l (lightness: -1 darker … +1 lighter), all -1..1 with 0 = unchanged. Pixels between two band centres belong to both with smooth weights, so there are no hard edges, and a band never affects hues beyond its neighbours (shifting red does not touch blue). Neutral greys are never changed. Omitted h/s/l keep their value. band "all" writes the given values into every band (e.g. s -1 → black and white). Alternatively pass bands = {red: {h, s, l}, …} to set several bands at once (omitted bands and fields are kept). Use segment.reset_hsl to clear one band or all of them. Typical recipes: bluer sky = blue {s: 0.3, l: -0.2}; greener foliage = yellow {h: 0.4} + green {s: 0.3}; skin = orange {s: -0.1, l: 0.1}.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `band` | string | no |  | `red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green`, `cyan`, `blue`, `purple`, `magenta`, `all` | Colour band to change, or "all" for every band. Required unless bands is given. |
| `bands` | object | no |  |  | Several bands at once: {"blue": {"s": 0.3, "l": -0.2}, "orange": {"l": 0.1}}. Keys are band names, values objects with h/s/l (-1..1). |
| `h` | number | no |  | -1 … 1 | Hue shift of the band, -1..1 (= -30°..+30°; positive moves towards the next band, e.g. red → orange). |
| `l` | number | no |  | -1 … 1 | Lightness of the band, -1..1 (-1 = much darker, 0 = unchanged, +1 = much lighter). |
| `s` | number | no |  | -1 … 1 | Saturation of the band, -1..1 (-1 = fully grey, 0 = unchanged, +1 = twice as saturated). |

**Returns:** {segment} — segment.adjust.hsl holds all eight bands {h, s, l} (omitted when every band is neutral).

Example — Deeper blue sky:

```json
{"band":"blue","l":-0.25,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","s":0.3,"segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Turn reds orange:

```json
{"band":"red","h":0.6,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Keep only reds (everything else grey):

```json
{"bands":{"blue":{"s":-1},"cyan":{"s":-1},"green":{"s":-1},"magenta":{"s":-1},"orange":{"s":-1},"purple":{"s":-1},"yellow":{"s":-1}},"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Desaturate every band by half:

```json
{"band":"all","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","s":-0.5,"segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

## Animation

2 commands: `animation.remove`, `animation.set`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/animation.html

### animation.remove

**Remove animation** · MCP tool `animation_remove` · `POST /api/v1/commands/animation.remove` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Animation/None

Removes the In, Out, Combo or Loop animation of a segment (choosing 'None' in CapCut's Animation tab). kind=all (default) removes every animation. Removing an animation that is not set succeeds without changes.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `kind` | string | no | `"all"` | `in`, `out`, `combo`, `loop`, `all` | Which animation to remove; all removes in, out, combo and loop. |

**Returns:** {segment_id, animations, loop_animation?} after removal.

Example — Remove the out animation:

```json
{"kind":"out","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Remove all animations:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### animation.set

**Set animation** · MCP tool `animation_set` · `POST /api/v1/commands/animation.set` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Animation

Applies an In, Out or Combo animation preset to a video, photo, sticker or text segment — the Animation tab in CapCut (In plays at the start, Out at the end, Combo runs across the clip). id comes from library.list {kind: "animation"} and is kind-qualified ("in_fade", "out_zoom_out", "combo_swing", "loop_pulse"); an id whose prefix names another slot is rejected. Setting a Combo removes In and Out, and setting In or Out removes Combo, like CapCut. duration_us defaults to 0.5 s for in/out and to the whole segment for combo, and is clamped to the segment; when in+out would exceed the segment, the other one is shortened. kind=loop adds a repeating animation (duration = one cycle, default 1 s) that runs for the whole clip on any picture segment (video, photo, sticker, text) and combines with In/Out/Combo.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes |  |  | Animation id from library.list {kind: "animation"}, e.g. "in_fade", "out_slide_left" or "combo_swing". |
| `kind` | string | yes |  | `in`, `out`, `combo`, `loop` | Animation slot: in (start), out (end), combo (whole clip) or loop (repeats for the whole clip). |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `duration_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Animation length; default 500000 for in/out, the segment length for combo, 1000000 for loop. |

**Returns:** {segment_id, animations: {in?, out?, combo?}, loop_animation?}.

Example — Fade in over 1 second:

```json
{"duration_us":1000000,"id":"in_fade","kind":"in","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Zoom out at the end:

```json
{"id":"out_zoom_out","kind":"out","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

## App

3 commands: `app.api.get`, `app.api.set`, `app.version`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/app.html

### app.api.get

**API address** · MCP tool `app_api_get` · `POST /api/v1/commands/app.api.get` · UI: Settings/API

Tells where this Kadr serves its local REST/WebSocket API (the same API kadrctl, kadr-mcp and AI agents use) — Settings → API. Returns the configured host and port, where they come from (source: env = the KADR_ADDR environment variable, settings = settings.json "api" saved by app.api.set, default = 127.0.0.1:7777), the URL clients should use right now, the token file that holds the Bearer token this API accepts, and the endpoint file (<data folder>/api-endpoint.json) that every running Kadr writes so tools find it automatically. listening=false or fallback=true means the configured port was busy: error and hint explain what holds it (another program, or another Kadr) and how to fix it. Read-only; never returns the token itself.

No parameters.

**Returns:** {host, port, url, docs, source env|settings|default, allow_remote, settings{host, port, allow_remote}, env_override?, token_file, endpoint_file, listening, listen_addr, fallback?, mode editor|headless, pid, error?, hint?, warning?}.

Example — Where is the API?:

```json
{}
```

### app.api.set

**Change API address** · MCP tool `app_api_set` · `POST /api/v1/commands/app.api.set` · UI: Settings/API

Changes the port (and optionally the host) of the local API and saves it in settings.json "api" — Settings → API → Port. The editor window moves the API immediately, without a restart: it binds the new port first (if that fails nothing changes and the error says why), then stops the old listener after this response is sent, rewrites <data folder>/api-endpoint.json and publishes app.api.changed. A headless kadr-server also moves live. kadrctl and kadr-mcp follow automatically because they read api-endpoint.json; scripts with a hard-coded address must use the returned url. The token does not change. Ports below 1024 are refused. host 127.0.0.1 (default) or localhost keep the API private to this computer; 0.0.0.0 exposes it to the network (token still required) and needs allow_remote=true. When KADR_ADDR is set it overrides the setting for this process: the value is saved but takes effect only when KADR_ADDR is removed (see warning). Calling it with the current values changes nothing. App setting, not a project edit: not undoable.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allow_remote` | boolean | no |  |  | Confirms exposing the API to other computers when host is 0.0.0.0. Anyone on the network who has the token can then control Kadr. |
| `host` | string | no |  | `127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `0.0.0.0` | Listen host: "127.0.0.1" (default, this computer only), "localhost", or "0.0.0.0" (all network interfaces; requires allow_remote=true). Omit to keep it. |
| `port` | integer (port) | no |  | 1024 … 65535 | TCP port for the API, 1024..65535 (default 7777). Omit to keep the current port. |

**Returns:** Same as app.api.get plus changed (false when nothing changed) and previous_url; warning explains a KADR_ADDR override or the risk of host 0.0.0.0.

Example — Move the API to port 7790:

```json
{"port":7790}
```

Example — Back to the default address:

```json
{"host":"127.0.0.1","port":7777}
```

Example — Expose to the local network (careful):

```json
{"allow_remote":true,"host":"0.0.0.0"}
```

### app.version

**About Kadr** · MCP tool `app_version` · `POST /api/v1/commands/app.version` · UI: Settings/About

Returns information about this Kadr installation — what the About section of Settings shows: the version (semver, e.g. 1.0.0; prerelease=true only for builds such as 1.1.0-beta.1), build details (git revision and time when available), Go version, OS and CPU architecture, the executable path, the data folder (projects, settings.json, api-token), whether it is a portable build, whether FFmpeg was found (path, version and where it came from), the active renderer (GPU adapter and backend, or the CPU fallback) and the GitHub repository used for updates (private: Kadr is distributed by invitation, see update.check). Use it to report bugs or to decide whether update.check / tools.install_ffmpeg are needed. Read-only and offline.

No parameters.

**Returns:** {name, version, prerelease, go_version, os, arch, build{module, vcs.revision?, vcs.time?, vcs.modified?}, executable, data_dir, portable, ffmpeg{found, ffmpeg_path, ffprobe_path, version, source, error}, update_repo, update_channel, update_signing_key, website, releases_url, renderer?{kind gpu|cpu, backend, device, ...}}.

Example — Show version and environment:

```json
{}
```

## Audio

12 commands: `audio.detect_beats`, `audio.extract`, `audio.loudness`, `audio.restore`, `audio.separate`, `audio.voice_effects`, `sfx.add`, `sfx.list`, `tts.from_text`, `tts.set_api_key`, `tts.speak`, `tts.voices`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/audio.html

### audio.detect_beats

**Detect beats** · MCP tool `audio_detect_beats` · `POST /api/v1/commands/audio.detect_beats` · undoable · UI: Toolbar/Beat

Finds the beats/onsets (drum hits, note attacks) of an audio clip or of a video clip's sound, like CapCut's auto Beat feature, and returns their times on the TIMELINE in microseconds (speed and reverse of the segment are taken into account; only beats inside the segment's timeline range are returned). The source range is decoded to mono 11025 Hz and analysed in pure Go: spectral flux of the log-magnitude spectrum (512-sample window, 11.6 ms hop), adaptive threshold (local mean + delta) with peak picking, then each beat is refined in the time domain to the attack sample (typically within a few milliseconds). bpm is a rough tempo from the median beat interval. With add_markers=true a timeline marker labelled "Beat" is added at every beat (existing markers within 10 ms are kept, not duplicated) so clips can be snapped to the music. At most the first 20 minutes of the clip are analysed. Without add_markers the project is unchanged (note: the call is still recorded as an undo step).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id. |
| `add_markers` | boolean | no | `false` |  | When true, add a timeline marker (label "Beat") at every detected beat. |
| `sensitivity` | number | no | `0.5` | 0 … 1 | 0..1. Higher finds weaker onsets and allows beats closer together (min gap 80 ms at 1, 250 ms at 0). 0.5 suits most music; use 0.7-0.9 for busy percussion, 0.2-0.4 to keep only strong downbeats. |

**Returns:** {segment_id, beats_us[] (timeline µs, ascending), strengths[] (0..1 per beat), count, bpm (0 when fewer than 4 beats), sensitivity, markers_added, analyzed_us}.

Example — List beats of a music clip:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_0a1b2c3d4e5f"}
```

Example — Mark beats on the timeline:

```json
{"add_markers":true,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_0a1b2c3d4e5f","sensitivity":0.7}
```

### audio.extract

**Extract audio** · MCP tool `audio_extract` · `POST /api/v1/commands/audio.extract` · undoable · UI: Timeline/Context menu/Extract audio

CapCut's "Extract audio": separates the sound of a video clip into its own audio clip. A new segment with the same material, source range, timeline range, speed (incl. keep_pitch/curve), reverse flag, volume, fades, volume keyframes, voice effect, noise reduction and loudness normalisation is placed on the first unlocked audio track that is free at that time range (a new audio track is created otherwise). The video segment is muted (volume 0, its volume keyframes move to the audio clip) and both segments are linked with a shared link_group so they move/trim together while timeline linkage is on (an existing link_group of the video segment is reused). Works on video clips on the main or overlay tracks whose material has an audio stream; fails with invalid_argument for photos, freeze frames or silent videos, and with conflict when the clip's track is locked or its audio was already extracted.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id. |

**Returns:** {video_segment_id, audio_segment_id, audio_track_id, created_track, link_group}.

Example — Separate the sound of a clip:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_0a1b2c3d4e5f"}
```

### audio.loudness

**Measure loudness** · MCP tool `audio_loudness` · `POST /api/v1/commands/audio.loudness` · UI: Inspector/Audio/Basic

Measures the loudness of a clip's sound over its source range with ffmpeg's ebur128 filter (EBU R128 / ITU-R BS.1770-4: K-weighted, gated integrated loudness in LUFS, loudness range in LU and true peak in dBFS; mono sources are measured as dual-mono because they play on both channels). Speed, reverse and voice effects are not applied to the measurement. Also reports the clip volume in dB, the gain that "Normalize loudness" applies (brings the clip to target_lufs = -14 LUFS, but never lifts the true peak above -1 dBTP; limited to -30..+20 dB) and effective_lufs = integrated + volume_db (+ normalize gain when enabled). Silence reports -70 LUFS / -144 dBFS. Useful for AI agents balancing music against voice-over: e.g. keep background music ~10-15 LU below speech. Results are cached per file and range.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id. |

**Returns:** {segment_id, integrated_lufs, loudness_range_lu, true_peak_dbfs, volume_db, normalize_gain_db, normalize_enabled, effective_lufs, target_lufs, source_start_us, source_duration_us, method}.

Example — Measure a voice-over clip:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_0a1b2c3d4e5f"}
```

### audio.restore

**Restore audio** · MCP tool `audio_restore` · `POST /api/v1/commands/audio.restore` · undoable · UI: Timeline/Context menu/Restore audio

Undoes a separation at any later time (CapCut's "Restore audio"): deletes the audio clip that audio.separate / audio.extract created from a video clip and gives the video its sound back. Pass EITHER segment of the pair: the video clip (main/overlay track) or the separated audio clip (same material and link_group on an audio track). The video gets the audio clip's current volume, fades, volume keyframes, voice effect, noise reduction and loudness normalisation, so it sounds as before; trims or moves made to the audio clip alone are dropped (the video plays its own source range). If the separated audio was split, every piece is removed. An audio track left empty is deleted, and the link_group is cleared when no other clip remains linked. Fails with invalid_argument when the clip has no separated audio, and with conflict when one of the tracks is locked.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id. |

**Returns:** {video_segment_id, removed_segment_ids[], removed_track_ids[], volume_db (restored video volume, -144 = muted), link_group}.

Example — Put the sound back into a video clip:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_0a1b2c3d4e5f"}
```

### audio.separate

**Separate audio** · MCP tool `audio_separate` · `POST /api/v1/commands/audio.separate` · undoable · hotkey Ctrl+Shift+S · UI: Timeline/Context menu/Separate audio

CapCut's "Separate audio" (Ctrl+Shift+S): moves the sound of a video clip into its own audio clip on an audio track, exactly like audio.extract. The new audio segment copies the material, source and timeline range, speed (incl. keep_pitch/curve), reverse, volume, fades, volume keyframes, voice effect, noise reduction and loudness normalisation; it goes on the first unlocked audio track that is free at that time (a new audio track otherwise). The video clip is muted (volume 0) and both clips share a link_group, so they move/trim/delete together while timeline linkage is on. Undo it with edit.undo, or later with audio.restore (puts the sound back into the video). Fails with invalid_argument for photos, freeze frames, non-video clips and videos without an audio stream, and with conflict when the track is locked or the sound was already separated.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id. |

**Returns:** {video_segment_id, audio_segment_id, audio_track_id, created_track, link_group}.

Example — Separate the sound of the selected clip:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_0a1b2c3d4e5f"}
```

### audio.voice_effects

**List voice effects** · MCP tool `audio_voice_effects` · `POST /api/v1/commands/audio.voice_effects` · UI: Inspector/Audio/Voice changer

Lists the built-in voice changer presets (Audio inspector → Voice changer): id, display name, category (Character, Space, Device, Fun, Studio) and what each sounds like (25 presets: pitch, reverbs, radios, ring modulation, whisper, studio enhancement...). Apply one with segment.set_audio{segment_id, voice_effect: <id>}; an empty voice_effect removes it. Effects are rendered with ffmpeg filters during preview and export and keep the clip's timing (pitch effects use pitch-shift + tempo correction).

No parameters.

**Returns:** Array of {id, name, category, description}.

Example — List voice effects:

```json
{}
```

### sfx.add

**Add sound effect** · MCP tool `sfx_add` · `POST /api/v1/commands/sfx.add` · undoable · UI: Library/Audio/Sound effects

Adds a built-in sound effect to the timeline as an audio clip — the "+" button (or drag) of a sound effect in the Audio panel. The effect's WAV is synthesised once into the library folder (<DataDir>/library/sfx/<id>.wav), imported as a material named after the effect (the same material is reused when the effect is added again) and placed at at_us (default: the playhead) on the first audio track that is free for its whole length; a new audio track is created when all are busy (or next to track_id when that track is busy). The clip keeps the effect's full length; trim, fade or change its volume afterwards with the usual segment commands. Typical use: whoosh on a cut, pop when a sticker appears, ding on a key point, riser that ENDS at a drop (at_us = drop_us - duration_us).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `sfx_id` | string | yes |  |  | Sound effect id from sfx.list (e.g. "whoosh_soft", "pop_bubble", "ding"). |
| `at_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Timeline time where the effect starts (1 second = 1000000). Defaults to the playhead. |
| `track_id` | string | no |  |  | Audio track to place it on. Omit to use the first free audio track (or a new one). |

**Returns:** {segment_id, track_id, material_id, sfx_id, name, start_us, duration_us}.

Example — Whoosh at 2 s:

```json
{"at_us":2000000,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","sfx_id":"whoosh_soft"}
```

Example — Pop at the playhead:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","sfx_id":"pop_bubble"}
```

### sfx.list

**List sound effects** · MCP tool `sfx_list` · `POST /api/v1/commands/sfx.list` · UI: Library/Audio/Sound effects

Lists Kadr's built-in sound effects (left panel → Audio → Sound effects), like CapCut's sound-effect library but entirely ORIGINAL: every effect is synthesised by the engine (no recordings). Categories: Popular, Transition (whooshes, swishes, risers, downlifter, glitch), UI (clicks, pops, ding, chimes, typing), Impact (booms, hits, punch, thud, metal, snare), Magic (sparkle, shimmer, chimes), Camera (shutter, flash, film), Countdown (tick, 3-2-1 beeps, buzzer), Cartoon & Game (boing, slide whistle, coin, laser, power-up, cash register) and Ambience (room tone, wind, pad, rain — quieter 6 s beds). Each item has an id for sfx.add, a name, categories, a description of how it sounds, its exact duration in µs, a 48-column waveform overview (peaks 0..1) and a preview path (GET it with the API token to play the WAV).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `category` | string | no |  |  | Only effects in this category (case-insensitive), e.g. "Transition", "Impact", "Popular". The result's categories lists all. |
| `query` | string | no |  |  | Case-insensitive search on id, name, category and description, e.g. "whoosh", "beep", "camera". |

**Returns:** {categories: [tab names in display order], total, items: [{id, name, category, categories, description, duration_us, channels, peak_db, peaks[48], preview, thumbnail}]}.

Example — All sound effects:

```json
{}
```

Example — Search whooshes:

```json
{"query":"whoosh"}
```

Example — Impact category:

```json
{"category":"Impact"}
```

### tts.from_text

**Speak text clip** · MCP tool `tts_from_text` · `POST /api/v1/commands/tts.from_text` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Text/Text to speech

Reads a text segment aloud (CapCut's Text → Text to speech): speaks the segment's content with a local voice and places the speech as an audio clip starting exactly at the text's start, on the first free audio track. The text and the speech are linked (shared link_group) so they move together. Running it again on the same text REPLACES its previous speech (handy after editing the words or changing the voice). sync_duration=true is CapCut's "sync text and speech": the text segment is stretched or shortened to the length of the speech (never overlapping the next clip on its track — then clamped=true). Fails with invalid_argument for non-text or empty segments, conflict for locked tracks, not_available without a speech engine.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of a text segment (on a text track) whose content is spoken. Get it from project.get or timeline.get. |
| `rate` | number | no | `1` | 0.5 … 2 | Speaking speed multiplier: 1 = the voice's normal speed, 0.5 = half as fast, 2 = twice as fast. |
| `sync_duration` | boolean | no | `false` |  | When true, set the text segment's duration to the length of the speech. |
| `voice` | string | no |  |  | Voice to use: an id from tts.voices (e.g. "sapi:Microsoft Zira Desktop", "espeak:en-us"), a voice name, a language code ("en-US", "de", "ru" — picks a voice of that language) or part of a name ("zira"). Omit for the default voice (an English system voice when installed). |

**Returns:** {segment_id (the new audio clip), track_id, material_id, start_us, duration_us, voice, provider, path, cached, text_segment_id, text_duration_us, synced, clamped, link_group, replaced_segment_ids[]}.

Example — Read a title aloud:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_0a1b2c3d4e5f"}
```

Example — Read and fit the text to the speech:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_0a1b2c3d4e5f","sync_duration":true,"voice":"en-US"}
```

### tts.set_api_key

**Set cloud voice API key** · MCP tool `tts_set_api_key` · `POST /api/v1/commands/tts.set_api_key`

Stores (or clears) the API key of an optional cloud speech provider so tts.voices / tts.speak / tts.from_text can use its voices next to the local engines. Supported provider: "elevenlabs" (natural multilingual voices; voice ids look like "elevenlabs:<voice_id>"). The key is saved only on this computer in the Kadr data folder (elevenlabs.key) — it is never returned by any command, never written to projects and only sent to the provider's own API. Text you synthesise is sent to the provider. The voice list is refreshed after saving and the result reports whether the key works.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `provider` | string | yes |  | `elevenlabs` | Cloud speech provider. |
| `api_key` | string | no |  |  | The provider API key (e.g. ElevenLabs keys start with "sk_"). Omit with clear=true to remove the stored key. |
| `clear` | boolean | no |  |  | true removes the stored key. |

**Returns:** {provider, stored: bool, working: bool, voices: count, error?} — the key itself is never echoed.

Example — Use ElevenLabs voices:

```json
{"api_key":"sk_your_key_here","provider":"elevenlabs"}
```

### tts.speak

**Text to speech** · MCP tool `tts_speak` · `POST /api/v1/commands/tts.speak` · undoable · UI: Library/Audio/Text to speech

Speaks text with a local voice and adds the speech to the timeline as a new audio clip (CapCut's Text to speech → Add to timeline). The speech is rendered by the selected engine (Windows SAPI, eSpeak NG or macOS say — see tts.voices), trimmed of leading/trailing silence, loudness-normalised to about -16 LUFS (peaks <= -1.5 dBTP, so voice-overs from every engine sound equally loud) and saved as a 48 kHz WAV in the project's cache (cache/tts/); the file is imported as a material named "Speech: <text>" and placed at at_us on the first free audio track (a new audio track when all are busy, or on track_id). The same text, voice and rate reuse the cached file. Up to 5000 characters per call; for narration split long scripts into sentences or paragraphs. Fails with not_available when no speech engine is installed (the hint explains what to install) and not_found for an unknown voice.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `text` | string | yes |  |  | What to say (plain text, up to 5000 characters). |
| `at_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Timeline time where the speech starts (1 second = 1000000). Defaults to the playhead. |
| `rate` | number | no | `1` | 0.5 … 2 | Speaking speed multiplier: 1 = the voice's normal speed, 0.5 = half as fast, 2 = twice as fast. |
| `track_id` | string | no |  |  | Audio track to put the clip on; when it is busy at that time a new audio track is created next to it. Omit to use the first free audio track. |
| `voice` | string | no |  |  | Voice to use: an id from tts.voices (e.g. "sapi:Microsoft Zira Desktop", "espeak:en-us"), a voice name, a language code ("en-US", "de", "ru" — picks a voice of that language) or part of a name ("zira"). Omit for the default voice (an English system voice when installed). |

**Returns:** {segment_id, track_id, material_id, start_us, duration_us, voice (voice id used), provider, path, cached}.

Example — Say a line at the playhead:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","text":"Welcome to my channel!"}
```

Example — Slower German narration at 2 s:

```json
{"at_us":2000000,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","rate":0.9,"text":"Guten Morgen","voice":"de"}
```

### tts.voices

**List text-to-speech voices** · MCP tool `tts_voices` · `POST /api/v1/commands/tts.voices` · UI: Library/Audio/Text to speech

Lists the speech voices installed on this computer that tts.speak and tts.from_text can use, like the voice picker of CapCut's Text to speech (local engines send nothing online; the optional ElevenLabs cloud provider is used only after tts.set_api_key): Windows SAPI desktop voices (via PowerShell System.Speech, e.g. "Microsoft Zira Desktop"), eSpeak NG voices (~130 languages, robotic but universal) and macOS `say` voices. Each voice has an id "<provider>:<name>", a display name, a language code and a gender when known. providers[] tells which engines are available and why the others are not; default_voice is what is used when voice is omitted. The list is cached for 10 minutes; refresh=true re-detects (e.g. after installing a voice).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `refresh` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Re-detect engines and voices instead of using the cached list. |

**Returns:** {voices: [{id, provider, name, language, gender}], default_voice (voice id or "" when none), providers: [{id, name, available, voices, error}]}.

Example — List voices:

```json
{}
```

Example — Re-detect voices:

```json
{"refresh":true}
```

## Audio properties

3 commands: `segment.set_audio`, `segment.set_fade`, `segment.set_volume`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/audio-properties.html

### segment.set_audio

**Set audio options** · MCP tool `segment_set_audio` · `POST /api/v1/commands/segment.set_audio` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Audio

Sets the sound processing options of an audio segment or video clip: voice_effect is a voice changer preset (Audio → Voice changer in CapCut; "" or "none" removes it): chipmunk, deep, monster, robot, pitch_up, pitch_down, whisper, echo, reverb, underwater, small_room, cathedral, stadium, megaphone, telephone, lofi, radio_am, walkie_talkie, bitcrush, vibrato, tremble, alien_ring, vocal_enhance, bass_boost, chorus_wide. reduce_noise toggles CapCut's Reduce noise, normalize_loudness toggles Normalize loudness (evens out the clip's perceived loudness). Only supplied fields change.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `normalize_loudness` | boolean | no |  |  | Normalise the clip to a standard loudness level. |
| `reduce_noise` | boolean | no |  |  | Remove steady background noise (hiss, hum, wind). |
| `voice_effect` | string | no |  |  | Voice changer id, e.g. "robot" or "chipmunk" (full list in the description; also library.list {kind: "voice_effect"}); "none" or "" removes the effect. |

**Returns:** {segment} with voice_effect / reduce_noise / normalize_loudness.

Example — Clean up a voice-over:

```json
{"normalize_loudness":true,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","reduce_noise":true,"segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Robot voice:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","voice_effect":"robot"}
```

### segment.set_fade

**Set audio fades** · MCP tool `segment_set_fade` · `POST /api/v1/commands/segment.set_fade` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Audio/Basic/Fade

Sets the audio fade-in and fade-out lengths of an audio segment or video clip — Audio → Basic → Fade in / Fade out in CapCut. Each fade is clamped to half of the segment's timeline duration (the result reports the applied values in a note when clamping happened); 0 removes the fade. Only supplied fields change. Fades are re-clamped automatically when the segment gets shorter (speed change, trim).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `fade_in_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Fade-in length from silence at the segment start (0 = none). 1000000 = 1 second. |
| `fade_out_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Fade-out length to silence at the segment end (0 = none). |

**Returns:** {segment, note?} with segment.fade_in_us / fade_out_us.

Example — 1 s fade in and 2 s fade out:

```json
{"fade_in_us":1000000,"fade_out_us":2000000,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Remove the fade-out:

```json
{"fade_out_us":0,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### segment.set_volume

**Set volume** · MCP tool `segment_set_volume` · `POST /api/v1/commands/segment.set_volume` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Audio/Basic/Volume

Sets the loudness of an audio segment or of a video clip's own sound — Audio → Basic → Volume in CapCut. volume_db is in decibels relative to the original: 0 = unchanged, -6 ≈ half as loud, +6 ≈ twice, -60 (the bottom of the slider) = muted, max +20. It is stored as linear gain in segment.volume (gain = 10^(dB/20)). If volume is animated by keyframes the value becomes a keyframe at the playhead. Photos, text, stickers, effects and filters have no sound and are rejected. Track-level mute is timeline.track.set {muted}.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `volume_db` | number (decibels) | yes |  | -60 … 20 | Gain in dB: 0 = original loudness, negative = quieter, positive = louder, -60 = mute. |

**Returns:** {segment, keyframed?} — segment.volume holds the linear gain.

Example — Lower background music by 12 dB:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","volume_db":-12}
```

Example — Mute a clip's own sound:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","volume_db":-60}
```

## Captions

16 commands: `captions.add`, `captions.asr_status`, `captions.auto`, `captions.cancel`, `captions.delete`, `captions.export`, `captions.from_transcript`, `captions.import`, `captions.list`, `captions.merge`, `captions.relayout`, `captions.set_style`, `captions.shift`, `captions.split`, `captions.status`, `captions.update`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/captions.html

### captions.add

**Add caption** · MCP tool `captions_add` · `POST /api/v1/commands/captions.add` · undoable · UI: Library/Captions/Manual captions

Adds a caption cue typed by hand (CapCut's Manual captions) on the caption track at at_us (default: the playhead). It takes the look and position of the existing captions on that track (or style_id, or the default style) and gets estimated word timings so highlight styles work. When the next cue starts earlier than at_us + duration_us the new cue is shortened to fit; starting inside an existing cue is a conflict.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `text` | string | yes |  |  | Caption text; \n breaks lines. |
| `at_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Start on the timeline (default: the playhead). |
| `duration_us` | integer (microseconds) | no | `2000000` | 100000 … 60000000 | Length of the cue (default 2 s). |
| `style_id` | string | no |  |  | Caption style id from library.list kind=caption_style, e.g. cap_clean, cap_highlight_word, cap_karaoke_bar, cap_pop_word, cap_box_dark. |
| `track_id` | string | no |  |  | Text track (default: the first caption track, created when missing). |

**Returns:** {segment_id, track_id, cue: {segment_id, track_id, index, start_us, end_us, text, style_id, words}}.

Example — Add a caption at 5 s:

```json
{"at_us":5000000,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","text":"Welcome back!"}
```

### captions.asr_status

**Speech recognition status** · MCP tool `captions_asr_status` · `POST /api/v1/commands/captions.asr_status`

Reports whether local speech recognition (auto captions, transcripts) works on this computer: the Python interpreter found (KADR_PYTHON overrides it), the faster-whisper version, whether an NVIDIA GPU is usable, which Whisper models are downloaded (tiny, base, small, medium, large-v3 — Kadr never downloads models itself), plus the list of recognisable languages and the defaults. When unavailable, code/message/hint explain what to install. The first call takes a few seconds (it starts Python); the answer is cached.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `refresh` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Probe again instead of using the cached answer (after installing something). |

**Returns:** {available, engine, python, python_version, version, cuda, models: {tiny: true, …}, code?, message?, hint?, default_model, models_list, devices, languages: [{code, name}]}.

Example — Check:

```json
{}
```

Example — Re-check after installing:

```json
{"refresh":true}
```

### captions.auto

**Auto captions** · MCP tool `captions_auto` · `POST /api/v1/commands/captions.auto` · UI: Library/Captions/Auto captions

Generates captions from the speech in the timeline, like CapCut's Captions → Auto captions → Generate, but fully offline: the sound of every audible clip (main track, overlays and audio tracks; muted tracks and clips with volume 0 are skipped — or only segment_ids) is recognised locally with Whisper (faster-whisper in a Python subprocess, word-level timestamps), the words are stored on each material as its transcript (source time, reused next time — see transcript.get) and turned into caption cues on a text track named "Captions": at most max_lines lines of max_chars characters, split at sentences, commas and pauses, each cue carrying per-word timings (TextStyle.words, relative to the cue start) so word-highlight caption styles animate. Existing cues on the Captions track over the transcribed clips are replaced (replace=false adds a second track). Recognition runs as a background job: the call returns {job_id, state…} at once; follow captions.progress events or poll captions.status {job_id} (or pass wait=true to block until done — fine for clips of a few minutes). Creating the cues is ONE undo step ("Create captions from transcript"); transcripts themselves are analysis data and are not undone. Errors not_available (code "not_available") when Python/faster-whisper/the model is missing — see captions.asr_status. Typical speed: small model ≈ 5× real time on an NVIDIA GPU, ≈ 1× on a CPU.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `device` | string | no | `"auto"` | `auto`, `cuda`, `cpu` | Where recognition runs: auto (CUDA GPU when usable, else CPU int8), cuda or cpu. A failing GPU falls back to the CPU. |
| `force` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Transcribe again even when the material already has a transcript (e.g. to use a bigger model). |
| `language` | string | no | `"auto"` |  | Spoken language: "auto" (detect, default) or a code/name such as en, uk, es, de, fr, pt, ru, zh, ja, ko, ar, hi, it, nl, pl, tr, vi, th, id, ms, bn, my, ro, tl (Filipino). Locales ("en-US") and English names ("Ukrainian") are accepted. captions.asr_status lists all ~100 languages. |
| `max_chars` | integer | no |  | 8 … 80 | Characters per line (default from the style, 42 for cap_clean; reduced automatically on portrait canvases). |
| `max_lines` | integer | no |  | 1 … 4 | Lines per caption (default 2, from the style). |
| `max_words` | integer | no |  | 0 … 50 | Words per caption; 0 = no limit, 1 = one word at a time (default from the style). |
| `model` | string | no | `"small"` | `tiny`, `base`, `small`, `medium`, `large-v3` | Whisper model size: tiny (fastest, least accurate), base, small (default: good accuracy, ~1× real time on a CPU, ~5× faster on an NVIDIA GPU), medium, large-v3 (best, slow without a GPU). Only models already downloaded can be used. |
| `prompt` | string | no |  |  | Optional hint text for the recogniser: names, jargon or spelling to prefer (e.g. "Kadr, CapCut, Kyiv"). |
| `replace` | boolean | no | `true` |  | Replace existing cues on the Captions track over the captioned clips (default). false keeps them and puts the new captions on a new track. |
| `segment_id` | string | no |  |  | Shortcut for a single clip (same as segment_ids with one id). |
| `segment_ids` | string[] | no |  |  | Only caption these clips (ids of video/audio clips with sound). Omit to caption every audible clip. |
| `style_id` | string | no |  |  | Caption style from library.list kind=caption_style, e.g. "cap_highlight_word" (default: the style of the existing captions, else "cap_clean"). |
| `wait` | boolean | no | `false` |  | true = block until the job finishes and return its final status (with the result); false (default) = return the job right away and report progress through captions.progress events / captions.status. |

**Returns:** Job status {job_id, project_id, kind: "captions", state: queued|running|done|failed|cancelled, phase, progress 0..1, material_ids (being transcribed), language, detected_languages, model, device, media_s, elapsed_s, error?, result?}. When done, result = captions.from_transcript's result {track_id, count, segment_ids, words, languages, removed, transcribed: [{material_id, language, words, text}]}.

Example — Caption the whole timeline (background job):

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Ukrainian speech, wait for the result:

```json
{"language":"uk","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","wait":true}
```

Example — One clip, word-highlight style, fast model:

```json
{"model":"base","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_ids":["seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"],"style_id":"cap_highlight_word"}
```

### captions.cancel

**Cancel auto captions** · MCP tool `captions_cancel` · `POST /api/v1/commands/captions.cancel`

Stops a running or queued captions.auto / transcript.transcribe job: the recognition process is killed, nothing is written to the project (transcripts already saved for other materials stay). Cancelling a finished job does nothing and returns its final status.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `job_id` | string | yes |  |  | Job id returned by captions.auto or transcript.transcribe. |

**Returns:** The job status (state "cancelled" unless it had already finished).

Example — Cancel:

```json
{"job_id":"cap_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### captions.delete

**Delete captions** · MCP tool `captions_delete` · `POST /api/v1/commands/captions.delete` · undoable

Deletes caption cues (no ripple: the video is not changed — use transcript.delete_words to cut speech). Pass segment_id / segment_ids, or all=true to clear every caption track (or only track_id). Caption tracks left empty are removed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `all` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Delete every cue of every caption track (or of track_id). |
| `segment_id` | string | no |  |  | Cue to delete. |
| `segment_ids` | string[] | no |  |  | Several cues to delete. |
| `track_id` | string | no |  |  | With all=true: only this text track. |

**Returns:** {deleted: [segment ids], count}.

Example — Delete one cue:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Remove all captions:

```json
{"all":true,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### captions.export

**Download captions** · MCP tool `captions_export` · `POST /api/v1/commands/captions.export` · UI: Library/Captions/Download captions

Exports the captions (CapCut's Download captions): SubRip (srt), WebVTT (vtt), plain text (txt — one cue per line, a transcript) or LRC lyrics (lrc). By default the cues of every caption track are exported in timeline order; when the project has no caption track, every text segment is. Pass track_id for one text track. With path the file is written (folders are created, existing files overwritten); without path the text is returned in content. The project is not modified.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `format` | string | no | `"srt"` | `srt`, `vtt`, `txt`, `lrc` | srt (default), vtt, txt or lrc. |
| `path` | string | no |  |  | Absolute path of the file to write, e.g. C:\Users\me\Videos\captions.srt. Omit to get the text back. |
| `track_id` | string | no |  |  | Only export this text track. |

**Returns:** {format, count, path? (when written), content? (when path is omitted)}.

Example — Save an SRT:

```json
{"path":"C:\\Users\\me\\Videos\\captions.srt","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Transcript as text:

```json
{"format":"txt","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### captions.from_transcript

**Create captions from transcript** · MCP tool `captions_from_transcript` · `POST /api/v1/commands/captions.from_transcript` · undoable · UI: Library/Captions/Create from transcript

Creates caption cues from the transcripts already stored on the materials (made by captions.auto or transcript.transcribe) without running speech recognition again — e.g. after editing the video, or to re-caption with other line rules. Words heard in the chosen clips (or every audible clip) are mapped to timeline time (speed, speed curves and reverse are honoured) and grouped into cues: a new cue starts after a pause of 0.7 s, after a sentence, or when max_lines × max_chars would overflow (preferring a comma in the second half); lines are balanced. Each cue is a text segment on the "Captions" track with text.words = per-word timings relative to the cue start (for word-highlight styles). With replace=true (default) existing cues on the caption track over those clips are removed first, and when style_id is omitted the look and position of the existing captions are kept. One undo step.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `max_chars` | integer | no |  | 8 … 80 | Characters per line (default from the style; 42 for cap_clean, fewer on portrait canvases). |
| `max_lines` | integer | no |  | 1 … 4 | Lines per cue (default from the style, usually 2). |
| `max_words` | integer | no |  | 0 … 50 | Words per cue; 0 = no limit, 1 = one word at a time (default from the style). |
| `replace` | boolean | no | `true` |  | Remove existing cues that overlap the captioned clips (default true). false = a new caption track. |
| `segment_ids` | string[] | no |  |  | Clips to caption (default: every audible clip whose material has a transcript). |
| `style_id` | string | no |  |  | Caption style id from library.list kind=caption_style, e.g. cap_clean, cap_highlight_word, cap_karaoke_bar, cap_pop_word, cap_box_dark. |
| `track_id` | string | no |  |  | Text track to fill (default: the existing Captions track, or a new one). |

**Returns:** {track_id, count, segment_ids (new cues), words, languages, style_id, removed (old cues removed), untranscribed_segment_ids}.

Example — Re-create captions:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — One word at a time:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","style_id":"cap_pop_word"}
```

### captions.import

**Import caption file** · MCP tool `captions_import` · `POST /api/v1/commands/captions.import` · undoable · UI: Library/Captions/Upload caption file

Imports a subtitle file as caption cues (CapCut's Upload caption file): SubRip .srt, WebVTT .vtt, Advanced SubStation .ass/.ssa (Dialogue lines; override tags stripped, \N = line break) or LRC lyrics .lrc ([mm:ss.xx] lines, [offset:], enhanced <mm:ss.xx> word tags become word timings). The format comes from the extension (or format). Cues go to a new "Captions" text track (or track_id / the existing caption track with replace=true) in the chosen caption style, shifted by offset_us; overlapping cues are trimmed. Without word timings in the file they are estimated from the text so word-highlight styles work. One undo step.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | yes |  |  | Absolute path of the subtitle file (UTF-8). |
