| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `estimate_words` | boolean | no | `true` |  | Give cues without word timings estimated ones (proportional to word length). |
| `format` | string | no |  | `srt`, `vtt`, `ass`, `lrc` | srt, vtt, ass or lrc (default: from the file extension / content). |
| `offset_us` | integer (microseconds) | no | `0` |  | Shift every cue by this much (negative = earlier; cues ending before 0 are dropped). |
| `replace` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Clear the target caption track (track_id or the existing Captions track) first. |
| `style_id` | string | no |  |  | Caption style (default "cap_clean"). |
| `track_id` | string | no |  |  | Text track to fill; it must be free where the cues go unless replace=true. |

**Returns:** {track_id, count, segment_ids, skipped (cues before 0), format}.

Example — Import an SRT:

```json
{"path":"C:\\Users\\me\\Videos\\talk.srt","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Lyrics as karaoke:

```json
{"path":"/home/me/song.lrc","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","style_id":"cap_karaoke_bar"}
```

### captions.list

**List captions** · MCP tool `captions_list` · `POST /api/v1/commands/captions.list` · UI: Library/Captions

Lists the caption cues — the caption editor's list: every text segment on caption tracks (text tracks named "Captions…", created by captions.auto / captions.import / captions.import_srt) in timeline order, with text, start/end, the caption style and the word timings (relative to the cue start). Pass track_id to list any text track. Use the segment ids with captions.update / split / merge / delete / set_style.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `include_words` | boolean | no | `true` |  | Include per-word timings (false = smaller answer). |
| `track_id` | string | no |  |  | List this text track only (default: all caption tracks). |

**Returns:** {tracks: [{track_id, name, count, locked}], count, cues: [{segment_id, track_id, index, start_us, end_us, text, style_id?, words?: [{text, start_us, end_us}]}]}.

Example — All captions:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Text only:

```json
{"include_words":false,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### captions.merge

**Merge captions** · MCP tool `captions_merge` · `POST /api/v1/commands/captions.merge` · undoable

Joins caption cues into one — Delete at the start of a cue in the caption editor merges it with the previous one. Pass segment_id with direction (next = merge with the following cue, previous = with the preceding one) or segment_ids (two or more cues of the same track). The result spans from the first start to the last end, keeps the first cue's look, joins the texts (re-wrapped into balanced lines) and keeps every word timing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `direction` | string | no | `"next"` | `next`, `previous` | Which neighbour segment_id merges with. |
| `segment_id` | string | no |  |  | Cue to merge with its neighbour (see direction). |
| `segment_ids` | string[] | no |  |  | Alternatively: the cues to merge (same track; everything between them is merged too). |

**Returns:** The merged cue {segment_id, track_id, index, start_us, end_us, text, style_id, words}.

Example — Merge with the next cue:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Merge two cues:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_ids":["seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","seg_6f5e4d3c2b1a"]}
```

### captions.relayout

**Re-split captions** · MCP tool `captions_relayout` · `POST /api/v1/commands/captions.relayout` · undoable

Re-splits caption cues from their word timings with new line rules — characters per line, lines per cue and words per cue (e.g. max_words=3 for punchy short captions, max_chars=32 for narrow vertical video). Cues are regrouped at pauses and sentence ends exactly like auto captions; their look and position are kept. Cues without word timings are left alone. Omitted rules come from each track's caption style.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `max_chars` | integer | no |  | 8 … 80 | Characters per line. |
| `max_lines` | integer | no |  | 1 … 4 | Lines per cue. |
| `max_words` | integer | no |  | 0 … 50 | Words per cue (0 = no limit). |
| `track_id` | string | no |  |  | Only this text track (default: every caption track). |

**Returns:** {count: cues after the change, segment_ids}.

Example — Three words per caption:

```json
{"max_words":3,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Short single lines:

```json
{"max_chars":24,"max_lines":1,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### captions.set_style

**Apply caption style** · MCP tool `captions_set_style` · `POST /api/v1/commands/captions.set_style` · undoable · UI: Library/Captions/Styles

Applies a caption style (library.list kind=caption_style) to every cue of every caption track, or to track_id / segment_ids — like picking a style in CapCut's caption panel. The look (font, size, colours, outline, shadow, box, glow, gradient, letter case and the active-word highlight: color, box/pill, scale, underline, karaoke, pop, bounce, reveal, dim, glow, sweep_line or slide_box) is replaced; text and word timings are kept; cues move to the style's vertical position unless keep_position=true. Styles that show a fixed number of words at a time (cap_pop_word = 1, cap_sunset_gradient = 3) re-split the cues from their word timings (relayout); switching back to a normal style re-joins them. The highlight is drawn by the text renderer from text.words + text.highlight.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `style_id` | string | yes |  |  | Caption style id from library.list kind=caption_style, e.g. cap_clean, cap_highlight_word, cap_karaoke_bar, cap_pop_word, cap_box_dark. |
| `keep_position` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Keep each cue's current position instead of the style's. |
| `relayout` | boolean | no |  |  | Force (true) or prevent (false) re-splitting the cues with the style's line rules. Default: only when the words-per-cue rule changes. |
| `segment_ids` | string[] | no |  |  | Only these cues. |
| `track_id` | string | no |  |  | Only the cues of this text track. |

**Returns:** {style_id, count (cues styled), relayout: bool, segment_ids (cue ids after the change)}.

Example — Highlight the spoken word:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","style_id":"cap_highlight_word"}
```

Example — Karaoke on one track:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","style_id":"cap_karaoke_bar","track_id":"trk_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### captions.shift

**Shift captions** · MCP tool `captions_shift` · `POST /api/v1/commands/captions.shift` · undoable

Moves caption cues in time by offset_us (negative = earlier) to fix out-of-sync subtitles: every cue of every caption track by default, or only segment_ids, or the cues of track_id, optionally only those starting at or after from_us. Word timings move with their cues. Cues may not start before 0 or overlap cues that stay in place (conflict).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `offset_us` | integer (microseconds) | yes |  |  | How far to move (e.g. 500000 = half a second later, -250000 = a quarter second earlier). |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `from_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Only cues starting at or after this time. |
| `segment_ids` | string[] | no |  |  | Only these cues. |
| `track_id` | string | no |  |  | Only the cues of this text track. |

**Returns:** {shifted: count, offset_us}.

Example — Captions 0.3 s later:

```json
{"offset_us":300000,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — From 1 minute on, 1 s earlier:

```json
{"from_us":60000000,"offset_us":-1000000,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### captions.split

**Split caption** · MCP tool `captions_split` · `POST /api/v1/commands/captions.split` · undoable

Splits a caption cue in two — what pressing Enter in the caption editor does. Give the split point as at_char (a character offset in the text, as a JavaScript caret position), at_word (index of the first word of the second cue) or at_us (timeline time; default: the playhead). With word timings the time split happens where the first word of the second part starts; without, in proportion to the text length. Both parts keep the look and position.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the caption cue (a text segment), e.g. "seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f". Get it from captions.list. |
| `at_char` | integer | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Split the text at this character offset (UTF-16 units, like a textarea's selectionStart). |
| `at_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Split at this timeline time (default: the playhead when neither at_char nor at_word is given). |
| `at_word` | integer | no |  | 1 … ∞ | Index of the first word of the second cue (0-based word index into the cue's words). |

**Returns:** {left: cue, right: cue}.

Example — Split where the caret is:

```json
{"at_char":14,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Split before word 4:

```json
{"at_word":4,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### captions.status

**Captions job status** · MCP tool `captions_status` · `POST /api/v1/commands/captions.status`

Returns the status of a captions.auto / transcript.transcribe job: state (queued, running, done, failed, cancelled), phase (waiting, extracting_audio, loading_model, transcribing, creating_captions, finished), progress 0..1, the device used and, when done, the result. With wait_s the call blocks until the job finishes or the time runs out (long polling — convenient for AI agents). Without job_id it lists the recent jobs of project_id (or of all projects), newest first. Jobs live in memory and are forgotten when Kadr restarts.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `job_id` | string | no |  |  | Job id returned by captions.auto or transcript.transcribe, e.g. "cap_1a2b3c4d5e6f". |
| `project_id` | string | no |  |  | Without job_id: only list the jobs of this project. |
| `wait_s` | number (seconds) | no |  | 0 … 600 | With job_id: wait up to this many seconds for the job to finish before answering (0 = answer now). |

**Returns:** With job_id: the job status (see captions.auto). Without: {jobs: [job status…]}.

Example — Poll a job:

```json
{"job_id":"cap_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Wait up to 30 s:

```json
{"job_id":"cap_1a2b3c4d5e6f","wait_s":30}
```

### captions.update

**Edit caption** · MCP tool `captions_update` · `POST /api/v1/commands/captions.update` · undoable

Edits one caption cue: its text (inline editing in the caption list; \n breaks lines) and/or its start and end on the timeline (time nudge). When the text changes, words that are still there keep their recognised timings and new/changed words share the time between them, so word highlighting stays in sync. Times may not overlap the neighbouring cues on the track (conflict). At least one of text, start_us, end_us is needed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the caption cue (a text segment), e.g. "seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f". Get it from captions.list. |
| `end_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 1 … ∞ | New end on the timeline (exclusive). |
| `start_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | New start on the timeline. |
| `text` | string | no |  |  | New caption text. |

**Returns:** The updated cue {segment_id, track_id, index, start_us, end_us, text, style_id, words}.

Example — Fix a typo:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","text":"Hello everyone"}
```

Example — Start 200 ms later:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","start_us":1200000}
```

## Edit

6 commands: `clipboard.copy`, `clipboard.cut`, `clipboard.paste`, `edit.history`, `edit.redo`, `edit.undo`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/edit.html

### clipboard.copy

**Copy** · MCP tool `clipboard_copy` · `POST /api/v1/commands/clipboard.copy` · hotkey Ctrl+C · UI: Timeline/Context menu/Copy

Copies clips to the editor's clipboard (kept in memory per project, not the OS clipboard) so they can be pasted with clipboard.paste — Ctrl+C in CapCut. All properties are copied (effects, filters, keyframes, text style…). Linked clips are copied along when linkage is on. The project is not changed and nothing is added to undo history.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | no |  |  | ID of the clip. Required unless segment_ids is given. |
| `segment_ids` | string[] | no |  |  | Several segment ids at once (multi-selection). Combined with segment_id when both are given. |

**Returns:** {copied: [segment ids]}.

Example — Copy a clip:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### clipboard.cut

**Cut** · MCP tool `clipboard_cut` · `POST /api/v1/commands/clipboard.cut` · undoable · hotkey Ctrl+X · UI: Timeline/Context menu/Cut

Copies clips to the editor's clipboard and deletes them from the timeline — Ctrl+X in CapCut. Deletion follows timeline.segment.delete (ripple on the magnet main track, linked clips included, emptied tracks removed). Undo restores the clips; the clipboard keeps the copy.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | no |  |  | ID of the clip. Required unless segment_ids is given. |
| `segment_ids` | string[] | no |  |  | Several segment ids at once (multi-selection). Combined with segment_id when both are given. |

**Returns:** {cut: [segment ids]}.

Example — Cut a clip:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### clipboard.paste

**Paste** · MCP tool `clipboard_paste` · `POST /api/v1/commands/clipboard.paste` · undoable · hotkey Ctrl+V · UI: Timeline/Context menu/Paste

Pastes the clips from clipboard.copy / clipboard.cut at at_us (default: the playhead) — Ctrl+V in CapCut. Clips keep their timing relative to each other and get new ids (pasted linked clips are linked to each other). Each clip goes back to its original track if it still exists (or to track_id when given and compatible); on the main track the magnet inserts at the nearest clip boundary and ripples, and the rest of the pasted selection follows by the same amount; on other tracks an occupied spot sends the clip to a new track. Transitions are not pasted. Fails with conflict when the clipboard is empty.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `at_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  |  | Timeline time in microseconds (1 s = 1000000). Defaults to the current playhead position. |
| `track_id` | string | no |  |  | Optional destination track for the pasted clips (used for clips whose type it accepts). |

**Returns:** {pasted: [{track_id, segment}]} — the new clips.

Example — Paste at the playhead:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Paste at 20 s:

```json
{"at_us":20000000,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### edit.history

**Get undo history state** · MCP tool `edit_history` · `POST /api/v1/commands/edit.history`

Reports whether undo/redo are available and the labels of the actions they would revert or re-apply. The editor uses this to enable the Undo/Redo buttons and show their tooltips.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |

**Returns:** {can_undo, can_redo, undo_label, redo_label}.

Example — Check history:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### edit.redo

**Redo** · MCP tool `edit_redo` · `POST /api/v1/commands/edit.redo` · hotkey Ctrl+Shift+Z · UI: Top bar/Redo

Re-applies the change most recently reverted by edit.undo. Any new edit after an undo clears the redo history. Returns nothing_to_undo when there is nothing to redo.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |

**Returns:** History state after redoing: {can_undo, can_redo, undo_label, redo_label}.

Example — Redo:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### edit.undo

**Undo** · MCP tool `edit_undo` · `POST /api/v1/commands/edit.undo` · hotkey Ctrl+Z · UI: Top bar/Undo

Reverts the most recent undoable change to the project (one command, or one whole batch). Works the same no matter whether the change was made in the UI or through the API. Returns nothing_to_undo when the history is empty.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |

**Returns:** History state after undoing: {can_undo, can_redo, undo_label, redo_label}.

Example — Undo last change:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

## Effects

5 commands: `effect.add`, `effect.apply`, `effect.get_params`, `effect.remove`, `effect.set_params`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/effects.html

### effect.add

**Add effect** · MCP tool `effect_add` · `POST /api/v1/commands/effect.add` · undoable · UI: Library/Effects

Adds a video effect as its own segment on an effect track, like clicking an effect card in the Effects tab. An effect-track segment applies to everything drawn below it (all lower tracks) for its time range. Placed at at_us (default: playhead) for duration_us (default 3 s) on the first free effect track or a new effect track above all visual tracks. Animated effects (shake, glitch, zoom pulse...) run from the segment start. To put an effect on one clip only use effect.apply instead.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `effect_id` | string | yes |  |  | Effect id from library.list kind=effect, e.g. "vhs", "shake", "sparkle". |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `at_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Timeline time where the new segment starts (1 second = 1000000). Defaults to the playhead position. |
| `duration_us` | integer (microseconds) | no | `3000000` | 100000 … 86400000000 | Length of the new effect segment on the timeline. CapCut's default is 3 seconds (3000000). |
| `params` | object | no |  |  | Optional named effect parameters, e.g. {"intensity": 0.8, "speed": 1.5, "levels": 4}. Every effect accepts intensity (0..1) and speed (0.1..10); the effect's own sliders are listed in library.get {kind: "effect"} → params.schema ([{id, label, min, max, default, step?, unit?}]). Values are clamped to their range; unknown names are rejected. |
| `track_id` | string | no |  |  | Put the segment on this existing track. Omit to use the first free track of the right type, or a new track created above all visual tracks. |

**Returns:** {segment_id, track_id, segment} — segment.effect holds {id, params}.

Example — VHS look at the playhead:

```json
{"effect_id":"vhs","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Strong shake for 1.5 s at 10 s:

```json
{"at_us":10000000,"duration_us":1500000,"effect_id":"shake","params":{"intensity":0.9},"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### effect.apply

**Apply effect to clip** · MCP tool `effect_apply` · `POST /api/v1/commands/effect.apply` · undoable · UI: Library/Effects/Drag onto clip

Applies a video effect directly to one clip (video, photo or sticker segment), like dragging an effect card onto a clip. The effect lasts as long as the clip; applying an effect the clip already has just updates its parameters. When segment_id is an effect-track segment its effect is replaced instead. Text, audio, filter and adjustment segments cannot carry video effects.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `effect_id` | string | yes |  |  | Effect id from library.list kind=effect. |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id. |
| `params` | object | no |  |  | Optional named effect parameters, e.g. {"intensity": 0.8, "speed": 1.5, "levels": 4}. Every effect accepts intensity (0..1) and speed (0.1..10); the effect's own sliders are listed in library.get {kind: "effect"} → params.schema ([{id, label, min, max, default, step?, unit?}]). Values are clamped to their range; unknown names are rejected. |

**Returns:** The updated segment (effects[] for clips, effect for effect-track segments).

Example — Glitch a clip:

```json
{"effect_id":"glitch","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

### effect.get_params

**Effect parameters** · MCP tool `effect_get_params` · `POST /api/v1/commands/effect.get_params` · UI: Inspector/Effect

Reads the current parameters of an effect in use together with its slider schema — what the Effect inspector shows. Target: the effect of an effect-track segment, or one of a clip's applied effects (effect_id selects which; optional when the clip has exactly one). params contains every schema parameter (defaults filled in for values never set); schema is [{id, label, min, max, default, step?, unit?}] in display order (intensity first, then speed for animated effects, then the effect's own sliders). Change values with effect.set_params.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id. |
| `effect_id` | string | no |  |  | Which applied effect to read (needed when a clip has several). |

**Returns:** {segment_id, effect_id, name, params: {id: value}, schema: [{id, label, min, max, default, step?, unit?}]}.

Example — Read the sliders of an effect segment:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

### effect.remove

**Remove effect** · MCP tool `effect_remove` · `POST /api/v1/commands/effect.remove` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Effect/Delete

Removes video effects. For a segment on an effect track the whole effect segment is deleted (an emptied effect track is removed too). For a clip, removes the applied effect effect_id, or all applied effects when effect_id is omitted.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id. |
| `effect_id` | string | no |  |  | Applied effect to remove from a clip; omit to remove all of them. |

**Returns:** {segment_id, deleted_segment: bool, effects: [remaining effects on the clip]}.

Example — Remove an effect segment:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

### effect.set_params

**Adjust effect** · MCP tool `effect_set_params` · `POST /api/v1/commands/effect.set_params` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Effect

Changes the slider parameters of an effect that is already used — CapCut's per-effect sliders in the Effect inspector (e.g. Intensity, Speed, Range). Target: the effect of an effect-track segment, or one of the effects applied to a clip (effect_id selects which; it may be omitted when the clip has exactly one). Every effect has intensity (0..1, 0 = off) and speed (animation speed multiplier, 0.1..10); most have their own named parameters listed in library.get {kind: "effect", id} → params.schema as [{id, label, min, max, default, step?, unit?}] (unit "%" = a 0..1 fraction shown as percent, "x" = multiplier, "/s" = per second, "s" = seconds, "°" = degrees). Pass them in params ({"levels": 4}) — intensity and speed may also be passed flat. Only the given parameters change; reset=true first restores every default. A value outside its range or an unknown parameter name is an invalid_argument error whose hint lists the valid parameters. Use effect.get_params to read the current values.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id. |
| `effect_id` | string | no |  |  | Which applied effect to change (needed when a clip has several). |
| `intensity` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Effect strength 0..1 (same as params.intensity). |
| `params` | object | no |  |  | Named parameter values from the effect's schema, e.g. {"strength": 0.2, "rate": 2}. Must be within each parameter's min..max. |
| `reset` | boolean | no |  |  | true restores all parameters to their defaults before applying the given ones (the slider panel's reset button). |
| `speed` | number | no |  | 0.1 … 10 | Animation speed multiplier, 1 = normal (same as params.speed). |

**Returns:** The updated segment (segment.effect.params for effect-track segments, segment.effects[i].params for clips).

Example — Softer effect:

```json
{"intensity":0.3,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

Example — Posterize with 4 levels:

```json
{"effect_id":"posterize","params":{"levels":4},"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

Example — Faster, stronger punch zoom:

```json
{"params":{"intensity":1,"rate":2.5,"strength":0.2},"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

Example — Back to defaults:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","reset":true,"segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

## Export

6 commands: `export.cancel`, `export.estimate`, `export.list`, `export.reveal`, `export.start`, `export.status`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/export.html

### export.cancel

**Cancel export** · MCP tool `export_cancel` · `POST /api/v1/commands/export.cancel` · UI: Export dialog/Cancel

Cancels a queued or running export — the Cancel button of the export progress view. A running job's FFmpeg process is killed and the partially written file is deleted; the call waits (up to 10 s) until the job has stopped and returns its final state "cancelled" (an export.cancelled event is published). Cancelling an already cancelled job is a no-op; cancelling a done or failed job returns conflict (delete the file yourself if needed).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `job_id` | string | yes |  |  | Export job id returned by export.start (e.g. "exp_1a2b3c4d5e6f"). export.list shows all known jobs. |

**Returns:** The job object (same shape as export.status), normally with state "cancelled".

Example — Stop an export:

```json
{"job_id":"exp_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### export.estimate

**Estimate export** · MCP tool `export_estimate` · `POST /api/v1/commands/export.estimate`

Resolves export settings without exporting: final width/height, frame rate, frame count, video bitrate, duration, estimated file size and the output path export.start would use right now (unique " (n)" name applied). Takes exactly the same parameters as export.start, so an agent can check the result first and the export dialog shows "Estimated size" from it. The size is bitrate × duration for video/audio (real files are usually a bit smaller with simple content) and a heuristic for GIF. encoder is the FFmpeg encoder that will be used (e.g. h264_nvenc or libx264); it is empty until hardware detection has finished (it starts on the first call).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `audio_format` | string | no |  | `mp3`, `wav`, `aac`, `flac` | Audio-only file type: mp3 (default, 320 kbps), wav (48 kHz 16-bit PCM), aac (192 kbps ADTS) or flac (lossless). Taken from the path extension when omitted. Video exports always use AAC 192 kbps. |
| `audio_only` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Export only the soundtrack (the dialog's Audio checkbox without Video). Uses audio_format; no frames are rendered. |
| `bitrate` | string | no | `"recommended"` | `lower`, `recommended`, `higher`, `custom` | Video quality preset. recommended ≈ YouTube upload bitrates (1080p30 H.264 = 10 Mbps, 4K30 = 40 Mbps); lower = 60 %, higher = 150 %; ×1.5 at 60 fps; HEVC uses 70 % of the H.264 value. custom uses bitrate_kbps. |
| `bitrate_kbps` | integer (kilobits per second) | no |  | 200 … 200000 | Video bitrate when bitrate is custom (e.g. 8000 = 8 Mbps). Rejected with any other bitrate preset. |
| `codec` | string | no | `"h264"` | `h264`, `hevc` | Video codec. h264 plays everywhere; hevc (H.265) gives smaller files at the same quality. A GPU encoder (NVENC, Quick Sync, AMF) is used automatically when it works on this machine, otherwise libx264/libx265. |
| `format` | string | no |  | `mp4`, `mov` | Video container: mp4 (default, most compatible) or mov (QuickTime). Taken from the path extension when omitted. Not used for GIF and audio-only exports. |
| `fps` | number (frames per second) | no |  | 1 … 120 | Output frame rate. The dialog offers 24, 25, 30, 50 and 60. Defaults to the project frame rate. GIFs are capped at 15 fps. |
| `gif` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Export an animated GIF instead of a video: at most 15 fps, longer side at most 720 px, optimised 256-colour palette, loops forever, no sound. |
| `overwrite` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Replace an existing file at path instead of choosing a unique " (n)" name. |
| `path` | string | no |  |  | Output file or folder. Omit to write "<home>/Videos/Kadr/<project name>.<ext>". A missing extension is added; an existing folder (or a path ending in / or \) gets "<project name>.<ext>" inside it. The extension may select the output kind: .mp4/.mov video, .gif GIF, .mp3/.wav/.aac/.flac audio only. If the file exists, " (1)", " (2)"… is appended unless overwrite is true. Missing folders are created. |
| `range_end_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 1 … ∞ | End (exclusive) of the exported part of the timeline. Defaults to (and is clamped to) the project duration. |
| `range_start_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Start of the exported part of the timeline. Default 0 (beginning). |
| `resolution` | string | no | `"1080p"` | `480p`, `720p`, `1080p`, `2k`, `4k` | Output size by its shorter side: 480p=480, 720p=720, 1080p=1080, 2k=1440, 4k=2160 px. The canvas aspect ratio is kept (16:9 1080p = 1920x1080, 9:16 1080p = 1080x1920); both sides are rounded to even numbers. |

**Returns:** {kind, resolution, width, height, fps, frames, bitrate, bitrate_kbps, codec, format, audio_kbps, range_start_us, range_end_us, duration_us, size_bytes, path, folder, file_name, encoder}.

Example — Size of a default 1080p export:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Size at 4K higher bitrate:

```json
{"bitrate":"higher","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","resolution":"4k"}
```

### export.list

**List exports** · MCP tool `export_list` · `POST /api/v1/commands/export.list`

Lists export jobs of this session, newest first — running and queued jobs as well as finished, failed and cancelled ones (the last 200 finished jobs are remembered; nothing survives a restart). Pass project_id to see only one project's exports, e.g. to find an export that is still running after the dialog was closed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | no |  |  | Only return jobs of this project. Omit to list the jobs of every project. |

**Returns:** Array of job objects (same shape as export.status).

Example — All jobs:

```json
{}
```

Example — Jobs of one project:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### export.reveal

**Open export folder** · MCP tool `export_reveal` · `POST /api/v1/commands/export.reveal` · UI: Export dialog/Open folder

Opens the folder containing a finished export in the system file manager (Explorer, Finder or the default Linux file manager) with the file selected where supported — the "Open folder" button shown when an export is done. Runs on the machine where Kadr runs. For a remote client, download the file from GET /api/v1/exports/{job_id}/file instead.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `job_id` | string | yes |  |  | Export job id returned by export.start (e.g. "exp_1a2b3c4d5e6f"). export.list shows all known jobs. |

**Returns:** {opened: true, path, folder}.

Example — Show the exported file:

```json
{"job_id":"exp_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### export.start

**Export** · MCP tool `export_start` · `POST /api/v1/commands/export.start` · hotkey Ctrl+E · UI: Top bar/Export

Starts exporting the project to a file in the background and returns immediately with a job_id — the Export button in the top bar. The project is snapshotted at this moment, so later edits do not change a running export. Every frame is rendered by the same compositor as the player and encoded with FFmpeg (H.264 or HEVC in MP4/MOV, yuv420p, BT.709, AAC 192 kbps stereo audio, +faststart for instant web playback). Set audio_only=true for an MP3/WAV/AAC/FLAC soundtrack, or gif=true for an animated GIF. Use range_start_us/range_end_us to export part of the timeline. Jobs run one at a time (others wait in state "queued"). Follow progress with export.status (poll every 1-2 s) or the export.progress / export.done / export.failed / export.cancelled events; stop with export.cancel. Call export.estimate first to preview size and path. Does not modify the project and is not undoable. It is a global command (project_id is passed explicitly) so it cannot be part of a batch or dry run. Fails with invalid_argument when the timeline is empty.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `audio_format` | string | no |  | `mp3`, `wav`, `aac`, `flac` | Audio-only file type: mp3 (default, 320 kbps), wav (48 kHz 16-bit PCM), aac (192 kbps ADTS) or flac (lossless). Taken from the path extension when omitted. Video exports always use AAC 192 kbps. |
| `audio_only` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Export only the soundtrack (the dialog's Audio checkbox without Video). Uses audio_format; no frames are rendered. |
| `bitrate` | string | no | `"recommended"` | `lower`, `recommended`, `higher`, `custom` | Video quality preset. recommended ≈ YouTube upload bitrates (1080p30 H.264 = 10 Mbps, 4K30 = 40 Mbps); lower = 60 %, higher = 150 %; ×1.5 at 60 fps; HEVC uses 70 % of the H.264 value. custom uses bitrate_kbps. |
| `bitrate_kbps` | integer (kilobits per second) | no |  | 200 … 200000 | Video bitrate when bitrate is custom (e.g. 8000 = 8 Mbps). Rejected with any other bitrate preset. |
| `codec` | string | no | `"h264"` | `h264`, `hevc` | Video codec. h264 plays everywhere; hevc (H.265) gives smaller files at the same quality. A GPU encoder (NVENC, Quick Sync, AMF) is used automatically when it works on this machine, otherwise libx264/libx265. |
| `format` | string | no |  | `mp4`, `mov` | Video container: mp4 (default, most compatible) or mov (QuickTime). Taken from the path extension when omitted. Not used for GIF and audio-only exports. |
| `fps` | number (frames per second) | no |  | 1 … 120 | Output frame rate. The dialog offers 24, 25, 30, 50 and 60. Defaults to the project frame rate. GIFs are capped at 15 fps. |
| `gif` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Export an animated GIF instead of a video: at most 15 fps, longer side at most 720 px, optimised 256-colour palette, loops forever, no sound. |
| `overwrite` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Replace an existing file at path instead of choosing a unique " (n)" name. |
| `path` | string | no |  |  | Output file or folder. Omit to write "<home>/Videos/Kadr/<project name>.<ext>". A missing extension is added; an existing folder (or a path ending in / or \) gets "<project name>.<ext>" inside it. The extension may select the output kind: .mp4/.mov video, .gif GIF, .mp3/.wav/.aac/.flac audio only. If the file exists, " (1)", " (2)"… is appended unless overwrite is true. Missing folders are created. |
| `range_end_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 1 … ∞ | End (exclusive) of the exported part of the timeline. Defaults to (and is clamped to) the project duration. |
| `range_start_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Start of the exported part of the timeline. Default 0 (beginning). |
| `resolution` | string | no | `"1080p"` | `480p`, `720p`, `1080p`, `2k`, `4k` | Output size by its shorter side: 480p=480, 720p=720, 1080p=1080, 2k=1440, 4k=2160 px. The canvas aspect ratio is kept (16:9 1080p = 1920x1080, 9:16 1080p = 1080x1920); both sides are rounded to even numbers. |

**Returns:** {job_id, state ("queued"|"running"), path (final file path, already made unique), kind (video|audio|gif), width, height, fps, frames, duration_us, bitrate_kbps, codec, format, estimated_size_bytes}.

Example — Export with CapCut defaults (1080p, recommended bitrate, H.264 MP4) to ~/Videos/Kadr:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — 4K 60 fps HEVC MOV to a chosen file:

```json
{"codec":"hevc","format":"mov","fps":60,"path":"C:/Users/me/Desktop/trip.mov","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","resolution":"4k"}
```

Example — First 5 seconds as a GIF:

```json
{"gif":true,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","range_end_us":5000000}
```

Example — Soundtrack only as WAV:

```json
{"audio_format":"wav","audio_only":true,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Custom 6 Mbps 720p:

```json
{"bitrate":"custom","bitrate_kbps":6000,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","resolution":"720p"}
```

### export.status

**Export status** · MCP tool `export_status` · `POST /api/v1/commands/export.status`

Returns the current state of one export job: state (queued, running, done, failed, cancelled), phase (audio, video, encoding, finalizing), progress 0..1, frames_done/frames_total, speed_fps (frames rendered per second), eta_s (seconds left, -1 while unknown), elapsed_s, output path, size_bytes once done, the encoder used and the error message on failure. Poll it every 1-2 seconds after export.start until state is terminal. Jobs are kept in memory only: after Kadr restarts the id is unknown (not_found), but finished files remain on disk.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `job_id` | string | yes |  |  | Export job id returned by export.start (e.g. "exp_1a2b3c4d5e6f"). export.list shows all known jobs. |

**Returns:** {job_id, project_id, project_name, state, phase, progress, frames_done, frames_total, speed_fps, eta_s, elapsed_s, path, size_bytes, encoder, error, settings, created_at, started_at, finished_at}.

Example — Check progress:

```json
{"job_id":"exp_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

## Filters

4 commands: `adjustment.add`, `filter.add`, `filter.apply`, `filter.remove`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/filters.html

### adjustment.add

**Add adjustment** · MCP tool `adjustment_add` · `POST /api/v1/commands/adjustment.add` · undoable · UI: Library/Adjustment/Custom adjustment

Adds a neutral adjustment layer — a segment on an adjustment track whose colour controls (brightness, contrast, saturation, exposure, temperature, tint, highlights, shadows, sharpen, vignette, LUT) apply to everything below it for its time range, like "Custom adjustment" in the Adjustment tab. Placed at at_us (default: playhead) for duration_us (default 3 s). Set the values afterwards with segment.set_adjust on the returned segment.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `at_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Timeline time where the new segment starts (1 second = 1000000). Defaults to the playhead position. |
| `duration_us` | integer (microseconds) | no | `3000000` | 100000 … 86400000000 | Length of the new adjustment segment on the timeline. CapCut's default is 3 seconds (3000000). |
| `track_id` | string | no |  |  | Put the segment on this existing track. Omit to use the first free track of the right type, or a new track created above all visual tracks. |

**Returns:** {segment_id, track_id, segment} — segment.adjust holds the (neutral) Adjustments.

Example — Adjustment layer for the first 10 s:

```json
{"at_us":0,"duration_us":10000000,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### filter.add

**Add filter** · MCP tool `filter_add` · `POST /api/v1/commands/filter.add` · undoable · UI: Library/Filters

Adds a colour filter as its own segment on a filter track, like clicking a card in the Filters tab. A filter-track segment recolours everything below it for its time range. Placed at at_us (default: playhead) for duration_us (default 3 s) on the first free filter track or a new filter track above all visual tracks. To filter one clip only use filter.apply.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `filter_id` | string | yes |  |  | Filter id from library.list kind=filter, e.g. "film", "warm", "teal_orange", "bw". |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `at_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Timeline time where the new segment starts (1 second = 1000000). Defaults to the playhead position. |
| `duration_us` | integer (microseconds) | no | `3000000` | 100000 … 86400000000 | Length of the new filter segment on the timeline. CapCut's default is 3 seconds (3000000). |
| `intensity` | number | no | `1` | 0 … 1 | Filter strength 0..1 (CapCut shows 0..100; 1 = full). |
| `track_id` | string | no |  |  | Put the segment on this existing track. Omit to use the first free track of the right type, or a new track created above all visual tracks. |

**Returns:** {segment_id, track_id, segment} — segment.filter holds {id, intensity}.

Example — Film look at the playhead:

```json
{"filter_id":"film","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Half-strength B&W for 5 s:

```json
{"at_us":0,"duration_us":5000000,"filter_id":"bw","intensity":0.5,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### filter.apply

**Apply filter to clip** · MCP tool `filter_apply` · `POST /api/v1/commands/filter.apply` · undoable · UI: Library/Filters/Drag onto clip

Sets the colour filter of one clip (video, photo or sticker) — a clip has at most one filter, so this replaces any previous one (a different filter also drops the clip's filter.intensity keyframes); call it again with the same filter_id to change only the intensity. When segment_id is a filter-track segment, its filter is replaced instead.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `filter_id` | string | yes |  |  | Filter id from library.list kind=filter. |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id. |
| `intensity` | number | no | `1` | 0 … 1 | Filter strength 0..1 (CapCut shows 0..100; 1 = full). |

**Returns:** The updated segment (segment.filter = {id, intensity}).

Example — Warm up a clip:

```json
{"filter_id":"warm","intensity":0.8,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

### filter.remove

**Remove filter** · MCP tool `filter_remove` · `POST /api/v1/commands/filter.remove` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Filter/Delete

Removes a colour filter: deletes a filter-track segment (and its track when it becomes empty), or clears the filter of a clip together with its filter.intensity keyframes.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id. |

**Returns:** {segment_id, deleted_segment: bool}.

Example — Remove:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

## Fonts

5 commands: `font.catalog`, `font.import`, `font.install`, `font.remove`, `font.rescan`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/fonts.html

### font.catalog

**Font catalogue** · MCP tool `font_catalog` · `POST /api/v1/commands/font.catalog` · UI: Inspector/Text/Font/More fonts

Lists Kadr's curated catalogue of downloadable font families — the "More fonts" section of the Text → Font picker. Every family is free and open-source (SIL Open Font License 1.1) from the google/fonts repository; most support Cyrillic (cyrillic=true; ukrainian is verified after installation). Each entry has an id (also the font id to use in text.update font once installed), name, style category (sans, serif, display, handwriting, monospace, pixel), a short note on its look and best use, download size, the exact file URLs, licence and specimen page, and installed=true when it is already available (downloaded into the Kadr data folder or bundled with the app). Use it to pick a font by mood, then call font.install {id} and text.update {font: id}. Read-only and offline: nothing is downloaded. Filters: query (name, id or note), category, cyrillic, installed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `category` | string | no |  | `sans`, `serif`, `display`, `handwriting`, `monospace`, `pixel` | Only families of this style: sans, serif, display, handwriting, monospace or pixel. |
| `cyrillic` | boolean | no |  |  | true = only families with Cyrillic letters (Ukrainian/Russian text); false = only Latin-only ones. |
| `installed` | boolean | no |  |  | true = only families that are already installed; false = only those that still need font.install. |
| `query` | string | no |  |  | Case-insensitive search in the family name, id and note, e.g. "script", "retro", "mono". |

**Returns:** {count, total, families:[{id, name, category, cyrillic, ukrainian? (after install), note, license, license_url, page_url, repo_path, variable, size_bytes, files:[{style, file, url, size_bytes}], installed, source?, font_id, job?{state, progress, error}}], categories, base_url, folders{downloaded, bundled[], system[]}}.

Example — All handwriting fonts with Cyrillic:

```json
{"category":"handwriting","cyrillic":true}
```

Example — Search for a pixel font:

```json
{"query":"pixel"}
```

### font.import

**Import font file** · MCP tool `font_import` · `POST /api/v1/commands/font.import` · UI: Inspector/Text/Font/Import font file

Installs a font file from this computer into the Kadr data folder so it can be used in texts — "Import font file" in the Text → Font picker. Accepts TrueType (.ttf), OpenType (.otf) and collections (.ttc/.otc); the file is checked (it must parse and draw Latin, digit or Cyrillic glyphs; web fonts .woff/.woff2 and CFF2 variable fonts are rejected with a hint) and copied — the original stays where it is. The family name inside the font becomes the font id ("My Brand Sans" → "my_brand_sans"); importing the other styles of the same family (Bold, Italic…) adds them to that family. The category (sans, serif, display, handwriting, monospace, pixel) is inferred from the font unless given. Publishes fonts.changed. Make sure the font's licence allows the use you plan.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | yes |  |  | Absolute path of the .ttf/.otf/.ttc file to import. |
| `category` | string | no |  | `sans`, `serif`, `display`, `handwriting`, `monospace`, `pixel` | Only families of this style: sans, serif, display, handwriting, monospace or pixel. |
| `replace` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Replace an already imported file of the same family and style (or a catalogue install of that family). |

**Returns:** {font_id, family, style, category, cyrillic, ukrainian, variable, path (the stored copy), replaced}.

Example — Import a downloaded font:

```json
{"path":"C:\\Users\\me\\Downloads\\MyBrandSans-Regular.ttf"}
```

Example — Import as a handwriting font:

```json
{"category":"handwriting","path":"/Users/me/Downloads/MyHand.otf"}
```

### font.install

**Install font** · MCP tool `font_install` · `POST /api/v1/commands/font.install` · UI: Inspector/Text/Font/More fonts

Downloads a font family from font.catalog into the Kadr data folder (<DataDir>/fonts/<id>/) so it can be used in any text — the Install button in the Text → Font picker. Fetches the family's font files and its OFL.txt licence over HTTPS from the google/fonts repository, checks every file (size limits, TrueType/OpenType signature, the font must draw), checks that the licence is the SIL Open Font License, then moves the folder into place atomically — a failed or interrupted download leaves nothing behind. Variable fonts get real Regular and Bold weights. Runs in the background and returns at once unless wait=true; progress arrives as font.progress events (state queued → downloading → verifying → installing → done | failed, with downloaded_bytes/total_bytes/progress), and fonts.changed when the font is ready. Afterwards use font_id with text.update {font}. An already installed family is not downloaded again (already_installed=true) unless force=true. Fails with not_found for unknown ids and not_available when the internet cannot be reached.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes |  |  | Catalogue id from font.catalog, e.g. "montserrat", "caveat", "press_start_2p". |
| `force` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Download and reinstall even when the family is already installed. |
| `wait` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Block until the font is installed (or failed) instead of returning immediately. |

**Returns:** {started, already_installed, font_id, message, job{id, font_id, state, file, downloaded_bytes, total_bytes, progress, error, hint}}.

Example — Install Montserrat in the background:

```json
{"id":"montserrat"}
```

Example — Install Caveat and wait until it is ready:

```json
{"id":"caveat","wait":true}
```

### font.remove

**Remove font** · MCP tool `font_remove` · `POST /api/v1/commands/font.remove` · UI: Inspector/Text/Font/Remove font

Deletes a font family that was installed with font.install or font.import (library.list kind=font category=Downloaded) from the Kadr data folder. Built-in, bundled and operating-system fonts cannot be removed here (conflict). Texts that use the removed font fall back to Go Sans until it is installed again (font.install restores catalogue fonts with the same id). Publishes fonts.changed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `font_id` | string | yes |  |  | Font id of a downloaded/imported family, e.g. "montserrat". |

**Returns:** {font_id, family, dir}.

Example — Remove Montserrat:

```json
{"font_id":"montserrat"}
```

### font.rescan

**Rescan fonts** · MCP tool `font_rescan` · `POST /api/v1/commands/font.rescan` · UI: Inspector/Text/Font/Rescan

Re-reads every font folder — the Kadr data folder (downloaded/imported fonts), the folders bundled with the app (<exe dir>/fonts, Kadr.app/Contents/Resources/fonts on macOS, KADR_FONTS_DIR) and, with system=true, the operating system's font folders — so fonts copied there while Kadr runs appear in library.list kind=font without a restart. Returns the number of families per source and the folders that were scanned. Publishes fonts.changed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `system` | boolean | no | `true` |  | Also rescan the operating-system font folders (slower; a few seconds with thousands of fonts). |

**Returns:** {downloaded, bundled, system, total (family counts), folders{downloaded, bundled[], system[]}}.

Example — Pick up newly installed fonts:

```json
{}
```

## Keyframes

4 commands: `keyframe.add`, `keyframe.clear`, `keyframe.list`, `keyframe.remove`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/keyframes.html

### keyframe.add

**Add keyframe** · MCP tool `keyframe_add` · `POST /api/v1/commands/keyframe.add` · undoable · UI: Inspector/◇ keyframe button

Adds (or updates) a keyframe of one animatable property — the diamond button next to a slider in the CapCut inspector. Once a property has two or more keyframes its value is interpolated between them; before the first / after the last keyframe it holds that keyframe's value. If a keyframe of the same property already exists within half a frame of time_us it is updated instead of duplicated. value defaults to the property's current (interpolated) value at that time, so calling it without value just 'pins' what is on screen. Values use the stored units: transform.x/y in canvas fractions (-2..2), transform.scale as multiplier (0.01..4), transform.rotation in degrees (-360..360), opacity 0..1, volume as LINEAR gain 0..10 (1 = 0 dB, 0.5 ≈ -6 dB; gain = 10^(dB/20)), adjust.* -1..1 (sharpen, fade, grain and lut_intensity 0..1; adjust.hue -1..1 = -180..180 degrees; adjust.shine -1..1 local contrast), filter.intensity 0..1 (strength of the clip's or filter segment's filter — CapCut's filter Intensity keyframe). easing shapes the motion from this keyframe to the next one. While a property has keyframes, segment.set_transform / set_opacity / set_volume / set_adjust record their value as a keyframe at the playhead instead of changing the static value. Picture properties need a video, photo, sticker or text segment; volume needs sound; adjust.* needs a video/photo clip or adjustment segment; filter.intensity needs a segment that has a filter (a clip after filter.apply, or a filter-track segment).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `property` | string | yes |  | `transform.x`, `transform.y`, `transform.scale`, `transform.rotation`, `opacity`, `volume`, `adjust.brightness`, `adjust.contrast`, `adjust.saturation`, `adjust.exposure`, `adjust.temperature`, `adjust.tint`, `adjust.highlights`, `adjust.shadows`, `adjust.sharpen`, `adjust.vignette`, `adjust.hue`, `adjust.fade`, `adjust.grain`, `adjust.shine`, `adjust.lut_intensity`, `filter.intensity` | Property to animate, e.g. "transform.scale" or "adjust.brightness". |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `easing` | string | no |  | `linear`, `ease_in`, `ease_out`, `ease_in_out` | Interpolation from this keyframe to the next: linear (default for new keyframes), ease_in, ease_out or ease_in_out. Omit to keep the easing of an existing keyframe. |
| `time_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Keyframe time relative to the segment start (0 = first frame of the clip). Defaults to the playhead position minus the segment start; the playhead must then be over the segment. |
| `value` | number | no |  |  | Value at this keyframe in the property's stored unit (see description). Defaults to the current value at time_us. |

**Returns:** {segment_id, keyframe: {property, time_us, timeline_us, value, easing}, keyframes: all keyframes of that property}.

Example — Zoom from 100% to 150% over the first 2 seconds (two calls):

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","property":"transform.scale","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","time_us":0,"value":1}
```

Example — Second keyframe with easing:

```json
{"easing":"ease_in_out","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","property":"transform.scale","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","time_us":2000000,"value":1.5}
```

Example — Pin the current opacity at the playhead:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","property":"opacity","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Duck the volume to -12 dB at 5 s:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","property":"volume","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","time_us":5000000,"value":0.251}
```

Example — Fade a filter in: intensity 0 at the start (then 1 at 1 s with a second call):

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","property":"filter.intensity","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","time_us":0,"value":0}
```

Example — Animate a hue sweep: +90° at 2 s:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","property":"adjust.hue","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","time_us":2000000,"value":0.5}
```

### keyframe.clear

**Clear keyframes** · MCP tool `keyframe_clear` · `POST /api/v1/commands/keyframe.clear` · undoable

Removes all keyframes of a segment, or only those of one property / group ("transform", "adjust"). Each property keeps the value it shows at the playhead (or at the segment start when the playhead is outside the segment) as its new static value. Clearing a segment without keyframes is a no-op that still succeeds.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `property` | string | no |  | `transform.x`, `transform.y`, `transform.scale`, `transform.rotation`, `opacity`, `volume`, `adjust.brightness`, `adjust.contrast`, `adjust.saturation`, `adjust.exposure`, `adjust.temperature`, `adjust.tint`, `adjust.highlights`, `adjust.shadows`, `adjust.sharpen`, `adjust.vignette`, `adjust.hue`, `adjust.fade`, `adjust.grain`, `adjust.shine`, `adjust.lut_intensity`, `filter.intensity`, `transform`, `adjust`, `filter` | Only clear this property or group ("transform", "adjust"). Omit to clear every keyframe of the segment. |

**Returns:** {segment_id, removed: number of keyframes removed, keyframes: remaining keyframes}.

Example — Remove all animation:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Clear only position/scale/rotation keyframes:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","property":"transform","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### keyframe.list

**List keyframes** · MCP tool `keyframe_list` · `POST /api/v1/commands/keyframe.list`

Lists the keyframes of a segment sorted by time, optionally filtered by property or group ("transform", "adjust"). Each item has time_us relative to the segment start and timeline_us on the timeline. Also returns the list of keyframeable properties that apply to this segment type.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `property` | string | no |  | `transform.x`, `transform.y`, `transform.scale`, `transform.rotation`, `opacity`, `volume`, `adjust.brightness`, `adjust.contrast`, `adjust.saturation`, `adjust.exposure`, `adjust.temperature`, `adjust.tint`, `adjust.highlights`, `adjust.shadows`, `adjust.sharpen`, `adjust.vignette`, `adjust.hue`, `adjust.fade`, `adjust.grain`, `adjust.shine`, `adjust.lut_intensity`, `filter.intensity`, `transform`, `adjust`, `filter` | Only list this property or group ("transform", "adjust"). |

**Returns:** {segment_id, start_us, duration_us, keyframes: [{property, time_us, timeline_us, value, easing}], properties: keyframeable property names for this segment}.

Example — All keyframes of a clip:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### keyframe.remove

**Remove keyframe** · MCP tool `keyframe_remove` · `POST /api/v1/commands/keyframe.remove` · undoable · UI: Inspector/◆ keyframe button

Removes the keyframe(s) at one time — clicking a filled diamond in the inspector. time_us defaults to the playhead (relative to the segment start) and matches keyframes within half a frame. With property only that property's keyframe is removed; property may also be a group ("transform", "adjust" or "filter"); without property the keyframes of every property at that time are removed. When a property loses its last keyframe it keeps the value it had at that time, so the picture does not jump. Returns not_found when nothing matches.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `property` | string | no |  | `transform.x`, `transform.y`, `transform.scale`, `transform.rotation`, `opacity`, `volume`, `adjust.brightness`, `adjust.contrast`, `adjust.saturation`, `adjust.exposure`, `adjust.temperature`, `adjust.tint`, `adjust.highlights`, `adjust.shadows`, `adjust.sharpen`, `adjust.vignette`, `adjust.hue`, `adjust.fade`, `adjust.grain`, `adjust.shine`, `adjust.lut_intensity`, `filter.intensity`, `transform`, `adjust`, `filter` | Property (or group "transform"/"adjust"/"filter") whose keyframe to remove. Omit to remove the keyframes of all properties at that time. |
| `time_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Keyframe time relative to the segment start (0 = first frame of the clip). Defaults to the playhead position minus the segment start; the playhead must then be over the segment. |

**Returns:** {segment_id, removed: number of keyframes removed, keyframes: remaining keyframes of the segment}.

Example — Remove the scale keyframe at 2 s:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","property":"transform.scale","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","time_us":2000000}
```

Example — Remove every keyframe at the playhead:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

## Library

3 commands: `library.get`, `library.list`, `library.preview`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/library.html

### library.get

**Get library item** · MCP tool `library_get` · `POST /api/v1/commands/library.get` · UI: Library

Returns one library item with all its details: name, categories, description, default parameters (effect intensity/speed, filter intensity, voice-effect ffmpeg filter), default duration, the full TextStyle of a text template, or the available styles of a font. Use it to inspect an id found in library.list or stored in a project (e.g. segment.transition_out.type). Animated items include preview {url, frames, fps, width, height} (the hover sprite strip); call library.preview to look at the motion as one image.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes |  |  | Item id from library.list, e.g. "mix", "vhs", "film", "in_fade". |
| `kind` | string | yes |  | `transition`, `effect`, `filter`, `animation`, `text_template`, `font`, `sticker`, `voice_effect`, `caption_style`, `generated`, `text_effect`, `text_animation`, `sound_effect` | Library kind of the item (see library.list). |

**Returns:** The item: {kind, id, name, category, categories, description, anim_kind?, default_duration_us?, params?, style?, thumbnail, preview?}.

Example — Inspect the VHS effect:

```json
{"id":"vhs","kind":"effect"}
```

### library.list

**List library items** · MCP tool `library_list` · `POST /api/v1/commands/library.list` · UI: Library

Lists the built-in library of one kind — exactly what the left panel tabs show: transitions, video effects, colour filters, clip animations (In/Out/Combo/Loop), text templates (style presets), fonts (embedded Go fonts, fonts installed on this computer, fonts bundled with Kadr and fonts downloaded with font.install — see font.catalog), stickers and voice effects. Every item has a stable id to pass to the matching command (transition.set type, effect.add effect_id, filter.add filter_id, animation.set id, text.add template_id, text.update font, sticker.add sticker_id, segment.set_audio voice_effect), a display name, CapCut-style categories, default parameters/durations and a thumbnail path (GET it with the API token for a PNG preview rendered by the engine). Filter by category tab and/or a case-insensitive search query, like the search box in the panel. More kinds: sound_effect (sfx.add), caption_style (captions.set_style), text_effect (text.apply_effect), text_animation (text.set_glyph_animation), generated (media.generate preset_id). Effects carry params.schema — the named sliders accepted by effect.set_params ({id, label, min, max, default}); transitions list their direction/softness options (see transition.set and transition.get). Items that move (transitions, effects, filters, clip animations, animated text templates/word art, text animations, caption styles with word highlight, animated stickers and generated clips) also carry preview {url, frames, fps, width, height}: GET url for a JPEG sprite strip (frames side by side, one seamless loop) — the app's hover preview; items without it are static. To SEE how an item plays, call library.preview (a PNG contact sheet).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | string | yes |  | `transition`, `effect`, `filter`, `animation`, `text_template`, `font`, `sticker`, `voice_effect`, `caption_style`, `generated`, `text_effect`, `text_animation`, `sound_effect` | Which library to list: transition, effect, filter, animation, text_template, font, sticker, voice_effect, sound_effect, caption_style, text_effect, text_animation or generated. |
| `category` | string | no |  |  | Only items in this category tab (case-insensitive), e.g. "Trending", "Basic", "In", "Retro". The result's categories field lists valid values. |
| `query` | string | no |  |  | Case-insensitive search on the item name, id, categories and description (the panel's search box). |

**Returns:** {kind, categories: [category tab names in display order], total, items: [{kind, id, name, category, categories, description, anim_kind?, default_duration_us?, params?, style? (text templates), thumbnail, preview? {url, frames, fps, width, height}}]}.

Example — All transitions:

```json
{"kind":"transition"}
```

Example — In-animations:

```json
{"category":"In","kind":"animation"}
```

Example — Search filters:

```json
{"kind":"filter","query":"warm"}
```

### library.preview

**Preview library item** · MCP tool `library_preview` · `POST /api/v1/commands/library.preview` · UI: Library

Renders how a library item PLAYS as one PNG contact sheet (frames left to right, top to bottom) so an AI agent can see a transition, effect, filter, clip animation, animated text template, text animation, caption style highlight, animated sticker or animated generated clip before applying it. Uses the same engine and sample pictures as the hover previews of the app: transitions go from a sunny landscape (clip A, progress 0) to a night city (clip B, progress 1); effects run over time on the landscape (static effects such as vignette show a before/after divider); filters show a before/after divider; clip animations move a small clip on a dark stage (dashed outline = rest position); text kinds render sample text. Static items (fonts, voice effects, non-animated templates/word art/stickers) return their thumbnail as a single tile with animated=false. Every item that animates has a preview field in library.list / library.get (the app's hover sprite: GET preview.url for a JPEG strip). Read-only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes |  |  | Item id from library.list, e.g. "cube_turn_left", "vhs", "film", "in_pop". |
| `kind` | string | yes |  | `transition`, `effect`, `filter`, `animation`, `text_template`, `font`, `sticker`, `voice_effect`, `caption_style`, `generated`, `text_effect`, `text_animation`, `sound_effect` | Library kind of the item: transition, effect, filter, animation, text_template, text_effect, text_animation, caption_style, sticker, generated (others are static). |
| `columns` | integer | no | `3` | 1 … 6 | Tiles per row; rows are added as needed. |
| `frames` | integer | no | `6` | 2 … 12 | Number of moments (tiles) to render; more tiles show the motion in finer steps. |
| `tile_width` | integer (pixels) | no | `256` | 64 … 480 | Width of each tile; the height follows the preview's aspect ratio (16:9 for most kinds, square for stickers and text animations). |

**Returns:** {kind, id, name, animated, frames, columns, rows, tile_width, tile_height, width, height, phases[] (0..1 position of each tile in the preview loop), times_us[] (the same in microseconds), loop_us (length of the hover loop), preview? ({url, frames, fps, width, height} of the JPEG sprite), png_base64, note (what the tiles show for this kind)}.

Example — See how a transition plays:

```json
{"id":"mix","kind":"transition"}
```

Example — An In animation in 8 steps:

```json
{"columns":4,"frames":8,"id":"in_pop","kind":"animation"}
```

Example — Before/after of a filter:

```json
{"columns":4,"frames":4,"id":"film","kind":"filter"}
```

## Media

9 commands: `media.create_proxy`, `media.delete`, `media.generate`, `media.get`, `media.import`, `media.list`, `media.relink`, `media.rename`, `media.usage`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/media.html

### media.create_proxy

**Create proxy** · MCP tool `media_create_proxy` · `POST /api/v1/commands/media.create_proxy` · UI: Library/Media/Create proxy

Generates a low-resolution proxy of a video (540p on the short side, H.264, short GOP for fast seeking) in the background, like CapCut's "Create proxy". The player and timeline decode the proxy instead of the original for smooth preview of 4K/HEVC footage; export always uses the original. The command returns immediately with status "started" (or "running" if a job is already in progress, or "ready" when a proxy for the current file already exists — then proxy_path is set right away). Progress is published as media.import.progress events with stage "proxy"; when done the material's proxy_path is saved and a media.ready event with stage "proxy" is sent. Only videos can have proxies.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `material_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the material (imported media item), e.g. "mat_1a2b3c4d5e6f". Get it from media.list or media.import. |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `force` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Regenerate the proxy even if one already exists for this file. |

**Returns:** {material_id, status: "started"|"running"|"ready", proxy_path}.

Example — Create a proxy for a 4K clip:

```json
{"material_id":"mat_1a2b3c4d5e6f","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### media.delete

**Remove media** · MCP tool `media_delete` · `POST /api/v1/commands/media.delete` · undoable · UI: Library/Media/Delete

Removes a material from the project's media library (Media panel → right-click → Delete). Like CapCut, every timeline segment that uses it is removed from all tracks too: on the main track with the magnet on, the following clips shift left to close the gap; a transition leading into a removed clip is dropped; overlay/audio tracks that become empty are removed (the main track is kept). The file on disk is never touched and cached thumbnails are kept so edit.undo restores everything instantly.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `material_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the material (imported media item), e.g. "mat_1a2b3c4d5e6f". Get it from media.list or media.import. |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |

**Returns:** {deleted: true, material_id, removed_segments: [segment ids], removed_tracks: [track ids]}.

Example — Remove a clip from the project:

```json
{"material_id":"mat_1a2b3c4d5e6f","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### media.generate

**Generate media** · MCP tool `media_generate` · `POST /api/v1/commands/media.generate` · undoable · UI: Library/Stickers/Generated

Creates a procedural media file — a background, texture, pattern, test card or countdown drawn by the engine itself (no stock footage, nothing downloaded) — and adds it to the project as a normal material, like CapCut's generated/stock backgrounds but fully original and offline. Still kinds (solid colours, still gradients, grids, checkers, stripes, textures, patterns, colour bars without tone) are written as a PNG (material type photo, duration 0: it can be stretched to any length on the timeline); banner and frame are PNGs with a transparent background meant for an overlay track; kinds that move (speed > 0, noise, countdowns, timers) or make sound (colour-bar tone, countdown beeps) are rendered frame by frame and encoded to an H.264 MP4 of duration_us (material type video). Files go to <project>/cache/generated/ and are reused when the same kind, params, size, duration and fps are asked again (cached = true; the existing material is returned instead of a duplicate). Pick a ready-made look with preset_id (ids from library.list kind=generated, e.g. "sunset_gradient", "neon_floor", "countdown_5", "film_grain") — params then override single preset values — or give kind + params yourself. Size defaults to the project canvas; videos use the canvas fps (or 30) and even pixel sizes. With add_to_timeline the new material is also placed in the same undo step, exactly like timeline.segment.add: on the main track at the clip boundary nearest at_us (magnet), or appended to the end of the main track when at_us is omitted; track_id / new_track choose another track (e.g. an overlay track for grain, confetti, light leaks, film dust, banners or frames on top of a clip — light_leak and film_dust are drawn on black for segment.set_blend mode screen). Moving backgrounds with a loop param (mesh, aurora, lava, plasma, bokeh, particles, light_leak) repeat seamlessly every loop seconds, which is also their default length. Rendering runs while the command executes (typically 2-10 s for 5 s of 1080p video); duration_us is limited to 60 s — for longer backgrounds use a still kind or add the clip several times. Undo removes the material (and the placed clip); the cached file stays on disk. Kinds: • solid — a flat colour card (PNG) — backgrounds, chroma-key plates, fade cards. Params: color (color, default "#000000"): Fill colour.. • gradient — a smooth linear or radial colour gradient (PNG, or a flowing video when speed > 0).
