Params: colors (colors, 2-6, default ["#FF7A59","#7B2FF7"]): Colour stops, evenly spaced, from start to end (2-6).; type (enum linear|radial, default "linear"): linear = along angle; radial = from the centre outwards.; angle (number -360..360, default 135): Direction of a linear gradient in degrees: 0 = left to right, 90 = top to bottom.; speed (number 0..5, default 0): Colour flow speed in back-and-forth cycles per 10 seconds. 0 = a still picture (PNG).. • color_bars — a test card of vertical colour bars (PNG, or a video with a sine tone when tone = true). Params: style (enum classic|rainbow|retro, default "classic"): classic = broadcast-style 75% bars with a lower calibration row; rainbow = 12 hues over a grey step wedge; retro = muted 70s palette.; tone (boolean, default false): Add a continuous sine test tone (the output becomes a video with sound).; tone_hz (number 100..8000, default 1000): Frequency of the test tone in hertz.. • noise — film grain, TV static, paper and soft cloudy textures from value noise (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: color (color, default "#808080"): Base colour; the noise brightens and darkens it.; color2 (color): Optional second colour: the noise blends between color and color2 instead of brightening/darkening.; amount (number 0..1, default 0.5): Strength (contrast) of the noise.; scale (number 1..400, default 1): Grain size in pixels at 1080p height: 1-2 = fine grain/static, 100+ = soft clouds.; octaves (integer 1..5, default 1): Layers of finer detail added on top (fractal noise); 3-4 for paper and smoke.; monochrome (boolean, default true): Same noise in R, G and B (false = coloured RGB noise).; speed (number 0..4, default 1): How fast the noise changes: 1 = 24 new grain patterns per second (soft noise drifts smoothly). 0 = a still picture (PNG).; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 1): Random seed: another number gives another pattern.. • shapes — circles, rounded squares, triangles and rings drifting over a colour (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: shape (enum mixed|circle|square|triangle|ring, default "mixed"): Which shapes to draw.; count (integer 1..80, default 18): Number of shapes.; colors (colors, 1-8, default ["#FF5C8A","#FFD23F","#3EC1D3","#9B5DE5","#00F5D4"]): Shape colours, used in turn.; background (color, default "#16161D"): Background colour.; size (number 0.01..0.5, default 0.07): Average shape radius as a fraction of the frame height.; opacity (number 0.1..1, default 0.9): Shape opacity.; speed (number 0..5, default 1): Drift speed (1 = calm). 0 = a still picture (PNG).; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 7): Random seed for positions, sizes and directions.. • countdown — a numeric countdown (from N to 1, one number per second by default) as a video. Params: from (integer 1..60, default 5): First number; the clip counts down to 1. Default length = from seconds.; style (enum ring|plain|film, default "ring"): ring = number inside an emptying progress ring; plain = big fading numbers; film = projector-leader look with a sweeping wedge and crosshair (use a light background).; background (color, default "#111114"): Background colour.; color (color, default "#FFFFFF"): Colour of the numbers (and of the film-style circles).; accent (color, default "#FF3B5C"): Colour of the progress ring / sweeping wedge.; beep (boolean, default false): Add a short beep at every number (the video gets a sound track).. • grid — a line grid — flat (blueprint, graph paper) or a perspective floor running to the horizon (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: style (enum flat|perspective, default "flat"): flat = square grid; perspective = floor grid towards a horizon with a sky above.; color (color, default "#FFFFFF"): Line colour.; background (color, default "#101018"): Background (floor) colour.; color2 (color): Sky colour at the top of a perspective grid (default: the background colour).; cells (integer 2..64, default 12): Number of grid cells across the frame width.; thickness (number 0.5..20, default 2): Line thickness in pixels at 1080p height.; glow (boolean, default false): Soft neon glow around the lines (and on the horizon).; speed (number 0..5, default 0): Scroll speed in cells per second (towards the viewer). 0 = a still picture (PNG).. • checker — a two-colour checkerboard, optionally rotated and scrolling (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: color (color, default "#FFFFFF"): First square colour.; color2 (color, default "#D9D9E0"): Second square colour.; cells (integer 2..128, default 8): Number of squares across the frame width.; angle (number -180..180, default 0): Rotation of the pattern in degrees.; speed (number 0..5, default 0): Diagonal scroll speed in squares per second. 0 = a still picture (PNG).. • stripes — diagonal or straight stripes in 2-6 colours, optionally moving like a barber pole (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: colors (colors, 2-6, default ["#FFD23F","#1B1B1F"]): Stripe colours, repeated in order.; width (number 0.005..0.5, default 0.06): Width of one stripe as a fraction of the frame height.; angle (number -180..180, default 45): Stripe direction in degrees: 0 = vertical stripes, 90 = horizontal.; speed (number 0..10, default 0): Movement in stripes per second. 0 = a still picture (PNG).. • mesh — a soft modern mesh gradient: colour clouds blended into each other, slowly drifting in a seamless loop (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: colors (colors, 2-6, default ["#FF9A8B","#FF6A88","#FF99AC","#FAD0C4","#A18CD1"]): Colours of the blended clouds (2-6).; softness (number 0..1, default 0.5): 0 = distinct colour patches, 1 = very soft, misty blending.; grain (number 0..0.3, default 0.04): Fine film grain on top (0 = clean).; speed (number 0..3, default 1): How far the colour clouds drift (1 = calm). 0 = a still picture (PNG).; loop (number 2..30, default 8): Seconds until the motion repeats exactly (seamless loop); also the default clip length.; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 3): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • aurora — northern lights: glowing curtains of light waving over a starry night sky (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: colors (colors, 2-4, default ["#00FFA3","#00C2FF","#B026FF"]): Curtain colours from the bottom edge of the light upwards.; background (color, default "#040714"): Night sky colour at the top.; color2 (color, default "#0A2A3C"): Sky colour near the horizon (bottom).; stars (boolean, default true): Twinkling stars in the sky.; landscape (boolean, default true): Dark mountain and forest silhouette along the bottom.; speed (number 0..3, default 1): Wave speed of the curtains. 0 = a still picture (PNG).; loop (number 2..30, default 10): Seconds until the motion repeats exactly (seamless loop); also the default clip length.; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 5): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • lava — glossy blobs that rise, sink, merge and split like a lava lamp (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: colors (colors, 1-4, default ["#FFB000","#FF3D6E","#B5179E"]): Blob colours from top to bottom of the frame.; background (color, default "#1B0B2E"): Background colour at the top.; color2 (color, default "#3A0D4F"): Background colour at the bottom.; count (integer 2..16, default 7): Number of blobs.; size (number 0.04..0.3, default 0.13): Blob radius as a fraction of the frame height.; speed (number 0..3, default 1): Rise/sink speed. 0 = a still picture (PNG).; loop (number 2..30, default 10): Seconds until the motion repeats exactly (seamless loop); also the default clip length.; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 11): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • plasma — a retro demo-scene plasma: interfering colour waves cycling through a palette (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: colors (colors, 2-6, default ["#120458","#7A04EB","#FF00A0","#FE75FE","#00F0FF"]): Palette the waves cycle through.; scale (number 0.3..6, default 1.5): Wave density: higher = more, smaller ripples.; speed (number 0..3, default 1): Wave speed. 0 = a still picture (PNG).; loop (number 2..30, default 8): Seconds until the motion repeats exactly (seamless loop); also the default clip length.; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 2): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • bokeh — out-of-focus light discs drifting and twinkling over a dark gradient, like city lights behind a lens (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: colors (colors, 1-6, default ["#FFD27A","#FF9F5A","#FFF2C4"]): Light colours.; background (color, default "#120E1C"): Background colour at the top.; color2 (color, default "#2B1B2E"): Background colour at the bottom.; count (integer 4..150, default 36): Number of light discs.; size (number 0.01..0.3, default 0.08): Average disc radius as a fraction of the frame height.; softness (number 0..1, default 0.35): Edge softness: 0 = crisp discs, 1 = very blurry.; speed (number 0..3, default 1): Drift speed. 0 = a still picture (PNG).; loop (number 2..30, default 10): Seconds until the motion repeats exactly (seamless loop); also the default clip length.; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 8): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • particles — light particles: floating dust, fireflies, falling snow, twinkling stars or rising embers (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: style (enum dust|fireflies|snow|stars|embers, default "dust"): dust = slow glowing motes; fireflies = wandering pulsing green-gold lights; snow = flakes falling with a sway; stars = twinkling starfield; embers = sparks rising and flickering.; color (color, default "#FFFFFF"): Particle colour (fireflies and embers tint it warmer).; background (color, default "#0B0F1A"): Background colour at the top.; color2 (color): Optional background colour at the bottom (vertical gradient).; count (integer 10..800, default 160): Number of particles.; size (number 0.2..5, default 1): Particle size multiplier.; speed (number 0..3, default 1): Movement speed. 0 = a still picture (PNG).; loop (number 2..30, default 8): Seconds until the motion repeats exactly (seamless loop); also the default clip length.; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 4): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • light_leak — film light leaks, burns, prism streaks and lens flares on black — put it on an overlay track with the Screen (or Add) blend mode (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: style (enum leak|burn|prism|flare, default "leak"): leak = soft warm glows drifting in from the edges; burn = hot film burn flaring from one side; prism = rainbow streaks sweeping across; flare = lens flare with a moving source, streak and ghost rings.; colors (colors, 1-5, default ["#FF3D00","#FF8A00","#FFC14D"]): Light colours (prism uses a rainbow when only defaults are given).; intensity (number 0.2..1.5, default 1): Brightness of the light.; speed (number 0..3, default 1): Movement speed. 0 = a still picture (PNG).; loop (number 2..30, default 6): Seconds until the motion repeats exactly (seamless loop); also the default clip length.; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 9): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • film_dust — old-film dirt on black: dust specks, hairs and vertical scratches flickering every frame — use the Screen blend mode on top of a clip (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: color (color, default "#FFFFFF"): Colour of the dirt.; amount (number 0..1, default 0.5): How much dirt.; speed (number 0..2, default 1): 1 = new dirt 12 times per second, like a projector. 0 = a still picture (PNG).; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 6): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • texture — a still material texture: paper, kraft paper, grunge wall, concrete, canvas, denim, marble, watercolour paper or wood (PNG). Params: style (enum paper|kraft|grunge|concrete|canvas|denim|marble|watercolor|wood, default "paper"): Material to imitate.; color (color): Base colour (default depends on the style).; color2 (color): Accent colour: fibres, stains, veins, watercolour blooms or grain (default depends on the style).; amount (number 0..1, default 0.5): Strength of the texture detail.; scale (number 0.25..4, default 1): Size of the texture features.; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 7): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • pattern — a decorative repeating pattern — memphis, waves, polka dots, halftone, terrazzo, chevron, honeycomb, gingham, scales, dot grid, isometric cubes or triangle mosaic (PNG, or a slowly scrolling video when speed > 0). Params: style (enum memphis|waves|dots|halftone|terrazzo|chevron|honeycomb|gingham|scales|dot_grid|cubes|triangles, default "memphis"): Pattern design.; colors (colors, 2-6, default ["#FFF4E6","#FF6B6B","#4ECDC4","#FFD93D","#6A4C93"]): Background colour first, then the pattern colours.; scale (number 2..64, default 8): Pattern repeats across the frame width.; angle (number -180..180, default 0): Rotation of the pattern in degrees.; speed (number 0..5, default 0): Diagonal scroll speed in repeats per second. 0 = a still picture (PNG).; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 12): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • timer — a styled countdown video from N to 1 — flip clock, neon ring, progress bar, vanishing dots or pop-art bursts. Params: from (integer 1..60, default 5): First number; the clip counts down to 1. Default length = from seconds.; style (enum flip|neon|bar|dots|pop, default "flip"): flip = split-flap clock cards that flip every second; neon = glowing ring and digits; bar = big number over a shrinking progress bar; dots = a ring of dots that go out one by one; pop = the number punches in over a coloured starburst.; background (color, default "#121216"): Background colour.; color (color, default "#FFFFFF"): Colour of the numbers.; accent (color, default "#FF3B5C"): Accent colour (cards, ring, bar, dots, bursts).; beep (boolean, default false): Add a short beep at every number (the video gets a sound track).. • banner — a text-free banner shape on a transparent background — lower third, pill, tab, ribbon, glass panel, news bar or brush stroke — to put your own text on (PNG with alpha). Params: style (enum lower_third|pill|tab|ribbon|glass|news|brush, default "lower_third"): Banner design.; color (color, default "#FFFFFF"): Main panel colour.; color2 (color, default "#FF3B5C"): Accent colour (bars, tags, ribbon ends, icon slot).; position (enum bottom|center|top, default "bottom"): Vertical position in the frame.; width (number 0.2..1, default 0.6): Banner width as a fraction of the frame width.. • frame — a border overlay with a transparent centre — film strip, neon, instant photo, vignette, torn paper, viewfinder, rounded, postage stamp or double line (PNG with alpha). Params: style (enum film|neon|polaroid|vignette|torn|viewfinder|rounded|stamp|double, default "rounded"): Frame design.; color (color, default "#FFFFFF"): Main frame colour (vignette: the shadow colour).; color2 (color, default "#FF3B5C"): Accent colour (neon glow, viewfinder REC dot, inner line).; thickness (number 0.01..0.25, default 0.05): Border thickness as a fraction of the frame height..

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `add_to_timeline` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Also place the material on the timeline (same undo step), following timeline.segment.add's rules. |
| `at_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | With add_to_timeline: where the clip should start (main track: nearest clip boundary). Default: appended to the end of the main track. |
| `duration_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 100000 … 60000000 | Length of a generated video (moving or sounding kinds). Default 5000000 (5 s); countdowns default to from × 1 s. For still pictures (PNG) it only sets the length of the clip placed by add_to_timeline (default 5 s). |
| `fps` | number (frames per second) | no |  | 1 … 60 | Frame rate of a generated video. Default: the project canvas fps, or 30. |
| `height` | integer (pixels) | no |  | 16 … 4096 | Output height in pixels. Default: the project canvas height (1080 for 16:9). Videos round down to an even number. |
| `kind` | string | no |  | `solid`, `gradient`, `color_bars`, `noise`, `shapes`, `countdown`, `grid`, `checker`, `stripes`, `mesh`, `aurora`, `lava`, `plasma`, `bokeh`, `particles`, `light_leak`, `film_dust`, `texture`, `pattern`, `timer`, `banner`, `frame` | What to generate: solid, gradient, color_bars, noise, shapes, countdown, grid, checker, stripes, mesh, aurora, lava, plasma, bokeh, particles, light_leak, film_dust, texture, pattern, timer, banner, frame. Required unless preset_id is given (must then match the preset's kind). |
| `name` | string | no |  |  | Display name of the new material in the Media panel. Default: the preset name, or the kind title (e.g. "Gradient"). |
| `new_track` | boolean | no |  |  | With add_to_timeline: put the clip on a brand-new overlay track (e.g. grain or confetti over existing clips). |
| `params` | object | no |  |  | Kind-specific settings, e.g. {"colors": ["#FF5E62", "#FFD86F"], "angle": 90} for a gradient or {"from": 3, "beep": true} for a countdown. Colours are "#RRGGBB"; numbers outside their range are rejected. Omitted keys use the defaults listed per kind in the description. |
| `preset_id` | string | no |  |  | Ready-made generator from library.list kind=generated (e.g. "sunset_gradient", "aurora_flow", "paper", "neon_floor", "countdown_5", "bars_tone"). Sets kind and params; params you also pass override single values. |
| `track_id` | string | no |  |  | With add_to_timeline: destination track (main_video or video_overlay). Default: the main track. |
| `width` | integer (pixels) | no |  | 16 … 4096 | Output width in pixels. Default: the project canvas width (1920 for 16:9). Videos round down to an even number. |

**Returns:** {material_id, material, kind, preset_id?, params (all values incl. defaults), output: "png"|"mp4", path, width, height, duration_us (0 for a still picture), fps?, has_audio, cached, track_id?, segment_id?, segment?} — the generated material, and the placed clip when add_to_timeline is true.

Example — Sunset gradient at the playhead on the main track:

```json
{"add_to_timeline":true,"at_us":0,"preset_id":"sunset_gradient","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Vertical two-colour gradient for a 9:16 story:

```json
{"height":1920,"kind":"gradient","params":{"angle":90,"colors":["#FF5E62","#FFD86F"]},"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","width":1080}
```

Example — 3-2-1 countdown with beeps:

```json
{"kind":"countdown","params":{"beep":true,"from":3},"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — 10 s of film grain on a new overlay track:

```json
{"add_to_timeline":true,"at_us":0,"duration_us":10000000,"new_track":true,"preset_id":"film_grain","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — 2 s black card at the start:

```json
{"add_to_timeline":true,"at_us":0,"duration_us":2000000,"kind":"solid","params":{"color":"#000000"},"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Seamless northern-lights background (10 s loop):

```json
{"add_to_timeline":true,"at_us":0,"preset_id":"aurora_north","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Neon border frame (transparent PNG) on a new overlay track:

```json
{"add_to_timeline":true,"at_us":0,"duration_us":5000000,"new_track":true,"preset_id":"frame_neon","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### media.get

**Get media** · MCP tool `media_get` · `POST /api/v1/commands/media.get`

Returns one material with everything known about it: the probed metadata, whether the file is missing, every timeline segment that uses it (track, segment id, timeline and source ranges), which background assets are ready (thumbnail, waveform, filmstrip, proxy) and the URLs of its preview endpoints. Use it to check a file after media.import or before deleting media that is in use.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `material_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the material (imported media item), e.g. "mat_1a2b3c4d5e6f". Get it from media.list or media.import. |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |

**Returns:** {…Material, in_use, use_count, missing, thumbnail_url, frame_url?, waveform_url?, usage: [{track_id, track_type, segment_id, start_us, end_us, source_start_us, source_duration_us}], assets: {thumbnail, waveform, filmstrip, proxy, proxy_running}}.

Example — Inspect a material:

```json
{"material_id":"mat_1a2b3c4d5e6f","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### media.import

**Import media** · MCP tool `media_import` · `POST /api/v1/commands/media.import` · undoable · hotkey Ctrl+I · UI: Library/Media/Import

Imports video, photo and audio files into the project's media library — the Import button of the Media panel (left panel → Media → Local), the native file dialog, or dropping files onto the window. Every file is probed with ffprobe: type (video / photo / audio, detected from the streams and extension; animated GIFs are videos, single-frame GIFs are photos), duration (photos get 0 because they can be stretched to any length), display width/height (already swapped for 90°/270° rotated phone videos), rotation, frame rate, video/audio codecs, sample rate, channels and file size. A folder path imports the supported media files directly inside it (not recursive, max 500). Files already in the project (same path) are not imported twice: they are reported in duplicates with their existing material_id. Files that cannot be imported (missing, relative path, not a media file) are reported in errors without failing the whole import; the command only fails when nothing at all could be imported. Importing does NOT place anything on the timeline — call timeline.segment.add with the returned material ids for that. After the command returns, thumbnails, the filmstrip and audio waveforms are generated in the background: watch the media.import.progress events and media.ready (data.stage = "assets") on the event stream; the thumbnail/frame/waveform endpoints also work immediately (they generate on demand).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `paths` | string[] | yes |  |  | Absolute paths of files (or folders) on the machine running Kadr, e.g. ["C:\\Users\\me\\Videos\\clip.mp4"]. Surrounding quotes and file:// URLs are accepted. |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |

**Returns:** {materials: [Material], duplicates: [{path, material_id}], errors: [{path, code, message}]}. Material = {id, type (video|photo|audio), name, path, duration_us, width, height, rotation, fps, video_codec, has_audio, audio_codec, sample_rate, channels, size_bytes, imported_at}.

Example — Import a clip and a song:

```json
{"paths":["C:\\Users\\me\\Videos\\beach.mp4","C:\\Users\\me\\Music\\summer.mp3"],"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Import every media file of a folder:

```json
{"paths":["/home/me/Footage/trip"],"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### media.list

**List media** · MCP tool `media_list` · `POST /api/v1/commands/media.list` · UI: Library/Media

Lists the materials (imported files) of the project in import order — the cards of the Media panel. Each item has the full probed metadata plus live information: in_use/use_count (how many timeline segments use it; the UI shows an "Added" mark), missing (the file is no longer on disk — fix it with media.relink) and the relative URLs of its thumbnail, source frame and waveform endpoints (append ?token=… or send the API token). Use the ids with timeline.segment.add to place media on the timeline.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `query` | string | no |  |  | Optional case-insensitive filter on the material name (the Media panel search box). |
| `type` | string | no |  | `video`, `photo`, `audio` | Only return materials of this type (the Media panel's type filter). Omit for all imported media. |

**Returns:** Array of {…Material, in_use, use_count, missing, thumbnail_url, frame_url?, waveform_url?}.

Example — All media:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Only audio:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","type":"audio"}
```

### media.relink

**Relink media** · MCP tool `media_relink` · `POST /api/v1/commands/media.relink` · undoable · UI: Library/Media/Relink

Points a material at another file — CapCut's "Link media" for files that were moved or renamed (the card shows a missing badge). The new file is probed and must be the same kind (video, photo or audio); the material keeps its id, so every timeline clip using it follows automatically. Metadata (duration, size, codecs…) is refreshed, the old proxy is dropped and thumbnails/waveform/filmstrip are regenerated in the background. If the new file is shorter than ranges used on the timeline, those segment ids are listed in warnings (the clips are left unchanged; trim them with timeline.segment.trim).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `material_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the material (imported media item), e.g. "mat_1a2b3c4d5e6f". Get it from media.list or media.import. |
| `path` | string | yes |  |  | Absolute path of the replacement file on the machine running Kadr. |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |

**Returns:** {material: Material, warnings: [{segment_id, message}]}.

Example — Relink a moved file:

```json
{"material_id":"mat_1a2b3c4d5e6f","path":"D:\\Footage\\beach.mp4","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### media.rename

**Rename media** · MCP tool `media_rename` · `POST /api/v1/commands/media.rename` · undoable · UI: Library/Media/Rename

Changes the display name of a material in the Media panel (right-click → Rename). Only the name shown in Kadr changes — the file on disk keeps its name. Timeline clips show the new name as their label.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `material_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the material (imported media item), e.g. "mat_1a2b3c4d5e6f". Get it from media.list or media.import. |
| `name` | string | yes |  |  | New display name; leading/trailing spaces are removed, must not be empty (max 255 characters). |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |

**Returns:** The updated Material.

Example — Rename:

```json
{"material_id":"mat_1a2b3c4d5e6f","name":"Intro drone shot","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### media.usage

**Media usage** · MCP tool `media_usage` · `POST /api/v1/commands/media.usage`

Lists every timeline segment that uses a material, on all tracks (main track, overlays, audio tracks). An empty list means the material is only in the media library. CapCut warns before deleting media that is in use; call this first to know which clips media.delete would remove.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `material_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the material (imported media item), e.g. "mat_1a2b3c4d5e6f". Get it from media.list or media.import. |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |

**Returns:** {material_id, count, segments: [{track_id, track_type, segment_id, start_us, end_us, source_start_us, source_duration_us}]}.

Example — Where is this clip used?:

```json
{"material_id":"mat_1a2b3c4d5e6f","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

## Playback

9 commands: `playback.pause`, `playback.play`, `playback.seek`, `playback.state`, `playback.step`, `playback.toggle`, `preview.contact_sheet`, `preview.frame`, `preview.layout`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/playback.html

### playback.pause

**Pause** · MCP tool `playback_pause` · `POST /api/v1/commands/playback.pause` · UI: Player/Pause

Pauses playback, leaving the playhead where playback reached (pressing Pause under the player). Pausing when nothing is playing is harmless and just returns the current state. Publishes a playback.state event {playing:false, time_us} and moves the playhead (playhead.moved). Use playback.seek afterwards to put the playhead at an exact time.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |

**Returns:** {playing, time_us, duration_us, fps}: time_us is the playhead after the command.

Example — Pause:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### playback.play

**Play** · MCP tool `playback_play` · `POST /api/v1/commands/playback.play` · UI: Player/Play

Starts playback from the playhead (or from from_us), like pressing Play under the player. If the playhead is at the end of the timeline, playback starts over from 0. While playing, the engine advances the playhead about 10 times per second (playhead.moved events, source "playback") and stops by itself at the end; the editor shows the composited stream (/stream) with sound (/audio). Publishes a playback.state event {playing, time_us}. Playing an empty timeline does nothing and returns playing=false. Playback state is not saved in the project and is not undoable.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `from_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Optional start time. Defaults to the current playhead position. |

**Returns:** {playing, time_us, duration_us, fps}: time_us is the playhead after the command.

Example — Play from the playhead:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Play from 5 seconds:

```json
{"from_us":5000000,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### playback.seek

**Seek** · MCP tool `playback_seek` · `POST /api/v1/commands/playback.seek` · UI: Timeline/Ruler click

Moves the playhead to time_us — clicking or dragging on the timeline ruler. The player then shows the frame at that time (render it yourself with preview.frame). If playback is running it continues from the new position (a playback.state event with the new time_us is published). Times are not clamped to the timeline length (CapCut lets the playhead sit past the last clip); negative values become 0. Publishes playhead.moved. Not undoable; does not modify the project.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `time_us` | integer (microseconds) | yes |  |  | Target playhead time in microseconds (2.5 s = 2500000). |

**Returns:** {playing, time_us, duration_us, fps}: time_us is the playhead after the command.

Example — Go to 2.5 seconds:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","time_us":2500000}
```

### playback.state

**Playback state** · MCP tool `playback_state` · `POST /api/v1/commands/playback.state` · UI: Player

Returns whether the project is playing, the current playhead time (advancing in real time while playing), the timeline duration and the project frame rate. Use it to poll playback started by the user or another client, or subscribe to playback.state / playhead.moved events on the WebSocket instead.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |

**Returns:** {playing, time_us, duration_us, fps}: time_us is the playhead after the command.

Example — Is it playing?:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### playback.step

**Step frame** · MCP tool `playback_step` · `POST /api/v1/commands/playback.step` · hotkey Left/Right · UI: Keyboard

Moves the playhead exactly one frame (1/fps of the project frame rate, e.g. 33333 µs at 30 fps) backward or forward — the Left/Right arrow keys. The playhead is first snapped to the frame grid, so repeated steps land on frame boundaries. Pauses playback if it is running. Stepping stops at 0 and at the end of the timeline. Publishes playhead.moved.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `direction` | string | yes |  | `backward`, `forward` | "backward" (Left arrow) or "forward" (Right arrow). |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |

**Returns:** {playing, time_us, duration_us, fps}: time_us is the playhead after the command.

Example — Next frame:

```json
{"direction":"forward","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### playback.toggle

**Play / Pause** · MCP tool `playback_toggle` · `POST /api/v1/commands/playback.toggle` · hotkey Space · UI: Player/Play button

Toggles between playing and paused — the Space key and the round play button under the player. When starting, playback begins at the playhead (from 0 if the playhead is at the end) and the engine advances the playhead in real time until the end of the timeline. When pausing, the playhead stays where playback reached. Publishes playback.state {playing, time_us}; every connected editor and API client sees the change.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |

**Returns:** {playing, time_us, duration_us, fps}: time_us is the playhead after the command.

Example — Play or pause:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### preview.contact_sheet

**Contact sheet** · MCP tool `preview_contact_sheet` · `POST /api/v1/commands/preview.contact_sheet` · UI: Player

Renders several evenly spaced frames of the project into one PNG grid (a contact sheet) so an AI agent can review the whole edit — pacing, cuts, text and overlays — in a single image instead of calling preview.frame many times. Frames are sampled at the centre of `count` equal slices of [start_us, end_us) (default: the whole timeline) and laid out left-to-right, top-to-bottom; times_us lists the time of each tile in that order. Uses the same renderer as the player and export. Read-only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `columns` | integer | no | `4` | 1 … 12 | Number of tiles per row; rows are added as needed. |
| `count` | integer | no | `12` | 1 … 48 | Number of frames (tiles) to render. |
| `end_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | End of the sampled range. Defaults to the end of the last segment. |
| `start_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Start of the sampled range. Defaults to 0 (timeline start). |
| `tile_width` | integer (pixels) | no | `320` | 32 … 960 | Width of each tile; the tile height follows the canvas aspect ratio. |

**Returns:** {width, height, columns, rows, tile_width, tile_height, times_us[], png_base64, warnings?}.

Example — Overview of the whole video:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Six frames of the first 10 seconds:

```json
{"columns":3,"count":6,"end_us":10000000,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### preview.frame

**Render frame** · MCP tool `preview_frame` · `POST /api/v1/commands/preview.frame` · UI: Player

Renders the composited picture of the project at one timeline time — exactly what the player shows and what export will contain, because the same renderer is used: every visible track in order (main video, overlays, stickers, text, then filter/effect/adjustment tracks applied to everything below them), transforms, crop, opacity, blend modes, masks, chroma key, filters, adjustments, effects, animations, keyframes and transitions. Use it after edits to SEE the result. Returns the frame as base64 PNG plus `url`, the binary endpoint GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/frame (add the API token as Authorization header or ?token=; supports &w=, &h= and &format=png|jpeg). time_us defaults to the playhead; times past the end show only the canvas background. The height follows the canvas aspect ratio. Missing or undecodable media is skipped and listed in `warnings`. Read-only: the project and playhead are not changed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `time_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Timeline time to render (1 second = 1000000). Defaults to the current playhead position. |
| `width` | integer (pixels) | no | `640` | 16 … 3840 | Output width in pixels; the height is derived from the canvas aspect ratio (640 → 640x360 for 16:9). |

**Returns:** {width, height, time_us, png_base64, url, warnings?, note}: png_base64 is the PNG file encoded as base64; url is the path of the same frame on the /frame endpoint (JPEG by default).

Example — Look at the frame 2 seconds into the video:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","time_us":2000000}
```

Example — Small preview at the playhead:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","width":320}
```

### preview.layout

**Canvas layout** · MCP tool `preview_layout` · `POST /api/v1/commands/preview.layout` · UI: Player

Returns where every visible clip is drawn on the canvas at one moment — the boxes the player uses for on-canvas selection, move/scale/rotate handles and snapping, and that agents can use to reason about composition (e.g. 'is the title over the face?'). Covers video, photo, sticker and text segments of visible tracks (effects, filters, adjustments and audio have no box). Coordinates are canvas pixels of Project.Canvas (e.g. 1920x1080), origin top-left, +y down. Each box gives the unrotated rectangle x, y, w, h, its centre cx, cy, rotation in degrees clockwise around the centre and the four rotated corners; w/h include crop, fit, transform.scale, keyframes and the current In/Out/Combo animation (exactly the renderer's placement); text boxes are the rendered text image (incl. stroke, shadow, box). transform holds the keyframed values without animation (what segment.set_transform edits) and base_w/base_h the size at scale 1, so a handle drag maps back to x = transform.x + dx/(canvas_width/2), scale = new_w/base_w. Boxes are in compositing order: the LAST box is on top, so hit-test from the end. Both clips of a running transition are listed. Read-only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `time_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Timeline time to lay out (1 second = 1000000). Defaults to the current playhead. |

**Returns:** {time_us, canvas_width, canvas_height, boxes:[{segment_id, track_id, track_type, type: video|photo|sticker|text, x, y, w, h, rotation, cx, cy, corners:[[x,y]×4 TL,TR,BR,BL], flip_h?, flip_v?, opacity, z, locked?, animated?, base_w, base_h, transform:{x, y, scale, rotation}, missing?}], warnings?}.

Example — Boxes at the playhead:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Boxes 3 seconds in:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","time_us":3000000}
```

## Presets

6 commands: `presets.apply`, `presets.delete`, `presets.get`, `presets.list`, `presets.rename`, `presets.save`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/presets.html

### presets.apply

**Apply preset** · MCP tool `presets_apply` · `POST /api/v1/commands/presets.apply` · undoable · UI: Library/My kit/Apply

Applies a preset from the user's kit to a clip, like clicking a card in "My kit" with a clip selected. Only the part stored in the preset changes (e.g. a filter preset sets only the filter). This is one undo step. Clips on locked tracks are rejected (conflict); a preset of the wrong kind for the clip fails with invalid_argument and a hint. Kinds and their targets: text_style → text clips (content, word timings and animations of the target are kept); adjust → video, photo and adjustment clips; filter → video, photo, sticker and filter clips; effect → video, photo and sticker clips (merged into the clip's effect list, same id replaced) or effect clips (first effect); transition → the LEFT clip of two touching clips on a video track (duration clamped to half of the shorter clip); animation → video, photo, sticker and text clips (In/Out replace Combo and vice versa, durations fit into the clip; loop and per-letter parts only for text).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preset_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of a saved preset ("pst_…"). Get it from presets.list. |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | Clip to apply the preset to (project.get → tracks[].segments[].id). |

**Returns:** {preset_id, kind, name, segment_id, segment: the updated segment, notes: adjustments made to fit the clip (e.g. a clamped transition duration)}.

Example — Apply a saved caption look to a text clip:

```json
{"preset_id":"pst_4c5d6e7f8a9b","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

### presets.delete

**Delete preset** · MCP tool `presets_delete` · `POST /api/v1/commands/presets.delete` · UI: Library/My kit/Delete

Removes a preset from the user's kit (My kit → card → Delete). Clips that already use the look keep it — presets are copied into clips when applied, never linked. This cannot be undone with edit.undo because the kit is not part of a project.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preset_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of a saved preset ("pst_…"). Get it from presets.list. |

**Returns:** {deleted: preset id, kind}.

Example — Delete a preset:

```json
{"preset_id":"pst_4c5d6e7f8a9b"}
```

### presets.get

**Get preset** · MCP tool `presets_get` · `POST /api/v1/commands/presets.get` · UI: Library/My kit

Returns one preset of the user's kit with all captured values (data.text_style, data.adjust, data.filter, data.effects, data.transition or data.animations depending on kind), so an AI agent can inspect what presets.apply would change before applying it.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preset_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of a saved preset ("pst_…"). Get it from presets.list. |

**Returns:** The preset: {id, kind, name, summary, source, created_at, updated_at, data}.

Example — Inspect a preset:

```json
{"preset_id":"pst_4c5d6e7f8a9b"}
```

### presets.list

**List My kit** · MCP tool `presets_list` · `POST /api/v1/commands/presets.list` · UI: Library/My kit

Lists the presets saved in the user's kit ("My kit" tab), newest first, optionally filtered by kind and by a case-insensitive name/summary search. Use the returned ids with presets.apply, presets.rename and presets.delete. counts reports how many presets exist per kind (before filtering), handy for building the kind navigation. The kit is per user, not per project.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | string | no |  | `text_style`, `adjust`, `filter`, `effect`, `transition`, `animation` | Only presets of this kind (text_style, adjust, filter, effect, transition, animation). |
| `query` | string | no |  |  | Case-insensitive text matched against the preset name and summary. |

**Returns:** {presets: [preset…], total: number returned, kinds: all valid kinds, counts: {kind: n}}.

Example — Everything in the kit:

```json
{}
```

Example — Only text styles:

```json
{"kind":"text_style"}
```

### presets.rename

**Rename preset** · MCP tool `presets_rename` · `POST /api/v1/commands/presets.rename` · UI: Library/My kit/Rename

Renames a preset in the user's kit (My kit → card → Rename). The name is trimmed and may be at most 80 characters; it does not need to be unique. Renaming changes nothing in any project.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes |  |  | New name shown in My kit (1–80 characters). |
| `preset_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of a saved preset ("pst_…"). Get it from presets.list. |

**Returns:** The renamed preset.

Example — Rename a look:

```json
{"name":"Teal & orange","preset_id":"pst_4c5d6e7f8a9b"}
```

### presets.save

**Save to My kit** · MCP tool `presets_save` · `POST /api/v1/commands/presets.save` · UI: Inspector/Add to kit

Saves part of a clip's look as a reusable preset in the user's kit ("My kit" in the left library panel, the "Add to kit" buttons in the inspector). The preset is stored per user in <DataDir>/presets.json, so it is available in every project. kind decides what is captured from segment_id: text_style copies the whole text look (font, size, colour, stroke, shadow, box, glow, gradient fill, extrude, curve, word-art effect, caption highlight) but not the words; adjust copies all colour adjustments; filter, effect, transition and animation copy those settings. Fails with invalid_argument when the clip has nothing of that kind (e.g. no filter). The project is not modified, so this is not an undo step. Re-apply with presets.apply. Kinds and their targets: text_style → text clips (content, word timings and animations of the target are kept); adjust → video, photo and adjustment clips; filter → video, photo, sticker and filter clips; effect → video, photo and sticker clips (merged into the clip's effect list, same id replaced) or effect clips (first effect); transition → the LEFT clip of two touching clips on a video track (duration clamped to half of the shorter clip); animation → video, photo, sticker and text clips (In/Out replace Combo and vice versa, durations fit into the clip; loop and per-letter parts only for text).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | string | yes |  | `text_style`, `adjust`, `filter`, `effect`, `transition`, `animation` | What to capture: text_style (look of a text clip), adjust (colour adjustments incl. HSL/curves/LUT), filter (filter id + intensity), effect (the clip's video effects with their parameters), transition (the transition after the clip), animation (In/Out/Combo plus text loop and per-letter animations). |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | Project that contains the clip to capture (from project.list). |
| `from_segment_id` | string | no |  |  | Alias of segment_id (accepted for compatibility); segment_id wins when both are set. |
| `name` | string | no |  |  | Name shown in My kit (max 80 characters). Default: "<Kind> <n>", e.g. "Text style 3". |
| `segment_id` | string | no |  |  | Clip to capture the look from (project.get → tracks[].segments[].id). Required unless from_segment_id is given. |

**Returns:** The saved preset: {id, kind, name, summary, source (clip type it came from), created_at, updated_at, data: {text_style|adjust|filter|effects|transition|animations}}.

Example — Save a caption look:

```json
{"kind":"text_style","name":"Bold yellow subtitles","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

Example — Save a colour grade:

```json
{"kind":"adjust","name":"Warm evening","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

Example — Save a transition with an automatic name:

```json
{"kind":"transition","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

## Projects

### project.create

**Create project** · MCP tool `project_create` · `POST /api/v1/commands/project.create` · hotkey Ctrl+N · UI: Home/Create project

Creates a new empty project, exactly like pressing "Create project" on the Home screen. Defaults match CapCut: 16:9 canvas at 1920x1080, 30 fps, black background, main-track magnet, auto snapping and linkage enabled. If name is omitted the project is named after today's date (MMDD).

| `name` | string | no |  |  | Project name shown on the Home screen and in the editor title bar. |
| `ratio` | string | no | `"16:9"` | `16:9`, `9:16`, `1:1`, `4:3`, `3:4`, `21:9`, `2.35:1`, `2:1`, `1.85:1`, `5.8-inch` | Canvas aspect ratio. 9:16 is vertical (TikTok/Reels/Shorts), 16:9 is landscape (YouTube), 1:1 is square. |

### project.set_canvas

**Set canvas** · MCP tool `project_set_canvas` · `POST /api/v1/commands/project.set_canvas` · undoable · UI: Player/Ratio

Changes the canvas (output frame) settings — the Ratio menu under the player and the canvas options in the inspector when nothing is selected. Changing the ratio recomputes width/height with the short side at 1080 px; existing clips keep their relative position and scale. Only the supplied fields change.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `background_blur` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Blur strength 0..1 used when background_type is blur. |
| `background_color` | string | no |  |  | Hex color like "#000000" used when background_type is color. |
| `background_type` | string | no |  | `color`, `blur`, `image` | How empty canvas areas are filled: a solid color, a blurred copy of the clip, or an image. |
| `fps` | number (frames per second) | no |  | 1 … 120 | New project frame rate. |
| `ratio` | string | no |  | `16:9`, `9:16`, `1:1`, `4:3`, `3:4`, `21:9`, `2.35:1`, `2:1`, `1.85:1`, `5.8-inch` | New aspect ratio. |

### project.set_cover

**Set cover** · MCP tool `project_set_cover` · `POST /api/v1/commands/project.set_cover` · undoable · UI: Timeline/Main track/Cover

Chooses the project's cover (thumbnail) frame — the Cover button at the start of the main track in CapCut. time_us is a TIMELINE time; the cover is the composited frame at that time (render it with GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/frame?t_us=<cover_us> or preview.frame). It must lie inside the project (0 ≤ time_us < project duration); an empty project has no frames and returns conflict. clear=true removes the choice so the first frame is used again. The value is stored in project.cover_us (null = first frame) and is one undo step. Moving or trimming clips later does not move the cover time.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `clear` | boolean | no |  |  | true = forget the chosen cover and use the first frame (time_us is ignored). |
| `time_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Timeline time of the cover frame in microseconds (1 s = 1000000). Required unless clear is true. |

**Returns:** {cover_us: chosen time or null (first frame), duration_us: project duration}.

Example — Use the frame at 2.5 s as the cover:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","time_us":2500000}
```

Example — Back to the first frame:

```json
{"clear":true,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

## Rendering

3 commands: `render.devices`, `render.settings.get`, `render.settings.set`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/rendering.html

### render.devices

**GPU devices** · MCP tool `render_devices` · `POST /api/v1/commands/render.devices` · UI: Settings/Rendering

Lists the graphics adapters Kadr can render on (Settings → Rendering → GPU): index, name, vendor (nvidia, amd, intel, apple), backend (vulkan, d3d12, metal), device type (discrete, integrated, cpu = software, virtual), total VRAM in MB, the OS budget for Kadr when known, driver, recommended (the high-performance default), supported (has the features Kadr needs; note explains why not), selected (used with the current settings) and effective_cap_mb (the VRAM Kadr would allow itself on that adapter: min(vram_limit_mb or total, total − reserve_mb, OS budget)). The same physical GPU can appear once per backend. available=false means no usable GPU or no wgpu library was found — Kadr then renders on the CPU (same picture, slower) and reason/hint explain it. Use an index or name from here with render.settings.set adapter. Read-only.

No parameters.

**Returns:** {available, adapters[{index, name, vendor, backend, device_type, driver?, vram_total_mb, vram_budget_mb?, recommended, supported, note?, selected, effective_cap_mb}], selected (index into adapters, -1 = CPU), mode, reason?, hint?}.

Example — Which GPUs can Kadr use?:

```json
{}
```

### render.settings.get

**Render settings** · MCP tool `render_settings_get` · `POST /api/v1/commands/render.settings.get` · UI: Settings/Rendering

Returns how Kadr renders previews and exports (Settings → Rendering): mode (auto = GPU when a working adapter exists, otherwise CPU; gpu = GPU only; cpu = always the CPU reference renderer) and where it came from (settings, or env when KADR_RENDER_MODE overrides it), the chosen adapter ("" = recommended), vram_limit_mb (0 = automatic) and reserve_mb (VRAM kept free for Windows/macOS and other apps, default 512), the resulting effective_cap_mb on the selected adapter (Kadr never allocates beyond it: texture pool, caches, frames in flight, decode look-ahead and the number of hardware decoders are sized by it), the adapter's total VRAM, the VRAM Kadr uses right now, and active — the renderer actually in use (kind gpu|cpu, backend, device, and reason when the CPU is used). Example: a 12 GB card with vram_limit_mb 12288 gives an effective cap of 11776 MB. Read-only.

No parameters.

**Returns:** {mode, mode_source settings|env, adapter, vram_limit_mb, reserve_mb, effective_cap_mb (0 = unknown), vram_total_mb, vram_budget_mb?, vram_used_mb, gpu_available, selected_adapter?{…render.devices entry}, active{kind, backend?, device?, vendor?, vram_total_mb?, cap_mb?, used_mb, reason?}, saved{mode, adapter, vram_limit_mb, reserve_mb}, note?, warning?}.

Example — Current render settings:

```json
{}
```

### render.settings.set

**Change render settings** · MCP tool `render_settings_set` · `POST /api/v1/commands/render.settings.set` · UI: Settings/Rendering

Changes how Kadr renders and how much video memory it may use (Settings → Rendering) and saves it in settings.json "render". Only the given fields change. mode: auto (default; GPU when available, else CPU), gpu (refused when no usable GPU exists), cpu (always the CPU renderer). adapter: an index or name from render.devices (or a part of a name such as "RTX 3060"; numbers are indexes), "" = the recommended high-performance one. vram_limit_mb: how much VRAM Kadr may use, 0 = automatic (all of it minus reserve_mb); at least 256 and not more than the adapter's total VRAM (a round size like 12288 on a card the driver reports as 12115 MB is taken as "all of it"). reserve_mb: VRAM always left free for the system (default 512). The effective cap is min(vram_limit_mb or total, total − reserve_mb, OS budget): choosing 12288 on a 12 GB card leaves 512 MB for Windows and uses at most 11776 MB. Applies to the next frame or export, no restart; an export already running keeps its renderer. App setting, not a project edit: not undoable. Calling it without changes returns the current settings with changed=false.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `adapter` | string | no |  |  | GPU to use: index or name from render.devices (a part such as "RTX 3060" is enough; a plain number is an index); "" = the recommended adapter. Omit to keep. |
| `mode` | string | no |  | `auto`, `gpu`, `cpu` | "auto" (GPU when available, otherwise CPU), "gpu" (GPU only) or "cpu" (CPU reference renderer). Omit to keep. |
| `reserve_mb` | integer (megabytes) | no |  | 0 … 65536 | VRAM in MB always left free for the operating system and other apps; 0 = default 512. |
| `vram_limit_mb` | integer (megabytes) | no |  | 0 … 1048576 | Maximum VRAM Kadr may use in MB (1024 MB = 1 GB); 0 = automatic (total minus reserve_mb). At least 256 and at most the adapter's total VRAM. |

**Returns:** Same as render.settings.get plus changed (false when nothing changed) and warning (e.g. the GPU is unavailable so the settings apply once it is, or KADR_RENDER_MODE overrides the mode).

Example — Let Kadr use 12 GB (keeps 512 MB for Windows):

```json
{"vram_limit_mb":12288}
```

Example — Use at most 6 GB:

```json
{"vram_limit_mb":6144}
```

Example — Render on the CPU:

```json
{"mode":"cpu"}
```

Example — Pick the RTX 3060, automatic VRAM:

```json
{"adapter":"RTX 3060","mode":"auto","vram_limit_mb":0}
```

## Smart tools

8 commands: `ai.auto_reframe`, `ai.cancel`, `ai.capabilities`, `ai.detect_scenes`, `ai.jobs`, `ai.remove_background`, `ai.remove_silence`, `ai.split_scenes`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/smart-tools.html

### ai.auto_reframe

**Auto reframe** · MCP tool `ai_auto_reframe` · `POST /api/v1/commands/ai.auto_reframe` · undoable · UI: Toolbar/Auto reframe

Re-frames a clip for another aspect ratio (e.g. landscape 16:9 footage for a 9:16 TikTok/Reels/Shorts canvas) and keeps the main subject in the picture, like CapCut's 'Auto reframe'. The clip is scaled to FILL the target ratio (no bars) and its position is animated with transform.x keyframes (transform.y when the source is taller than the target) that follow the subject: frames are sampled at sample_fps, the subject centre is estimated from motion, edge density and skin-tone cues, and the path is smoothed with a critically damped filter (smoothing 0 = responsive, 1 = very calm camera). Positions are clamped so the clip always covers the canvas. Existing transform.x/y/scale keyframes of the clip are replaced; rotation, crop and animations are kept. With set_canvas=true the project canvas is switched to `ratio` too (other clips are not reframed — run the command for each clip). ratio defaults to the current canvas ratio. Photos get a static best position. Takes about a second per minute of video. One undo step. Undoable.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | Video or photo clip to reframe. |
| `ratio` | string | no |  | `16:9`, `9:16`, `1:1`, `4:3`, `3:4`, `21:9`, `2.35:1`, `2:1`, `1.85:1`, `5.8-inch` | Target aspect ratio, e.g. 9:16 (vertical), 1:1, 4:5-like 3:4, 16:9. Defaults to the project's canvas ratio. |
| `sample_fps` | number | no | `6` | 1 … 15 | Analysis frames per second of video; higher follows fast motion better but is slower. |
| `set_canvas` | boolean | no | `false` |  | true also changes the project canvas to ratio (what CapCut does); false only reframes the clip. |
| `smoothing` | number | no | `0.5` | 0 … 1 | Camera smoothness 0..1: 0 follows quick moves, 1 pans slowly (ignores small motion). |
| `zoom` | number | no | `1` | 1 … 3 | Extra zoom on top of the fill scale (1 = just fill, 1.3 = tighter framing). |

**Returns:** {segment_id, ratio, canvas_width, canvas_height, canvas_changed, scale, axis: x|y|xy|none, samples, keyframes, track:[{time_us (relative to the clip start), x, y}], note}.

Example — Make a landscape clip vertical and switch the canvas:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","ratio":"9:16","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","set_canvas":true}
```

Example — Square crop that follows the subject calmly:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","ratio":"1:1","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","smoothing":0.8}
```

Example — Reframe for the current canvas:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### ai.cancel

**Cancel smart tool job** · MCP tool `ai_cancel` · `POST /api/v1/commands/ai.cancel`

Cancels a queued or running background smart-tool job (e.g. a long background removal). The partial result is discarded and the clips stay as they were; ai.progress reports state 'cancelled'. Cancelling a finished job is a no-op that returns its final state.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `job_id` | string | yes |  |  | Job to cancel (from ai.remove_background or ai.jobs). |

**Returns:** The job {job_id, state, ...} as known when the cancel was requested.

Example — Stop a background removal:

```json
{"job_id":"aij_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### ai.capabilities

**Smart tools status** · MCP tool `ai_capabilities` · `POST /api/v1/commands/ai.capabilities` · UI: Inspector/Video/Remove BG

Reports which smart tools work on this machine. Scene detection, silence removal, auto reframe and video clean-up only need ffmpeg. Background removal needs a local model provider; the report says which one was found (rembg / onnx / torch), the model file and Python used, which Python packages are importable and where models were searched — or, when none is usable, the error and an install hint (e.g. `pip install rembg onnxruntime`, or put an ONNX matting model at <DataDir>/models/matting.onnx / set KADR_MATTING_MODEL). Detection results are cached; pass refresh=true after installing something. Read-only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `refresh` | boolean | no | `false` |  | true re-runs provider detection instead of using the cached result. |

**Returns:** {ffmpeg, background_removal:{available, provider?, model?, python?, packages?, searched_models?, error?, hint?, checked_at}, commands[]}.

Example — What can the smart tools do here?:

```json
{}
```

Example — Re-check after pip install rembg:

```json
{"refresh":true}
```

### ai.detect_scenes

**Detect scenes** · MCP tool `ai_detect_scenes` · `POST /api/v1/commands/ai.detect_scenes` · UI: Toolbar/Split scene

Finds the scene changes (camera cuts) inside a video clip without changing anything. ffmpeg's scene detector scores every frame of the clip's source range by how different it is from the previous frame; frames scoring at least `threshold` are cuts. Cut times are mapped onto the timeline with the clip's speed, speed curve and reverse, so time_us can be passed straight to timeline.segment.split. Use it to preview what ai.split_scenes would do, to place markers, or to pick shots. Takes a few seconds per minute of video (results are cached). Read-only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | Video clip to analyse (timeline.get lists segment ids). |
| `min_scene_us` | integer (microseconds) | no | `500000` | 0 … 600000000 | Shortest scene to keep: cuts closer than this to another (stronger) cut or to the clip edges are ignored (flashes, strobes). |
| `threshold` | number | no | `0.3` | 0.05 … 1 | Scene-change sensitivity: ffmpeg scene score 0..1 a frame must reach. 0.2 = sensitive (also soft cuts), 0.3 = default, 0.5+ = only hard cuts. |

**Returns:** {segment_id, threshold, min_scene_us, frames_analyzed, cuts:[{time_us, source_us, score}], scenes:[{start_us, end_us, duration_us}], note}.

Example — Find the cuts in a clip:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Only hard cuts:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","threshold":0.5}
```

### ai.jobs

**Smart tool jobs** · MCP tool `ai_jobs` · `POST /api/v1/commands/ai.jobs`

Lists background smart-tool jobs (currently background removal started by ai.remove_background without wait) with their state (queued, running, done, failed, cancelled), progress 0..1, frames done and total, estimated seconds left (eta_s, -1 = unknown), the matte file when done, or the error and a hint when failed. The same objects are pushed as 'ai.progress' events. Filter by project_id or fetch one job with job_id. Finished jobs are kept for a while (the last 50). Read-only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `job_id` | string | no |  |  | Return only this job (as a one-element list). |
| `project_id` | string | no |  |  | Only jobs of this project (omit for all projects). |

**Returns:** Array of {job_id, kind, project_id, material_id, segment_ids, provider, model?, state, progress, frames, total_frames, eta_s, matte_path?, error?, hint?, created_at, finished_at?}.

Example — Jobs of a project:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Poll one job:

```json
{"job_id":"aij_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### ai.remove_background

**Remove background** · MCP tool `ai_remove_background` · `POST /api/v1/commands/ai.remove_background` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Video/Remove BG

Removes the background of a video, photo or sticker clip automatically (CapCut's 'Remove background → Auto removal'), leaving the person/main subject on a transparent background so lower tracks or the canvas background show through. A local segmentation model computes a greyscale alpha matte per frame (saved in the project cache and recorded as the material's matte_path); the renderer multiplies it into the clip's alpha, so preview, preview.frame and export agree. The matte belongs to the material, so split or duplicated clips of the same file reuse it. Only the frames the project's clips use (+1 s margin) are processed. Providers are detected at run time (see ai.capabilities): Python `rembg`, or `onnxruntime` with an ONNX matting model (KADR_MATTING_MODEL, <DataDir>/models/matting.onnx or rembg's ~/.u2net cache), or `torch` with a TorchScript model; without one the command fails with not_available and an install hint. Matting is slow (roughly 2-10 frames per second on a CPU): by default the command returns at once with state 'running' and a job_id, publishes 'ai.progress' events and, when the matte is ready, applies it as its own undoable step. Agents can pass wait=true to block until it is done (the project cannot be edited meanwhile) and get state 'done'. When a matte already exists the clip is switched on immediately. enabled=false switches the removal off (the matte is kept for later). Undoable.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | Video, photo or sticker clip whose background to remove. |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | `true` |  | true removes the background (computing the matte if needed); false shows the clip unmasked again. |
| `regenerate` | boolean | no | `false` |  | true recomputes the matte even when a usable one exists (e.g. after installing a better model). |
| `wait` | boolean | no | `false` |  | true blocks until the matte is computed and returns state done (short clips; matting runs at roughly 2-10 frames/s). If the caller disconnects, the job keeps running and is applied when done. false returns at once with a job_id. |

**Returns:** {segment_id, state: done|off|running|queued, enabled, job_id?, provider?, model?, matte_path?, reused?, note}. With state running/queued, follow the job with ai.progress events or ai.jobs{job_id}.

Example — Cut out the person in a clip (background job):

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Agent: wait for the result:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","wait":true}
```

Example — Show the original background again:

```json
{"enabled":false,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### ai.remove_silence

**Remove silence** · MCP tool `ai_remove_silence` · `POST /api/v1/commands/ai.remove_silence` · undoable · UI: Toolbar/Smart tools/Remove silence

Cuts the silent parts out of a clip with sound (talking-head videos, voice-overs, podcasts) and closes the gaps: ffmpeg's silencedetect finds stretches where the clip's own audio stays below threshold_db for at least min_silence_us; padding_us of each silence is kept on both sides so words are not clipped; the remaining parts are joined (ripple). On the main track with the magnet everything after the clip moves left; elsewhere the following clips on the same track move left. Linked clips (e.g. extracted audio) are cut identically. Silence at the clip edges is trimmed too. Works on video clips with an audio stream and on audio clips; times honour speed and reverse. The whole edit is one undo step; removed lists what was cut (timeline times before the ripple). When the entire clip is below the threshold nothing changes and an error explains how to adjust it. Undoable.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | Video (with sound) or audio clip to tighten. |
| `min_silence_us` | integer (microseconds) | no | `500000` | 50000 … 60000000 | Shortest pause to remove (timeline time). Shorter pauses are natural speech rhythm and are kept. |
| `padding_us` | integer (microseconds) | no | `100000` | 0 … 2000000 | Silence kept on each side of a cut so speech does not start or end abruptly. |
| `threshold_db` | number (dBFS) | no | `-40` | -90 … -5 | Audio quieter than this counts as silence. -40 suits clean voice recordings; use -30 for noisy rooms, -50 for very quiet ones. |

**Returns:** {segment_id, threshold_db, removed:[{start_us, end_us, duration_us, source_start_us, source_end_us}], removed_total_us, segment_ids[] (remaining clips in order), rippled, note}.

Example — Tighten a talking-head clip:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Only long pauses in a noisy room:

```json
{"min_silence_us":1000000,"padding_us":150000,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","threshold_db":-30}
```

### ai.split_scenes

**Split scenes** · MCP tool `ai_split_scenes` · `POST /api/v1/commands/ai.split_scenes` · undoable · UI: Toolbar/Split scene

CapCut's 'Split scene': detects the scene changes of a video clip (exactly like ai.detect_scenes) and splits the clip at every cut, so each shot becomes its own clip that can be trimmed, reordered or deleted. Linked clips (e.g. the extracted audio) are split at the same times. The original segment id stays on the first scene; segment_ids lists all resulting clips in timeline order. The whole split is one undo step. When no cut is found nothing changes (lower threshold to be more sensitive). Undoable.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | Video clip to analyse (timeline.get lists segment ids). |
| `min_scene_us` | integer (microseconds) | no | `500000` | 0 … 600000000 | Shortest scene to keep: cuts closer than this to another (stronger) cut or to the clip edges are ignored (flashes, strobes). |
| `threshold` | number | no | `0.3` | 0.05 … 1 | Scene-change sensitivity: ffmpeg scene score 0..1 a frame must reach. 0.2 = sensitive (also soft cuts), 0.3 = default, 0.5+ = only hard cuts. |

**Returns:** {segment_id, threshold, min_scene_us, frames_analyzed, cuts[], scenes[], segment_ids[], note}.

Example — Split a clip into its shots:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Sensitive split, scenes of at least 1 s:

```json
{"min_scene_us":1000000,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","threshold":0.2}
```

## Speed

2 commands: `segment.set_speed`, `segment.set_speed_curve`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/speed.html

### segment.set_speed

**Set speed** · MCP tool `segment_set_speed` · `POST /api/v1/commands/segment.set_speed` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Speed/Normal

Changes the playback speed of a video clip or audio segment — Speed → Normal in CapCut (0.1x..100x). The source range stays the same and the timeline duration is recomputed: duration = source duration / speed (2x halves the clip, 0.5x doubles it). Any speed curve is removed. On the main track with the magnet on, the following clips ripple left/right to stay gapless (linked segments on other tracks move with them). On other tracks, slowing a clip down so it would overlap the next segment fails with conflict. Keyframes keep their position relative to the content; fades, animations and transitions are clamped to the new length. keep_pitch preserves the voice pitch (CapCut's Pitch toggle off = chipmunk effect).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `speed` | number (multiplier) | yes |  | 0.1 … 100 | Playback speed: 1 = normal, 2 = twice as fast, 0.5 = slow motion. |
| `keep_pitch` | boolean | no |  |  | Keep the original audio pitch when the speed is not 1 (omit to keep the current setting). |

**Returns:** {segment, rippled_segments?: number of other segments moved}. segment.target.duration_us is the new length.

Example — Double speed:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","speed":2}
```

Example — Slow motion keeping the voice pitch:

```json
{"keep_pitch":true,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","speed":0.5}
```

### segment.set_speed_curve

**Set speed curve** · MCP tool `segment_set_speed_curve` · `POST /api/v1/commands/segment.set_speed_curve` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Speed/Curve

Applies a variable speed curve to a video clip or audio segment — Speed → Curve in CapCut. Presets: montage (fast/slow alternating), hero (slow-motion moment in the middle), bullet (extreme bullet-time slowdown), jump_cut (sudden speed burst), flash_in (starts very fast), flash_out (ends very fast), custom (flat 1x curve to edit) and none (remove the curve, back to the normal speed in segment.speed). Instead of a preset you can pass points: 2..20 objects {x, y} where x is the position within the segment on the timeline (0..1, strictly increasing, first 0 and last 1) and y the speed multiplier there (0.1..100); speed is linear between points. The timeline duration becomes source duration / mean curve speed, with the same ripple/conflict rules as segment.set_speed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `keep_pitch` | boolean | no |  |  | Keep the original audio pitch while the speed varies. |
| `points` | object[] | no |  |  | Custom curve: array of {x, y} with x 0..1 (timeline position in the segment) and y the speed 0.1..100. |
| `preset` | string | no |  | `none`, `custom`, `montage`, `hero`, `bullet`, `jump_cut`, `flash_in`, `flash_out` | Curve preset name; none removes the curve. Use custom with points for your own curve. |

**Returns:** {segment, rippled_segments?} — segment.speed_curve holds the points, segment.target.duration_us the new length.

Example — Hero time:

```json
{"preset":"hero","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Custom ramp from slow to fast:

```json
{"points":[{"x":0,"y":0.5},{"x":1,"y":3}],"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Remove the curve:

```json
{"preset":"none","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

## Stickers

1 commands: `sticker.add`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/stickers.html

### sticker.add

**Add sticker** · MCP tool `sticker_add` · `POST /api/v1/commands/sticker.add` · undoable · UI: Library/Stickers

Adds a built-in sticker to a sticker track, like clicking a card in the Stickers tab. The sticker PNG (512×512, transparent, generated by the engine) is registered once per project as a material of type "sticker" and a segment using it is placed at at_us (default: playhead) for duration_us (default 3 s) on the first free sticker track, or a new sticker track above all visual tracks. The sticker starts centred at 30% of the canvas height (transform scale 0.3); move/resize it with segment.set_transform. Sticker ids come from library.list kind=sticker. Animated stickers (the "Animated" tab; their library item has params.loop_anim, optional params.in_anim and params.loop_us) get that loop animation (period loop_us) and entrance animation applied automatically, exactly as animation.set would; pass animate=false to place them still. Change or remove the animations later with animation.set / animation.remove.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
