| `sticker_id` | string | yes |  |  | Sticker id from library.list kind=sticker, e.g. "heart", "badge_subscribe", "arrow_curved". |
| `animate` | boolean | no | `true` |  | Apply the sticker's default loop/entrance animation when it has one (animated stickers only); false places it without animation. |
| `at_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Timeline time where the new segment starts (1 second = 1000000). Defaults to the playhead position. |
| `duration_us` | integer (microseconds) | no | `3000000` | 100000 … 86400000000 | Length of the new sticker segment on the timeline. CapCut's default is 3 seconds (3000000). |
| `track_id` | string | no |  |  | Put the segment on this existing track. Omit to use the first free track of the right type, or a new track created above all visual tracks. |

**Returns:** {segment_id, track_id, segment, material_id} — the sticker segment and the sticker material it uses.

Example — Heart at the playhead:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","sticker_id":"heart"}
```

Example — Subscribe badge from 5 s for 2 s:

```json
{"at_us":5000000,"duration_us":2000000,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","sticker_id":"badge_subscribe"}
```

Example — Animated grin face placed without its default animation:

```json
{"animate":false,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","sticker_id":"emoji_grin"}
```

## Text

8 commands: `captions.export_srt`, `captions.import_srt`, `text.add`, `text.apply_effect`, `text.apply_template`, `text.remove_glyph_animation`, `text.set_glyph_animation`, `text.update`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/text.html

### captions.export_srt

**Export captions** · MCP tool `captions_export_srt` · `POST /api/v1/commands/captions.export_srt` · UI: Library/Captions/Export

Writes the project's text segments to a SubRip (.srt) file — Captions → Export. By default every text segment of every text track is exported in timeline order (overlapping texts from different tracks become separate cues); pass track_id to export a single caption track. The project is not modified. Existing files are overwritten; the folder must exist.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | yes |  |  | Absolute path of the .srt file to write, e.g. C:\Users\me\Videos\captions.srt. |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `track_id` | string | no |  |  | Only export this text track. |

**Returns:** {path, count}.

Example — Export subtitles:

```json
{"path":"C:\\Users\\me\\Videos\\captions.srt","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### captions.import_srt

**Import captions** · MCP tool `captions_import_srt` · `POST /api/v1/commands/captions.import_srt` · undoable · UI: Library/Captions/Import captions

Imports a SubRip (.srt) subtitle file as text segments — one per cue — on a new text track (or on track_id), like Captions → Import captions. Timings come from the file (shifted by offset_us); overlapping cues are trimmed so they do not overlap, formatting tags such as <i> are stripped and multi-line cues keep their line breaks. Captions use the "Caption" look (white, size 9, thin black outline) or template_id, and sit in the lower part of the frame (transform y = 0.6, i.e. centred at 80% of the height). Edit any caption afterwards with text.update.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | yes |  |  | Absolute path of the .srt file to import (UTF-8). |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `offset_us` | integer (microseconds) | no | `0` |  | Shift every cue by this much on the timeline (may be negative; cues before 0 are dropped). |
| `template_id` | string | no |  |  | Text template for the captions, e.g. "caption_box" or "caption_yellow" (default "caption_classic"). |
| `track_id` | string | no |  |  | Existing text track to fill; it must be free where the captions go. Omit to create a new text track. |

**Returns:** {track_id, count, segment_ids: [...], skipped: cues dropped because they ended before 0}.

Example — Import subtitles:

```json
{"path":"C:\\Users\\me\\Videos\\talk.srt","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Boxed captions starting 2 s later:

```json
{"offset_us":2000000,"path":"/home/me/talk.srt","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","template_id":"caption_box"}
```

### text.add

**Add text** · MCP tool `text_add` · `POST /api/v1/commands/text.add` · undoable · UI: Library/Text/Default text

Adds a text segment to a text track, like clicking "Default text" or a text template in the Text tab. The segment starts at at_us (default: playhead) and lasts duration_us (default 3 s). Without track_id the first text track that is free over that range is used; if every text track is occupied (or none exists) a new text track is created above all other visual tracks so the text draws on top. Default look (CapCut "Default text"): white Go Sans, size 15 (font height ≈ 1/20 of the canvas height), centred, positioned in the middle of the frame (transform x=0, y=0, scale 1). template_id applies a text-template preset (library.list kind=text_template, may include glyph animations); style overrides individual TextStyle fields on top of the default or template — including the wave-2 fields (case, glow, fill gradient, extra_strokes, extrude, curve, glyph_in/out/loop, words, highlight). style.effect_id applies a word-art preset (library kind text_effect) first, so other style fields in the same object override it. Change the look later with text.update, move it with segment.set_transform.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `at_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Timeline time where the new segment starts (1 second = 1000000). Defaults to the playhead position. |
| `duration_us` | integer (microseconds) | no | `3000000` | 100000 … 86400000000 | Length of the new text segment on the timeline. CapCut's default is 3 seconds (3000000). |
| `style` | object | no |  |  | Optional TextStyle overrides: {font, size, color, bold, italic, underline, align, line_spacing, letter_spacing, stroke{color,width}, shadow{color,opacity,blur,distance,angle}, box{color,opacity,radius}, case, glow{color,intensity,radius}, fill{type,colors,angle}, extra_strokes[{color,width}], extrude{color,depth,angle}, effect_id, curve, glyph_in/glyph_out/glyph_loop{id,duration_us}, words[{text,start_us,end_us}], highlight{style,color,scale,text_color}} — same units as text.update. Wave 4: stroke_fill{type,colors,angle,stops}, fill.stops[], pattern{type,colors,scale,angle,opacity,speed}, bevel{depth,angle,strength,gloss,highlight,shade,round}, inner_shadow{color,opacity,blur,distance,angle}, inner_glow{color,intensity,radius}, echo{colors,distance,angle,hollow}, distress{type,amount,scale}, sparkle{color,amount,size,speed}, drip{amount,length}, rough, pixelate, box{…, fill, border{color,width}, shadow{…}, per_line, skew, pad, knockout}, highlight.text_color. |
| `template_id` | string | no |  |  | Text template id from library.list kind=text_template, e.g. "title_bold", "neon_sign_pink", "gradient_pop_title". |
| `text` | string | no |  |  | Text content; use \n for line breaks. Defaults to the template's sample text or "Default text". |
| `track_id` | string | no |  |  | Put the segment on this existing track. Omit to use the first free track of the right type, or a new track created above all visual tracks. |

**Returns:** {segment_id, track_id, segment} — the new text segment (segment.text holds its TextStyle).

Example — Default text at the playhead:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","text":"Hello world"}
```

Example — Title template at 2 s for 4 s:

```json
{"at_us":2000000,"duration_us":4000000,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","template_id":"title_bold","text":"My trip"}
```

Example — Yellow outlined text:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","style":{"color":"#FFE600","stroke":{"color":"#000000","width":0.4}},"text":"Subscribe!"}
```

Example — Gold word art that types itself:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","style":{"effect_id":"fx_gold_metal","glyph_in":{"duration_us":1500000,"id":"in_typewriter"},"size":24},"text":"Grand opening"}
```

### text.apply_effect

**Apply text effect** · MCP tool `text_apply_effect` · `POST /api/v1/commands/text.apply_effect` · undoable · UI: Library/Text/Effects

Applies a word-art preset ("text effect": gradient, metal, luxury, neon, candy, texture, sticker, hand-made, outline, 3D, retro, spooky, gaming and cute looks from library.list kind=text_effect) to a text segment, like clicking a card in the Text → Effects grid. The preset WRITES its fields into the TextStyle — fill gradient, glow, extra_strokes, extrude, the wave-4 pattern / bevel / inner shadow / inner glow / echo / distress / sparkle / drip / rough / pixelate fields and, where the preset uses them, stroke, shadow and color — after clearing the previous preset's fill/glow/extra outlines/extrusion, and records its id in effect_id. Rendering uses only the stored fields, so every value stays editable with text.update afterwards. Words, font, size, alignment, animations and timing are kept. effect_id "none" removes the preset's fill, glow, extra outlines and extrusion (a transparent hollow colour becomes white).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `effect_id` | string | yes |  |  | Text effect id from library.list kind=text_effect, e.g. "fx_gold_metal", "fx_neon_outline", "fx_3d_extrude", or "none" to remove. |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id. |

**Returns:** The new TextStyle of the segment.

Example — Gold metal word art:

```json
{"effect_id":"fx_gold_metal","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

Example — Remove the effect:

```json
{"effect_id":"none","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

Example — Holographic sticker look:

```json
{"effect_id":"fx4_holo_sticker","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

### text.apply_template

**Apply text template** · MCP tool `text_apply_template` · `POST /api/v1/commands/text.apply_template` · undoable · UI: Library/Text/Templates

Replaces the whole look of a text segment with a text-template preset (font, size, colours, stroke, shadow, box, spacing, glow, gradient, outlines, 3D, curve and the template's text animations) while keeping its words, timing, position, clip loop animation, caption word timings and any per-letter animation or highlight the template does not define — like clicking a template in the Text tab while a text clip is selected. Get template ids from library.list kind=text_template.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id. |
| `template_id` | string | yes |  |  | Text template id, e.g. "neon_cyan", "caption_box", "lower_third_news". |

**Returns:** The new TextStyle of the segment.

Example — Make it neon:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f","template_id":"neon_cyan"}
```

### text.remove_glyph_animation

**Remove text animation** · MCP tool `text_remove_glyph_animation` · `POST /api/v1/commands/text.remove_glyph_animation` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Text/Animate

Removes the per-letter / per-word text animation of a text segment from the in, out or loop slot (or all three with kind=all) — choosing "None" in the Text → Animate panel. Clip-level animations set with animation.set are not touched. Removing an empty slot changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | string | yes |  | `in`, `out`, `loop`, `all` | Which slot to clear: in, out, loop or all. |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id. |

**Returns:** The updated TextStyle.

Example — Remove the in animation:

```json
{"kind":"in","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

Example — Remove all text animations:

```json
{"kind":"all","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

### text.set_glyph_animation

**Set text animation** · MCP tool `text_set_glyph_animation` · `POST /api/v1/commands/text.set_glyph_animation` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Text/Animate

Sets a per-letter / per-word text animation (library.list kind=text_animation) — the Text → Animate panel: typewriter with caret, letter rise/drop/pop/zoom/spin, karaoke sweep, random spell (scramble), word pop, word focus (blur-in), wave, jitter, rainbow, glow pulse, shine and more. These play INSIDE the text image and combine freely with each other and with the clip-level animations of animation.set. kind=in plays over duration_us from the segment start, kind=out over duration_us up to the segment end (in and out are shortened proportionally when they do not both fit), kind=loop repeats with duration_us as the period for the whole segment. A bare name is qualified with kind ("typewriter" + in → "in_typewriter"). Without duration_us the slot keeps its current duration, else the item's default_duration_us is used; in/out durations are clamped to the segment length.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes |  |  | Text animation id from library.list kind=text_animation (in_*, out_*, loop_*), e.g. "in_typewriter", "out_letter_drop", "loop_wave". |
| `kind` | string | yes |  | `in`, `out`, `loop` | Which slot: in (plays from the segment start), out (ends at the segment end) or loop (repeats for the whole segment). |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id. |
| `duration_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 100000 … 60000000 | Duration of the in/out animation, or the period of one loop cycle (1 second = 1000000). |

**Returns:** The updated TextStyle (glyph_in / glyph_out / glyph_loop = {id, duration_us}).

Example — Typewriter over 1.5 s:

```json
{"duration_us":1500000,"id":"in_typewriter","kind":"in","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

Example — Letters fall away at the end:

```json
{"id":"out_letter_drop","kind":"out","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

Example — Endless wave:

```json
{"duration_us":1200000,"id":"wave","kind":"loop","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

### text.update

**Edit text** · MCP tool `text_update` · `POST /api/v1/commands/text.update` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Text

Changes the content and look of a text segment — the Text tab of the inspector (Basic: font, size, style, colour, case, alignment, spacing; Stroke; Extra outlines; Shadow; Background box; Glow; Gradient fill; 3D extrude; Curve; Word-art effect; caption highlight). Only the parameters you pass change. Units: size is CapCut's scale (15 = default, font height ≈ size/300 of the canvas height); letter_spacing and line_spacing are in em (0.1 = 10% of the font size) added to the normal spacing; stroke_width, shadow_blur and shadow_distance are 0..1 (stroke up to 0.25 em thick, shadow offset/blur up to 0.5 em); shadow_angle, fill_angle and extrude_angle are in degrees counter-clockwise from the right (-45 = down-right, -90 = downwards / top→bottom); box_radius 0..1 rounds the corners (1 = pill). Stroke, shadow, box, glow and extrude are enabled by setting any of their parameters (missing ones get defaults: black stroke width 0.3, black shadow opacity 0.6/blur 0.3/distance 0.15/angle -45, black box opacity 0.6/radius 0.2, glow in the text colour intensity 0.6/radius 0.35, dark-grey extrude depth 0.15/angle -45) and removed with stroke_width=0, shadow_opacity=0, box_opacity=0, glow_intensity=0 or extrude_depth=0. Gradient fill: fill_type linear|radial with 2–4 fill_colors (evenly spaced; radial goes centre→edge), fill_type=solid removes it (the text colour is used again); passing only fill_colors turns on a linear gradient. A color with alpha 00 ("#FFFFFF00") plus a stroke gives hollow outline text. curve -1..1 bends the lines into an arc (1 = half circle arch, -1 = smile). case upper|lower|title converts letters when rendering (the stored content is unchanged; none = as typed). effect_id applies a word-art preset from library.list kind=text_effect FIRST (it writes fill, glow, extra_strokes, extrude and the stroke/shadow/color it uses — the rendered look comes only from the stored fields), so other parameters in the same call override it; effect_id "" or "none" removes the preset's fill/glow/extra outlines/extrusion. Captions: words (timings relative to the segment start) plus highlight_style color|box|scale|underline|karaoke|pop|bounce|reveal|dim|glow|sweep_line|slide_box highlight the spoken word (highlight_style=none removes it). Per-letter animations are set with text.set_glyph_animation. Wave-4 word art (all optional; each group is enabled by any of its parameters and removed by its zero amount): fill_stops (hard-edged chrome/duotone gradients, up to 8 fill_colors); stroke_fill_* (gradient outline); pattern_* (procedural texture over the fill: stripes, checker, dots, halftone, hearts, stars, grain, glitter, holo, foil, brushed metal, marble, camo, galaxy, lava flow, aurora, rainbow…, pattern_speed animates the moving ones); bevel_* (emboss lighting; bevel_round + bevel_gloss = puffy glossy letters); inner_shadow_* and inner_glow_* (inside the letters); echo_* (stacked offset copies, retro 3D stacks / trails); distress_* (grunge, chalk, stamp, spray, scratch, worn); sparkle_* (star glints, sparkle_speed twinkles); drip_* (paint or slime drips); rough (hand-made wobble); pixelate (pixel-art blocks); box_* extras (gradient box, border, card shadow, one box per line, skew, padding, knockout stencil); highlight_text_color (letter colour of the active caption word). Highlight styles also include pop, bounce, reveal, dim, glow, sweep_line and slide_box.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id. |
| `align` | string | no |  | `left`, `center`, `right` | Horizontal alignment of lines within the text block. |
| `bevel_angle` | number (degrees) | no |  | -180 … 180 | Direction the bevel light comes from, counter-clockwise from the right (135 = upper left, the default). |
| `bevel_depth` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Bevel / emboss lighting: width of the lit edge 0..1 (1 = 0.25 em); 0 removes the bevel. |
| `bevel_gloss` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Sharp specular highlight on the bevel (glossy plastic / puffy balloon look) 0..1. |
| `bevel_highlight` | string | no |  |  | Bevel light colour #RRGGBB (default white; gold-ish for warm metal). |
| `bevel_round` | boolean | no |  |  | Rounded pillow profile (puffy, inflated letters) instead of a flat chisel. |
| `bevel_shade` | string | no |  |  | Bevel shade colour #RRGGBB (default black). |
| `bevel_strength` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Contrast of the bevel light and shade 0..1 (default 0.8). |
| `bold` | boolean | no |  |  | Bold style (a real bold face when the font has one, otherwise synthesised). |
| `box_border_color` | string | no |  |  | Colour #RRGGBB of an outline drawn inside the edge of the background box. |
| `box_border_width` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Box outline thickness 0..1 (1 = 0.25 em); 0 removes it. |
| `box_color` | string | no |  |  | Background box colour #RRGGBB. Enables the box if it was off. |
| `box_fill_angle` | number (degrees) | no |  | -360 … 360 | Direction of the box gradient, counter-clockwise from the right. |
| `box_fill_colors` | string[] | no |  |  | 2–8 colours of a gradient background box (left→right unless box_fill_angle); [] removes the gradient. Enables the box if it was off. |
| `box_knockout` | boolean | no |  |  | Cut the letters out of the box so the video shows through them (stencil look). |
| `box_opacity` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Background box opacity 0..1; 0 removes the box. |
| `box_pad` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Extra padding around the text inside the box 0..1 (1 = 0.5 em). |
| `box_per_line` | boolean | no |  |  | One box per text line (ribbon / highlighter captions) instead of one box around the block. |
| `box_radius` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Corner roundness 0..1 (fraction of half the box height; 1 = pill). |
| `box_shadow_angle` | number (degrees) | no |  | -180 … 180 | Box shadow direction, counter-clockwise from the right (-45 = down-right). |
| `box_shadow_blur` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Box shadow softness 0..1 (1 = 0.25 em). |
| `box_shadow_color` | string | no |  |  | Colour #RRGGBB of a drop shadow under the background box (blur 0 = flat offset "card" shadow). |
| `box_shadow_distance` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Box shadow offset 0..1 (1 = 0.5 em). |
| `box_shadow_opacity` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Box shadow opacity 0..1; 0 removes it. |
| `box_skew` | number | no |  | -1 … 1 | Slants the box into a parallelogram (-1..1; positive leans right) — sports and news lower thirds. |
| `case` | string | no |  | `none`, `upper`, `lower`, `title` | Letter case conversion at render time: upper (ABC), lower (abc), title (Abc Def) or none (as typed). |
| `color` | string | no |  |  | Text colour as #RRGGBB (or #RRGGBBAA; alpha 00 + a stroke = hollow text). |
| `content` | string | no |  |  | New text content; \n starts a new line. Must not be empty. |
| `curve` | number | no |  | -1 … 1 | Arc bend of every line: 0 = straight, 1 = half-circle arch (∩), -1 = half-circle smile (∪). |
| `distress_amount` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | How much is eroded 0..1; 0 removes the distress. |
| `distress_scale` | number | no |  | 0 … 10 | Texture size multiplier (0 = 1). |
| `distress_type` | string | no |  | `none`, `grunge`, `chalk`, `stamp`, `spray`, `scratch`, `worn` | Erodes the whole text with a texture: grunge (rough print), chalk (chalkboard), stamp (rubber stamp), spray (speckled spray paint), scratch (scratched lines), worn (faded vintage print); none removes it. |
| `drip_amount` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Paint / slime drips hanging from the letters 0..1 (horror, slime, melting looks); 0 removes them. |
| `drip_length` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Longest drip 0..1 (1 = 1.2 em; default 0.5). |
| `echo_angle` | number (degrees) | no |  | -180 … 180 | Direction of the echo copies, counter-clockwise from the right (-45 = down-right). |
| `echo_colors` | string[] | no |  |  | Echo: 1–6 colours #RRGGBB(AA) of offset copies of the letters stacked behind the text, nearest first (retro 70s/80s stacks, motion trails with fading alpha); [] removes the echo. |
| `echo_distance` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Distance between echo copies 0..1 (1 = 0.5 em); 0 removes the echo. |
| `echo_hollow` | boolean | no |  |  | Draw the echo copies as thin outlines instead of solid shapes. |
| `effect_id` | string | no |  |  | Word-art preset from library.list kind=text_effect (e.g. "fx_gold_metal", "fx_neon_outline"), applied before the other parameters; "" or "none" removes the preset's fill/glow/extra outlines/extrusion. |
| `extra_strokes` | object[] | no |  |  | Additional outlines OUTSIDE the main stroke, inner → outer, each {color:"#RRGGBB", width:0..1} (width like stroke_width); at most 4; [] removes them. |
| `extrude_angle` | number (degrees) | no |  | -180 … 180 | Extrusion direction, counter-clockwise from the right: -45 = down-right (default), -90 = straight down. |
| `extrude_color` | string | no |  |  | 3D extrusion colour #RRGGBB (shaded darker with depth); #RRGGBBAA with alpha < FF draws a fading long shadow. Enables the extrusion if it was off. |
| `extrude_depth` | number (em) | no |  | 0 … 1 | Extrusion depth 0..1 em; 0 removes it. |
| `fill_angle` | number (degrees) | no |  | -360 … 360 | Direction of a linear gradient, counter-clockwise from the right: 0 = left→right, -90 = top→bottom, 90 = bottom→top. |
| `fill_colors` | string[] | no |  |  | 2–4 gradient colour stops #RRGGBB(AA), evenly spaced: first at the start (linear) or centre (radial), last at the end/edge. |
| `fill_stops` | number[] | no |  |  | Positions 0..1 of the fill_colors stops (one per colour, ascending; two equal neighbours make a hard edge such as a chrome horizon); [] = evenly spaced. |
| `fill_type` | string | no |  | `solid`, `linear`, `radial` | Fill of the letters: solid (the text colour; removes a gradient), linear or radial gradient through fill_colors. |
| `font` | string | no |  |  | Font id from library.list kind=font (e.g. "go_sans", "go_mono", "sys_arial", or a downloaded font such as "montserrat" — install free fonts with font.catalog + font.install). Characters the font lacks (Cyrillic, CJK…) fall back to system fonts automatically. |
| `glow_color` | string | no |  |  | Glow (soft coloured halo) colour #RRGGBB. Enables the glow if it was off. |
| `glow_intensity` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | How strong/opaque the glow is near the letters, 0..1; 0 removes the glow. |
| `glow_radius` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Glow size 0..1 (1 ≈ a halo reaching 1.3 em beyond the letters). |
| `highlight_color` | string | no |  |  | Highlight colour #RRGGBB (default #FFD600). Enables a color highlight if none was set. |
| `highlight_scale` | number | no |  | 0.5 … 3 | Growth of the active word for highlight_style=scale (default 1.15). |
| `highlight_style` | string | no |  | `none`, `color`, `box`, `scale`, `underline`, `karaoke`, `pop`, `bounce`, `reveal`, `dim`, `glow`, `sweep_line`, `slide_box` | How the spoken word is highlighted when words are set: color (word turns highlight_color), box (rounded box behind it), scale (word grows), underline, karaoke (fills left→right as spoken), pop (springs up with an overshoot), bounce (hops once), reveal (later words hidden until spoken), dim (later words dimmed), glow (halo behind the word), sweep_line (underline grows while spoken), slide_box (box glides from word to word); none removes the highlight. |
| `highlight_text_color` | string | no |  |  | Colour #RRGGBB of the active word's letters for the box / slide_box / underline / sweep_line / glow highlight styles (e.g. black text on a yellow box); "" keeps the text colour. |
| `inner_glow_color` | string | no |  |  | Inner glow colour #RRGGBB: light seeping in from the letter edges (neon tube, lit-from-within). Enables it if it was off. |
| `inner_glow_intensity` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Inner glow strength 0..1; 0 removes it. |
| `inner_glow_radius` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | How far the inner glow reaches into the letters 0..1 (1 = 0.3 em). |
| `inner_shadow_angle` | number (degrees) | no |  | -180 … 180 | Inner shadow offset direction, counter-clockwise from the right (-60 = down, slightly right). |
| `inner_shadow_blur` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Inner shadow softness 0..1 (1 = 0.25 em). |
| `inner_shadow_color` | string | no |  |  | Inner shadow colour #RRGGBB: a shadow cast INSIDE the letters (debossed / cut-out look). Enables it if it was off. |
| `inner_shadow_distance` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Inner shadow offset 0..1 (1 = 0.25 em). |
| `inner_shadow_opacity` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Inner shadow opacity 0..1; 0 removes it. |
| `italic` | boolean | no |  |  | Italic style (real italic face or a synthetic slant). |
| `letter_spacing` | number (em) | no |  | -0.5 … 2 | Extra space between characters in em (0 = normal). |
| `line_spacing` | number (em) | no |  | -0.5 … 3 | Extra space between lines in em (0 = normal, 0.5 = half a line more). |
| `pattern_angle` | number (degrees) | no |  | -360 … 360 | Rotates the pattern from its default orientation. |
| `pattern_colors` | string[] | no |  |  | Pattern colours #RRGGBB(AA); their meaning depends on pattern_type (see its list); omitted = the type's defaults, "" = use the text fill. |
| `pattern_opacity` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | How strongly the pattern covers the fill, 0..1 (0 = fully, same as 1). |
| `pattern_scale` | number | no |  | 0 … 20 | Pattern feature size multiplier (1 = default size relative to the font, 2 = twice as big; 0 = default). |
| `pattern_speed` | number | no |  | -10 … 10 | Animation speed of moving patterns (holo shimmer, glitter twinkle, flowing lava, rainbow sweep, scrolling stripes…), cycles per second; 0 = still. |
| `pattern_type` | string | no |  | `none`, `stripes`, `pinstripe`, `checker`, `gingham`, `plaid`, `dots`, `halftone`, `hearts`, `stars`, `grain`, `static`, `scanlines`, `brushed`, `foil`, `carbon`, `glitter`, `holo`, `rainbow`, `aurora`, `flow`, `galaxy`, `marble`, `wood`, `camo`, `leopard`, `zebra`, `frost`, `grid` | Procedural texture painted over the letter fill: stripes (diagonal two-colour stripes (candy cane / barber pole); colors [stripe, gap] (gap defaults to the fill); speed scrolls them); pinstripe (thin vertical pinstripes over the fill; colors [line]); checker (checkerboard (racing flag); colors [a, b]); gingham (picnic gingham: translucent crossing bands, darker where they overlap; colors [band, background]); plaid (woven tartan with a twill texture; colors [main, dark band, secondary, thin accent]); dots (polka dots on a staggered grid; colors [dot, background]); halftone (comic halftone dots growing from the top to the bottom of the text; colors [dot] (default: a darker shade of the fill)); hearts (tiny repeating hearts (kawaii, love); colors [heart, background]); stars (tiny repeating five-point stars; colors [star, background]); grain (film grain / risograph noise that roughens flat colour; speed makes it flicker); static (black-and-white TV static noise; speed animates it); scanlines (dark horizontal CRT scanlines; speed rolls them); brushed (brushed-metal streaks along the pattern angle (shades the fill)); foil (crinkled metal foil facets of random brightness (gold leaf, tinsel); speed makes facets glint); carbon (woven carbon fibre; colors [dark, highlight]); glitter (glitter flakes of varying brightness with bright sparkles; colors [glitter] (default: the fill); speed twinkles); holo (holographic / iridescent pastel rainbow with a soft sheen; colors = palette (2–8); speed shimmers); rainbow (saturated rainbow bands; speed sweeps them across the letters); aurora (northern-lights curtains of green, teal and violet; colors = palette; speed drifts them); flow (flowing lava / fire plasma; colors = palette from dark to bright; speed makes it flow); galaxy (deep-space nebula with tiny stars; colors = palette; speed twinkles the stars); marble (polished marble with thin veins; colors [stone, vein] (stone defaults to the fill)); wood (wood grain rings; colors [light, dark]); camo (camouflage blobs in four colours; colors [1..4]); leopard (leopard rosettes; colors [fur, ring, spot centre] (fur defaults to the fill)); zebra (wavy zebra stripes; colors [stripe, background]); frost (frosted ice cracks and rime; colors [frost]); grid (glowing synthwave grid lines; colors [line]; speed scrolls the grid). none removes it. |
| `pixelate` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Blocky pixel-art rendering 0..1 (1 = 0.2 em pixels); 0 = smooth. |
| `rough` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Hand-made wobble: shaky outlines and slightly tilted letters 0..1 (marker, crayon, doodle looks); 0 = clean. |
| `shadow_angle` | number (degrees) | no |  | -180 … 180 | Shadow direction, counter-clockwise from the right: -45 = down-right, 90 = up. |
| `shadow_blur` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Shadow softness 0..1 (1 = 0.5 em blur radius). |
| `shadow_color` | string | no |  |  | Shadow colour #RRGGBB. Enables the shadow if it was off. |
| `shadow_distance` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Shadow offset 0..1 (1 = 0.5 em). |
| `shadow_opacity` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Shadow opacity 0..1; 0 removes the shadow. |
| `size` | number | no |  | 1 … 300 | Text size on CapCut's scale (default 15 ≈ 1/20 of the canvas height). |
| `sparkle_amount` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | How many four-point star glints sit on the letters 0..1; 0 removes them. |
| `sparkle_color` | string | no |  |  | Colour of the star glints #RRGGBB (default white). Enables sparkles if they were off. |
| `sparkle_size` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Star size 0..1 (1 = 0.6 em rays). |
| `sparkle_speed` | number | no |  | 0 … 10 | Twinkles per second; 0 = still stars. |
| `stroke_color` | string | no |  |  | Outline colour #RRGGBB. Enables the stroke if it was off. |
| `stroke_fill_angle` | number (degrees) | no |  | -360 … 360 | Direction of a linear stroke gradient, counter-clockwise from the right (0 = left→right, -90 = top→bottom). |
| `stroke_fill_colors` | string[] | no |  |  | 2–8 colour stops #RRGGBB(AA) of the stroke gradient; passing them alone turns on a linear stroke gradient (and a stroke if there was none). |
| `stroke_fill_type` | string | no |  | `solid`, `linear`, `radial` | Gradient along the main stroke: linear or radial through stroke_fill_colors; solid removes it (stroke_color is used again). |
| `stroke_width` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Outline thickness 0..1 (1 = 0.25 em); 0 removes the stroke. |
| `underline` | boolean | no |  |  | Underline every line. |
| `words` | object[] | no |  |  | Caption word timings [{text, start_us, end_us}] in microseconds relative to the segment start (normally written by captions.auto); matched in order onto the words of the text; [] removes them. |

**Returns:** The updated TextStyle object of the segment.

Example — Change the words:

```json
{"content":"New caption","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

Example — Bigger yellow bold text:

```json
{"bold":true,"color":"#FFE600","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f","size":24}
```

Example — Add a black outline and drop shadow:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f","shadow_opacity":0.7,"stroke_color":"#000000","stroke_width":0.4}
```

Example — Remove the background box:

```json
{"box_opacity":0,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

Example — Sunset gradient, all caps, pink glow:

```json
{"case":"upper","fill_angle":-90,"fill_colors":["#FFB347","#FF5E62","#8E2DE2"],"fill_type":"linear","glow_color":"#FF3FD8","glow_intensity":0.7,"glow_radius":0.4,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

Example — 3D extrusion and an arched baseline:

```json
{"curve":0.5,"extrude_angle":-45,"extrude_color":"#E04E39","extrude_depth":0.2,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

Example — Two extra outlines:

```json
{"extra_strokes":[{"color":"#FFFFFF","width":0.3},{"color":"#FF3B6B","width":0.3}],"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f","stroke_width":0.2}
```

Example — Apply a word-art preset but keep a red colour:

```json
{"color":"#FF4040","effect_id":"fx_3d_extrude","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

Example — Karaoke caption highlight:

```json
{"highlight_color":"#FFD400","highlight_style":"karaoke","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f","words":[{"end_us":400000,"start_us":0,"text":"Hello"},{"end_us":900000,"start_us":400000,"text":"world"}]}
```

Example — Back to a plain solid fill:

```json
{"extrude_depth":0,"fill_type":"solid","glow_intensity":0,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

Example — Glossy puffy glitter letters with twinkling stars:

```json
{"bevel_depth":0.8,"bevel_gloss":0.8,"bevel_round":true,"pattern_colors":["#E2B23C"],"pattern_speed":0.8,"pattern_type":"glitter","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f","sparkle_amount":0.5,"sparkle_speed":1.2}
```

Example — Retro 70s stack on a slanted card:

```json
{"box_color":"#1B1B1B","box_opacity":1,"box_pad":0.2,"box_shadow_blur":0,"box_shadow_opacity":1,"box_skew":0.3,"echo_angle":-45,"echo_colors":["#F7B32B","#F26B1D","#C0392B"],"echo_distance":0.16,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

Example — Chrome with a hard horizon:

```json
{"fill_angle":-90,"fill_colors":["#FFFFFF","#5B86B5","#2A1E14","#F3D9B5"],"fill_stops":[0,0.5,0.5,1],"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

Example — Black text on a yellow box under the spoken word:

```json
{"highlight_color":"#FFE14D","highlight_style":"slide_box","highlight_text_color":"#111111","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

## Timeline

23 commands: `timeline.get`, `timeline.marker.add`, `timeline.marker.delete`, `timeline.marker.move`, `timeline.marker.set`, `timeline.segment.add`, `timeline.segment.crop`, `timeline.segment.delete`, `timeline.segment.delete_left`, `timeline.segment.delete_right`, `timeline.segment.duplicate`, `timeline.segment.freeze`, `timeline.segment.mirror`, `timeline.segment.move`, `timeline.segment.replace`, `timeline.segment.reverse`, `timeline.segment.rotate`, `timeline.segment.split`, `timeline.segment.trim`, `timeline.settings.set`, `timeline.track.add`, `timeline.track.delete`, `timeline.track.set`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/timeline.html

### timeline.get

**Get timeline** · MCP tool `timeline_get` · `POST /api/v1/commands/timeline.get` · UI: Timeline

Returns a compact view of the timeline made for AI agents — much smaller than project.get. Tracks are listed top-to-bottom exactly as the CapCut timeline shows them: text/sticker/effect/filter and overlay tracks first, then the main_video track, then audio tracks. Each track has its id, type, layer (its compositing index in project.tracks: 0 is drawn first, at the bottom), lock/hide/mute flags and its clips in time order. Each clip has id, kind (video, photo, audio, sticker, text, effect, filter, adjustment), label (file name, text content or effect/filter id), start_us, end_us, duration_us, the source range it uses, speed, volume (video/audio), link_group, transition_out, filter and effects. Also returns markers, the current playhead, the timeline settings and a compact list of materials with how often each is used. Call it before editing to find segment and track ids, and after editing to check the result.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |

**Returns:** {project_id, name, duration_us, playhead_us, fps, settings, tracks: [{id, type, name?, layer, muted, locked, hidden, segments: [{id, kind, label, start_us, end_us, duration_us, material_id?, source_start_us, source_duration_us, speed, reverse?, still?, volume?, link_group?, transition_out?, filter?, effects?}]}], markers: [{id, time_us, label?, color?}], materials: [{id, type, name, duration_us, uses}]}.

Example — Read the timeline:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### timeline.marker.add

**Add marker** · MCP tool `timeline_marker_add` · `POST /api/v1/commands/timeline.marker.add` · undoable · hotkey M · UI: Toolbar/Marker

Adds a marker on the timeline ruler at at_us (default: the playhead) — CapCut's marker button / M. Markers are labelled points used to remember spots (e.g. beats) and clip edges snap to them. If a marker already exists at exactly that time it is returned instead of adding a duplicate (its label/colour are updated when given).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `at_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  |  | Timeline time in microseconds (1 s = 1000000). Defaults to the current playhead position. |
| `color` | string | no |  |  | Optional marker colour as #RRGGBB (default: the editor's accent colour). |
| `label` | string | no |  |  | Optional marker label (shown when hovering the marker). |

**Returns:** The marker {id, time_us, label?, color?}.

Example — Marker at the playhead:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Labelled marker at 12 s:

```json
{"at_us":12000000,"color":"#ff5a5f","label":"Drop","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### timeline.marker.delete

**Delete marker** · MCP tool `timeline_marker_delete` · `POST /api/v1/commands/timeline.marker.delete` · undoable · UI: Timeline/Ruler/Marker/Delete

Removes a marker from the ruler (right-click a marker → Delete in CapCut). Clips are not affected.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `marker_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the marker (from timeline.get → markers[].id or timeline.marker.add). |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |

**Returns:** {deleted: marker_id}.

Example — Delete a marker:

```json
{"marker_id":"mrk_1a2b3c4d5e6f","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### timeline.marker.move

**Move marker** · MCP tool `timeline_marker_move` · `POST /api/v1/commands/timeline.marker.move` · undoable · UI: Timeline/Ruler/Drag marker

Moves a marker to another time on the ruler (dragging a marker in CapCut). Markers stay sorted by time; moving a marker never moves clips.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `marker_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the marker (from timeline.get → markers[].id or timeline.marker.add). |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `time_us` | integer (microseconds) | yes |  | 0 … ∞ | New marker time in microseconds. |

**Returns:** The moved marker {id, time_us, label?, color?}.

Example — Move a marker to 7.5 s:

```json
{"marker_id":"mrk_1a2b3c4d5e6f","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","time_us":7500000}
```

### timeline.marker.set

**Edit marker** · MCP tool `timeline_marker_set` · `POST /api/v1/commands/timeline.marker.set` · undoable · UI: Timeline/Ruler/Marker/Edit

Changes the label and/or colour of a marker (CapCut's marker edit popover). Only the given fields change; an empty label clears it, an empty color returns to the default colour.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `marker_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the marker (from timeline.get → markers[].id or timeline.marker.add). |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `color` | string | no |  |  | New colour as #RRGGBB (empty string = default accent colour). |
| `label` | string | no |  |  | New label text (empty string clears it). |

**Returns:** The updated marker {id, time_us, label?, color?}.

Example — Rename a marker:

```json
{"label":"Chorus","marker_id":"mrk_1a2b3c4d5e6f","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### timeline.segment.add

**Add to timeline** · MCP tool `timeline_segment_add` · `POST /api/v1/commands/timeline.segment.add` · undoable · UI: Library/Media/Card/+ (or drag to the timeline)

Places an imported material (from media.import / media.list) on the timeline as a new clip — like pressing + on a media card or dragging it onto the timeline in CapCut. Where it goes: without track_id, video and photo clips go to the main track (created if needed); audio, sticker and other clips go to the first track of their type that is free at at_us, otherwise to a new track. On the main track with the magnet on (default) the clip is inserted at the clip boundary nearest to at_us and every later clip ripples right — there are never gaps; when at_us is omitted it is appended to the end of the main track. With the magnet off it lands at at_us and later clips are pushed right only if they would overlap. On other tracks the clip starts exactly at at_us (default: the playhead); if that spot on the requested track is taken, CapCut creates a new track directly above it and puts the clip there. new_track forces a brand-new track. Length: the whole material for video/audio (from source_start_us), 5 s for photos, 3 s for stickers; duration_us overrides it but cannot exceed the material for video/audio. Video clips keep their own sound until audio.extract. Locked tracks cannot receive clips (conflict).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `material_id` | string | yes |  |  | Material to place, e.g. "mat_1a2b3c4d5e6f". Get ids from media.list or timeline.get → materials. |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `at_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  |  | Where the clip should start on the timeline. Default: end of the main track for video/photo going to the main track, the playhead for everything else. On the magnet main track the nearest clip boundary is used. |
| `duration_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 1 … ∞ | Clip length on the timeline. Default: the whole material (video/audio), 5000000 for photos, 3000000 for stickers. |
| `new_track` | boolean | no |  |  | Put the clip on a brand-new track (an overlay track for video/photo) — next to track_id when given, otherwise at the default position on top. |
| `source_start_us` | integer (microseconds) | no | `0` | 0 … ∞ | In-point inside the material for video/audio (the clip shows the material from this time on). |
| `track_id` | string | no |  |  | Destination track. Must accept the material: video/photo → main_video or video_overlay, audio → audio, sticker → sticker. Omit to let the editor choose (see description). |

**Returns:** {track_id, segment} — the track that received the clip and the full new segment (id, source and target ranges, defaults: speed 1, scale 1, opacity 1, volume 1).

Example — Append a video to the end of the main track:

```json
{"material_id":"mat_1a2b3c4d5e6f","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Insert a clip at 5 s on the main track:

```json
{"at_us":5000000,"material_id":"mat_1a2b3c4d5e6f","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Picture-in-picture: first 4 s of a video on a new overlay track at 2 s:

```json
{"at_us":2000000,"duration_us":4000000,"material_id":"mat_1a2b3c4d5e6f","new_track":true,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Background music from 0 s:

```json
{"at_us":0,"material_id":"mat_6f5e4d3c2b1a","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### timeline.segment.crop

**Crop** · MCP tool `timeline_segment_crop` · `POST /api/v1/commands/timeline.segment.crop` · undoable · UI: Toolbar/Crop

Crops a video or photo clip — the Crop button in the timeline toolbar, which opens CapCut's crop dialog with ratio presets. Rectangle fields are fractions of the source frame (x,y = top-left corner, w,h = size; omitted fields keep the current crop, or the full frame). ratio fits the rectangle to an aspect ratio of the source pixels: with no rectangle it picks the largest centred area of that ratio; with a rectangle it shrinks it around its centre to match. 'free' keeps the rectangle as given. Calling it with neither a rectangle nor a fixed ratio resets the crop to the full frame (CapCut's Reset). A legacy rect object {x,y,w,h} is also accepted.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `h` | number (source fraction) | no |  | 0.01 … 1 | Height of the kept area as a fraction of the source height (1 = full height). |
| `ratio` | string | no |  | `free`, `16:9`, `9:16`, `1:1`, `4:3`, `3:4` | Aspect-ratio preset of the crop dialog. free = any shape. |
| `rect` | object | no |  |  | Alternative to x/y/w/h: an object {x, y, w, h} in 0..1 source fractions. |
| `w` | number (source fraction) | no |  | 0.01 … 1 | Width of the kept area as a fraction of the source width (1 = full width). |
| `x` | number (source fraction) | no |  | 0 … 1 | Left edge of the kept area as a fraction of the source width (0 = left edge). |
| `y` | number (source fraction) | no |  | 0 … 1 | Top edge of the kept area as a fraction of the source height (0 = top edge). |

**Returns:** {segment} with segment.crop set (omitted when the crop was reset).

Example — Crop to a vertical 9:16 strip in the middle:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","ratio":"9:16","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Keep the top-left quarter:

```json
{"h":0.5,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","w":0.5,"x":0,"y":0}
```

Example — Reset crop:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### timeline.segment.delete

**Delete** · MCP tool `timeline_segment_delete` · `POST /api/v1/commands/timeline.segment.delete` · undoable · hotkey Delete · UI: Toolbar/Delete

Deletes clips from the timeline (the media stays in the library). On the main track with the magnet on the following clips shift left to close the gap (ripple delete); on other tracks a gap remains. Linked clips (e.g. a video and its extracted audio) are deleted together when linkage is on. Tracks other than the main track that become empty are removed, as in CapCut. The transition into a deleted clip is removed. Clips on locked tracks cannot be deleted.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | no |  |  | ID of the clip to delete. Required unless segment_ids is given. |
| `segment_ids` | string[] | no |  |  | Several segment ids at once (multi-selection). Combined with segment_id when both are given. |

**Returns:** {deleted: [segment ids]} — every removed clip including linked ones.

Example — Delete a clip:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Delete several clips:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_ids":["seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","seg_6f5e4d3c2b1a"]}
```

### timeline.segment.delete_left

**Delete left** · MCP tool `timeline_segment_delete_left` · `POST /api/v1/commands/timeline.segment.delete_left` · undoable · hotkey Q · UI: Toolbar/Delete left

Removes the part of a clip to the left of at_us (default: the playhead) — CapCut's "Delete left" (Q). On the main track with the magnet on the remaining part stays where the clip started and everything after it moves left, so the frame that was under the playhead is now at the clip's start (playhead_us; the editor moves the playhead there). Elsewhere the clip now starts at at_us. Linked clips are trimmed the same way. Without segment_id the main-track clip under at_us is used. at_us must lie strictly inside the clip.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `at_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  |  | Timeline time in microseconds (1 s = 1000000). Defaults to the current playhead position. |
| `segment_id` | string | no |  |  | ID of the segment (clip) to edit. Optional: when omitted the clip on the main track under at_us is used (what CapCut does when nothing is selected). |

**Returns:** {track_id, segment, playhead_us} — the shortened clip and the time the frame that was under the playhead now sits at.

Example — Delete left of a clip at 3 s:

```json
{"at_us":3000000,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Delete left at the playhead on the main track:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### timeline.segment.delete_right

**Delete right** · MCP tool `timeline_segment_delete_right` · `POST /api/v1/commands/timeline.segment.delete_right` · undoable · hotkey W · UI: Toolbar/Delete right

Removes the part of a clip to the right of at_us (default: the playhead) — CapCut's "Delete right" (W). The clip now ends at at_us; on the main track with the magnet on the following clips move left to close the gap. Linked clips are trimmed the same way. Without segment_id the main-track clip under at_us is used. at_us must lie strictly inside the clip.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `at_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  |  | Timeline time in microseconds (1 s = 1000000). Defaults to the current playhead position. |
| `segment_id` | string | no |  |  | ID of the segment (clip) to edit. Optional: when omitted the clip on the main track under at_us is used (what CapCut does when nothing is selected). |

**Returns:** {track_id, segment, playhead_us} — the shortened clip and the time the frame that was under the playhead now sits at.

Example — Delete right of a clip at 3 s:

```json
{"at_us":3000000,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Delete right at the playhead on the main track:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### timeline.segment.duplicate

**Duplicate** · MCP tool `timeline_segment_duplicate` · `POST /api/v1/commands/timeline.segment.duplicate` · undoable · hotkey Ctrl+D · UI: Timeline/Context menu/Duplicate

Duplicates a clip with all its properties and places the copy directly after the original. On the main track the following clips ripple right (magnet) or are pushed right if they would overlap; on other tracks the copy goes right after the original when there is room, otherwise to a free or new track of the same type. Linked clips are duplicated too and the copies are linked to each other. The copy does not inherit the transition.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the segment (clip) to edit, e.g. "seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f". Get it from timeline.get → tracks[].segments[].id. |

**Returns:** {track_id, segment} — the new copy.

Example — Duplicate a clip:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### timeline.segment.freeze

**Freeze frame** · MCP tool `timeline_segment_freeze` · `POST /api/v1/commands/timeline.segment.freeze` · undoable · UI: Toolbar/Freeze

Freezes the video frame at at_us (default: the playhead) for 3 seconds — CapCut's Freeze button. The clip is split at at_us, a 3-second still image of that frame (a new segment with still: true, silent, keeping the clip's look: transform, crop, filters, adjustments, effects, mask) is inserted, and the rest of the clip plus everything after it on that track moves 3 s to the right (linked clips follow). Works on video clips only (not photos or freeze frames). Without segment_id the main-track clip under at_us is used.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `at_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  |  | Timeline time in microseconds (1 s = 1000000). Defaults to the current playhead position. |
| `segment_id` | string | no |  |  | ID of the segment (clip) to edit. Optional: when omitted the clip on the main track under at_us is used (what CapCut does when nothing is selected). |

**Returns:** {track_id, segment} — the new freeze-frame segment (3000000 µs long).

Example — Freeze the frame at 2.5 s:

```json
{"at_us":2500000,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### timeline.segment.mirror

**Mirror** · MCP tool `timeline_segment_mirror` · `POST /api/v1/commands/timeline.segment.mirror` · undoable · UI: Toolbar/Mirror

Mirrors a visual segment — the Mirror button in the timeline toolbar. Each call toggles the flip, so calling it twice restores the original. axis=horizontal (default) flips left↔right (Transform.flip_h); vertical flips upside down (flip_v). Use segment.set_transform {flip_h} to set an explicit state instead of toggling.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `axis` | string | no | `"horizontal"` | `horizontal`, `vertical` | Which flip to toggle: horizontal (mirror) or vertical (upside down). |

**Returns:** {segment} with the toggled transform.flip_h / flip_v.

Example — Mirror a selfie clip:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### timeline.segment.move

**Move segment** · MCP tool `timeline_segment_move` · `POST /api/v1/commands/timeline.segment.move` · undoable · UI: Timeline/Drag clip

Moves a clip to a new start time and/or another track — the same as dragging it in the CapCut timeline. On the main track with the magnet on, a move re-orders the clips: the clip is taken out (its gap closes) and re-inserted at the clip boundary nearest to start_us, so there are never gaps. On other tracks the clip starts exactly at start_us; if it would overlap another clip there, a new track is created directly above the destination track (below it for audio) and the clip goes there. Cross-track moves must respect the track type: video/photo between main_video and video_overlay tracks, audio between audio tracks, text/sticker/effect/filter only within their own type. Moving a clip off the main track closes its gap (magnet). Linked clips (link_group, e.g. video + extracted audio) move by the same amount when linkage is on; a linked clip on the magnet main track leads. Snapping (auto_snapping, 100 ms) aligns either edge with other clip edges, the playhead, markers or 0. Start times below 0 are clamped to 0. Clips on locked tracks, or a locked destination, give a conflict error. Tracks left empty by the move disappear.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the segment (clip) to edit, e.g. "seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f". Get it from timeline.get → tracks[].segments[].id. |
| `new_track` | boolean | no |  |  | Create a new track for the clip next to track_id (or next to its current track): directly above for visual tracks, directly below for audio — like dropping a clip in the empty space between or above tracks. |
| `snap` | boolean | no |  |  | Snap to the nearest clip edge, the playhead, a marker or 0 when within 100 ms (100000 µs). Defaults to the project's auto_snapping setting; pass false for an exact position. |
| `start_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  |  | New start time of the clip on the timeline. Omit to keep the current start (track change only). |
| `track_id` | string | no |  |  | Destination track (must accept the clip type). With new_track: the track the new track is created next to. Omit to stay on the current track. |

**Returns:** {track_id, segment} — where the clip ended up (start may differ from start_us because of the magnet or snapping).

Example — Move a text clip to 10 s:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","start_us":10000000}
```

Example — Move a main-track clip onto an overlay track at 3 s:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","start_us":3000000,"track_id":"trk_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Re-order: put a main-track clip first:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","start_us":0}
```

Example — Exact position without snapping:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","snap":false,"start_us":4950000}
```

### timeline.segment.replace

**Replace clip** · MCP tool `timeline_segment_replace` · `POST /api/v1/commands/timeline.segment.replace` · undoable · UI: Timeline/Context menu/Replace clip

Replaces the media of a clip while keeping its position, length, speed and every edit (filters, effects, adjustments, animations, keyframes, transitions, volume) — CapCut's "Replace clip". Video and photo clips accept video or photo materials, audio clips accept audio, stickers accept stickers. A video/audio replacement must be long enough: it needs duration × speed of source from source_start_us, otherwise invalid_argument explains how much is missing. The crop is reset because the new media may have another shape.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `material_id` | string | yes |  |  | The new material, e.g. "mat_6f5e4d3c2b1a" (from media.list). |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the segment (clip) to edit, e.g. "seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f". Get it from timeline.get → tracks[].segments[].id. |
| `source_start_us` | integer (microseconds) | no | `0` | 0 … ∞ | In-point inside the new material (video/audio). |

**Returns:** {track_id, segment} — the clip with its new material.

Example — Replace a clip's video:

```json
{"material_id":"mat_1a2b3c4d5e6f","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### timeline.segment.reverse

**Reverse** · MCP tool `timeline_segment_reverse` · `POST /api/v1/commands/timeline.segment.reverse` · undoable · UI: Toolbar/Reverse

Plays a video clip (or audio segment) backwards — the Reverse button in the timeline toolbar. The clip keeps its position, length and source range; only the playback direction flips (segment.reverse). Without the reverse parameter each call toggles; pass reverse=true/false to set it explicitly. Photos and freeze frames cannot be reversed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `reverse` | boolean | no |  |  | true = play backwards, false = forwards. Omit to toggle. |

**Returns:** {segment} with segment.reverse.

Example — Reverse a clip:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Play forwards again:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","reverse":false,"segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### timeline.segment.rotate

**Rotate** · MCP tool `timeline_segment_rotate` · `POST /api/v1/commands/timeline.segment.rotate` · undoable · UI: Toolbar/Rotate

Rotates a visual segment by 90° — the Rotate button in the timeline toolbar. Clockwise by default; the result is normalised into -360..360 so four clicks return to 0°. For arbitrary angles use segment.set_transform {rotation}. If rotation is keyframed, the new angle becomes a keyframe at the playhead.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `direction` | string | no | `"clockwise"` | `clockwise`, `counterclockwise` | Rotate 90° clockwise (default) or counter-clockwise. |

**Returns:** {segment, keyframed?} with the new transform.rotation.

Example — Rotate a sideways phone video:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Rotate back:

```json
{"direction":"counterclockwise","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### timeline.segment.split

**Split** · MCP tool `timeline_segment_split` · `POST /api/v1/commands/timeline.segment.split` · undoable · hotkey Ctrl+B · UI: Toolbar/Split

Splits a clip into two at at_us (default: the playhead), exactly like CapCut's Split button / Ctrl+B. Both halves keep every property (transform, filters, effects, adjustments, volume, speed, mask…); the left half keeps the original id and the in-animation and fade-in, the right half gets a new id, the out-animation, fade-out and the transition to the next clip. Keyframes are divided at the cut with an interpolated keyframe on both sides so the motion does not change. Linked clips that span the same time are split too and the right halves stay linked to each other. Without segment_id the main-track clip under at_us is split. at_us must lie strictly inside the clip.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `at_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  |  | Timeline time in microseconds (1 s = 1000000). Defaults to the current playhead position. |
| `segment_id` | string | no |  |  | ID of the segment (clip) to edit. Optional: when omitted the clip on the main track under at_us is used (what CapCut does when nothing is selected). |

**Returns:** {track_id, left, right, linked_right_ids?} — both halves (full segments) and the ids of linked right halves.

Example — Split a clip at 4 s:

```json
{"at_us":4000000,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Split the main-track clip under the playhead:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### timeline.segment.trim

**Trim segment** · MCP tool `timeline_segment_trim` · `POST /api/v1/commands/timeline.segment.trim` · undoable · UI: Timeline/Drag clip edge

Moves the left or right edge of a clip to to_us — like dragging a clip edge in CapCut — which changes which part of the source is used. Video and audio cannot be extended past the start or end of their media (the edge stops there); photos, freeze frames, text, stickers, effects and filters can be stretched freely. Speed is respected: at 2x one second on the timeline uses two seconds of source (source_duration = duration × speed). A clip is never shorter than one frame. On the main track with the magnet on, the clip keeps its start and every later clip ripples (trimming the left edge removes content from the beginning and pulls the rest left); elsewhere the edge cannot pass the neighbouring clip. Linked clips are trimmed by the same amount. Keyframes stay attached to the content, fades and animations are shortened if needed, and a transition is shortened to at most half of either neighbour. If the request was limited, clamped is true and the segment shows the actual result.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `edge` | string | yes |  | `left`, `right` | Which edge to move: left = the clip's start (in-point), right = its end (out-point). |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the segment (clip) to edit, e.g. "seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f". Get it from timeline.get → tracks[].segments[].id. |
| `to_us` | integer (microseconds) | yes |  |  | New timeline position of that edge (for the magnet main track: where the edge would be before the ripple). |
| `snap` | boolean | no |  |  | Snap to the nearest clip edge, the playhead, a marker or 0 when within 100 ms (100000 µs). Defaults to the project's auto_snapping setting; pass false for an exact position. |

**Returns:** {track_id, segment, clamped} — the trimmed clip and whether the edge was limited by the media length, a neighbour or the minimum length.

Example — Cut the first second of a clip that starts at 0:

```json
{"edge":"left","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","to_us":1000000}
```

Example — Make a clip end at 8 s:

```json
{"edge":"right","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","to_us":8000000}
```

### timeline.settings.set

**Timeline settings** · MCP tool `timeline_settings_set` · `POST /api/v1/commands/timeline.settings.set` · undoable · UI: Toolbar/Right toggles (magnet, snapping, linkage, preview axis)

Toggles the timeline helpers on the right of CapCut's timeline toolbar. main_track_magnet: the main track never has gaps — inserts ripple later clips right and deletes close gaps; turning it on closes existing gaps immediately. auto_snapping: dragged clip edges, trims and moves snap to clip edges, the playhead, markers and 0 within 100 ms. linkage: clips sharing a link_group (a video and its extracted audio) are selected, moved, trimmed, split and deleted together. preview_axis: the player previews the frame under the mouse while hovering the timeline. Only the given toggles change; all default to on except preview_axis.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `auto_snapping` | boolean | no |  |  | Snap clip edges to other edges, the playhead, markers and 0 (100 ms). |
| `linkage` | boolean | no |  |  | Edit linked clips (video + extracted audio) together. |
| `main_track_magnet` | boolean | no |  |  | Main-track magnet: keep the main track gap-free (ripple editing). |
| `preview_axis` | boolean | no |  |  | Preview the frame under the mouse while hovering the timeline. |

**Returns:** The settings after the change {main_track_magnet, auto_snapping, linkage, preview_axis}.

Example — Turn the magnet off:

```json
{"main_track_magnet":false,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Disable snapping and linkage:

```json
{"auto_snapping":false,"linkage":false,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### timeline.track.add

**Add track** · MCP tool `timeline_track_add` · `POST /api/v1/commands/timeline.track.add` · undoable · UI: Timeline/Track header

Adds an empty track. CapCut usually creates tracks automatically when you drop clips (see timeline.segment.add and timeline.segment.move with new_track); use this when you want to target a fresh track explicitly. Position follows CapCut: video_overlay tracks go above the main/overlay tracks, text/sticker/effect/filter/adjustment tracks on top of all visual tracks, audio tracks below the existing audio tracks. A project has exactly one main_video track, so adding another one is a conflict. Note: tracks other than the main track disappear when an edit removes their last clip.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `type` | string | yes |  | `main_video`, `video_overlay`, `audio`, `text`, `sticker`, `effect`, `filter`, `adjustment` | Track type: main_video (only if missing), video_overlay (picture-in-picture), audio, text, sticker, effect, filter or adjustment. |
| `name` | string | no |  |  | Optional track name shown in the track header. |

**Returns:** The new track {id, type, name?, muted, locked, hidden, segments: []}.

Example — Add an overlay track:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","type":"video_overlay"}
```

### timeline.track.delete

**Delete track** · MCP tool `timeline_track_delete` · `POST /api/v1/commands/timeline.track.delete` · undoable · UI: Timeline/Track header/Delete track

Deletes a track together with every clip on it. The main track cannot be deleted (delete its clips instead) and locked tracks must be unlocked first. Clips on other tracks that were linked to the removed clips stay where they are and lose their link.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `track_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the track to delete (from timeline.get → tracks[].id). |

**Returns:** {deleted_track: id, deleted_segments: [ids]}.

Example — Delete a track:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","track_id":"trk_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### timeline.track.set

**Set track options** · MCP tool `timeline_track_set` · `POST /api/v1/commands/timeline.track.set` · undoable · UI: Timeline/Track header/Lock, Hide, Mute

Changes the toggles in a track header: locked (clips on a locked track cannot be selected, moved, trimmed, split or deleted — every edit returns conflict until it is unlocked), hidden (the track is not drawn in the preview or export; visual tracks only), muted (the sound of every clip on the track is silenced; video and audio tracks) and the track name. Only the given fields change. Works on locked tracks so they can be unlocked.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `track_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the track (from timeline.get → tracks[].id). |
| `hidden` | boolean | no |  |  | Hide (true) or show (false) the track's picture in the preview and export. |
| `locked` | boolean | no |  |  | Lock (true) or unlock (false) the track against edits. |
| `muted` | boolean | no |  |  | Mute (true) or unmute (false) the sound of every clip on the track. |
| `name` | string | no |  |  | New track name; empty string clears it. |

**Returns:** The updated track (with its segments).

Example — Lock a track:

```json
{"locked":true,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","track_id":"trk_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Mute the main track:

```json
{"muted":true,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","track_id":"trk_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

## Tools

4 commands: `tools.cancel`, `tools.install_ffmpeg`, `tools.set_ffmpeg_dir`, `tools.status`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/tools.html

### tools.cancel

**Cancel FFmpeg download** · MCP tool `tools_cancel` · `POST /api/v1/commands/tools.cancel` · UI: First run/Cancel

Stops a running tools.install_ffmpeg download (the Cancel button under the progress bar). The partial file is deleted and the job ends in state "cancelled"; FFmpeg stays missing until tools.install_ffmpeg is called again. Does nothing (cancelled=false) when no download is running.

No parameters.

**Returns:** {cancelled: true when a running download was stopped}.

Example — Cancel the download:

```json
{}
```

### tools.install_ffmpeg

**Download FFmpeg** · MCP tool `tools_install_ffmpeg` · `POST /api/v1/commands/tools.install_ffmpeg` · UI: First run/Download FFmpeg

Downloads FFmpeg for Kadr — the first-run "Download now" button. Fetches the BtbN GPL build of FFmpeg 7.1 for Windows x64 (about 100 MB) from GitHub, verifies its SHA-256 against the checksums.sha256 file of the same release (a mismatch deletes the download and fails), then extracts ONLY ffmpeg.exe and ffprobe.exe into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Kadr\tools\ffmpeg\bin where Kadr finds them immediately (no restart). Runs in the background and returns at once unless wait=true; progress arrives as tools.progress events (state downloading → verifying → extracting → done | failed | cancelled), or poll tools.status; stop it with tools.cancel. When FFmpeg is already available (PATH, next to Kadr, chosen folder) nothing is downloaded and already_installed=true, unless force=true. FFmpeg is licensed under the GPL (https://ffmpeg.org/legal.html). Only supported on Windows x64 (not_available elsewhere).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `force` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Download Kadr's own copy even when an FFmpeg is already found (e.g. a broken or very old one on PATH). |
| `source` | string | no | `"btbn"` | `btbn` | Download source. Only "btbn" (github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds, GPL build, FFmpeg 7.1 branch) is available. |
| `wait` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Block until the download is verified and installed (can take minutes) instead of returning immediately. |

**Returns:** {started, already_installed, message, ...tools.status fields}.

Example — Download FFmpeg in the background:

```json
{}
```

Example — Download and wait until installed:

```json
{"wait":true}
```

### tools.set_ffmpeg_dir

**Use my FFmpeg** · MCP tool `tools_set_ffmpeg_dir` · `POST /api/v1/commands/tools.set_ffmpeg_dir` · UI: First run/I have FFmpeg

Points Kadr at an FFmpeg that is already on this computer — "I have FFmpeg — choose folder".
