The folder (or its bin subfolder) must contain both ffmpeg.exe and ffprobe.exe and ffmpeg must run ("-version"); it is saved as ffmpeg_dir in settings.json, used from now on (no restart) and on every start, and takes precedence over the copy next to Kadr, the downloaded copy and PATH. clear=true forgets the folder.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clear` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Forget the chosen folder and go back to automatic lookup. |
| `dir` | string | no |  |  | Absolute folder path, e.g. "C:\\ffmpeg\\bin" or "C:\\ffmpeg" (its bin subfolder is checked too). Required unless clear is true. |

**Returns:** The tools.status object after the change.

Example — Use FFmpeg from C:\ffmpeg\bin:

```json
{"dir":"C:\\ffmpeg\\bin"}
```

Example — Forget the folder:

```json
{"clear":true}
```

### tools.status

**Tools status** · MCP tool `tools_status` · `POST /api/v1/commands/tools.status` · UI: Settings/FFmpeg

Reports whether FFmpeg and FFprobe — required for importing, previewing and exporting media — are available, where they were found (source: env = KADR_FFMPEG, custom_dir = folder chosen with tools.set_ffmpeg_dir, next_to_exe, downloaded = Kadr's tools folder, path = system PATH) and their version, plus the state of a running tools.install_ffmpeg download and where it would download from (source, license, approximate size). Kadr does not bundle FFmpeg; when ffmpeg.found is false call tools.install_ffmpeg (Windows x64) or tools.set_ffmpeg_dir.

No parameters.

**Returns:** {ffmpeg{found, ffmpeg_path, ffprobe_path, version, source, error}, tools_dir, ffmpeg_dir, auto_download_supported, install{tool, state idle|downloading|verifying|extracting|done|failed|cancelled, downloaded_bytes, total_bytes, progress, error}, source{id, name, url, checksums_url, page, license, license_url, approx_size_mb}}.

Example — Is FFmpeg installed?:

```json
{}
```

## Transcript

7 commands: `transcript.clear`, `transcript.delete_text`, `transcript.delete_words`, `transcript.get`, `transcript.remove_fillers`, `transcript.remove_pauses`, `transcript.transcribe`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/transcript.html

### transcript.clear

**Delete transcript** · MCP tool `transcript_clear` · `POST /api/v1/commands/transcript.clear` · undoable

Removes the stored transcript of a material (e.g. before transcribing again in another language). Captions already created are kept. Undoable.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `material_id` | string | yes |  |  | Material whose transcript is removed (from media.list or transcript.get). |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |

**Returns:** {material_id, words: number of words removed}.

Example — Forget a transcript:

```json
{"material_id":"mat_1a2b3c4d5e6f","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### transcript.delete_text

**Delete text** · MCP tool `transcript_delete_text` · `POST /api/v1/commands/transcript.delete_text` · undoable

Finds a phrase in the transcript and cuts it out of the video — the easiest transcript edit for an AI agent ("delete 'so basically what I mean is'"). Matching ignores case and punctuation and is word by word within one clip. By default the first occurrence on the timeline is deleted (or the occurrence-th); all=true deletes every occurrence. The cut works like transcript.delete_words (split, delete, ripple, captions follow). One undo step; not_found when the phrase is not in the transcript.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `text` | string | yes |  |  | The words to delete, e.g. "you know what I mean". |
| `all` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Delete every occurrence instead of one. |
| `occurrence` | integer | no | `1` | 1 … ∞ | Which occurrence to delete when all=false (1 = the first on the timeline). |
| `ripple_captions` | boolean | no | `true` |  | Make caption cues follow the cut (later cues move left, removed words disappear from their cue). Default true. |
| `segment_id` | string | no |  |  | Only search this clip (default: every transcribed audible clip). |

**Returns:** {matches: total found, cuts: [{segment_id, start_us, end_us, text}], removed_us, captions_changed, duration_us}.

Example — Cut a sentence:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","text":"let me start again"}
```

Example — Cut every 'you know':

```json
{"all":true,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","text":"you know"}
```

### transcript.delete_words

**Delete words** · MCP tool `transcript_delete_words` · `POST /api/v1/commands/transcript.delete_words` · undoable · UI: Library/Transcript/Delete

Transcript-based editing: deletes words from a clip by cutting the video/audio where they are spoken (select words in the transcript → Delete). ranges are inclusive word indices from transcript.get for that segment_id. Each range removes the time from the first word's start to the last word's end plus the silence after it (up to 0.5 s, so the next word follows naturally): the clip is split, the part is deleted together with linked clips (extracted audio), and the rest of the track moves left (on the magnet main track every later clip ripples, and linked clips follow). Caption cues follow the cut unless ripple_captions=false. Everything is ONE undo step. Word indices of the clip change after the edit — call transcript.get again.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `ranges` | object[] | yes |  |  | Word ranges to delete: [{"from": 3, "to": 5}] (inclusive indices from transcript.get → words[].index). [3, 5] pairs and single indices are accepted too. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | Clip whose words are deleted (from transcript.get → segments[].segment_id). |
| `ripple_captions` | boolean | no | `true` |  | Make caption cues follow the cut (later cues move left, removed words disappear from their cue). Default true. |

**Returns:** {cuts: [{segment_id, start_us, end_us, text}] (timeline times before the edit), removed_us, captions_changed, duration_us (project length after)}.

Example — Delete words 3–5:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","ranges":[{"from":3,"to":5}],"segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Delete two separate words:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","ranges":[2,9],"segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### transcript.get

**Get transcript** · MCP tool `transcript_get` · `POST /api/v1/commands/transcript.get` · UI: Library/Transcript

Returns the transcript of the timeline — the Transcript panel: for every clip with sound (main track, overlays, audio tracks; or only segment_id) the recognised words mapped onto the TIMELINE (speed, speed curves, reverse and trims are honoured; words outside the clip's trimmed range are left out), with their source times and confidence, plus the clip's text. Clips whose material has not been transcribed are listed with transcribed=false (run transcript.transcribe). Word indices are per clip and are what transcript.delete_words expects; they change when the clip is edited, so re-read after edits. Clips that are not heard (muted track, volume 0 — e.g. a video whose sound was extracted to a linked audio clip) are omitted unless include_silent=true.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `include_silent` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Also list clips that are muted or have volume 0. |
| `include_words` | boolean | no | `true` |  | Include the word list (false = text only). |
| `segment_id` | string | no |  |  | Only this clip (a video or audio clip). |

**Returns:** {segments: [{segment_id, track_id, track_type, material_id, material_name, transcribed, audible, language, model, start_us, end_us, text, words: [{index, text, start_us, end_us (timeline), source_start_us, source_end_us, confidence}]}], count, words (total), untranscribed_material_ids}.

Example — Whole timeline:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — One clip:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### transcript.remove_fillers

**Remove filler words** · MCP tool `transcript_remove_fillers` · `POST /api/v1/commands/transcript.remove_fillers` · undoable · UI: Library/Transcript/Remove filler words

Cuts filler words out of the speech ("Remove filler words"): hesitation sounds that are always fillers — English um, uh, er, erm, ah, hmm, mm; Ukrainian/Russian е, еее, ем, ммм, а-а, хм, ну (elongated spellings like "ummm" match too) — and words often used as fillers only when they are set off by commas or sentence breaks: English like, you know, I mean, so, well, basically, actually, literally, kind of, sort of; Ukrainian типу, коротше, значить, ніби, як би, ну от, власне; Russian типа, короче, значит, как бы, вот, в общем. language=auto uses each transcript's language (all lists for other languages); words adds your own fillers (always removed). Each filler is cut like transcript.delete_words. Use preview=true to see the list first. One undo step.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `language` | string | no | `"auto"` | `auto`, `all`, `none`, `en`, `uk`, `ru` | Built-in filler lists: auto (transcript language), all, none (only words), en, uk or ru. |
| `preview` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Only report what would be removed; the project is not changed. |
| `ripple_captions` | boolean | no | `true` |  | Make caption cues follow the cut (later cues move left, removed words disappear from their cue). Default true. |
| `segment_id` | string | no |  |  | Only this clip (default: every transcribed audible clip). |
| `words` | string[] | no |  |  | Extra filler words or phrases to remove wherever they occur, e.g. ["okay", "right so"]. |

**Returns:** {found: [{segment_id, text, start_us, end_us}], count, removed_us, preview, cuts, captions_changed, duration_us}.

Example — Remove fillers:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Preview Ukrainian fillers:

```json
{"language":"uk","preview":true,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Also remove 'okay':

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","words":["okay"]}
```

### transcript.remove_pauses

**Remove pauses** · MCP tool `transcript_remove_pauses` · `POST /api/v1/commands/transcript.remove_pauses` · undoable · UI: Library/Transcript/Remove pauses

Shortens every silence between words that lasts at least min_pause_us ("Remove pauses > X s"), using the word timings of the transcript: each pause is cut down to keep_us (half kept before, half after) so speech does not sound chopped. With edges=true the silence before the first and after the last word of a clip is trimmed too. Clips without any recognised words are left alone. Cuts ripple like transcript.delete_words; captions follow. Use preview=true to see the pauses first. One undo step. (For silence detection from the audio level instead of words see ai.remove_silence.)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `edges` | boolean | no | `true` |  | Also trim the silence at the start and end of each clip. |
| `keep_us` | integer (microseconds) | no | `300000` | 0 … 5000000 | How much of each pause to keep (default 0.3 s). |
| `min_pause_us` | integer (microseconds) | no | `1000000` | 100000 … 60000000 | Pauses at least this long are shortened (default 1 s). |
| `preview` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Only report what would be removed; the project is not changed. |
| `ripple_captions` | boolean | no | `true` |  | Make caption cues follow the cut (later cues move left, removed words disappear from their cue). Default true. |
| `segment_id` | string | no |  |  | Only this clip (default: every transcribed audible clip). |

**Returns:** {found: [{segment_id, start_us, end_us}], count, removed_us, preview, cuts, captions_changed, duration_us}.

Example — Remove pauses over 1 s:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Tight edit: pauses over 0.5 s, keep 0.15 s:

```json
{"keep_us":150000,"min_pause_us":500000,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### transcript.transcribe

**Transcribe** · MCP tool `transcript_transcribe` · `POST /api/v1/commands/transcript.transcribe` · UI: Library/Transcript/Transcribe

Recognises the speech of one material (or of the materials of segment_ids, or of every audible clip when both are omitted) and stores it as the material's transcript: every word with its start/end in SOURCE time and a confidence. This is the Transcript panel's "Transcribe" button; no captions are created (use captions.auto or captions.from_transcript for that). Afterwards transcript.get shows the words on the timeline and transcript.delete_words / delete_text / remove_fillers / remove_pauses edit the video by editing the text. Materials that already have a transcript are skipped unless force=true or a different explicit language is requested. Runs as a background job like captions.auto (wait=true blocks). Not undoable (transcripts are analysis data; transcript.clear removes one).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `device` | string | no | `"auto"` | `auto`, `cuda`, `cpu` | Where recognition runs: auto (CUDA GPU when usable, else CPU int8), cuda or cpu. A failing GPU falls back to the CPU. |
| `force` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Transcribe again even when the material already has a transcript (e.g. to use a bigger model). |
| `language` | string | no | `"auto"` |  | Spoken language: "auto" (detect, default) or a code/name such as en, uk, es, de, fr, pt, ru, zh, ja, ko, ar, hi, it, nl, pl, tr, vi, th, id, ms, bn, my, ro, tl (Filipino). Locales ("en-US") and English names ("Ukrainian") are accepted. captions.asr_status lists all ~100 languages. |
| `material_id` | string | no |  |  | Material to transcribe (from media.list). Omit to use segment_ids or every audible clip. |
| `model` | string | no | `"small"` | `tiny`, `base`, `small`, `medium`, `large-v3` | Whisper model size: tiny (fastest, least accurate), base, small (default: good accuracy, ~1× real time on a CPU, ~5× faster on an NVIDIA GPU), medium, large-v3 (best, slow without a GPU). Only models already downloaded can be used. |
| `prompt` | string | no |  |  | Optional hint text for the recogniser: names, jargon or spelling to prefer (e.g. "Kadr, CapCut, Kyiv"). |
| `segment_id` | string | no |  |  | Shortcut for a single clip. |
| `segment_ids` | string[] | no |  |  | Transcribe the materials of these clips. |
| `wait` | boolean | no | `false` |  | true = block until the job finishes and return its final status (with the result); false (default) = return the job right away and report progress through captions.progress events / captions.status. |

**Returns:** Job status like captions.auto (kind "transcript"); when done result = {transcribed: [{material_id, language, model, words, text (first ~280 characters)}]}.

Example — Transcribe a material and wait:

```json
{"material_id":"mat_1a2b3c4d5e6f","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","wait":true}
```

Example — Transcribe everything on the timeline in English:

```json
{"language":"en","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

## Transitions

4 commands: `transition.apply_all`, `transition.get`, `transition.remove`, `transition.set`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/transitions.html

### transition.apply_all

**Apply transition to all** · MCP tool `transition_apply_all` · `POST /api/v1/commands/transition.apply_all` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Transition/Apply to all

Puts the same transition between every pair of touching clips on a track (default: the main video track) — CapCut's "Apply to all" button. type/duration default to the transition of segment_id if given, else the first transition already on the track, else Mix 0.5 s. Each duration is clamped to half of the shorter clip of its pair; pairs with a gap or clips shorter than 0.2 s are skipped and counted. direction and softness work as in transition.set (they are applied on top of the copied type).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `direction` | string | no |  | `left`, `right`, `up`, `down` | Optional direction for transitions that have one (library item params.directions): the way the motion travels. For directional families (wipe_*, slide_*, push_*, cube_turn_*, whip_*) it selects the sibling id. |
| `duration_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 100000 … 10000000 | Transition length; clamped per pair. See the description for the default. |
| `segment_id` | string | no |  |  | Copy type and duration from this clip's transition (the selected transition in the UI). |
| `softness` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Optional edge softness 0..1 (0 = hard edge, 1 = very soft) for mask transitions with params.softness=true (wipes, irises, shape reveals, checkerboard, luma/ink dissolves, burns, light sweep). |
| `track_id` | string | no |  |  | Track to process (main or overlay video track). Defaults to the main video track. |
| `type` | string | no |  |  | Transition id from library.list kind=transition. See the description for the default. |

**Returns:** {track_id, type, duration_us, applied: number of pairs set, skipped: number of pairs skipped}.

Example — Mix between every clip:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","type":"mix"}
```

Example — Copy the selected clip's transition:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

### transition.get

**Get transition** · MCP tool `transition_get` · `POST /api/v1/commands/transition.get` · UI: Inspector/Transition

Describes the transition that follows a clip — what the Transition inspector shows when a transition badge is selected: the stored type, its library id and name, duration, the current direction and softness (defaults filled in) and which options the transition supports, plus the longest duration the pair allows. has_transition=false (and no transition fields) when the cut is a hard cut. Change it with transition.set.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id. |

**Returns:** {segment_id, has_transition, next_segment_id?, max_duration_us?, type?, id?, name?, duration_us?, direction?, softness?, options?}.

Example — Inspect the transition after a clip:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

### transition.remove

**Remove transition** · MCP tool `transition_remove` · `POST /api/v1/commands/transition.remove` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Transition/Delete

Removes the transition that follows a clip (segment.transition_out), turning it back into a hard cut. Removing from a clip without a transition is a no-op that reports removed=false.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id. |

**Returns:** {segment_id, removed: bool}.

Example — Back to a hard cut:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f"}
```

### transition.set

**Set transition** · MCP tool `transition_set` · `POST /api/v1/commands/transition.set` · undoable · UI: Library/Transitions

Adds or replaces the transition between a clip and the NEXT clip on the same track (main or overlay video track), like dropping a transition between two clips in CapCut. The transition is stored on the left clip (segment.transition_out) and plays across the cut. The two clips must touch (the next clip starts where this one ends, within half a frame); otherwise a conflict error explains how to fix it. duration_us is clamped to half of the shorter of the two clips (the result reports clamped=true); both clips must be at least 0.2 s long. Optional direction (left/right/up/down) and softness (0..1) apply to transitions whose library item lists them in params (directions, softness); they are stored in the type as URL-style options, e.g. "bars_stagger?direction=up&softness=0.3" (directional families such as wipe_left + direction up store the sibling id "wipe_up"; values equal to the defaults are dropped). Strip everything from "?" to get the library id. Asking a transition for an option it does not have is an invalid_argument error listing its options.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id. |
| `type` | string | yes |  |  | Transition id from library.list kind=transition, e.g. "mix", "black_fade", "wipe_left", "cube_turn_left", "iris_heart". A stored type with options ("blinds_h?direction=up") is accepted too. |
| `direction` | string | no |  | `left`, `right`, `up`, `down` | Optional direction for transitions that have one (library item params.directions): the way the motion travels. For directional families (wipe_*, slide_*, push_*, cube_turn_*, whip_*) it selects the sibling id. |
| `duration_us` | integer (microseconds) | no | `500000` | 100000 … 10000000 | Transition length (default 0.5 s). Clamped to half of the shorter neighbouring clip. |
| `softness` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Optional edge softness 0..1 (0 = hard edge, 1 = very soft) for mask transitions with params.softness=true (wipes, irises, shape reveals, checkerboard, luma/ink dissolves, burns, light sweep). |

**Returns:** {segment_id, next_segment_id, transition: {type, duration_us}, id, name, direction?, softness?, options: {directions, default_direction, softness, default_softness, direction_by_sibling}, clamped, max_duration_us}.

Example — Cross-dissolve after a clip:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f","type":"mix"}
```

Example — One-second dip to black:

```json
{"duration_us":1000000,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f","type":"black_fade"}
```

Example — Cube turning upwards:

```json
{"direction":"up","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f","type":"cube_turn_left"}
```

Example — Soft heart iris:

```json
{"duration_us":800000,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9a8b7c6d5e4f","softness":0.6,"type":"iris_heart"}
```

## Updates

6 commands: `update.check`, `update.download`, `update.install`, `update.settings`, `update.skip`, `update.status`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/updates.html

### update.check

**Check for updates** · MCP tool `update_check` · `POST /api/v1/commands/update.check` · UI: Menu/Check for updates…

Asks GitHub whether a newer Kadr is published — Settings → Updates → "Check now" and Menu → "Check for updates…". Downloads latest.json (+ latest.json.sig) from the release repository (stable: the latest regular release; beta: the newest release including pre-releases, via the GitHub API), verifies its Ed25519 signature with the key built into Kadr and compares versions with semver rules (1.1.0-beta.1 < 1.1.0-rc.1 < 1.1.0). Nothing is downloaded or installed. The release channel is PRIVATE (Kadr is distributed by invitation): without an access token, or with a token that cannot read the repository, the check succeeds with private=true, access="none", available=false and a reason ("ask the vendor for the latest installer"), the updater state becomes no_access and no event is published; save a GitHub token with update.settings {github_token} (or set KADR_UPDATE_TOKEN) to receive updates automatically. available=true means a newer version exists; skipped=true means the user chose "Skip this version" for it (it is still reported here but never announced automatically); can_install=false (with reason) means this build cannot self-update — portable builds, development builds without a signing key, or a release without a Windows installer — so open release_url instead. A pre-release is never offered on the stable channel. Publishes update.available when a newer, not skipped version is found. Fails with not_available when GitHub cannot be reached, not_found when the repository has no release yet, and internal when the signature does not verify (the update is refused).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `channel` | string | no |  | `stable`, `beta` | Release channel to look at: "stable" = regular releases only (the GitHub "latest" release), "beta" = also pre-releases such as 0.2.0-beta.1. Omit to use the channel saved in settings (update.settings). |

**Returns:** {current, latest, available, channel, prerelease, notes_markdown, notes_url, release_url, published_at, size (installer bytes), installer, signed, skipped, required (current is older than min_supported), min_supported, portable, can_install, reason, checked_at, private (no access to the private channel), access public|token|none}.

Example — Check the configured channel:

```json
{}
```

Example — Look for pre-releases too:

```json
{"channel":"beta"}
```

### update.download

**Download update** · MCP tool `update_download` · `POST /api/v1/commands/update.download` · UI: Settings/Updates/Download & install

Downloads the installer of the newest version found by update.check (runs a check first when none was done in this session) into %TEMP%\Kadr-update\ and verifies its exact size and SHA-256 against the signed latest.json; a file that does not match is deleted and the update is refused. Runs in the background and returns immediately (state "downloading") unless wait=true; progress arrives as update.progress events, completion as update.ready, errors as update.failed. An installer already downloaded and verified is reused. Does not install anything — call update.install afterwards. Refused with not_available for portable builds, development builds without a signing key and releases without a Windows installer (open release_url instead), and with conflict when Kadr is already up to date.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `wait` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Block until the download finished and was verified (can take minutes for ~100 MB) instead of returning at once. |

**Returns:** The update.status object (state downloading, ready or failed).

Example — Start downloading in the background:

```json
{}
```

Example — Download and wait until verified:

```json
{"wait":true}
```

### update.install

**Install update** · MCP tool `update_install` · `POST /api/v1/commands/update.install` · UI: Settings/Updates/Download & install

Installs the newest version and restarts Kadr — the "Download & install" button. Downloads and verifies the installer first if update.download has not finished (SHA-256 + size from the Ed25519-signed latest.json, checked again right before running), then starts it detached with /VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART /CLOSEAPPLICATIONS /RELAUNCH and closes the desktop app about a second later. The installer upgrades in place, keeps all projects and settings, closes running Kadr processes (Kadr.exe, kadr-server.exe, kadr-mcp.exe) and starts Kadr again when done, so API clients lose their connection for a minute. UNSAVED WORK: projects are saved after every command, but running exports are cancelled. Requires confirm=true as a safety check. In the headless server nothing quits by itself: the result asks to exit. Refused for portable builds and builds without a signing key (not_available).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `confirm` | boolean | yes |  |  | Must be true: confirms that Kadr may close (running exports stop) and the installer may run. |

**Returns:** {started, version, installer, args (the exact installer arguments), quitting (the app exits shortly), message}.

Example — Install the downloaded update and restart:

```json
{"confirm":true}
```

### update.settings

**Update settings** · MCP tool `update_settings` · `POST /api/v1/commands/update.settings` · UI: Settings/Updates

Reads or changes the updater preferences stored in <data dir>/settings.json (key "update"). Without arguments it only returns them. auto_check (default on) makes Kadr check GitHub in the background after startup, at most once every 24 hours, never blocking the editor (a private channel without access stays silent); channel picks stable releases or also beta pre-releases. Regular builds such as 1.0.0 use the stable channel; builds that are themselves pre-releases default to beta. github_token stores the GitHub access token the vendor gave you for the private release channel (a fine-grained token with read-only Contents access to the release repository, or a classic token with repo scope); it is saved as update.github_token in settings.json, used only for requests to the GitHub API, and NEVER returned — results only show github_token_set and github_token_source (env = the KADR_UPDATE_TOKEN environment variable, which wins over the saved one; settings). Pass "" to remove it. Changing settings does not check by itself — call update.check afterwards.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `auto_check` | boolean | no |  |  | Check for updates automatically on startup (once a day). Omit to leave unchanged. |
| `channel` | string | no |  | `stable`, `beta` | "stable" (regular releases) or "beta" (also pre-releases). Omit to leave unchanged. |
| `github_token` | string | no |  |  | GitHub access token for the private release channel (github_pat_… or ghp_…); "" removes the saved token. Never echoed back. Omit to leave unchanged. |

**Returns:** {auto_check, channel, last_check (RFC 3339, omitted before the first check), skipped_version, github_token_set, github_token_source (env|settings, omitted when none)}.

Example — Read the settings:

```json
{}
```

Example — Join the beta channel:

```json
{"channel":"beta"}
```

Example — Turn automatic checks off:

```json
{"auto_check":false}
```

Example — Save the access token from the vendor:

```json
{"github_token":"github_pat_EXAMPLE"}
```

Example — Remove the saved access token:

```json
{"github_token":""}
```

### update.skip

**Skip this version** · MCP tool `update_skip` · `POST /api/v1/commands/update.skip` · UI: Settings/Updates/Skip this version

Remembers a version as skipped — "Skip this version" under the release notes. A skipped version is no longer announced by the automatic startup check (no update.available event, no badge) but update.check still reports it with skipped=true, and any newer version is offered again normally. Only one version can be skipped; clear=true forgets it. Stored in settings.json.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clear` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Forget the skipped version instead (version is ignored). |
| `version` | string | no |  |  | Version to skip, e.g. "0.2.0" (a leading v is accepted). Omit to skip the latest version found by update.check. |

**Returns:** The saved settings {auto_check, channel, last_check, skipped_version, github_token_set, github_token_source}.

Example — Skip 0.2.0:

```json
{"version":"0.2.0"}
```

Example — Stop skipping:

```json
{"clear":true}
```

### update.status

**Update status** · MCP tool `update_status` · `POST /api/v1/commands/update.status` · UI: Settings/Updates

Returns the updater state without contacting GitHub: state (idle | checking | up_to_date | available | downloading | ready | installing | failed | no_access — the private release channel cannot be read, see latest.reason), the result of the last check (latest, null before the first check), download progress, the verified installer path when ready, the last error, the saved settings, whether this is a portable build and whether this build carries an update signing key. Poll it every 1-2 s during update.download, or listen to the update.progress / update.ready / update.failed events instead.

No parameters.

**Returns:** {state, current, latest (update.check result or null), downloaded_bytes, total_bytes, progress 0..1, installer_path, error, settings{auto_check, channel, last_check, skipped_version, github_token_set, github_token_source}, portable, signing_key, repo, releases_url}.

Example — Poll the updater:

```json
{}
```

## Video

1 commands: `segment.set_video_cleanup`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/video.html

### segment.set_video_cleanup

**Video clean-up** · MCP tool `segment_set_video_cleanup` · `POST /api/v1/commands/segment.set_video_cleanup` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Video/Basic

Sets the video clean-up of a video clip: 'Reduce image noise' (denoise) and 'Remove flicker' (deflicker) from the Basic section of CapCut's video inspector. Both are applied by the renderer while decoding the clip, so the preview, preview.frame and export all show them. denoise is a strength 0..1 (0 = off): up to 0.7 a fast spatio-temporal denoiser (ffmpeg hqdn3d) is used, above 0.7 a stronger but slower non-local-means denoiser (nlmeans) — expect slower previews/exports at high values. deflicker smooths frame-to-frame brightness changes (mains-light flicker, timelapse exposure jumps) with a 5-frame window. Only video clips are supported (photos have no frame-to-frame noise). Omitted parameters keep their current value; pass at least one. Undoable.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | Video clip to clean up (timeline.get lists segment ids). |
| `deflicker` | boolean | no |  |  | true removes brightness flicker, false turns it off. |
| `denoise` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Noise reduction strength 0..1 (0 = off, 0.3 = light, 0.6 = strong, > 0.7 = very strong/slow). |

**Returns:** {segment_id, denoise, deflicker, filter}: filter is the ffmpeg filter chain now used for the clip.

Example — Reduce noise moderately:

```json
{"denoise":0.4,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Remove flicker from a timelapse:

```json
{"deflicker":true,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Turn both off:

```json
{"deflicker":false,"denoise":0,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

## Video properties

9 commands: `segment.get`, `segment.reset`, `segment.set_background`, `segment.set_blend`, `segment.set_chroma_key`, `segment.set_crop`, `segment.set_mask`, `segment.set_opacity`, `segment.set_transform`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/video-properties.html

### segment.get

**Get segment properties** · MCP tool `segment_get` · `POST /api/v1/commands/segment.get` · UI: Inspector

Returns one segment with everything the inspector shows for it: the raw segment, its track, the kind (video, photo, audio, text, sticker, effect, filter, adjustment), the material, which property commands apply (capabilities), the keyframeable properties, and the evaluated values (transform, opacity, volume, adjustments and source time, keyframes interpolated) at time_us — by default at the playhead (clamped into the segment). Use it to check the effect of segment.* / keyframe.* commands.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `time_us` | integer (microseconds) | no |  | 0 … ∞ | Time relative to the segment start to evaluate keyframes at. Defaults to the playhead. |

**Returns:** {segment, track_id, track_type, kind, material?, capabilities, keyframe_properties, time_us, evaluated, volume_db}.

Example — Inspect a clip:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### segment.reset

**Reset properties** · MCP tool `segment_reset` · `POST /api/v1/commands/segment.reset` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Section/Reset

Resets one group of a segment's properties to CapCut's defaults — the ↺ buttons of the inspector sections. Groups: transform (position, scale 100%, rotation 0, flips + their keyframes), blend (opacity 100%, normal blend + opacity keyframes), crop, mask, chroma_key, background (canvas fill → project default), adjust (all colour adjustments, LUT, adjust.* keyframes), audio (0 dB, no fades, voice effect, noise reduction and normalisation off, volume keyframes), speed (1x, no curve, pitch off — the timeline length changes and the main track ripples like segment.set_speed), animation (in/out/combo/loop), keyframes (every keyframe) and all (every group that applies to this segment type). A specific group that does not apply (e.g. audio on a photo) is rejected with invalid_argument. Content (text, source range, filters, effects, transitions) is never touched.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `group` | string | yes |  | `transform`, `blend`, `crop`, `mask`, `chroma_key`, `background`, `adjust`, `audio`, `speed`, `animation`, `keyframes`, `all` | Which group of properties to reset; all resets every applicable group. |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |

**Returns:** {segment, rippled_segments?} after the reset.

Example — Reset position/scale/rotation:

```json
{"group":"transform","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Back to the original clip:

```json
{"group":"all","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### segment.set_background

**Set canvas background** · MCP tool `segment_set_background` · `POST /api/v1/commands/segment.set_background` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Video/Basic/Canvas

Sets the canvas fill shown behind a main-track clip where it does not cover the frame (e.g. a vertical video on a 16:9 canvas) — Video → Basic → Canvas in CapCut. type: color (solid colour), blur (blurred, zoomed copy of the clip; blur 0..1 = strength), image (a picture file), none (use the project's canvas background from project.set_canvas). apply_to_all copies the setting to every video/photo clip on the main track (CapCut's 'Apply to all'). Only main-track clips have a canvas background.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `type` | string | yes |  | `none`, `color`, `blur`, `image` | Fill type: color, blur, image, or none to fall back to the project background. |
| `apply_to_all` | boolean | no | `false` |  | Also apply to every other video/photo clip on the main track. |
| `blur` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Blur strength for type=blur: 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1 match CapCut's four blur levels (default 0.5). Unit: fraction 0..1. |
| `color` | string | no |  |  | Fill colour #RRGGBB for type=color (default #000000). |
| `image` | string | no |  |  | Absolute path of an image file for type=image. |

**Returns:** {segment, note?} — the selected segment after the change; note reports how many clips were updated by apply_to_all.

Example — Blurred background behind a vertical clip:

```json
{"blur":0.5,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","type":"blur"}
```

Example — White background everywhere:

```json
{"apply_to_all":true,"color":"#ffffff","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","type":"color"}
```

### segment.set_blend

**Set blend mode** · MCP tool `segment_set_blend` · `POST /api/v1/commands/segment.set_blend` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Video/Basic/Blend

Sets how a clip mixes with the layers below it — Video → Basic → Blend in CapCut. Blend modes only show a difference on overlay tracks (or text/stickers) because the main track has nothing below it except the canvas. Modes: normal, darken, screen, overlay, multiply, lighten, hard_light, soft_light, linear_burn, color_burn, color_dodge, add (linear dodge / lighter), difference, exclusion. Optionally sets opacity in the same call.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `mode` | string | no |  | `normal`, `darken`, `screen`, `overlay`, `multiply`, `lighten`, `hard_light`, `soft_light`, `linear_burn`, `color_burn`, `color_dodge`, `add`, `difference`, `exclusion` | Blend mode; normal resets to plain alpha compositing. |
| `opacity` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Optional opacity 0..1 (the slider in the same Blend section). Unit: fraction 0..1. |

**Returns:** {segment, keyframed?}.

Example — Screen a light-leak overlay:

```json
{"mode":"screen","project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Multiply at 80%:

```json
{"mode":"multiply","opacity":0.8,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### segment.set_chroma_key

**Set chroma key** · MCP tool `segment_set_chroma_key` · `POST /api/v1/commands/segment.set_chroma_key` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Video/Remove BG/Chroma key

Removes a colour from a video/photo clip (green/blue screen) — Video → Remove BG → Chroma key in CapCut. color is the colour to key out (#RRGGBB, CapCut's colour picker); intensity 0..1 is how wide a range of similar colours becomes transparent (default 0.5 when the key is created); shadow 0..1 keeps/darkens shadows cast on the screen. enabled=false removes the chroma key. Usually applied to a clip on an overlay track above a background clip.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `color` | string | no |  |  | Key colour as #RRGGBB, e.g. "#00ff00" for a green screen. Required when creating the key. |
| `enabled` | boolean | no |  |  | false removes the chroma key (other parameters are then ignored). |
| `intensity` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | How aggressively similar colours are removed: 0 = nothing, 1 = very wide range. Unit: fraction 0..1. |
| `shadow` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Shadow strength kept from the keyed area: 0 = none. Unit: fraction 0..1. |

**Returns:** {segment} with segment.chroma_key (omitted when removed).

Example — Key out a green screen:

```json
{"color":"#00ff00","intensity":0.45,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Turn chroma key off:

```json
{"enabled":false,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### segment.set_crop

**Set crop rectangle** · MCP tool `segment_set_crop` · `POST /api/v1/commands/segment.set_crop` · undoable · UI: Toolbar/Crop

Crops a video or photo clip to a rectangle given in source fractions (0..1 of the original frame, before rotation/scale): x,y is the top-left corner of the kept area, w,h its size. The full frame {x:0,y:0,w:1,h:1} removes the crop. The rectangle must lie inside the frame (x+w ≤ 1, y+h ≤ 1). For ratio presets or resetting use timeline.segment.crop, which is what the toolbar Crop dialog calls.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `h` | number (source fraction) | yes |  | 0.01 … 1 | Height of the kept area as a fraction of the source height (1 = full height). |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `w` | number (source fraction) | yes |  | 0.01 … 1 | Width of the kept area as a fraction of the source width (1 = full width). |
| `x` | number (source fraction) | yes |  | 0 … 1 | Left edge of the kept area as a fraction of the source width (0 = left edge). |
| `y` | number (source fraction) | yes |  | 0 … 1 | Top edge of the kept area as a fraction of the source height (0 = top edge). |

**Returns:** {segment} with segment.crop set (omitted when the crop was removed).

Example — Keep the centre 50%:

```json
{"h":0.5,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","w":0.5,"x":0.25,"y":0.25}
```

### segment.set_mask

**Set mask** · MCP tool `segment_set_mask` · `POST /api/v1/commands/segment.set_mask` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Video/Mask

Adds, edits or removes the mask of a video/photo clip — Video → Mask in CapCut. Shapes: linear (one straight edge through the centre, rotate it to choose the side), mirror (a band of height h), circle (ellipse w×h), rectangle (w×h with round corners), heart, star; none removes the mask. Geometry is in clip fractions: x,y is the centre (0.5,0.5 = middle of the clip), w,h the size (1 = clip size), rotation in degrees, feather 0..1 softens the edge, round 0..1 rounds rectangle corners, invert shows the outside instead. Changing the type resets the geometry to that shape's defaults; omitted fields keep their value. type may be omitted to tweak an existing mask.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `feather` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Edge softness: 0 = hard edge, 1 = very soft. Unit: fraction 0..1. |
| `h` | number (clip fraction) | no |  | 0.01 … 4 | Mask height relative to the clip height (mirror band height, circle, rectangle, heart, star). |
| `invert` | boolean | no |  |  | Show the area outside the shape instead of inside. |
| `rotation` | number (degrees) | no |  | -360 … 360 | Rotation of the mask shape in degrees clockwise. |
| `round` | number | no |  | 0 … 1 | Corner roundness of the rectangle mask: 0 = square corners, 1 = pill shape. Unit: fraction 0..1. |
| `type` | string | no |  | `none`, `linear`, `mirror`, `circle`, `rectangle`, `heart`, `star` | Mask shape; none removes the mask. Required when the clip has no mask yet. |
| `w` | number (clip fraction) | no |  | 0.01 … 4 | Mask width relative to the clip width (circle, rectangle, heart, star). |
| `x` | number (clip fraction) | no |  | -1 … 2 | Horizontal centre of the mask (0 = left edge of the clip, 0.5 = middle, 1 = right edge). |
| `y` | number (clip fraction) | no |  | -1 … 2 | Vertical centre of the mask (0 = top edge of the clip, 0.5 = middle, 1 = bottom edge). |

**Returns:** {segment} with segment.mask (omitted when removed).

Example — Circular spotlight:

```json
{"feather":0.2,"h":0.5,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","type":"circle","w":0.5}
```

Example — Split screen with a linear mask:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","rotation":90,"segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","type":"linear"}
```

Example — Remove the mask:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","type":"none"}
```

### segment.set_opacity

**Set opacity** · MCP tool `segment_set_opacity` · `POST /api/v1/commands/segment.set_opacity` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Video/Basic/Blend/Opacity

Sets how opaque a visual segment is — Video → Basic → Blend → Opacity in CapCut (0 = invisible, 1 = fully opaque; the inspector shows 0..100%). Works for video, photo, sticker and text segments. If opacity is animated by keyframes the value is recorded as a keyframe at the playhead.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `opacity` | number | yes |  | 0 … 1 | Opacity: 0 = transparent, 0.5 = half see-through, 1 = opaque. Unit: fraction 0..1. |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |

**Returns:** {segment, keyframed?}.

Example — Half transparent overlay:

```json
{"opacity":0.5,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### segment.set_transform

**Set transform** · MCP tool `segment_set_transform` · `POST /api/v1/commands/segment.set_transform` · undoable · UI: Inspector/Video/Basic/Transform

Sets position, scale, rotation and flips of a visual segment — Video → Basic → Transform in the CapCut inspector (also used for text and stickers). Only supplied fields change. Units: x and y move the centre of the clip in canvas fractions (0 = centred, 1 = centre on the right/bottom edge, -1 = left/top edge; positive y is down; range -2..2); scale is a multiplier where 1 = fit inside the canvas (0.01..4, i.e. 1%..400%); rotation is in degrees clockwise (-360..360). If a property is animated by keyframes, its new value is stored as a keyframe at the playhead instead (listed in result.keyframed), exactly like dragging a slider in CapCut after adding a keyframe. Audio, effect, filter and adjustment segments have no picture and are rejected with invalid_argument.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get. |
| `flip_h` | boolean | no |  |  | Mirror horizontally (same as timeline.segment.mirror). |
| `flip_v` | boolean | no |  |  | Flip vertically (upside down mirror). |
| `rotation` | number (degrees) | no |  | -360 … 360 | Rotation in degrees clockwise around the clip centre. |
| `scale` | number (multiplier) | no |  | 0.01 … 4 | Size relative to 'fit inside the canvas': 1 = 100%, 0.5 = 50%, 2 = 200%. |
| `x` | number (canvas fractions) | no |  | -2 … 2 | Horizontal offset of the clip centre: 0 = centred, 1 = centre on the right edge, -1 = on the left edge. |
| `y` | number (canvas fractions) | no |  | -2 … 2 | Vertical offset of the clip centre: 0 = centred, 1 = centre on the bottom edge, -1 = on the top edge. |

**Returns:** {segment: the updated segment, keyframed?: properties written as keyframes at the playhead}.

Example — Picture-in-picture in the top-right corner at 40%:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","scale":0.4,"segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f","x":0.6,"y":-0.6}
```

Example — Tilt 15 degrees:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","rotation":15,"segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

Example — Mirror the clip:

```json
{"flip_h":true,"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

## Window

4 commands: `ui.library_tab`, `ui.open_project`, `ui.select`, `ui.toast`.
Reference page: https://gitkalenyuk.github.io/kadr/docs/ai/reference/window.html

### ui.library_tab

**Switch library tab** · MCP tool `ui_library_tab` · `POST /api/v1/commands/ui.library_tab`

Switches the left library panel of the open window to a tab (Media, Audio, Text, Stickers, Effects, Transitions, Captions, Transcript, Filters, Adjustment, My kit), like clicking the tab. Purely visual.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tab` | string | yes |  | `media`, `audio`, `text`, `stickers`, `effects`, `transitions`, `captions`, `transcript`, `filters`, `adjustment`, `templates` | Tab id; "templates" is the My kit tab. |

**Returns:** {ok: true}.

Example — Show transitions:

```json
{"tab":"transitions"}
```

### ui.open_project

**Show project in the window** · MCP tool `ui_open_project` · `POST /api/v1/commands/ui.open_project`

Opens a project in the editor window, exactly like double-clicking it on the Home screen. Changes no project data and is not undoable; it only tells every open Kadr window (desktop app or web mode) to switch to this project so a human can watch the edits an AI agent makes through the API. Has no effect when no window is open.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |

**Returns:** {ok: true}.

Example — Show the project being edited:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f"}
```

### ui.select

**Select clip in the window** · MCP tool `ui_select` · `POST /api/v1/commands/ui.select`

Selects a clip on the timeline of the open window (and shows its properties in the inspector), like clicking it. Pass segment_id "" to clear the selection. Purely visual — no project data changes, nothing is undoable; useful so a human can follow which clip an AI agent is working on.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | string | yes |  |  | ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create. |
| `segment_id` | string | yes |  |  | Clip to select (from timeline.get), or "" to clear the selection. |

**Returns:** {ok: true}.

Example — Select a clip:

```json
{"project_id":"prj_1a2b3c4d5e6f","segment_id":"seg_9f8e7d6c5b4a"}
```

### ui.toast

**Show a message in the window** · MCP tool `ui_toast` · `POST /api/v1/commands/ui.toast`

Shows a short notification at the top of the open window — handy for an AI agent to narrate what it is doing ("Adding captions…") while a human watches. Purely visual; nothing is stored.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values / range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | string | yes |  |  | Bold first line of the notification. |
| `body` | string | no |  |  | Optional second line with details. |

**Returns:** {ok: true}.

Example — Narrate a step:

```json
{"body":"Cube turn between every clip","title":"Adding transitions"}
```
